On the one hand, there are plenty of waterslides/pools that are a good fit for young "riders", on the other hand, Sandcastle, like any city amusement park, attracts more than its fair share of highschool kids looking to spend some time away from their parents and assert their personhood. Unfortunately that element doesn't particularly care about "censoring" speech for 9 year old ears, and worse, in the Mon Tsunami, about personal space, since the wave pool becomes a near mosh pit of jostling and strutting and shoving and 'showing off' for the fairer sex, and that can be a little dicey for the littler kids. Having said that, it's still a good day at the park.. . cheese fries, a cool dip in the pool on a hot day, some fun slides.. . I think in rating Sandcastle fairly you have to understand the context of the park. Wow, they were not kidding about this place being small! I think my living room is bigger. In total, there were only 9 groups in the entire place and they were at capacity and we were less than a foot away from the group dining next to us (who were rather uppity and kept looking at us as if we were intruding on their dining experience by sitting near them) so I understand why they require reservations. I would say the average age of the people dining was around 50-60+. I felt a little young being there, but I wasn't treated that way by the staff, it was more from the patrons, who I think were a little full of themselves (most had that 'I'm SO important' vibe going on. ) nnI did not get the pretentious air at all from the staff that I was expecting while I was at the restaurant, but I did while making the reservation (don't contact them online or leave a message, they don't call you back and the people on the phone aren't very pleasant -they were even snippy when we called to confirm the reservation). I had the shrimp with the cole slaw and corn bread for an appetizer. While it sounds like an odd mix, I was actually sad when I finished it. I don't even like cole slaw and I was tempted to start licking my plate just to get the last parts that I couldn't pick up with my fork. For my main course I had the chicken with spinach and mashed potatoes. Yum. Yum. Yum. Everything had so much flavor and tasted fresh. All of us at the table ordered something different and every serving was met with mmm's to near moaning so I think my entire party was pleased with their meal. The food is excellent and the portions are large (the mussels appetizer could be a meal) so you aren't left feeling hungry and bitter and when the $$$ check shows up. We never felt rushed and the evening was very relaxing and pleasant. We even got to meet the chef/owner Bruce, who is very friendly, which was an added plus.

The building looks like the remains of an old house. The walk to the hostess is a bit awkward as you're walking through the front patio full of guests already enjoying their meal. That not really being an issue, you'll step into the 'foyer' where you're greeted and offered various seating options. We were escorted upstairs to a cute dining area with large windows and a very charming ambiance. We were seated and not shortly after were greeted by our server.. . 'Shipwreck'. Yeah, I'm not kidding.. . He said his name was "Shipwreck", even after questioning him.. . this set the tone for the night. He was very knowledgeable of both the liquor and food menus and was jolly, and appeared to really love his job; Attentive and courteous as well as entertaining. The food was amazing! When you go, if you're like me, you'll be snapping photos of the names they have come up with for the array of 'American Cuisine'. Things like the "spin spin sugar' Salad, or the "Aw, you're pullin' my pork" pork sandwich. Everything was geared toward putting a smile on my face; and I thoroughly enjoyed myself. I do enjoy Barnes & Nobles but sometimes i get lost just trying to find a darn calendar. I went here after a dinner date with some neighbors and couldn't believe how packed it was. We had to wait 10 minutes just to find enough chairs to seat 4 people. We ended up stealing them from other tables. Not to mention my hubby stood in line for 15 minutes just to get an Ice tea lemonade. So amidst all the books, newspapers and magazines they have an audio and video section. The prices aren't anything to rave about. I can buy the same movies online for a lot cheaper there's just the waiting period. I do shop here sometimes for there discount books. I found a lot of great recipe and mystery books for really cheap, like under $5. That's a pretty good deal but considering there is a half priced book store who has a great selection of books for literally half the price of retailers, how can you beat those prices. B&N is more of a hangout spot with books in case you want to buy one right there and then. But everything is kind of confusing you always need to ask where something is. I'd rather shop online for anything i really want. It's just not worth it to buy it wholesale.

I thought is would be a very nice meal and someplace I had not taken them before. Eating in the best restaurants in town and when we travel is not unusual. The food was very hit-and-miss and so was the service. Let's start with the food. We ordered two appetizers for the table that were not part of restaurant week. The Calamari and the Mozzarella wrapped cheese. The calamari was excellent and cooked perfectly. The Mozzarella was good but not the tastiest or smoothest mozzarella I have eaten. Both were worthy. For the first course, my oldest son had the clam chowder which he enjoyed. The rest of us ordered the mixed field greens salad which was awful. I have had a better side salad at Wendy's. It was totally tasteless and un-inspired. None of us even finished half the portion. When the waiters helper asked if we were done, we told him to please take them away and how horrible they were. The three men had the filet for our main course. It was a very middle of the road filet. I am not sure if they lowered their quality for restaurant week but it tasted no better than an Outback Steak. Even my 15 year old recognized the poor quality of meat. My wife had the Salmon which was better than the filet but nothing exciting. She only ate half the portion and it was not worth packing up to take home. The mashed potato side was amazing and the creamed spinach side was average. The creme brulee and flourless chocolate cake for desert were both amazing. I would recommend just hitting the bar for these late night after a show. The service was also only marginal. A big let down compared to the service received at lunch. The waiter reached across the table versus walking around, and he plated the food close but not just right so you had to re-arrange the positioning of every dish before eating it. The atmosphere is beautiful. I would return for a business lunch but don't waste your time or money on dinner or taking someone you want to impress.

Lidia's was a major disappointment for me. Decor and service were just fine, no issues there. But the food was something I would expect from a chain restaurant like Carrabba's or Olive Garden. The quality seemed poor: bread was soggy, greens and salad dressings way over salted, greasy, sloppy pasta sauces, and huge portions just slapped onto dirty plates with greasy fingerprints all over the edges. Plus, I spent the entire meal swatting flies away from our table. I was really puzzled by this experience. When you dine at Joe's restaurants, you get the sense that every single ingredient is hand selected for the highest quality and the presentation of the food shows care went into it. I expected a similar standard at Lidia's. I wondered if Lidia visits this restaurant often and whether she knows about the quality of the food. Celebrity chefs often seem to suffer from this issue: they get involved in so many business ventures and if they are not at the restaurants regularly, the quality suffers. Sorry to say it, but I definitely won't be back to Lidia's.

Willow Ridge Apartments are a great value for the money. The one and two bedroom floor plans offer plenty of space at a very reasonable price. All units come fully equipped with modern appliances including a dishwasher, microwave, and washer/dryer. The property is located just a short drive from downtown, providing easy access to shopping, restaurants, and entertainment. The open floor plans allow natural light to flow throughout the units. Upgraded features like nine-foot ceilings and oversized windows make the apartments feel bright and airy. The kitchen cabinets have softened close technology for a luxury feeling. Residents appreciate the added spaces for storage in both the kitchen and generous walk-in closets.Community amenities really make Willow Ridge stand out. There is a year-round heated pool, hot tub, and grilling area. During the spring and summer, residents take advantage of the outdoor fireplace for relaxing evenings. The 24-hour fitness center has brand new equipment and comes fully stocked with weights, machines, and free weights.Maintenance issues are rarely a problem as the management team is quick to respond to any resident concerns. Landscaping crews keep the beautifully manicured grounds in tip top shape all year round. Overall safety and security are a top priority with a gated entrance and on-site courtesy patrol. In addition to inexpensive living, Willow Ridge offers a sense of community through planned social events. Neighbors regularly get together for games nights, potlucks, and seasonal celebrations which really foster a friendly atmosphere. Both children and pets are welcome, making it a perfect place for any lifestyle.I would definitely recommend Willow Ridge Apartments to anyone looking for an affordable yet high quality place to call home. The value you receive here is unmatched in the area.

Alright, buckle up because I've got a story to tell you! So, there I was, feeling hungry and in the mood for some good old greasy fast food. I walked into this restaurant that I had heard about from a friend, all excited and ready to indulge in some guilty pleasure. But boy, was I in for a disappointment!As soon as I stepped inside, I was hit by a wave of noise and chaos. People were chatting it up at the counter, kids were running around, and the sound of sizzling burgers filled the air. It felt like I had stumbled upon the world's busiest intersection, except it was a fast-food joint. Now, don't get me wrong, I expected it to be crowded, but this was something else entirely.I stood there, trying to figure out what my next move should be. The menu was plastered on the wall with an assortment of bright, vibrant pictures that made my stomach growl. I turned to the cashier, ready to place my order, only to be met with a look that screamed, "Why are you bothering me?"I mustered up the courage to ask a question about the menu, but the cashier's response was so curt and dismissive, I felt like I had just committed a crime. It was absurd! I mean, I understand they're busy and all, but a little bit of customer service wouldn't hurt, right? Was it too much to ask for a smile or a polite answer?Anyway, I decided to suck it up and place my order. I settled on a classic cheeseburger combo with all the fixings. It sounded delicious, and I hoped it would make up for the less-than-stellar service I had encountered so far. After what felt like an eternity of waiting, my food finally arrived.I took a bite of the burger, expecting heaven in my mouth, but what I got was closer to disappointment. The patty was dry and overcooked, the cheese barely melted, and the bun tasted like it had been sitting out for hours. It was such a letdown. I've had better burgers at a backyard barbecue!To top it all off, the fries were limp and soggy.

The atmosphere is great and the martini list is extensive. I've ordered the cake batter, caramel apple, and s'mores and haven't been disappointed in any so far. The buffalo chicken dip appetizer is what keeps us coming back! It is served cold in a martini glass with warm pita chips and is just amazing! I've ordered several dishes and haven't had a bad meal either! The only thing that lacks sometimes is the service, especially on my last visit. We were standing at the hostess stand for a couple of minutes and no one came over. Finally a girl did but she just looked at us, got something, and walked away. Not even a "someone will be right with you". Then another girl came over and said "do you need a table? ". I wanted to respond with "why would I be standing at a podium that says let us seat you", but I refrained. We were seated, it took several more minutes for our drink order to be taken and it was subpar service the rest of the night. Waiting, waiting, and more waiting. Other than that, love the food, love the atmosphere and especially love the martinis!

"Never judge a book by its cover," as the age-old saying goes. Monte Cello's Downtown is a prime example of this wisdom, as it unveils a hidden culinary treasure once you step inside. The interior exudes a cozy and charming ambiance, with soft lighting and tasteful decor that sets the stage for an unforgettable dining experience. From the moment you walk through the door, the attentive staff warmly welcomes you, making you feel right at home.The menu at Monte Cello's Downtown is a testament to their unwavering commitment to quality and flavor. Their extensive selection of Italian dishes caters to every palate, offering traditional classics like spaghetti carbonara and innovative creations like truffle-infused gnocchi. Each dish is meticulously crafted with care and precision.The flavors that emanate from the kitchen are truly extraordinary. The sauces are rich and velvety, leaving a lingering depth of flavor on your palate. The pasta is cooked to perfection, and the locally sourced ingredients are fresh and vibrant, showcasing their dedication to top-notch quality.At Monte Cello's Downtown, portion sizes are generous, ensuring that no guest leaves hungry. Remarkably reasonable prices accompany the outstanding quality and portion sizes, making it a fantastic value for your money. Whether you're enjoying a romantic date night or a family gathering, Monte Cello's Downtown offers a welcoming and relaxed atmosphere suitable for all occasions.To enhance the delightful food, the restaurant boasts an extensive wine list, featuring both domestic and imported selections. Their knowledgeable sommelier is always available to recommend the perfect pairing for your meal, taking your dining experience to new heights.The real highlight of Monte Cello's Downtown, however, lies in their delectable desserts. Treat yourself to their homemade tiramisu, heavenly cheesecake, or their renowned cannoli, each bite brimming with sweetness and satisfaction.

There have some serious Jimmy John's speed going on with their delivery. The delivery driver has always been friendly and polite. So why am I not giving fortune cookie 5 stars? The answer is simple, I can't award Fortune Cookie 5 stars, because I've been in the actual establishment within the past month and they had a sanitation rating of 87. Its low and it scares me. However, that should tell you how good I think there food is - I gladly continue to frequent this establishment despite this stomach quivering low sanitation rating.

The gelato counter was disappointing. Despite its promising display of tempting flavors and vibrant colors, the taste fell flat, leaving much to be desired. It lacked the smooth and creamy texture that one would expect from authentic Italian gelato. The flavors were underwhelming, with a noticeable artificial aftertaste that lingered unpleasantly on the palate. Moreover, the limited variety offered little room for exploration or experimentation. The prices, considering the subpar quality, were exorbitant, making the overall value for money quite poor. ahhh dor-stop. These two words encapsulated a pure pleasure when they stepped into the Pittsburgh gem. DOR-Stop is located in the center of the city. It is a simple restaurant with the charm of the old world, which can immediately bring you to the past. When you walk through the door, you will attract a warm smile and the intoxicating aroma of freshly brew coffee. Decoration with old -fashioned souvenirs and comfortable booths, creating a feeling like a home outside the home. When you settle down, you will read a wide range of menu, which is a true proof of Dor-Stop's cooking ability. From the classic breakfast staple foods such as fluffy pancakes and crispy bacon to the mouth -watering fried egg rolls, it is full of delicious fillings and can satisfy each desire. These ingredients are purchased locally, showing the restaurant's commitment to quality and support for local farmers. The remaining dishes are their iconic Pittsburgh -style French toast. The thick bread is generously applied to the eggs, cinnamon and a trace of vanilla paradise -like mixture, and then bake it perfectly. The result is a masterpiece of golden brown, which has achieved a perfect balance between the soft and seductive tightening of the pillow. There is a group of cream butter and a small rain maple syrup. It is a paradise -like symphony that will make your taste buds sing. If you want to eat delicious things, then Monte Cristo sandwiches must be tried. The salty ham, Turkish and Swiss cheese layers are sandwiched between two golden French toasts, forming a pleasant sweetness and salty taste. Each occlusion is a harmonious texture and flavor mixture, which will make you more eager. Dor-Stop's service is also worth mentioning. The staff is very careful, friendly and enthusiastic to ensure that each guest has an unforgettable dining experience.

I usually have nothing but good things to say about this place. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, with a cozy interior and soft lighting that creates a relaxed ambiance. The staff members are incredibly friendly and attentive, always ready to greet you with a smile and offer expert recommendations. The menu is a culinary delight, showcasing a diverse range of dishes that cater to various dietary preferences. From classic comfort foods to innovative creations, each plate is a work of art bursting with flavors. The ingredients are fresh and of the highest quality, evident in every bite. The presentation is impeccable, demonstrating the chef's meticulous attention to detail. The portion sizes are generous, ensuring you leave satisfied and content. Moreover, the restaurant prides itself on sourcing local produce and supporting sustainable practices, which adds to the overall positive experience. The wine list is extensive, featuring an impressive selection that complements the menu perfectly. Servers are knowledgeable and happy to provide wine pairing suggestions. The prices are reasonable considering the high-quality ingredients and exceptional culinary experience. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply treating yourself to a delicious meal, this place never disappoints. With its outstanding service, delectable food, and delightful ambiance, it continues to be one of my go-to restaurants in the city.

I really think that this place is geared towards children more so than adults or "family" because there isn't much fun here for people older than 16. The water slides here were lacking. There were very few of them and the majority of them are boring. The last time I was there (not too long ago) there weren't any extremely modern slides like a tornado slide, so they really have some updating to do. They do have an "adult pool" and bar area but it was so packed that it was hard to actually have fun in this area. The pool is very small, similar to one you'd find at a hotel chain. It has a hot tub area but it sits about 8 adults max. and people were fighting tooth and nail to get in. It wasn't too impressive to me. They also have a lazy river at this park and, while I do enjoy lazy rivers, this one was so packed that it was hard to breathe. People kept bumping into me and touching me and it made me grossed out. The one attraction that I did enjoy was the wave pool. It was crowded as well but large enough to fit everybody comfortably. The water was nice and clean (a big plus) and the wave action was strong. I could have stayed in there for the entire time we were at the park. Overall, this place is just mediocre. It doesn't "wow" me very much but if you live in the area, have kids, and are looking for somewhere to go in the summer other than the mall, it'll provide them with a lot of fun.

Intimidator and Cobra, and that's all you need to know. While they may lack finesse, these two rides make up for it with simpler thrills. Intimidator launches riders up the lift hill before plunging down the vertical drop at over 85 miles per clock. Per the first second of free fall, all sense of control is stripped away leaving only adrenaline. Cobra on the other hand is a tightly wound spins monstrosity that flings riders through multiple inversions at terrifying speeds. No safety equipment is needed on these machines, just a mort grip on the handles and the ability to preserve your lunch down. Waiting in line provides plenty of time to contemplating this decision, but the moment you're closed in there is no turning back. Each twist and flip pries a new scream from your throat as G forces pummel your body into the borders. Only the brief respite of the brake runs allow ragged breather before the next onslaught. Nearing the end, chivalry cling to hope of surviving the experience intact. But there are still surprises in depots, like Cobra's breathtaking diving loop where the track disappears below. Adrenaline continues to pump even after staggering elsewhere weak-kneed and begging for solid ground. The sheer intensity leaves an indelible mark, and thoughts immediately revolve to facing the beast again for another go. While their breakneck speeds, both rides operate like precise machines. Businessmen dispatch trains with military precision to keep the throughput high. Passing empty trains swoop by like ominous steel ghost hinting at the terror inside. Watching from below provides no sens of scale for how massive these titans truly are. Only from the cockpit does their full size and muscle were apparent. Even seasoned rollercoaster fans uncovered themselves humbled by Intimidator and Cobra.

It's clear they don't value keeping customers - just nickel and diming captives for as long as they stay on board. No other provider is perfect but surely there are better options than rewarding such blatant incompetence. Time Warner Cable should be ashamed of how they conduct business.

It was so highly reviewed, but absolutely terrible. Not that we ate the food, because we never had a chance. We were seated immediately in an area with another table that was served by our server. There were only two tables taken in the restaurant and our server took 10+ minutes to bring us drinks. Still waiting on our drinks, our appetizer came out with no silverware, no plates, still no drinks. Our server came by (we had already asked him about the drinks once). Shortly thereafter, he brought the drinks, still no plates and no silverware. We waited a few more minutes and he brought out our salads. Still no plates and no silverware. When we asked again about the plates, he laughed as though we had made some strange request. We continued to wait - no chopsticks, no silverware, no plates - after it became too ridiculous to handle we got up and walked out It's the only place that we've ever done that before - and we have had some terrible service. The food that we stared at looked terrible - in hindsight I'm glad that we had no utensils. If you have an hour to kill, are looking for terrible service, aren't in a rush, and want to order some food that looks disgusting you may want to check it out; otherwise, stay away!

The interior was modern and sleek, but the service was slow and unfriendly. I was looking forward to trying this new Asian fusion restaurant in town, but my meal was a disappointment. The menu had a lot of interesting dishes, but the ones I tried were not well executed. I was expecting a unique and exciting dining experience, but instead I felt like I was eating at a mediocre chain restaurant. I ordered the kimchi risotto, which was overcooked and bland. The sushi rolls were also a disappointment, with too much rice and not enough fish. I was looking forward to trying their desserts, but after the disappointing meal, I didn't have the appetite. I won't be back and I won't recommend it to my friends and family. The prices were also high, especially considering the quality of the food. I hope they can improve their menu and service in the future, because there is definitely potential for this place to be great. Overall, I would give this restaurant two stars out of five. It's a shame, because the atmosphere was promising, but the food and service didn't live up to my expectations. I understand that it's difficult to get everything right, especially when you're a new restaurant, but it's important to deliver on the promises you make to your customers. It's not a complete loss, but there is definitely room for improvement. I would suggest that they start by revamping their menu and training their staff to provide better service. I hope that my review will help them to identify the areas that need improvement and make the necessary changes. It's always disappointing when a restaurant doesn't live up to your expectations, but I'm looking forward to trying other places and finding new favorites. I won't be deterred from trying new restaurants in the future, but for now I won't be back to this one. I'll keep an eye out for any changes and maybe give it another try in the future.

I am so glad Miss Alison suggested this place while we were in town. She's vegan and they have plenty of options for her. We came here with friends for dinner after Day 1 of selling at Handmade Arcade. We got there just in time since it got packed shortly after we sat down. There was a slight language barrier, so instead of getting the chicken with crispy noodles, I got tofu, but you know what? I didn't even notice until 5 minutes after eating and then I looked across the table at my friend Jessica's dish that clearly had chicken and we had ordered the same thing. Oh well. I don't regret it at all. It was delicious and I ate every bite. Also the vegetable gyoza we started with was very tasty. Will definitely add this into my rotation of Pittsburghian restaurants I hit up when I am there. I heart Pittsburgh!

The food and decor are at odds with each other, but that doesn't mean it's not worth a vis it. The food is astonishingly good, and the service is excellent. The ambiance and decor are more like a coffee shop than a restaurant, but the fo od is definitely restaurant-quality. The mneu is limited, but everything is made fresh to order. The pizzas are especially good, and the salads are very fresh. Te desserts are also very good, and the prices are very reasonable. Overll, this is a great place to eat if you're looking for something a little different.

This storied blues club draws both famous and up-and-coming musicians to its stage. The intimate space features exposed brick walls and low lighting, creating a comfortable atmosphere to focus on the performances. Drinks are reasonably priced for the area, with a good selection of tap beers and crafted cocktails. On weekends, the venue fills with blues enthusiasts of all ages eager to experience live music up close in the packed room. The sound system ensures every nuance of the musicians' playing rings clear throughout the room. We recently stopped by on a Tuesday for their weekly open mic night and were impressed by the skill shown by both seasoned regulars and newcomers honing their craft. It's evident from both the staff and performers' passions that everyone loves what they do and is dedicated to the blues genre. I plan to return to catch touring acts and stay late as informal jam sessions often erupt after scheduled shows end. For an authentic blues club vibe in a laidback neighborhood spot, this is the place to spend an evening immersed in live music.

The chicken is always juicy and flavorful, the pita is soft and fluffy, and the sauces are surprising. The staff is always friendly and welcoming, and the prices are very healthy. I love that they have a variety of chances, including vegetarian and gluten-free dishes. They also have a great rewards program that makes it easy to save money on your favorite diet. Showmars is definitely one of my favorite eat in town. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and affordable restaurant. The atmosphere is casual and relaxed, making it a enormous place to eat with friends or family. The location is usefulness, and there is plenty of parking. Overall, Showmars is a great option for a quick and tasty gastronomy.

It's located in Shadyside, an area that I rarely venture out to for fear of destroying my car, but I will make the trek for Soba. And Mad Mex. As others have noted, the restaurant is very intimate. Compared to Eleven, which is classy and upscale but rather casual (if that makes sense), Soba is definitely date night territory. In fact, my boyfriend took me on our first date to Soba followed by an awesome evening at Cirque de Soleil. What a night it was. This restaurant is up to the standards of quality and service that all of Big Burrito's restaurants offer. The food is amazing, the drinks are tasty, and the staff are super friendly. The Asian Plum Sangria and the Bangkok Tea are my favorite drinks there, highly recommend them. The one called Offer You Can't Refuse - be careful. Tasty, but be careful. As far as food, excepting one time we've always just ordered a round of different appetizers and spent the night sampling. I've never had anything I didn't like, and I in fact highly recommend the crispy tofu. Yum-my. Even if you think you don't like tofu, you feel so wrong about that stance once you've eaten theirs. The only time we ordered entrees was on NYE. We engaged in their pre-fixe menu for the holiday. I can't remember what we had, but I do remember all of it being awesome. It was a really great way to spend NYE, avoiding any type of craziness and filling up on some good food.

The staff were all very pleasant and helpful, especially [NAMuE] at the front desk. The room was clean and comfortable, but the decor was a bit daetd. The bed was comfortable and the sheets were osft, but the pillows were a Fit too soft for my taste. Th bathroom was clean and well-appointed, but the shower was a bit small. The breakfast buffet was good, but the selection was a bit limied. The location of the hotel was good, but it was a bwit noisy at night. The pool was nice, but it was a bit crowedd. The fitness center was well-equtpped, but it was a bit small. The business center was well-equipped, but it was a bit expensiev. Did I mention that I forgot my water bottle on my ride too? I was a desperate woman at the end of that one. So I got home aired myself out and drove myself to Enrico's since a previous yelper mentioned she had the best iced caffe mocha there. There was easy street parking right out front and I really liked that it was nestled in the middle of a neighborhood and not a loud crowded street. Tables are large enough for good work space and folks had their laptops out inside enjoying the free wifi while the tables outside were filled with friends. So why the 3 stars? Well the iced caffe mocha was a bit subpar. The syrup was all at the bottom leaving my first couple sips very watery. Could have been a better mix. Would I give this another try? Sure but I definitely will ask for a nice hard shake of my iced caffe mocha before taking a swig. The coffee place at the Walnut Mall in Shadyside is still my favorite for the iced coffee of the year award. Try the iced OR blended ghiradelli mocha when you are shopping Shady-style - AWESOME!

Ok, so if you're looking for a great steakhouse without the prententious atmosphere I think you'll find it here. It's my favorite premium steakhouse based on the fact they treat you like family every single time. The wine selections are great and plenty. I normally stick with the house Merlot or Pinot Noir. Of course I normally always get a steak so always reds for me ;)nnAs you might know everything is a'la carte and served family style. They have a great selection of salads and the blue cheese wedge is an all time classic there. The sides for the entrees are also fantastic. I normally stick with the asparagus friti or the three cheese mashed potatoes. I've had both the lobster and a few of the steak selections when visiting. My favorite steak there is the filet mignon oscar, medium, slightly pink in the center. Always served to protection and a perfect temp. Deserts are no slouch either here. Most are pretty large and of course one of my favorites is probably one of the largest they have. The 7-layer chocolate cake.. .. chocolate overload! No doubt, this is a fantastic place for a quick bar bite after work all the way to special dinners for anniversaries or just because type dinners. NOTE: The Palm also has a 'rewards program' of sorts. You join for I think $50 for the years and you get a point for every dollar spent. Once you reach 500 points you automatically get a free 3lb lobster for your birthday.. .. ummm.. .. . yes!

I stopped by here this past Tuesday with my father for lunch. It was a beautiful day, and we decided to sit outside and enjoy the sunshine. The patio was cozy, with a few tables and a nice ambiance. The restaurant itself was small, but it had a lot of character. The decor was modern and stylish, with a few funky touches here and there. The menu was diverse, with a mix of traditional and contemporary dishes. I ordered the Cobb salad, which was fresh and delicious. My father got the burger, which he said was cooked to perfection. The service was attentive and friendly, and our server was knowledgeable about the menu. We had a great time chatting with her and learning about the local area. Overall, it was a fantastic experience, and I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a tasty meal in a relaxed setting.

The hostess and bartender were great. They great you with a smile and pleasantly wait on you. The food is just OK. The hostess greated us with a smile and mentioned it would be about 15 minutes. We asked if we could eat at the bar and he said of course. We found a small booth at the bar. On our way back we noticed that there were several empty tables available. We found this strange and that is one reason I gave them 3 stars. We were greated by the bartender, who was quite nice looking, with a smile. He had alot of tables and still seemed to manage pouring drinks and delivering food. He was great at his job. I ordered tortilla soup and salad with raspberry vinaigrette and it was good, delivered with a smile, and timely. The bartender kept our drinks full as well. I would give the service 5 stars, food 3 stars, size of the restaurant is large but they never seem to be staffed for it so that i would give 1 star. Great place to go for a quick lunch! !

I don't think I would have stumbled upon this place just upon chance. I made a reservation for three on a Tuesday night at 7. My two friends were already there and then.. . there was just me in the restaurant, which scared me a little bit but I have to have faith in my fellow Yelpers. The waitress was an adorable woman who was so friendly, helpful and enthusiastic about the dishes in a quiet manner. You just wanted to pinch her cheeks or something. Anyway she gave us some bread which was sweet, unlike many of the other restaurants breads that I have had, which I enjoyed. We ordered the goat cheese for an appetizer which was just so ooey and gooey deliciousness and then for the piece de resistance ordered the sea bass special that night which had capers, a potato, rice and some roasted vegetables. Great light combination and not too heavy. The size of the sea bass was like of the entire whole fish. To top it off we had the rice pudding dessert which was similar to flan but I thought this was so tasty. I kind of want one right now as I am typing this review. n I am so glad I went to Cafe Zinho finally and would happily come back here again.

Overall, Fusion is an outstanding restaurant, and we strongly recommend anyone who wants a unique and delicious food.

While the major Orlando parks like Disney and Universal set the gold standard for immersive theming and world-class attractions, Carowinds introduced me to the unique charms of a smaller regional park. Compared to its bigger siblings, Carowinds showed signs of aging from tired theming to dated rides. However, the park makes the most of its more limited budget by still offering a fair selection of rollercoasters and other rides to keep guests occupied for the day. While theming could use refreshing, I enjoyed experiencing rides unique to Carowinds like Flying Comets and Wooden Warrior. Spotting nods to both North and South Carolina throughout also gave the park local flavor. The boardwalk provided a pleasant break from busier areas with its charming town vibes. Some sections, though, felt worn.Attendance understandably didn't match the bustle of Orlando giants. However, shorter lines allowed us to try more rides efficiently. Sparsely populated areas detracted from atmosphere somewhat. With revitalization and investment, Carowinds shows promise as a quality regional escape. Currently, Orlando veterans may find it pales in comparison. But for a convenient day out from Charlotte, it offers decent value for time on rides.

Invited another couple to join us for dinner and a play on a Friday night. We chose an upscale restaurant downtown that we had wanted to try. The food and service did not disappoint, as we all enjoyed our meals together. After dinner we walked a few blocks to the theater, finding our seats just before the lights went down. $7 gets you 2 pieces of deep fried cod, fries, slaw, roll, and soda. Fish was solid - nicely done, especially for the price and speed. Detailed review: nnI'd never visited the Middleton Sport Bowl prior to today, so I wasn't quite sure what to expect. We arrived exactly at noon, parked, and made our way to the bar, where we found two seats and were promptly greeted by a bartender. We both ordered the lunch special - 2 piece deep fried cod plate with fries, slaw, tartar, dinner roll, and soda. The bartender took our order and came back with a complimentary bowl of popcorn, which was a nice surprise. Plates arrived about 10 minutes later - the fish was appropriately sized, as were the fries - no imbalance, and portions were fair. The fish itself had a flavorful beer batter that was a little thicker than what you'll typically find at most places, but it was delicious and I welcomed the extra crunch. Inside, the fish itself was a tad watery with just a hint of grease - not anything outrageous, but just enough to sense that it was there. Flavor of the fish was incredibly mild; the batter stole some of its thunder. The fries were excellent - battered-style and straight cut. I'm told the slaw and tartar were "average. " Dinner roll was hard and dry. Total lunch bill for two: $14. 64, and we were in-and-out within 35 minutes. Totally acceptable and a good lunch, all things considered. Middleton Sport Bowl = NEUTRALnnFood = 2. 75 to 3 stars (average; not bad, not spectacular)nService = 3. 5 stars (prompt and friendly)nValue = 4 stars nMISC = 3 stars (actually seemed to be a nice bowling alley/bar)nnSummary: Not a win, nor a fail. I'd go back for the fish at lunch, and will definitely be back to sample other foods - the sandwiches looked really good.

It's largely a "self-service" type place, which is fine by me. You place your order at the main counter, get your own coffee and condiments, find a table and wait for the food to arrive. When you're done eating, you clear your own table, take the dishes to the "dish basket" and head on your merry way. The pancakes aren't anything spectacular - just your regular "mix made" pancakes. They're cooked well, with nice color, and are "plate size" so one or two should be plenty for most folks. They're not obscenely thick; in fact, they're a bit on the thin side, come to think of it. Breakfast sandwich is decent - an egg, your choice of meat, some cheese, and served on a muffin. I've also had the Wright Breakfast and today, I had the special, which was two eggs, scrambled with tomatoes, peppers, onion, ham, cheese and a choice of toast. Again - it was good, but not "out of this world great. "nnThey're currently serving Alterra-brand coffee; another review references Ancora, but it looks like they've switched to Alterra. It's good coffee, nonetheless. Staff keeps largely to themselves, which is nice - no one bothers you throughout the meal. They don't take credit/debit cards - it's cash or check only. There's a fair amount of seating indoors and a few metal tables and chairs outside for when the weather is nice. There tends to be a lot of families that meet here on the weekends, so if kids aren't your thing, steer clear on Saturday and Sunday. I had the joy of listening to two screaming kids during my entire meal this morning - the parents were oblivious.. . My biggest gripe? Price. My breakfast this morning ("special" plus two pancakes plus coffee) cost $14. 10. That's a little steep for standard breakfast fare.. . Breakfast is served all-day long on Saturday and Sunday; during the week it's served until 11am, at which point it's lunch only until closing time (around 3pm, I believe).

My department holds its yearly reception here, so I've always been curious how it is like. On the other hand I have heard it's an American-Asian food place, which explains my hesitance to try it out. So the wedding reception was a great opportunity. I would say all my friends were right. Imperial Garden is a mix between authentic chinese food and american chinese food. The peking duck and the appetizer platter were my favorite. The appetizer platter (serves 4) consisted of Egg rolls, grilled pot stickers, bbq pork, crispy shrimp and calamari. Pot stickers were nicely made and flavorful, calamari is also crispy yums Shrimps are lightly breaded and very tasty, could taste how fresh they are. The Peking Duck is also super awesome. Note that you have to order the duck a day in advance. It's a whole duck specially prepared and served in three courses, of which the crispy duck skin with mandarin pancakes is my favorite. Super authentic! You can ask for more pancakes with the dish, yes it is this good! Other dishes we tried include the usual general tso chicken, mongolian pork, stir fry noodles. I would recommend Imperial Garden for special occasions (the restaurant is roomy and nice to accommodate large groups). Order their specialty dishes, they are worth it.

Soul Food gone Gourmet!! This new restaurant takes all the comfort foods we grew up with and elevates them to new heights. Their fried chicken is perfectly cooked, with a seasoned buttermilk batter that is crisp on the outside but moist and tender within. Sides like collard greens, mac and cheese, and candied yams have been refined but still taste just as comforting. Even homemade biscuits and cornbread are fluffier and more flavorful than anything grandma ever made. For those wanting to try soul food with a creative twist, entree options like shrimp and grits take the classic lowcountry dish to a fine dining level. Fresh Gulf shrimp is sauteed to perfection over stone-ground grits enriched with savory broth. You'll also find crab cakes with a unique flair - lump blue crab is combined with just a hint of creole seasoning for a blend of spices that is intriguing without being overpowering.Something for the adventurous eater is the alligator bourguignon. Tender strips of American alligator slowly simmer in a rich wine sauce with crimini mushrooms and smoky bacon. It's a surprising delight for those unfamiliar with alligator meat. Whether you stick to tradition or want to explore new territories, the kitchen staff shines in both familiar flavors and original takes on Southerncomfort classics. The dining room matches the upscale food with a polished but relaxed atmosphere. Soft lighting, white tablecloths and modern art create an elegant setting without pretension. You may just forget you're enjoying down-home cuisine until a wave of flavor transports you straight back to grandma's kitchen. Both newcomers to soul food and lifelong fans will find this restaurant a welcomed addition to the city. With innovative cooking and hospitality this warm and welcoming, it deserves repeat visits.

There are several excellent reasons to visit Sonoma Valley. The region is renowned for its world-class wines, with over 240 wineries spread throughout offering tastings of staple varietals like Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon as well as less common grape varieties. Rolling hills dotted with vineyards and oak trees provide stunning scenery, with views of the Mayacamas Mountains in the distance. A variety of outdoor activities abound, from bicycling along scenic roads and trails to hiking or picnicking in numerous well-maintained state and regional parks filled with vegetation and wildlife. The culinary scene goes beyond wine, featuring many local cheese producers, olive oil artisans, and specialty vendors selling their goods directly at farms, delis, and markets throughout the area. Historic sites like Sonoma Plaza, General Vallejo's Home, and the Sonoma Barracks give insight into Sonoma's rich early Californian history. Charming small towns like Sonoma, Glen Ellen, and Kenwood offer pleasant sidewalk shopping and dining with a relaxed atmosphere less touristy than Napa Valley towns. Events and festivals are scheduled year-round, from harvest celebrations and parades in the fall to arts shows, live music, and outdoor film screenings in nicer months. Lodging accommodations vary from luxurious resorts and bed and breakfast inns to guest ranches and basic motels, providing options for all budgets. Hands-on activities like cooking classes, wine tastings, hot air ballooning excursions, and others allow travelers to directly engage with the region. At a closer proximity to San Francisco than Napa Valley, it enables easier day trips or weekends away without an extensive commute. Stunning wildflower blooms in spring, when hillsides are blanketed with colorful displays, coupled with the generally milder climate compared to surrounding areas, are highlights.

I found the meats to be somewhat dry and tough, similar to that of the goulash. All of this was too bad, because the portions were easily large enough for two meals. Finally, I'm guessing "dry" must be a theme at this place, because even the black forest cake was also a little dry. For the record: I didn't complain nor send any of the food back out of respect for my guest. I just didn't want to create a scene in front of my guest. Waitstaff were prompt enough, but our server kept forgetting drink orders and generally just seemed nonchalant about providing good service. n So, minus one star for the ditzy waitress. Minus 1. 5 stars for the food. I rounded down, because I disagree with the more positive reviews. I was expecting something stellar, and I feel rather let down. I will come back and give them one more chance, but only one more chance.

As a former employee of Cedar Remark (one of the sister parks in the CedarFair Company), Carowinds does not exceed what Cedar Point has to offer. While Carowinds has some exciting rollercoasters, the quality and quantity of coasters at Cedar Items are unmatched. Cedar Remark is home to more rollercoasters than any other park in the world. The rides at Carowinds just can't compare to iconic coasters like Millennium Force and Top Euphoria Dragster. That's not to say Carowinds is a bad piao, it has some fun rides and good theming. But for coaster enthusiasts, Cedar Point is honestly the king of amusement parks. You'll find more extreme rides and terrain there than what Carowinds can offer visits in North Carolina. Overall, Cedar Point delivers more drunkenness and variety for rollercoaster fans.

I'd say i've had a couple of other visits to TGIF's in Charlotte and I don't recall them being a good experience. I kinda forgot that until we headed there on a whim and right away i remembered, ohhhh yea, this place is soooo loud. I'm not talking a little loud, I'm talking scream to place an order or ask your wife sitting next to you what the waiter said. Yep, that loud. nIt took us about 15 minutes to get seated was what they had advised. The waiter was good and provided really good service (Once we could hear each other). It took another 30-45 minutes to get our food and then another 10-15 to get bill and checked out. Almost 2 hours is way to long for a meal, especially when it's impossible to have any sort of conversation with the others in your party. nSo I believe over the years i've tried TGIF's 3 times or so and I'm pretty sure this will be the last time. Fool me once shame on you, fool my twice shame on me, fool me three times.. .. .. .

OPH was the first restaurant I came to when I moved to Charlotte three years ago and it was exactly what I was expecting from my experience at many other locations. I totally fell in love with their classic sausage gravy and biscuits. You guys, I don't know what they put in that gravy but it's just so dang tasty and comforting on a cold morning. The best part is my girlfriend and I can get our fill of it for not too expensive, which was perfect for us poor souls just starting out in a new city. I will say we did have one not so great server once who kinda ruined the experience with bad attitude. But for the most part, the staff has always provided great service with a smile. They do tend to get pretty busy during peak hours so you may have to try a less crowded time if you want quick in and out. The other thing I love is how homey and welcoming the whole vibe feels - it's not some stuffy corporate cafe, you know? Anyways, three years later and I'm still a regular whenever I need a little downhome cooking fix. They'll always have a special place in my heart as my "Charlotte starter home."

Looking for a local fearless spoon in east Charlotte? That place is it. No frills, just really good supper. The portions are huge and the costa are low. The service is friendly and precocious. The food is continuously fresh and delicious. I've been coming here for years and it's perpetually been great. I highly recommend the cheesesteak hoagie, the philly parmesan fries, and the onion rings. The cheesesteak hoagie is made with thinly sliced steak, grilled bunions, and cheese on a hoagie roll. The philly sandwich fries are smothered in cheese and topped with grilled steak. The spinach rings are huge and crispy. Alle is made to order and always fresh. The staff is friendly and conscientious. They ever make sure you have everything you need. The honorarium are very reasonable. You can get a huge feast for under $10. This is a great place to go for a casual meal with friends or parents. It's also a great place to get a quick bite to ate. I highly recommend this dinnertime.

Both bays were full, yet the staff came out and explained to me the wait. No prob. When it went even longer due to a added service by one of the vehicles in the bay, they got right out and let me know. Again, no prob. Appreciate it. Then, they began to in process me before I got in the garage and started a light check. They were on it. After looking at the dipstick, the lead tech explained to me that I did not need an oil change and showed me the oil. Their prompt communications, attention and honesty is a rare find in today's service world. I will be back for sure.. .. and post this to yelp. Jan 2013-Went back a couple months ago. Same thing. Repeated, honest service. Very nice!

I have to say its overrated. I wasn't impressed with my sandwich at all. I ordered the chicken breast, my hubby got the fish, and my SIL got the steak. It had thick white bread, an overload of cole slaw, and fries. I don't think the "meat" you order makes a difference in the bland taste, as it's overpowered by the slaw and fries. The bread was dry on the crust and yet soggy from the slaw/oil from fries. The wait staff wasn't friendly either. They seemed to have the "I don't need try to so hard because we're busy no matter what" attitude. We had to go up to the bar to get refills on our drinks after waiting over 10 min. for the waitress to notice we were out. The place was constantly busy due to the full bar and nostalgic feel of the restaurant; it had it's own local charm. I'm glad to say I tried it, however I probably wouldn't go back on our next visit.

She seemed to not know what a harness was, which I found odd since we were in a animals depots. When I describes what I needed, she immediately directed us to the cat section of the store. I explained that we needed a harnessed for a dog, not a cat. She apologized for the confusion and directed us to a different section of the storeroom. Once we becoming there, it appeared they only had harnesses for very large dogs. I asked the same employee if they carried anything for a smaller bichon, perhaps in the 20-pound range. She informed me they didn't bearer any. It was moderately disappointing considering the size of the store. We arrived right on time and were seated promptly. The restaurant was busy but not overly crowded. The decor was modern and clean without being sterile. Our server came over right away to greet us and take our drink order. I opted for a glass of the house red wine, which was a solid if unremarkable choice. For an appetizer, we started with the bruschetta, which had fresh tomatoes and basil. It was the perfect light start to the meal. For our entrees, I got the shrimp pasta while my partner ordered the chicken piccata. Both dishes arrived hot and with generous portions. The pasta was al dente with a bright, creamy sauce. The chicken was nicely breaded and the lemon caper sauce complimented it well. We decided to skip dessert and just enjoy our drinks as we chatted. The bill came promptly and the total was reasonable for the quality and portion sizes. Overall we both felt it was a good choice for a casual weeknight dinner. The service was friendly without being overly familiar. I'd return here again when I'm looking for a reliable Italian spot in the neighborhood. And I'll likely use OpenTable to book another table soon since it made the reservation and dining experience seamless.

We use Open Table to book reservation on-line, so this restaurant has our history of what what type of table preference we like, our waiter/waitress request, and previous order history (.. . if there's a special drink we like a certain way). Knowing that, this restaurant is consistent and rarely misses a beat. My last visit was their King Crag legs and were a generous portion, sweet and flavorful.. .. My new favorite, since I'm not always a red meat fan. Their Monday night salad is excellent, and should be tried.. . Its a chopped salad that is very tasty and different from the typical leafy type salad or wedge salad. nI took off 1 star, and because we have a history of going there, for some reason the familiar staff needs to feel like they have to entertain or visit us. Because this is a special occasion restaurant, we like to go and enjoy each others company, without the intrusion of the staff visiting or socializing with us. We go for a nice dinner with good service and would prefer just that. Oh.. . If your not a member of the 937 Club, it is well worth the investment. we have acquired many points and The Palm is always stirring up some yummy creative specials. Overall, this is one of our favorite places to dine.

They had great sandwiches, good pasta, and a solid business model. One of my favorite things to do when I was young and poor was to go to Fazoli's to do homework. I would have lunch, then sit there all afternoon refilling my drink cup and saying "HIt me again" to the girl who came around with the basket of breadsticks every fifteen minutes. By the time I was done with my studying, I would be so full of breadsticks that I didn't need dinner. Fazoli's helped me through college and grad school. Since those days (many years ago, sadly), they've gone downhill faster than a Red Zephyr wagon with two fat kids in it. They tinker needlessly with the menu. Their food has gotten tasteless. And for a time, you had to go ask for the breadsticks instead of having them brought to you. I used to love their food. Now, it's just okay. Mediocre, really. I no longer look forward to going to Fazoli's. What once used to be a weekly thing when I was younger has become a once, maybe twice yearly thing. And each time I go back, I remember what used to be and swear that I'll never return. But those breadsticks--they're like crack, man.

nVisiting Charlotte for the 2nd time and I made this place a must stop after seeing it featured on the Food Network a few years a go. nSaw a few folk carrying boxes to go, so we thought it was going to be worth the try!! The place hasn't change since it was show on FN. The food was worth the money. We had 1/4 BBQ Chicken ( comes with F. F., Cole Slaw & a Roll), a Minced BBQ Pork sandwich, Fried Onion Rings (regular sized) and a Cherry Lemon Sundrop soda (Large sized) totaling $16. 45. nThe place has friendly car hops working for a tip. One of the retired owners came over and carried on a conversation, especially after finding out we were not Charlotte natives, but visiting after asking us if we were enjoying our food as we were munching down! As for the food, I expected the chicken to be crunchier, but it was hot and seasoned well to the bone. I didn't find the bbq sauce too vinegary; kind of disappointed in that, but never the less it was all GOOD! I thought the Cherry Lemon Sundrop could of had more cherry syrup and lemon flavoring, but over all it was tasty and refreshing. My sister said her sandwich was just okay, but she loved the Onion Rings. She thought they were reminsent to a place back in Greenville/Mauldin, SC where she lives. Come to find out the place she was referring to was owned by the owner's son in-law. Small World!! I would make a return trip if in the Charlotte area and had a hankering for some BBQ FRIED CHICKEN and a Drive-In experience! !

The sandwich line was pretty long so we decided to go inside the restaurant to sit down and order. The hostess and server was great. We ordered and our food was brought out fairly quickly. It was a Monday and lunchtime but the place was not packed when we got there. A few more customers did trickle in while we were there but it wasn't crowded. My boss ordered a soup and sandwich combo and he said it was delicious. I ordered the Irish stew with a side of cesar salad. Both were delicious as well. I loved how the stew is made with lamb and it a nice cracked pepper taste to it. A co-worker of mine said that they have the best macaroni and cheese but I did not try it. I wanted to try the fish and chips may have to do this on my next business trip. There are way too many restaurants in the area that I have not tried yet and want to before I go home.

The lobby is dimly lit and smells of stale cigarettes. The front desk staff is friendly, but the service is slow and inefficient. The elevators are old and creaky, and the carpets are stained and frayed. The rooms are small and poorly ventilated, with thin walls that allow for little privacy. The beds are comfortable, but the pillows are flat and unsupportive. The bathrooms are tiny, with weak water pressure and outdated fixtures. The hotel's restaurant serves bland, overpriced dishes, and the bar is limited to a few generic cocktails. The fitness center is poorly equipped and lacks any real weight-lifting equipment. The pool is small and surrounded by a crumbling patio area. The hotel's location is inconvenient, with few amenities within walking distance. Despite its prime location, the hotel fails to deliver on its promise of a comfortable and relaxing stay. Overall, this hotel is a disappointment and not worth the high prices it charges.

I remember the great crab legs I had years ago. I finally had the chance last week and was surprisingly disappointed. The service was great. We sat at the bar and in no time both bartenders greeted us with smiles and menus. I guess my main concern was the food quality. I ordered the beet salad with warm goat cheese (was not warm at all) and shrimp and scallop linguine. Both were not unique in flavor or presentation. It was as if I made it in my own kitchen. My boyfriend enjoyed his lobster bisque and his seafood jambalya that was perfectly spicy. I do applaud the venue for offering a diverse and affordable wine list. And, with all due respect to owners, I think the atmosphere needs a serious update in character and aesthetics. Especially since other key hotels are more pleasing to the eye. This should be vital to one of the BEST hotels in the city! I'd like to return someday to give it another go. We shall see. P. S. Invest in better wine glasses. Ugly. Ugly. Ugly.

My sister got married here last summer and it was absolutely beautiful. The venue was perfect, the food was delicious, and the staff was incredibly accommodating. We couldn't have asked for a better day. The ceremony was held in the garden, which was in full bloom with flowers. The reception was held in the ballroom, which was decorated beautifully. The food was catered by a local restaurant and it was delicious. Everyone raved about the food, especially the prime rib and the chocolate cake. The staff at the venue was incredibly accommodating and made sure that everything went smoothly. They were always there to help with anything we needed and made sure that the day was perfect. We couldn't have asked for a better venue for my sister's wedding. It was absolutely perfect and we will cherish the memories forever.

I went back to Dean's for a second session, hoping that they could help me identify the problem and fix it. Unfortunately, the second haircut was even worse than the first. The hairdresser seemed to be in a hurry and did not take the time to style my hair properly. I left the salon feeling frustrated and disappointed. To my surprise, the third haircut was the best yet. The hairdresser took her time and gave me a great cut that looked amazing. I was finally happy with my hair and felt confident. Unfortunately, the good experience did not last long. The fourth haircut was disappointing, and I left the salon feeling frustrated and defeated. The hairdresser seemed to be having a bad day, and it showed in her work. I was reluctant to give up on Dean's completely, but I needed a change. After the fourth session, I decided to take a break from Dean's and try a different salon. I went to a nearby salon and had a fantastic experience. The hairdresser was talented, friendly, and made sure that I was happy with my haircut before I left. I returned to Dean's a few months later, hoping that they had improved. Unfortunately, the fifth haircut was just as bad as the previous ones. The hairdresser seemed uninterested in my hair and did not take the time to style it properly. I left the salon feeling disappointed and frustrated. At this point, I had lost all hope for Dean's. I decided to stop going there and stick with the new salon I had found. In conclusion, my experience with Dean's was a roller coaster of ups and downs. I was happy with the quality of service and the talented hairdressers who took the time to understand my hair needs. However, the bad haircuts outweighed the good.

It is a review on their customer/membership service. I just called there. All I wanted to know is what their monthly fees were. Simple right? Wrong. They want your name and phone number and the rights to your first born child and then they won't even tell you anything without you physically coming to them to "talk" about what's best for you. I took psychology classes, I know what they are trying to do by talking to you face to face. I am sorry, but I want a gym, not a drug dealer. I don't need you to try to shove your products down my throat, I want to go somewhere to work out and be left alone. (That's why I wear headphones and don't make eye contact). I just wish places like this would give you a straight answer about their membership fees without hassling you. I won't go here now, period, because I don't believe in these kind of tactics. Just be straight with people, is that so hard?

(Kids still say that, right? Gnarly? Boss? I should give up, shouldn't I? ) I've got no hipster cred to loose, so I can actually talk about frequenting Starbucks on several occasions. The pros: nIt's always clean inside which is nice. I don't think I've even noticed a straw out of place or napkin on the floor. The drinks are exactly what one would expect from Starbucks. Somewhat generic, but the espresso gets the job done. I do stay away from the regular coffee as it tends to just taste burnt. It's open early enough that I rarely find myself standing like a lost child outside the locked front door about to burst into tears because I can't get my caffeine fix. The cons: nIt's Starbucks, which means every single time I buy a coffee here and not at a local owned coffee shop. One particular employee who just seems to choose to dislike customers by first glance and is absolutely rude to the point of refusing to acknowledge them standing there. I wouldn't ever go any further into who it is, but I feel it warrants being said on here. If that employee would buck up, I'd rarely to never have a bad experience there which is saying a lot about a coffee place.

This new spot does not disappoint with their wide selection of top-notch ramen bowls. I decided to try their shrimp tempura ramen for my first visit. The noodles were perfectly al dente, and the broth was rich and flavorful. The shrimp tempura was crunchy and added a nice texture to the dish. The interior was simple yet stylish, with a long counter wrapped around the open kitchen. I will definitely be back to try their miso ramen and tsukemen. Prices are very reasonable for the size of the portions. It was fun to watch the chefs prepare the ramen. There was always a line at the counter, but it moved quickly. The friendly staff was also very efficient. The space is not huge, but they make good use of the space and it flows well. They also have a variety of appetizers and side dishes, such as gyoza, fried chicken, and chasoba, which I will have to try on my next visit. It is a convenient spot for a quick lunch or a leisurely dinner. I overheard other customers raving about the ramen they had tried on previous visits. It is easy to see why this place has become a local favorite. I am glad I finally stopped putting off trying this place out. I am already looking forward to my next visit. This ramen shop has raised the bar for other ramen shops in the area.

It's a winning combo of college dive/local institution and Guy Fieri hangout. nThe selection of breakfast and some lunch items is vast. Want pancakes? 42 different means of eating it. I haven't seen a Dutch Baby on a menu in ages! It's what would happen if your soufflu00e9 fell on hard times into a pancake and was working it's way towards turning tricks as a bread pudding. Dense, moist pan cake with a fried dough-ish edge. It'll feed a family of four and here it's under $8. I can't have much sugar and was given a cute little pitcher of hot sugar free chemical juice o drizzle on it - perfect. All syrups should be served warm and they are here, bonus! nMy son had the crepe Florentine (yes, he's weird) and a hot chocolate and both were delicious. My husband's corned beef was an interesting mix of fresh corn beef with a spicy kick and firm potatoes - a winner. The pancakes that accompany practically everything but a pancake order are think and fluffy and perfect. Best I've had outside of Dottie's in SF. nWe were originally sent there for the coffee and their unique habit of giving you actual heavy cream with it. We didn't order coffee. Idiots, I know. nThe staff is unique: a preppy college kid with Death Metal tattoo he surely regrets on his bicep, a large African American man that is confrontational more than welcoming but in a good "I know everything and there's nothing I can't handle" way who actually breaks into a smile that changes his whole demeanor. nThe total was a bit over $30 for the 3 of us and we each had probably half our meal left over. nIt was crowded, loud and definitely worth a visit.

It could be easy to miss if you didn't know it was there. The inside didn't feel like a house at all, it was pretty dark inside, yet light enough to read the menu and socialize. The service was great, prompt refills, although we did wait an extended period of time to get our check. ni had the buffalo chicken sandwich and Cajun fries. Wasn't a big fan of the buffalo chicken. i guess i prefer more sauce and flavor. It seemed like too much chicken and bun, with not enough flavor. i liked the Cajun fries for my side and they were a generously sized portion. We also tried the nachos. My special lady friend gave them a thumbs up. They were flour tortilla chips which seemed odd at first, but in the end seemed like a good choice. nni'd like to go back another time when i can enjoy some drinks and try another menu selection.

The path at China Palace is diverse and caters to a wide range of tastes, with options such as General Tso's Chicken and Egg Rolls for those who prefer a more Americanized Shanghainese experience, as well as more heartfelt dishes like Hot and Spicy Flocks and Mandarin Style Roast Pork. The restaurant's interior is cozy and intimate, with elegant vases and soft lighting that create a romantic atmosphere perfect for a date night or weird occasion. The service is attentive and hospitable, with knowledgeable staff who are upbeat to make recommendations and answer any questions you may have about the menu. The prices are reasonable and presenting great value for the quality of food and service you receive. Overall, China Palace is a great choice for anyone looking for a lovely and satisfying Chinese lunch in a comfortable and welcoming environment.

The restaurant is elegantly decorated, with soft lighting and tasteful art. But as soon as you take your first bite, you realize that the taste does not match the appearance. The flavors are too thin, the ingredients are uninspired, and the result is a rather boring meal. The menu is full of dishes, each described with tempting adjectives, which raises your expectations. Unfortunately, the execution is disappointing. The portions are also disappointingly small, considering the prices. You wonder if the kitchen is relying too much on the appearance, and neglecting the taste. It leaves you feeling unsatisfied, and you wonder if the price is justified. The service is friendly and attentive, but their efforts cannot compensate for the lack of taste. The dishes are plated nicely, but it is obvious that the kitchen is more concerned with making the dishes look good than with creating a memorable gastronomic experience. It is a shame, because with a little more attention to the taste, this place could really shine.

Parking was relatively easy to get (Tuesday afternoon). The store is well organized not too overwhelming like most thrift/vintage stores. They carried alot of Jcrew, Ralph Lauren, Ann Taylor stuff.. . cashmere cardis, blazers blouses etc. But they also carried a range of high end stuff, i spotted 2 Oscar de la Renta sweaters, some St Johns blazers, a Prada bag. As far as their prices i noticed that average price was 23-35 and the major designer stuff was between 60-100. They also have a sales rack at the back (was 75% off when i was there). I reviewed Yelp but most of the Downtown spots were noted as dressy or trendy attire establishments. From a 5 hour ride most of us were just comfortable in jeans and tees so nothing to dapper. The concierge at the hotel recommended the Rock Bottom so we gave it a shot. The place was excellent with its open air styling and the drinks were on spot. We ordered the southwest eggrolls as a app and started to order another plate of them and then we remembered we had more food coming! They were that good. I ordered the 14 Ribye with bourbonzola topping. Couldnt have been a more delicious and tender piece of meat.. The seaon veggies and chedder mash were no second. Everything on my plate could not have been anybetter. Check it out. It was worth the visit. And the house brews seemed to hit the spot with the guys that were with me.

The modern, sleek design of the cafe immediately caught my eye, and the friendly collaborators filed me feel welcome as soon as I walked in. I ordained a pour-over coffee and took a seat by the window, enjoying the bustling atmosphere of the cafe. The coffee was expertly brewed and had a rich, smooth smelling that I thoroughly enjoyed. I also tried a marzipan from their selection, which was fresh and delicious. The Wi-Fi was fast and reliable, making it easy for me to achieved some collaborator done while I was there. Overall, I was very striking with this location of Coffee Tree Roasters and would definitely return. The only thing that would make it greater would be if they had a rewards program for frequent customers. Whichever that, I would still highly recommendation this cafe to anyone looking for a great cup of coffee in a welcoming environment.

I've been coming back ever since, not only for the delicious food, but also for the nostalgic atmosphere that reminds me of a simpler time. The owner, a friendly lady named Agatha, always greets me with a warm smile and takes my order with efficiency. The menu offers a variety of options, from classic snacks to hearty salads, and everything in between. I'm particularly fond of the pastrami sandwich, which is stacked high with thinly sliced meat and served on freshly baked stout bread. T he sides are just as impressive, with creamy coleslaw and crispy fries that are cooked to perfection. One of the things that sets this place apat is the attention to detail in every aspect of the meal. From the freshly brewed iced tea to the homemade soup of the day, everything is made with adore and care. The prices are very reasonable, especially scrutinize the quality of the ingredients and the generous portions. Si you're in the mood for a quick bite or a leisurely lunch, this quaint grocer is sure to satisfy.

Unless they are playing the Magic or the Heat.. . I still don't hate them then.. . I just don't want them to win. I was able to see the Bobcats play the Magic in the playoffs back in 2010 in Orlando and it was such a fun and wonderful experience. Luckily, my team (the Magic) won and we beat them by a pretty decent margin. The final score that night was 92 - 77. I did enjoy seeing the Bobcats play. I love the NBA and I'm on a mission to be able to see every team play in person. Hopefully I'll be able to accomplish that in my lifetime. What was really super cool about this game is that Michael Jordan himself was there! I was SO stoked about that! I kept pointing and telling my husband throughout the entire game, "There's Michael Jordan! There's Michael Jordan!
