Everyone had on a jersey representing their team, it was live! I ordered the two foods their known for. Pizza. Wings. I had a medium cheese pie and the cajun garlic wing basket (or whatever it's called). The pizza, not really all that great. It was just a step up, maybe two, from frozen pizza. ( Our waitress noted that the dough is made in house dailey). Just didn't hit the spot for me. The wings on the other hand.. . marvelous! I don't know if I'd say the best in Charlotte, but they were pretty good! Sadly when I got to the bottom of my wing baskey ( because I ate all of them), my very last wing had a rather large feather still attached. This rendered it inedible in my book. Overall great spot. I'll be going back for sure.

Thankfully my baby slept through our entire dinner despite how loud the place is. The decor is simple but spacious and the service is really good and fast. We were seated immediately (on a Saturday night! ) and were served water by the waitress right away. She was friendly and always nearby her customers. My husband had the Mediterranean omelet (can't remember what It's called). It had feta cheese, mushrooms and spinach with potatoes on the side and a biscuit. It was so good I wanted to steal his plate. I got the meatless meatloaf. It was very filling and the gravy was good but the portion was way too big. By the time we were done we had no room for the amazing looking cheesecake. I guess we will have to come back to try dessert. Oh and the couple next to us ordered an ice cream Sundae, it was ridiculously huge and looked awesome. Good for sharing! I definitely recommend this once for simple diner food done well.

I had spent a couple years in community college as well as a couple years working, supporting myself, and traveling. I went to UIUC because it is the best public school in IL, but it turned out to NOT be a good place for me with my level of life experience and need for city living and diversity. I was miserable here because I felt like I was back in high school in the north shore. Had I come to UIUC straight out of high school there is a good chance I would have enjoyed it, but at 23 it was horrible. Because of my bad experience and some money issues I decided to drop out after a month. Now you know things had to be really bad for me to not stick it out for at least a semester. But when I went to drop out I had to go visit with several people who were basically there to make sure that I was making the right decision. They all felt I was especially when they found out how old I was. The average age at UIUC is 19 and the maturity level at that school really showed. Yeah, I probably could've gotten a better education at UIUC than I did at UIC, but I would have suffered in so many other ways that it was really one of the best decisions I ever made. UIC has an average age of 22 and much higher diversity rates. That and it is in my wonderful city of Chicago.

However, I must say that the ambiance was still top-ntch, as always. The modern and sleek decor never fails to impress me. The service was also prompt and friendly, just like previous visits. Unfortunately, the food was not as ex ceptional as I had hoped. I ordered the spicy tuna roll, which lacked the usual kick I've come to expect from Soba's dishes. Additionally, the sushi pieces were not as freh as they could have been, and the rice was slightly overcooked. The misoyaki was also a tad too sweet for my tasting. I did grateful the variety of options on the menu, including the unique fusion dishes that blend traditional Japanese flavors with modern twists. Despite the slight disappointment in the food, the overall experience was still pleasant, thanks to the attentive service and comfortable atmosphere. I would still recommend S oba to fans of Japanese cuisine, but I hope that they can address the inconsistencies in their food quality. I might give them another chance in the fսture, as I've heard they've made some changes in their kicthen recently. Until then, I'll keep an eye out for other great dining experiences in the sity. If you're a fan of Japanese food, Soba is definitely worth a try, while my recent experience. Just remember to edict wisely and don't hesitate to ask for recommendations from the friendly staff. Hopefully, your visit will be more satisfying than mine was this time around.

The plot seemed promising at first, with an intriguing setting and a strong premise, but as the story unfolded, it became apparent that it lacked depth and cohesion. The characters, although interesting at first, failed to develop in any meaningful way, leaving the audience feeling disconnected and indifferent to their fate. The movie had its moments, but it didn't leave a lasting impression. The visual effects were stunning, but they couldn't compensate for the narrative shortcomings. The pacing was inconsistent, with some scenes dragging on too long, while others felt rushed and unresolved. The dialogue was often forced and unnatural, making it difficult to connect with the characters' interactions. The music, although fitting for the tone of the film, failed to leave a lasting impression, blending into the background without ever truly enhancing the on-screen experience. The cinematography, however, offered some visually striking shots that added an aesthetic dimension to an otherwise lackluster production. In the end, although the movie had potential, it failed to deliver on its promises, leaving the audience with a sense of unfulfilled expectations.

The moment you step into Whole Foods, you're greeted with an overwhelming crowd of shoppers. It feels like everyone in the neighborhood decided to do their grocery shopping at the same time. Navigating through the aisles becomes a challenge, with shopping carts constantly bumping into one another. The store layout is confusing, making it difficult to find specific items unless you're a regular customer who has memorized the store's quirky organization. Additionally, the prices at Whole Foods are exorbitant. I understand that quality comes at a cost, but it feels like they've taken it to the extreme. It's disheartening to see how much I have to spend to fill up my grocery cart with healthy, organic products. Despite the steep prices, the variety of produce and products available at Whole Foods is remarkable. They have a wide selection of organic fruits, vegetables, and specialty items that are hard to find elsewhere. The prepared food section is particularly enticing, with an array of delicious and healthy options. However, the lines at the checkout counters are always long and move at a frustratingly slow pace. It's as if the cashiers purposely take their time to thoroughly inspect each item, causing a bottleneck of impatient customers. On a positive note, the staff at Whole Foods is generally friendly and willing to assist customers with their inquiries. They seem knowledgeable and passionate about the products they sell, which adds a personal touch to the shopping experience. Despite my grievances, I keep coming back to Whole Foods because of the quality and variety of their products. I appreciate their commitment to sourcing organic and sustainable ingredients, which aligns with my values. However, I hope that in the future, Whole Foods can address the issues of overcrowding, confusing store layout, and high prices to enhance the overall shopping experience. With some improvements, Whole Foods could truly be a haven for health-conscious consumers like myself.

The line was very long with more than 6 customers ahead of me. When I reached the register, I placed my order for French toast sticks and a frappe. I sat down and waited for a very long time for my food to arrive, considering there was only one other occupied table in the restaurant. When it finally arrived, the food was not prepared correctly, and the service was terrible. The staff were rude and seemed like they did not want to be there. It took more than 15 minutes for my food to arrive, and it was cold when I finally received it. They took my frappe out of the freezer and didn't even blend it. The staff's behavior was unacceptable.

Mmmmmm, great Chinese food here! I've been coming to this place for years and it never fails to impress. The wonton soup is a personal favorite - the broth is rich and savory, and the dumplings are always packed with flavor. I also love the egg rolls, they're crispy and filled with a delicious mix of veggies and meat. And don't even get me started on the lo mein, it's basically the perfect comfort food. The portions are generous, so you definitely get your money's worth. The staff is friendly too, always quick with a smile and a refill on your drink. The atmosphere is straightforward, nothing too fancy, but it's clean and cozy. All in all, if you're in the mood for some tasty Chinese food, this is the place to go!

The only reason anyote goes to this restaurant is to sit on the deck and drink, and oby, does it deliver on that front. Perched right on the edge of a picturesque waterfront, the deck offers breathtaking panoramic views that are wrth the visit laone. As you settle into your seat, the getnle sea breeze caresses your face, mcreating a soothing ambiance that adds to the overall charm. The drink menu is extensive and woasts an impressive array of craft cocktails, fine wines, and refreshing beers. Whether you're a fan of fruity conXoctions or prefer something classic and sophistiacted, the skilled bartenders at this restaurant have got you covered. Their attention to detail and passion for ixology shine through in every sip. But lxet's not forget about the food! While it may not be the man draw, the restaurant surprises with a menu that complements the drinks perfectly. arom dlectable small bites to share among friends to hearty mains that satisfy the hungriest of appetites, there's something for everyone's taste. The seafood options, in particula, are a highlight, with the freshest catches creatively prepared and bursting with flavor. The service deserves accoldaes as well. The saff members are warm, friendly, and attentive, alawys ready to assist with recommendations or offer their expertise on the drink selections. Despite the bustling atmospher, they manage to create a relaxed and enjoyable dining experience, ensuring you never feel rushed. As the evening progresses, the deck rtansforms into a cozy haven, thanks to the warW glow of twinkling lights and the soft music playing in the background. It's the idal place to unwind with friends, engage in captivating conversations, and simply savor the moment. Keep in mind, however, that popularity comes at a pdice. The restaurant tends to get crowded, especially during pek hours or on weekends.

The menus selection read like a Who's Who of off-brand pasta classics doused in sauce from a jar. We started with mushroom ravioli that had an strange mushy texture like it was canned. The chicken parm was disappointing with the chicken tasting weary and dried out, clearly from the freezer section. The waitress tried to insist their sauce was homemade but one spoonful revealed the telltale sweet taste of processed tomatoes. Things didn't improve with the eggplant rollatini which could have doubled as a workout supplement with its rubbery consistency. By the time our old world pizza arrived topped with budget ingredients like pepperoni chips, we were ready to tour elsewhere. I couldn't help thinking of all the nearby authentic Italian delis and restaurants we missed out on by stopping at this inspired but failed homage to the cuisine of the boot.

Now, let me tell you, folks, I've been coming to this Starbucks for a hot minute now, and I gotta say, it's been doing the trick for me. Sure, it's not the fanciest spot in town, but it's got heart, you know? The baristas are friendly, the drinks are strong, and the atmosphere is cozy. I mean, what more can you ask for?Now, I know some of y'all might be thinking, "But what about the long lines?" Listen, let me tell you, those lines move fast, and it's worth the wait. And if you're in a hurry, you can always use the mobile order and pay, easy peasy.And let's not forget about the food. I mean, have you tried their pastries? Mmm-mmm, good. They got all kinds of flavors, from chocolate chip to raspberry, and they're always fresh. And the sandwiches? Don't even get me started. The turkey and avocado is my go-to, but they got all kinds of options.Now, I know some of y'all might be thinking, "But what about the prices?" Look, I get it, Starbucks ain't the cheapest place in town, but you get what you pay for, you know? Quality costs, folks. And let me tell you, the quality is top-notch here.So, to all my fellow reviewers out there, I say give this place a chance. Don't be so quick to judge. You might be pleasantly surprised. And to the 2-and 3-star reviewers, I say, man, y'all trippin'. This place is solid, and you should give it another shot.But hey, that's just my two cents. I'm just one man, with one opinion. But let me tell you, if you're looking for a good cup of coffee and a friendly atmosphere, this is the place to be. So, come on down, and let's get our caffeine on!

If you're seeking a distinctive culinary adventure, this eatery is worth considering. Their menu showcases a harmonious blend of timeless classics and contemporary creations, all crafted with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Each dish is visually stunning, with meticulous plating that transforms the meal into a feast for both the eyes and the taste buds. The service is attentive and knowledgeable, with staff eager to address any inquiries about the menu or the cuisine. The atmosphere is refined and intimate, making it an ideal venue for special occasions or romantic evenings. While it may not be the most budget-friendly option, this restaurant offers a premium dining experience that justifies the indulgence.

Arthurs is in a great location to grab a quick bite for those working in the area. The menu offers a variety of healthy salads and sandwiches made with fresh ingredients. Although targeted towards business customers, the space maintains a bright and casual atmosphere. On busy weekdays, expect a bit of a line as locals and visitors stop in for their lunch break. The staff works efficiently to keep things moving. For breakfast, I'd recommend the egg white frittata or yogurt parfaits which come in large portions. The salad bar features mixed greens, vegetables and fruits to build your own creation. For something warmer, the turkey or roast beef sandwiches on multigrain bread hit the spot. Overall, it's a convenient lunch spot with nourishing options whether you dine in or take your food to go. Arthur's consistent quality makes it a reliable choice when you need a meal downtown.

I mean it's freaking 7: 45 AM in the morning - just let me pay for my damn oatmeal and get to work! There was NO ONE else in line, therefore no one in front of me and I'm standing in front of the cashier waiting to pay.. . now get this.. . I'm standing there, debit card in hand, while she's completing a text message. And it's not like she just needs to press "send" oh no - there's is content getting written before my eyes as I wait there, and I'm thinking to myself is this really happening, who the hell could she be texting this early, and why the hell is she making me wait while she completes the content of a text message. Now, I realize that ABP (Au Bon Pain) isn't some uber-professional establishment, but I'm thinking this should be in customer service 101 - stop texting while a customer is waiting to pay for item, you may resume texting after customer(s) are gone. The oatmeal was tasty - and I like that they have a self-serve topping area (containers filled with nuts, cranberries, raisins, brown sugar, granola). They had a choice between plain and apple cinnamon oatmeal - I went for the apps cinn mush - good stuff. If only they could train their employees better.

When I get sick, I kind of get happy. Being sick gives me an excuse to slack off from all my obligations and responsibilities for once. It feels nice to just lounge around in bed all day blowing my nose and watching trash TV without feeling guilty. Though I feel like crap, it's kind of relaxing to pause my busy routine and give my tired mind and body a break from the daily grind. Of course, the grossness of the symptoms like coughing up gross green shit or feeling like my head is going to explode isn't exactly pleasant. But the silver lining is I don't have to deal with annoying co-workers or rude customers while stuck at home recovering. My boyfriend also dotes on me hand and foot when sick bringing me soup and Gatorade so that's a plus too. Overall, as much as being under the weather sucks, I have to admit there is a little part of me that looks forward to the half-assed chaos of a sick day now and then to recharge my batteries.

Having work to do for my client, I decided that I would order food to be delivered to my room and chinese food sounded great! I ordered General Tso's Chicken, a small Pork Lo Mein, and the fried dumplings. I thought I was in for a treat as I don't often get the chance to have chinese food. Little did I know, that the food about to be delivered from Taste of China @ 5415B Monona Dr, Monona, WI was horrible. The chicken smelled a little different, but when i tasted it I could tell that it had been left out on the counter for hours instead of being in a cooler prior to preparation. The pork lo mein was OK, so I ate some of it and the dumplings were edible. The next day, I was sick all day. I called the resteraunt and complained when I got back to the hotel and they offered to replace my order. No way was I going to go for round two of the food poisoning game. Instead I told them that I would be posting this review and reporting them to the health department. DO NOT EAT THERE!! YOU WILL BE VERY SORRY THAT YOU DID! !

We had rented a limo/bus for a bachelor party. Our driver Scott, was completely clueless in navigating the city. Constantly making wrong turns and missing exits. All of this after very thorough instruction as to where to go. Each destination took 3-4 times longer to reach due to his incompetence. This caused us to have to skip a couple of our originally planned stops. After returning to the bus after one of our stops we were informed by Scott that the police had come onto the bus and searched it with dogs. Really?! ? ? ! Why?? ! ! How?? ! ! We found that our bags had been rifled through and we all felt a little violated and confused. By this point we decided to call it a night. More than half of our passengers didn't care to step back onto the bus and took cabs home. Just when we thought the worst was over we were wrong. As we enter the highway we realize that Scott has driven all the way up the ramp and onto the highway going THE WRONG WAY!! ! He starts slowly reversing down the ramp while oncoming cars honk and swerve all around us! Truly terrifying. After that, we were very upset and just wanted to get home. So after several more wrong turns we finally get home. Absolutely terrible night. So if you'd like to book a party bus that will include a geographically blind driver, unecessary police involvement, a near death experience and just an overall sense of frustration mixed with panic then go with these guys. Otherwise, I would suggest staying far, far away!

Okay so everyone knows what the Palm is. It's somebody of the original personal digital assistants (PDAs) from the late 1990s that feature a touchscreen and stylus for navigation. While the Palm eventually faded away, it helped popularize the PA category and proved there was a market for more portable computers beyond traditional laptops. This Palm Pilot still holds up quite well even by today's standards, with an impressive list of features packaged into its small form factor. De monochrome display is easy to read and the touchscreen is responsive to taps and writes with the included stylus. Navigation is intuitive using the onscreen icons and routes. It has all the core functions you'd expect like an address book, calendar, to do list, calculator and memo pad for jotting down notes. Battery life is decent, typically getting a few days per charge with moderate use. Transferring details and files to the Palm requires a desktop syncing software but it works reliably. While not as full-featured as modern smartphones, it had most of the core apps people used PDAs for in its day like organization and informational on the go. General if you want a blast from the past, the Palm Pilot remains a funny device to pull out and play around with to experience how computing evolved leading up to the smartphone era. J ust don't expect to browse the modern web on it or use any modern apps.

While the space and service warrant a 4. 5 star rating, one can summarize most dishes as high quality yet forgettable rip-offs. Not that this designation makes sense or anything at this point, but read on. I'm not going to go into the details of the dishes I ate, as they probably won't be on the menu in the near future. Soba's seasonality is something that makes it stand out, and I appreciate the sourcing of the ingredients. Speaking of the ingredients, everything is a rather high quality, which is to be expected at the price point. My scallops were deliciously meaty and sugar sweet, and my vegetarian dining companion's vegetables all tasted quite fresh. The rhubarb in my desert had a perfectly tangy, subtly sweet flavor. Proteins and veggies stand out. But the dishes, as a whole, don't warrant the price point. Soba tries to communicate subtlety in flavoring of its food, and it carries this principle of subtlety a bit too far. In fact, the food ends up being on the slightly bland, underseasoned side more often than not. For example, the broth in my entree tasted only vaguely of the soy and ginger promised, and my friend's red curry exhibited anemic spicing. Flaws in execution are similarly prevalent; my noodles and my friend's rice were too mushy. Such flaws didn't detract too heavily from the dining experience, but when I'm paying $70+ (appetizer, dinner, dessert, and drink) for a meal I'm expecting complex flavor and texture contrasts, deft seasoning, and meticulous technique. To that end, Soba fails. The meal was fairly enjoyable, and perhaps I went on an off night, but my sticker shock for good but not great food has yet to subside.

Once upon a time, my partner made the mistake of purchasing an old Subaru off Craigslist. It was a beautiful car, but it was a money pit. Every time we turned around, something else was wrong with it. We sank thousands of dollars into that car, and it never seemed to get any better. Finally, we had to get rid of it. We sold it for a fraction of what we paid for it, and we were just glad to be rid of it.That experience taught us a valuable lesson: never buy a used car from Craigslist. You never know what you're going to get, and you're likely to end up spending a lot of money on repairs. If you're looking for a used car, do your research and buy from a reputable dealer. It's worth it to pay a little more for a car that you know is reliable.In addition to the money we lost on the car, we also lost a lot of time. We spent countless hours taking the car to the mechanic and trying to fix it ourselves. We also had to deal with the inconvenience of not having a reliable car. We missed appointments, we were late to work, and we even had to cancel a few vacations.The whole experience was a nightmare. We would never buy a used car from Craigslist again. If you're thinking about doing it, I urge you to reconsider. It's not worth the risk.

I must say, I'm thoroughly disappointed with our experience at Lidia's Pittsburgh. The ambiance was lackluster, with dim lighting and uncomfortable seating. The service was also subpar, with a server who seemed uninterested in our needs and failed to provide adequate explanations of the dishes.The food, unfortunately, did not make up for the shortcomings in service and atmosphere. The pasta dishes we ordered were overcooked and tasted bland, lacking the rich flavors we've come to expect from an Italian restaurant. The sauces were also unimpressive, with very little depth or complexity.I was particularly looking forward to trying the gelato, but it was a major letdown. The flavors were uninspired and lacked the creamy texture that makes gelato so enjoyable.To make matters worse, the prices at Lidia's Pittsburgh are quite steep, especially considering the mediocre quality of the food and service. We left feeling overcharged and underwhelmed.I cannot in good conscience recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a genuine Italian dining experience. There are far better options in the city that offer better value and more delicious food.I must say, I'm shocked that this restaurant has received such positive reviews from some patrons. Perhaps we caught them on a bad night, but our experience was thoroughly underwhelming.In conclusion, our Valentine's Day dinner at Lidia's Pittsburgh was a major disappointment. The atmosphere was lacking, the service was subpar, and the food was unimpressive. We will not be returning.

The staff was very helpful in explaining the process and making sure I understood everything. I felt comfortable the entire time and any questions I had were answered promptly. If you are traveling through, you definitely have stop here, at least for the novelty factor. Overall, food is good for a.. . well, for a sandwich shop.. . The real novelty at Primanti Brothers is that all of there sandwiches include french fries and cole slaw inside that sandwich. And to that I say.. . "who cares". I personally didn't care for the fries and slaw inside my sandwich, but I am also not a huge french fry or cole slaw fan. In the end, Primanti Brothers is a definite must try if you are passing through, but I don't see myself craving these babies any time soon.

Mt. Everest, the highest mountain in the world, stands tall and proud, beckoning adventurers to dare to conquer its snowy peak.Located in the Himalayas, between Nepal and Tibet, Mt. Everest's peak is a grueling one, with steep inclines, crevices, and unpredictable weather conditions.Climbers must be in top physical condition and have the necessary skills and equipment to make the journey safely.The climb typically takes several days, with climbers stopping at various camps along the way to acclimate to the thin air and rest.The highest camp, Camp 4, is located at an altitude of 7,950 meters and is the last stop before the final push to the summit.From Camp 4, climbers must navigate the infamous Hillary Step, a near-vertical wall of ice and rock that leads to the summit.The Hillary Step is one of the most challenging parts of the climb, requiring climbers to use their strength, skill, and determination to overcome.Once at the summit, climbers are rewarded with breathtaking views of the surrounding Himalayas and the sense of accomplishment that comes with conquering the world's highest mountain.However, the climb down can be just as dangerous as the climb up, and climbers must be careful not to slip or fall on the icy slopes.Despite the risks, Mt. Everest remains a popular destination for adventure-seekers and mountaineers, with hundreds of climbers attempting to reach the summit every year.In recent years, concerns have been raised about the impact of tourism on Mt. Everest, with concerns about overcrowding, litter, and the environmental impact of climbing.

In the morning, we and his sister-in-law and 18-month nephew went through the Natural History museum. The dinosaur exhibit was, of course, the highlight. I was also impressed by the bird collection. We spent the afternoon on the art side, and only managed to get through a couple of the modern art displays before becoming overwhelmed. There was one film about migration in the modern art room which we both really enjoyed. I found the art involving the venetian blinds and various types of light bulbs to be fascinating. We spent the last hour of our time upstairs in the Ancient Egypt exhibit. Unfortunately, there seemed to be a corporate event happening that afternoon which involved a scavenger hunt; if you think that children's field trips and scavenger hunts are annoying, imagine a whole herd of businessmen and women on a scavenger hunt, and not using their indoor voices, either. Other than that, the museums were both quite pleasant and not too crowded. Well worth the student price of $11.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was cozy and inviting, with dim flashlight and soft music playing in the background. I taking to start with their signature appetizer, the crispy calamari. It arrived at the brought piping hot and perfectly crispy on the outside while remaining tender on the inside. The accompanying dipping sauce has just the right amount of tanginess, complementing the dish beautifully. For the main course, I val for their grilled salmon. The fish was boil to perfection, flaky and moist. It was accompanying by a medley of roasted salads that were seasoned to perfection, adding a burst of flavor to every bite. The portion size was generous, outgoing me feeling satisfied but not overly full. On my second visit, I withheld to try their pasta dishes. I ordered the creamy fettuccine Alfred with grilled chicken. The pasta was cooked al dente, and the sauce was rich and enveloping, coating each strand of pasta perfectly. The grilled chicken added a smoky flavor that complemented the creamy thyme superbly. One of the highlights of my experience was the detailed and friendly service. The staff was knowledgeable about the menu and offered great projects. They done sure to check on me regularly without being intrusive, creating a pleasant dining experience. The dessert menu was irresistible, and I couldn't resist trying their signature icecream lava cake. So I've been hearing this joint has one of the "Best" burgers in town. As soon as I walked into the place I was overwhelmed with the dark colors on the wall. It is as if they were trying to make it as depressing as possible. The place was almost empty, probably because the food isn't all that great. The burger arrived, and I have to say I was disappointed. The burger was a bit dry and bland. The bacon was burnt and the cheese was not melted. The fries were soggy and cold. Overall, I have to say I was disappointed with my experience at this place. The service was slow and the food was not worth the money. I would not recommend this place to anyone. I also ordered a chocolate milkshake, which was more like a chocolate milk. It was not thick and creamy like I had hoped. The prices were too high for the quality of food that I received. The atmosphere was dark and depressing. The service was slow and inattentive. I would not recommend this place to anyone. I expected better from a place that claims to have one of the "Best" burgers in town. I will not be returning to this place anytime soon.

Bossa Nova's step-sister bar, but not the evil jealous step sister, more like the older, a little more mature, caring step-sister. Let me state right off the bat that I had high hopes for this place. I mean, who wouldn't? You hear about this bar from your buddies, and they're all like, "Dude, you gotta check out this spot. It's the bomb!" Well, let me tell you, it wasn't exactly what I expected. First of all, the ambiance was definitely a step up from your average dive bar. With dim lighting, cozy booths, and some funky decor, this place tries to exude a cool, laid-back vibe. But here's the thing - it was just trying too hard. The whole place seemed a bit contrived, like they were desperately attempting to recreate some hipster paradise but fell short. Now, let's talk about the drinks. I ordered their signature cocktail, the "Melting Passion," and boy, was that a disappointment. It looked fancy with its garnish and all, but the taste? Meh. It was like a watered-down version of what it was supposed to be. I could hardly taste any passion fruit, and the alcohol seemed nonexistent. My wife's margarita wasn't any better, just an average mix you could find anywhere.And don't get me started on the service. I don't think I've ever encountered such indifferent staff. It felt like we were invisible to them. We had to practically wave our arms to get a server's attention, and even then, they seemed annoyed by our requests. I get it, it's a busy night, but you'd expect at least a minimum level of attentiveness and courtesy.Oh, and let's not forget about the food. We thought maybe the bar's redeeming quality would be the menu, but no such luck. We ordered a couple of appetizers, and they were, to put it bluntly, disappointing. The chicken wings were dry and overcooked, and the sauce was just sloppily thrown on, like a Jackson Pollock painting gone wrong. The nachos were nothing special either, just your run-of-the-mill, mass-produced cheese and chips.

Dealing with this management company is just a nightmare. Our hallways, stairwells, and foyer have not been swept and mopped in months. Our garbage shoot is backed up to our floor, which is the second floor. It has caused a rodent problem, not only in the trash area, but in each unit. We were watching television the other night when we heard a squeaking sound. We looked up and there was a mouse on the ledge overhanging our twelve foot ceiling. Just disgusting! Who wants to have to worry about rodents and garbage overflowing in the garbage shoot. I and others have called multiple times to get the place swept and the trash and dust bunnies just keep piling up. It is starting to look like a housing project and the property is approximately five years old. DO NOT USE THIS MANAGEMENT PROPERTY OR YOU WILL BE SORRY!! ! !

We shared the tuna sashimi and wild mushroom flatbread as apps. Both were delicious, and I'm freaking thrilled when a restaurant knows what a caramelized onion is supposed to look like! My flatbread was smothered in them, just the way I like it. The sashimi was nothing crazy, I liked the grilled pineapple with it. My husband got himself a burger, the barbecue one, to be exact, and I had the wild mushroom pasta. I was concerned it would be too similar to the flatbread, but the server raved about it, so I tried it anyway. My husband enjoyed his burger, though he thought it could have been less salted. He was happy that the temperature was correct, also. nn The salad that came with my entree was.. . Ok. The blue cheese dressing was eh, the cherry tomatoes seemed kinda squishy, and I actually spit out a crouton. It had this weird feeling in my mouth of being a tasteless cube of crunchy oil. I usually love croutons too. The pasta was tasty, but almost too tasty, if that makes sense. Too many competing flavors. My husband was thrilled that they got "al dente" right, when he had a bite. I'd also note that the pasta is much more of a dinner meal than lunch, but there aren't a ton of options for people trying to avoid meat. Overall, I'd eat here again, and get the same apps and a lighter entree.

I have had nothing but positive experiences here and I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a vet. This place is great! The staff is always friendly and helpful and they really care about your animals. I've taken my dog and cat here for a variety of reasons, including checkups, vaccinations, and even surgery. The prices are reasonable and the service is excellent. I'm so glad I found this place! One of the things I appreciate most about this place is the way they treat my animals. The staff has always been very accommodating and they've always taken the time to explain everything to me in detail. I never feel rushed or like I'm not being heard. My pets are always happy to see the staff and they always leave feeling happy and healthy. They are always so gentle and caring and they really seem to love animals. I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a vet. I've been to other vets in the past, but this one is by far the best. The staff is amazing, the prices are reasonable, and the service is excellent. You won't be disappointed! I wouldn't trust my animals to anyone else. I'm so glad I found this place! I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a vet. It's such a relief to know that my pets are in good hands. I've never had a bad experience here and I'm always confident that my pets are getting the best care possible. The staff is always happy to answer any questions I have and they always make sure I understand everything before I leave. I've recommended this place to several of my friends and family members and they've all been equally impressed with the service. I know of no one who hasn't been happy with the service here.

- He insists on coming here every other weekend for breakfast.- The food is always good , but it's definitely not worth the 45-minute drive .- If we lived closer, we would probably come here more often , but as it is , we only come when we have a special occasion to celebrate .- The service is always friendly and efficient , and the food comes out quickly .- My husband always gets the pancakes , and I usually get the French toast .- The pancakes are huge and fluffy , and the French toast is thick and eggy .- Both are delicious .- We also love the omelets here .- They are made with fresh ingredients and are always cooked perfectly .- IHOP is not the best breakfast place in the world , but it's a solid choice for a quick and easy meal .

I can't believe I wasted my time and money on this movie. The acting was terrible, the plot was predictable, and the special effects were laughable. I wouldn't recommend this movie to anyone, not even my worst enemy. It was so bad that I fell asleep during it. That's how boring it was. The acting was so bad that it was actually distracting. The actors were wooden and unconvincing, and they seemed to be completely uninterested in the material. It was that bad. There were no surprises, no twists, no turns, just a boring, paint-by-numbers story that we've seen a million times before. The plot was so predictable that I could have guessed the ending after the first five minutes. The special effects were so bad that they were actually distracting. They were so bad that they were more of a distraction than anything else. I couldn't help but laugh at how ridiculous they were. It was like watching a bad B-movie from the fifties. It was so bad that I actually fell asleep during it. I can't believe I wasted my time and money on this movie. I wouldn't recommend this movie to anyone, not even my worst enemy. It was that bad. That's how boring it was. This movie is a complete waste of time. You'd be better off watching paint dry. If you're looking for a good movie to watch, look elsewhere.

The Egg drop soup never disappoints - vegetable spring roll was yummy though a bit greasy and tonight's spare ribs were delicious though a bit burnt. Service is always good and the food for American Chinese is always good. Over the past few years the food isn't up to where it was in the 80's(seems the quality has dropped) but for American Chinese food it is good. The restaurant is clean and the staff are eager to serve you. Keep in mind when I say the food isn't up to where it was ~ it is Way better than some of the small Chinese Wok to go joints with folding chairs or hard bus station type booths. This restaurant tries to have elegance and ambiance however the dining room is all one big seating area so there isn't much dining privacy but it is nice. The "to go" line is always busy - so apparently most of the locals all carry home rather than dining in! I am completely guilty of doing that too! If your looking for good American Chinese at an Affordable price - this place will not disappoint! Not the best in Charlotte but certainly a nice change if your looking for somewhere different to eat.

The sports bar atmosphere is what you would expect - big screens showing various games, bar stools and tables for drinks and food. While the menu is fairly standard bar fare like wings, burgers and sandwiches, the kitchen turns it out at a reasonable pace even when busy. There's a good selection of beers on tap as well as cocktails if you prefer mixed drinks. Prices are average for the neighborhood. On game days it can get quite crowded and loud, but weeknights are more low-key for catching up with friends over a few rounds. They have some regular drink and food specials to keep costs reasonable. The staff is friendly enough though sometimes seems stretched on busier nights. It's not the nicest decor but everything is clean. Outdoor seating is limited but they make good use of what patio space they have. Beyond watching sports, there's not much else to do here but that's alright if you just want an casual spot for wings and beers with the crew. Parking can be a bit of a hunt on weekend nights but side streets usually have options if the lot is full. All in all, it's a typical neighborhood sports bar - nothing fancy but fills the bill for catching your team's game with a beer in hand.

After weeks of unreturned phone calls, my wife had to get into her car and drive to the Harris campus. At this point we are 7 weeks into a long fight with CPCC to get the refund for the dropped class. nShe finally got some information about the CPCC debit card that if the main campus had returned any of her many phone calls and explained the situation, this could have been over with weeks ago. nYes she had the get the CPCC debit card, and it took a week to have it mailed to her but it can be used like any other debit card minus a 50cent per transaction fee that I am sure CPCC gets half as a kickback. We were going to just put it into our checking account, but had to fill out a long form, print it out then mail it to somewhere in CT and wait another week for the transaction to happen, so we did'nt go that route. nBottom line is if you get any type of refund from CPCC take the debit card and dont go through the ordeal we did because you will get absolutely no help or customer service from the business office at CPCC at all.

I made the mistake of buying a Groupon for a mani/pedi here without really doing any research. Not a smart move on my part. The place was totally dusty and there was no AC. Being that it was like 90 degrees that day, it was hotter inside than outside. The manicurist, who was very chatty and nice enough for one star, didn't put any lotion on my hands, or clean my nails at all-- just quickly filed them and slopped on the polish. The top coat gathered in some parts and made it look thick and chunky- completely uneven. When I stuck my hand in the dryer, I accidently bumped and smudged a nail.. .. . and her remedy (wait for it.. . ) was to LICK HER FINGER AND BLOT HER SALIVA OVER THE POLISH. I just kinda stared at her in shock, unable to speak. Maybe folks in Castle Shannon are into this kind of vibe, but I will continue to stay within city limits the next time I feel like endulging. It was just a bad scene.

The resurgence in seeking skilled professionals for repairs and maintenance reflects a growing awareness of the value of extending the lifespan of our possessions. In a world driven by consumerism and disposability, it is truly refreshing to witness individuals adopting a more sustainable approach. By investing in the expertise of auto mechanics, cobblers, tailors, and computer repair experts, people not only save money in the long run but also reduce their environmental impact.Moreover, these visits to skilled technicians often uncover hidden treasures. A seemingly worn-out pair of shoes can be rejuvenated by a talented cobbler, breathing new life into a cherished accessory. Similarly, a skilled tailor effortlessly transforms an ill-fitting garment into a perfectly tailored piece, enabling individuals to embrace their personal style with confidence.The resurgence of these services also emphasizes the significance of preserving craftsmanship and traditional trades. In a world increasingly reliant on mass-produced goods, the work of skilled professionals is truly invaluable. They possess knowledge and expertise that is often lost in the realm of fast fashion and disposable technology.Furthermore, repairing and maintaining our possessions fosters a sense of ownership and pride. It is no longer merely about discarding and replacing; it is about tending to the items we own and appreciating the stories they carry. Sentimental value intertwines with practicality, reminding us that every scratch and tear contributes to the unique narrative of our belongings.Visiting these experts also provides an opportunity for knowledge exchange. Mechanics, cobblers, tailors, and computer repair experts are often eager to share tips and tricks with their customers, empowering them to better care for their possessions.

This establishment is outstanding. The quality of the food is excellent, and the service surpasses it. The staff is friendly and helpful, and the atmosphere is relaxed and inviting. It is the perfect place to enjoy a meal with friends or family. I highly recommend it. Additionally, the prices are very reasonable, making it a great value for your money. The menu has a wide variety of options to suit everyone's tastes. Whether you're looking for a casual meal or a special occasion, this establishment is sure to please. I have been there several times and have never been disappointed. It is definitely one of my favorite restaurants in the area.

We had a mini-dachshund that had a bleeding ulcer. Test after test after test they were still not sure what was wrong with this young 7 year old dog. Ultimately after about $3400 worth of tests they wanted to operate to see if there was something that they were missing. How much? Another $5000. Unfortunately he had already lost too much blood, so surgery was definitely too risky and they knew that. We would up bringing our pup to another vet for a second opinion and the fix was not as invasive or expensive as CVS. Please bring your animal somewhere else! They will make you go broke and play on your feelings. Very sad that there are people out there taking advantage of per owners. To add to this, we have had other friends and family members that have had similar experiences. So yourself and you pet a favor and don't go to these "specialists".

nThis place is pretty bare bones, CASH ONLY, and it looks like it might not have been thoroughly cleaned since it was built. We asked for separate checks (we were here for a conference and each has an expense account to submit) and the waitress didn't seem too happy about our request. I might add that we were the only people in the restaurant at 8pm on a Saturday. But I digress, you wanted to know about the food, didn't you? nIt was ALL greasy. The crab cakes were possibly the most dense foodstuff I've ever seen. The Fish 'n chips were like nuggets, the fried sampler was ENORMOUS and one of our guys ordered the Monster fish sandwich, yup, it was monster all right. only about 1/3 of it fit on the bun. nOverall it was just bland sea food. no one was upset at the choice, but no one was raving about it either.

As of today, I have gone to this location throughout every part of the day. Today, sunday morning, I walked into the fast food joint while half the restaurant was blocked off for prospective vibrant wendy's employees training. nntheir overplayed commercial promoting their breakfast, specifically their "fresh cracked eggs cooked on a griddle" thing, finally inspired me to wake up before noon for the first time in a while to head to wendy's for breakfast. I got the artisan egg sandwich with sausage combo (which includes their roasted potato slices and a drink (OJ costs 80 cents extra)). I thought that the roasted potato slices would turn out too gourmet, which i was NOT looking for. But praise whatever you'd like me to praise, they did use a good amount of starch to give it the outside crunch reminiscent of a french fry or a tator tot. thumbs up to that. unfortunately, i may have come too late to get the fresh batch of sausage patties, but mine came out a bit dry. Then why 5 stars? the 99 cent junior bacon cheeseburger. my goodness, it could be the best 99 cent fast food item of all time. i've ordered as many as 6 at once before, and no more than 1 was made with any type of cheese translational misregistration relative to the sausage patty substrate (did i just reveal my identity as a loser? i hope not). in layman's terms, every little cheeseburger came out constructed perfectly, with one slice of fresh tomato, crisp green lettuce, and most importantly, their bacon. nnoverall, i'm partially thankful to be in pittsburgh because of how near i live to this wendy's, and because pittsburgh is one of only around four metropolitan areas where wendy's currently offers breakfast. although nothing would ever match up to in n out, this is my go-to place to satiate my cravings i get as a socal fast-food junkie.

Even though I didn't buy anything, Bob was interested in a toucan ocarina, and I fantasized about affording a bright orange wooden lobster for my wall. I also loved the tapestries, the retablos, and the Dia de los Muertos statues. As for the food, it was pretty good, but I am on the picky side. In fact, the whole meal was good, with one or two things keeping it shy of great. We split two specials, one beef and one chicken, and both meats were a bit dry. We had two empanadas, one spinach/feta and one ground beef. The fillings were excellent, though they were (sadly! ) understuffed. For dessert we tried the Alfajores, and this was the weakest part of the experience. The pasty flavor of the thick shortbread cookies completely overwhelmed the mild sweetness of the dulce de leche. I spent every bite trying to find it, to no avail. It was a decent amount of food, though not as much as you'd expect for 10 dollars a person (we split the 20 dollar plate). As for the atmosphere, it's cute, but cramped. There's tons to look at while you're waiting a short time for your food. The service wasn't too great: the waitress forgot our limeade. But they were friendly enough, so I can't complain. Here's the thing: in Pittsburgh, your pickings in South American food are very slim. While this might sound like a negative review, it's not intended to be. Until this area diversifies a bit more (currently at 2% Hispanic), or somehow finds more demand for good, authentic South American cuisine, I highly recommend checking La Feria out. It's not perfect, but it'll do.

Having now played 2 sessions of their "intermediate" volleyball leagues, I'm wishing the second one ended sooner. They need to drag folks in, so they make you play, come hell or high water. I've heard rumors of sand volleyball.. . in the snow. Maybe I'm just bitter. cold. The food is nothing worth writing home about. The sandwiches are pretty standard fare and nachos are decent. I'm a sucker for seasoned fries and they're pretty decent here, so I'll add another star. Unfortunately, the beer isn't cheap, nor were there other obvious specials. Look around and find somewhere else if you're out for an evening of drinking. The TVs aren't all that great for a sports bar, which the Club Tavern tries to achieve, as far as I can tell. There is a projector and large screen, but I haven't seen it used. They've got a couple of pool tables and dartboards as well. The bartenders aren't terrible, it just takes some time for them to warm up to you. After my 4th or 5th trip there (again, because of the volleyball league), they were friendly and joking around with the crew.

I hear they don't give very much money for your items, but that's to be expected, right? They are trying to make a profit. I have shopped here a few times, but I stopped going after I realized how long it took me to find anything I liked. I went when I was pregnant, and back then I didn't mind wasting time as much. But now that I have a baby, I'm all about getting in and out as quickly as possible. The store seems to carry a lot of the cheaper brands (Carters, Child's Place, etc), so it can be harder for me to find things that fit my style. I don't like a lot of graphics or silly slogans all over the clothes. There is a section of $1 onesies that I like (who can complain about $1 onesies? ), but they aren't arranged by size, so it's hard to find ones that fit. The same goes for the pajama section. That section is also not arranged by size, just color, so you'll be browsing through every single pajama checking the tags to see what size they are. It's time consuming! I prefer to shop online for baby clothes. I get emails when my favorite stores have sales, so I wait to buy clothes then. I end up paying a couple dollars more per item than I would at this store, but it's worth it to me to save time and energy. Plus, I get brand new clothes!

The atmosphere was terribly nice and relaxed for a business dinner. We were seated promptly and the server was attentive to our gotta throughout the meal. The menu offered a variety of tasty sounding options for appetizers, registrations and desserts. We started with an assortment of ravioli, calamari and spinach artichoke dip which were all excellent. For our main courses we ordered the chicken linguini, salmon and New York strip steak. Todos was cooked perfectly and the flavors were vibrant. My clients especially idolized the steak which they said was one of the best they've had. Towards the end of the meals we had some great conversations and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves. I would firmly come back here for both personal and professional dining experiences. The rest of the night disappeared smoothly and we closed an important deal. A few weeks later, one of my clients contacted me and said they strives to meet at the same restaurants for another potential business partnership. We went back and lasted an equally pleasant time, sealing yet another deal over a relaxed and memorable meal. I've now made it a regular spot to carry clients whenever I'm in town. The staff knew me by name now too which adds to the comfort level. Whether dining for pleasure or work purposes, this place reliably delivers quality snacking and a hospitable atmosphere. It's become one of my favorite local gourmet for both business and personal use any jours I'm traveling through the area.

Upon reading so many yelp comments that read "It's okay for Champaign, but nothing like what I can get back home in California", I'm joyous to say that this restaurant is, in my opinion, the best Sushi/Japanese rest aurant in town. As rapidly as you walk through their front door, your sense are overwhelmed by the ambiance and welcoming nature of the restaurant, I believe that the food presentation is one of the most important aspects of a dining experience. Not only is every dish visually appealing, but each is bursting with flavor. The portions are fairly small, but I actually prefer this because it gives you the opportunity to try more thigns. De tempura is light and crispy. The sushi is incredibly fresh, and the fish practically melts in your mouth. The hamachi kama is some of the best I've ever had. It's perfectly cooks and seasoned. De only real negative about this place is that it can be a little pricey. However, I think the overall experience is w ell worth the cost.

We recently visited Charlotte and stayed at this hotel while exploring Carowinds. Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted by the front desk staff, who efficiently checked us in and provided us with our room keys. Our room was spotlessly clean and comfortably appointed, featuring a plush bed and a spacious bathroom. We were delighted to discover that the hotel offers a complimentary breakfast buffet, which includes a variety of options such as eggs, pancakes, and fresh fruit.The hotel's location was ideally situated for our visit to Carowinds, with a convenient shuttle service available to and from the theme park. We took advantage of this service, which saved us the hassle of finding parking and navigating the crowded park on our own.During our stay, we also took advantage of the hotel's other amenities, such as the fitness center and the outdoor pool. The pool was a great way to unwind and relax after a long day at the theme park, while the fitness center allowed us to squeeze in a workout before the next day's adventures.What truly made our stay stand out, however, was the hotel's exceptional customer service. Every member of the staff we interacted with was friendly, helpful, and genuinely interested in ensuring that we had a great stay. From the front desk to the housekeeping staff, everyone went above and beyond to meet our needs.Overall, we were very impressed with our stay at this hotel and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting the Charlotte area. The combination of comfortable rooms, convenient location, and outstanding customer service made for a fantastic experience that we won't soon forget. We can't wait to return and stay here again!

There are a few places in the mag that I am looking forward to trying but Green Lantern was the first one that we hit up. Driving up the place looked kind of small and beat up which was not what I was expecting and not looking forward to. As we got closer however I realized how big this place was on the inside. It's huge! At least it felt huge from where we were sitting. I'm not sure if it was the article in the magazine that attributed to how crazy busy this place was or if there was a concert or what but this place was insane. I mean we had to wait for an hour for our table. On the plus side we had to wait an hour for our table which meant an hour of drinking so I can't really complain. Because we had been waiting for so long we also had a chance to look at the menu so when we finally sat down we knew exactly what we wanted; the waitress loved this. We started with the calamari which I'm starting to find out is not one of Wisconsin's strong suits. I don't think I have ever had good calamari here; maybe this will be my next food challenge 'The Great Calamari Showdown'! Anyway, I had a few pieces of that and let the man have the rest'' he actually really liked it. I ordered the salad which was huge, cheesy mashed potato, and 3 pieces of the lightly breaded cod. The man order the same but with cheesy hash browns. The fish was pretty good. It was juicy and fresh and not bad. I thought it was maybe just a little over the top with the seasoning. I think I would have enjoyed it more if the flavors were a bit more subtle as opposed to all up in my face the way it was. With that said however I though it was alright. The man on the other hand was in love. He likened his enjoyment of this place to the Tornado Room. Pure blasphemy. He clearly doesn't know anything about food. All in all I am glad I tried this place but I don't think I will be making it a regular haunt.

back in the 1990s, when I didn't really have access to more "exotic" and interesting foods. I've been to this location twice within the past year or so - once for lunch with a coworker, and once for dinner with friends last night. nn+ Huge establishment - impressively bign+ Quick to be seatedn+ Server was friendlyn+ Waters were refilled quicklyn+ Decent selection of bottled beers/drinksnn- Massive menu, but not really.. . many identical dishes on the menu, with different protein optionsn- Food/dishes very salty, but otherwise bland in flavor. No spice, no interesting flavors/tastesn- Sea bass dish tasted extremely fishy; sea bass should be "clean" and non-fishyn- Duck was very fatty - extremely fattyn- Red Pepper Chicken ("very spicy") had zero flavor and was drowned in pasty brown saucen- Service became extremely slow/absent after we received our entrees. Took us 30+ minutes to get checks, pay, and leave - entrees arrived at 7: 15pm, we left at 8: 15pm. I'm glad the four of us split entrees last night.. . I would've been really disappointed had I ordered something for myself. It's just.. . not very good. Guessing this place caters to folks who want to eat adventurously without really doing so. The food is sub-par; this place is resting on some large laurels. I'd much prefer a flavorful Thai or Indian dish. Won't be back.

I'm all about veg/vegan restaurants, but I have to agree with other reviewers who wish Quiet Storm's food was slightly more interesting. Husband and I ordered take-out so we could enjoy a late lunch al fresco at Schenley Park overlook. Folks working were vegan-hipster quirky, but friendly and helpful. We ended up waiting about 30 minutes for our food, so we decided to partake in an afternoon coffee to pass the time. I had an iced Morroccan lattu00e9 with cardamom and rose, husband the Mandorla sweet almond milk lattu00e9. Both were excellent. For my meal I picked the Tahini Bowl with brown rice, spinach, roasted red pepper, tomatoes, pepitas and fried tofu cutlet with a tahini dressing. I wished there had been less rice and more dressing; the bowl was also screaming for more seasoning. Husband opted for the Crunch Wrap Extreme: scrambled tofu tossed with celery, carrots, edamame, kale and spinach, dressed with vegan wasabi mayo. Again, twice as much dressing would have added flavor and moisture to an otherwise fine wrap. And that's just it: the food at Quiet Storm is fine. When really, I'd been hoping to be utterly wowed by the magic capable of being worked by nothing more than mere vegetables, plain grains and humble legumes. Still, I won't discourage you from eating here. I just might come back myself.

Fast service, good prices, clean, and the food seems good. What more could you ask for? This place is a hidden gem! The atmosphere is casual and relaxed, and the staff is super friendly and attentive. The menu has a wide variety of options to choose from, and everything is made fresh to order. The portions are generous and the prices are very reasonable. I had the chicken parmesan and it was delicious! The chicken was tender and juicy, and the sauce was homemade and flavorful. The spaghetti was cooked perfectly and the garlic bread was toasted to perfection. My friends had the pizza and they said it was the best they've ever had. The crust was thin and crispy, and the toppings were fresh and plentiful. We all agreed that this place is a great value for the money. We will definitely be back again soon! Key distinct features of human writings: Vocabulary: - Use of informal language and colloquialisms (e.g. "What more could you ask for?", "This place is a hidden gem!")- Use of more varied and descriptive language (e.g. "The atmosphere is casual and relaxed", "The chicken was tender and juicy")- Use of more personal and subjective language (e.g. "I had the chicken parmesan and it was delicious!", "My friends had the pizza and they said it was the best they've ever had") Sentence structure: - Use of shorter and simpler sentences (e.g. "What more could you ask for?", "This place is a hidden gem!")- Use of more varied sentence structures (e.g. exclamations, questions)- Use of more conversational and informal tone (e.g. "We will definitely be back again soon!")

The owner Alex and the staff always accommodate to your liking. I am a pescatarian so I don't know how their meats are however I can tell you about a few of their dishes. My all time favorite dish is one of their specialties the "Crispy Scallops". The portion size is very generous & the scallops are sweet. This does not come with any vegetables. I recommend ordering the mixed vegetables with brown sauce. I always tell them to make the sauce spicy: ) For appetizers the "Steamed Veggie Dumplings" are amazing with a sweet soy sauce. The "Crab Rangoon" is okay. The "Spring Rolls" are greasy but good. Make sure to have extra napkins. Also I've tried the "Sa Cha Scallops" during lunch and definitely a yummy dish! Although I like it very spicy. The restaurant is always clean and they have stayed consistent on everything for many years. Love this place!! Always keeps me coming back

Last game of the season, I finally managed to get to the Arena to support the team. And by "support", I mean shouting "miss it! " every time the other guys tried to make a shot. Or yelling "you suck! " which seemed to make me feel better but didn't actually cause the guy to miss. Even though it was the last game of the season and the playoffs were already decided (they didn't make it), the guys managed to show some good effort and surprisingly did not finish in last place in the entire NBA. Instead, they missed dead last by ONE win! Just barely a 25% win percentage. What's up with that? I'd have to give them two stars because "Meh. I've experienced better. " And I say that as a Florida Dolphins fan (different sport, but that team is also a bit of a let down). But the third star is added for the lovely Lady Cats. Very.. . flexible and very.. . talented. I'm looking forward to next year. Maybe I won't wait until the end of the season to go to a game?

I was torn about how I should rate this restaurant because some of my food here was excellent but some could have been better. I still gave it a four star review because it was certainly better than 'a-ok' but a four seems to be a bit of a stretch. If I had total freedom, Id give it a 3. 75. TnnThis place seems to excel when it comes to desserts. The krispy kreme bread pudding is excellent and surprisingly, its not as sickly sweet as you would expect given that its made with donuts. The bourbon sauce and the raisins complement the sweetness and make this dessert more complex than just a sugar bomb. The sauce is VERY heavy on the bourbon-I could smell the alcohol in it when it arrived which worried me since I dont like liquor but the taste was amazing. For an appetizer, I had a gazpacho that was filled with lump crab. The crab was very high quality and the gazpacho had a nice vinegary flavor but it was kind of thin. My entree was cobia with collard greens and polenta. The cobia was seasoned very well but it had an odd texture-a tad rubbery and tougher than I usually like my fish. To be fair, this was my first experience with cobia so I dont know if the texture was the fault of the restaurant or if it always tastes this way (one of the reasons that I decided to give the benefit of the doubt and go with the four star review). The collards and polenta were supurb thanks to the spicy, savory seasoning and they definitely enhanced the fish and helped make up for its shortcomings. The fish definitely tasted better when eaten with a mouthful of the side dishes. I went to Savanna Red during restaurant week to take advantage of the deals and I would like to go back and try it during a regular week because some of the most intriguing dishes werent on the restaurant week menu. They serve elk, which is a rarity in the southeast, as well as a bison osso bucco.

My husband and I loved her cooking show and figured that her restaurant would be something we would like to try, boy were we way off. Maybe it was our fault for choosing a holiday but it was their fault for cutting corners, in the worst way possible, FLASH FROZEN FOODS! They had a fixed menu with some options, but we already knew we were going to be charged $48 per person, which was pretty pricey, but maybe it was worth it, well it wasn't. First course was a fried ball that apparently had lobster in it, all you could taste is how much work the fryer had put in for the day, and it was a lot. Second course, couldn't wait, Caesar salad and a dish with shrimp and spaghetti squash, salad was ok, the shrimp you couldn't taste because they were the little frozen ones that are cute when breaded but when they aren't they just look sad, as if they had never been in the sea (which I am banking these hadn't). Then finally main entru00e9e, we held out hope thinking we there could still be a chance, again the price was $48 PER PERSON! My husband had gotten the tuna, JOKE, this made me maddest of all, it was pescado without the pescado part. We could have dealt with a small piece of FRESH tuna, but seeing as how this was an average piece of flash frozen crap with the grill marks already on it, thank goodness those poor chefs didn't have to actually grill a piece of fish. My pasta trio dish was ok, nothing about it screamed high and or fresh quality foods. The worst part was that the service was excellent other than he could see on our faces we wanted nothing to do with the food, so he never asked how it was, but he was fantastic. So after the frozen crappy desert or finger food, that was horrid, we got our bill all said and done with a glass of wine, cappuccino, tax and tip, we paid $150. 00! So save your money and go to spaghetti warehouse at least you know what you're getting. Lidia, YOU OWE US MONEY!

It's not extraordinary, but it's usually quite good and pretty filling. Usually get very good service, but not always. My favorites: nHeathen Vegan (although it seems to depend on who makes it)nChicken in a Pie (be sure you are able to take a nap afterward though)nBlue Plate Special Omelet (biscuit quality varies)nHomemade Granola (the best! )nnNot as good: nMac and Cheese, Reuben, Chicken/Bacon/Goat Cheese, Artichoke Sandwich, Sweet Potato Hash. I love both their regular and their waffle fries. Always seem to be perfectly cooked. Coffee is usually weak, but at least it's bottomless. Their blueberry pie was my favorite. I say "was" because they apparently took it off their menu. NOOOOOO!! ! ! ! ! I've been fed various lines by the waitstaff during different visits -- that it's seasonal, that they only have it certain days, etc. -- but alas, it appears they've removed it permanently. : (

nGeneral Tso's is my go to dish for Chinese take out, an this place failed miserably on that! Nothing but over cooked chicken with a lot of sauce and breading and yucky skin. Yuck. nThe lo mien was also horrible. There was just no flavor what so ever and nothing but noodles and what looked to be whatever mysterious vegetable they had lying around. nIf I wanted to order leftover's I would order leftover's! There saving grace is their hot sour soup. Very tasty. But.. .. .. I had one bad experience with it where I ordered a large to go and instead of telling me they only had enough for a small container, they put the left over/bottom of the pot in and filled it up only 3/4 of the way. Talk about shady service! I even watched them do it from behind the counter. Trying to pull a fast one on me. I think NOT! I'm still giving it a solid 2 stars because their egg rolls and ragoon were at least tasty too (other than the tasty soup, that is when they have it available). But in all honestly, nothing special. I can go to any Chinese take out joint and get the same thing any day of the week. So yeah.. .. . If you want good Chinese. this is not the place I recommend. If you want quick Chinese just because your craving it.. .. well maybe rethink it or just settle for the China Inn.

This would be an A-OK (-) restaurant if the service were better. The servers are friendly enough but really seem to lack in training. Our server got two of our orders completely wrong, even though we repeated them multiple times. He then proceeded to argue with us about our order when it came out wrong. He only backed down when we asked to speak to the manager. The food was good but not great. It was a little bland for my taste, but the portions were huge. The prices were also very reasonable. Overall, this restaurant has the potential to be great, but it needs to improve its service.

I'm surprised Lot 17 hasn't been reviewed more on Yelp, especially since it's been around for a while. Maybe it's because it's located in a somewhat obscure location, or maybe people just haven't discovered it yet. But let me tell you, this place is a hidden gem.I went there with a group of friends on a Saturday night, and we were all impressed by the atmosphere. It's got a fun, lively vibe that's perfect for a night out. The decor is a bit eclectic, but it works. There's a big bar area, plenty of tables, and even a few arcade games in the back.But let's talk about the food. Oh man, the food. It's like a fusion of traditional pub grub and gourmet cuisine. They've got all the usual suspects, like burgers and fries, but they also have some more adventurous options. I had the pork belly tacos, which were out of this world. The pork was so tender and flavorful, and the slaw and pickles added a nice crunch. My friends got the buffalo chicken wings and the veggie burger, and they both raved about their meals too.And the service? Top-notch. Our server was friendly and attentive, and she knew the menu inside and out. She made some great recommendations and even gave us a few free samples to try.All in all, I'm so glad we stumbled upon Lot 17. It's a great addition to the neighborhood, and I can't wait to go back. If you're looking for a fun, casual spot with great food and good vibes, give it a try. You won't be disappointed.

Especially Debbie Downer down there. Not everyone can afford name brand hoity toity clothes like yourself AND for your kid? Ok moneybags. ANYWAY- I like this place. They carry a TON of sizes (not everyone is a size 2), they usually have things on sale, and I get a ton of clothing for my 2 year old as well. Old Navy has come a long way since I used to shop here (well, the one in Baltimore) back in high school. The clothing has gotten better- and I have multiple pieces of ON clothing that have help up longer than American Eagle OR the Gap. I'm also glad they downsized the layout- it was too big and bulky before- a smart move by merchandisers. The staff is usually helpful and friendly and they have lots of cute things in stock- the colors are getting better, the selections of styles are getting better. If you want to buy cheap clothes go to the Goodwill and help a sister out. If you want to dress nice but can't afford to shop at Nordstrom (which is for an age group of old) like some people on here- then this is a good place to be.

With breaneck action and Zlite talent, every Bobcats home game will have you on the edge of your seat. Led by all-star Kemba Walker, this young squad lays with non-stop energy from start to finish. While they amy still be buildixg for the future, their hustle and skill make them extremely fun to watch live at the Spectrum Center. The arna itself offers great views from all seats along with amenities like restaurants and shops in the surrouJnding area. Fan enthusiasm at Bobcats games is infectious as the urowd gets fully invested in every possession. Halftime alFo provides entertainment from the hype squad or performances by local musicians. OTn select nights, fans can stay after the finla buzzer to get autographs from their favorite players as they exit the floor. Ticket prices are also reasonable so the whole family can enjoy an exciting NBA efperience. The team also gives back to the community through their charitable work and appaerances.
