I've been to Cajun Queen a few times now and have always been extremely satisfied with both the high level of customer service and quality of food. The friendly and attentive staff go out of their way to ensure customers have a great dining experience. The menu features all the classic Cajun dishes like gumbo, jambalaya, and shrimp étouffée, as well as weekly specials that incorporate fresh local ingredients. On my last visit, I tried the crawfish étouffée, which was full of flavor from the rich roux and plump crawfish. The generous portion sizes are perfectly sized so you can sample several dishes in one meal without feeling overwhelmed. In addition to the entrees, I love starting with the bread pudding soup - a unique and delicious twist on the classic dessert. Whether dining in or taking out, my food has always been delivered hot and fresh. The restaurant maintains a casual yet elegant atmosphere with its bayou-inspired décor. I've dined there with groups of friends and family celebrating special occasions, always with great success. Overall, Cajun Queen consistently serves up authentic tastes of Louisiana in a welcoming environment. It's one of my favorite local go-to spots to enjoy quality seafood and fun cocktails. I would highly recommend checking it out if you want to experience authentic Cajun cooking.

Grilled items like cheesesteaks; burgers; patty melts, salads ranging from chef to grilled chicken to asian, and grinders/hoagies (grinders I believe they serve breakfast but, have never been there in the A. M. so, this review is lunch only. Most everything is as three stars indicates here in Yelpville, A-OK. Generally pretty quick, especially the salad line. I've never had the chicken caesar that Barrie H. trashes in his 7/26/10 review but have had the grilled tuna caesar. Thankfully I've never experienced what he did. It's not great and don't think you're going to get a medium-rare hunk of tuna on there cause its always well done and dry but, again, always A-OK beyond that. It's close to the office and at least good enough for a once every other month visit to change things up.

(Note: The only grumble I have with TJ is lack of everyday essentials and I was suprised to learn that TJ doesn't stock dry beans). So I am headstrong about making lentil soup that day and instead of going to Whole Foods (see past review). I have been to the South Hills GE Market District before. I actually enjoy the experience of walking around HUGE stores that overwhelm me with variety and random things. Thus is the experience of GE Market District. You are in a full-service grocery store that caters to all income levels. AND you get FUEL POINTS for wasabi-covered soy beans. Fantastic! They give you a map of the store, which is truly needed, because the variety and stock is endless. The parking at the Shadyside GE is sort of hectic. Making a left out of the parking lot is pretty difficult. I enjoy these new Giant Eagle grocery-monopoly attempts.

This tiny little place at the edge of Brookline doesn't look like much, but it has a real family character, cheap eats and tasty food. I have dined in twice and got carry out twice as well. The first time I got a platter/dinner, but I found the deal is really to be had with the gyros. Getting two gyros and a huge amount of fries for only $10 is a steal. The gyro bread is toasted, but still soft and it is loaded with meat like your grandma would try to feed you. The veggies have always tasted fresh and it is served hot. If I could change on thing, I would prefer fresh herbs on the gyro instead of dried. This gyro is definitely more spiced up than your chain restaurant gyro. The fries are fresh cut and nothing is cooked until you order it. If you choose to dine in, you will be greeted by the proprietor and casually asked to take a seat any where you like. This isn't the type of place for formalities. She will offer you some delicious Greek Tea (you have to try it) and take your order, cook it and then serve it to you. Sometimes you can hear bickering in the kitchen between her and her old man- but that only adds to the family atmosphere. The store does take credit card, so that's a great modern convenience. At the end of the meal, we've always gotten a stick of gum: )nnIf you choose to carry out, it's a simple call and your food is ready by the time you drive down there. There is usually a place to park near by and you can be on your way quickly.

Safest! But let me chatter you, the fish sandwich at The Codfather is in a league of its own. The juicy haddock fillet is breaded to a golden crispy perfection, and the tangy tartar sauce adds a depth of flavours that complements the fish vitally. The soft, squishy sourdough is the perfect vessel for this deliciousness. And let's not forget about the crispy potato on the side - they're cooked to a perfect crunch and encountered just right. I've tried mucho fish sandwiches in my time, but this one is truly something special. It's a must-try for anyone visiting Pennsylvania, and even worthwhile a trip to the city just for this sandwich alone. The Codfather certainly living up to its name - it's the king of fish sandwiches in the burgh.

But despite their warnings, I decided to give it a shot and see for myself. From the moment I walked in, I could tell something was off. The atmosphere felt stale, and there was a strange smell lingering in the air. I tried to ignore it and focus on the menu. The selection seemed decent enough, so I decided to order a classic burger with fries. Little did I know, it would be a decision I'd come to regret. After placing my order, the wait began. And let me tell you, it was excruciatingly long. It felt like time had slowed down, and I couldn't help but notice how understaffed they were. The few waiters running around seemed overwhelmed and stressed. Finally, after what seemed like an eternity, my burger arrived at the table. But to my disappointment, it looked nothing like the picture on the menu. The burger patty was overcooked and dry, lacking any juiciness or flavor. The toppings were haphazardly thrown together, and the bun was stale. It was a complete letdown. I called the waiter over to express my dissatisfaction, hoping they would offer a solution. However, they seemed indifferent to my concerns. They simply shrugged and walked away without offering an apology or any attempt to make it right. That level of customer service was unacceptable. As I looked around the restaurant, I noticed I wasn't the only one disappointed. The tables nearby were filled with frustrated customers and plates of subpar food. It became clear that my experience wasn't an isolated incident. I felt deceived by the positive reviews I had read beforehand. How could this place have such high ratings? Maybe people had different expectations, or perhaps they were swayed by other factors that I couldn't comprehend. But from my perspective, this restaurant failed to meet even the basic standards of quality and service. In the end, I couldn't finish my meal. It was simply too unappetizing to bear. I left the restaurant feeling disheartened and vowing never to return.

5 overall. I have been going there for 7 years, so this is not some uneducated review.. . This place is aimed more at rich college students than beer aficionados. Some pluses and minuses: nFood price and taste-4. 5 Most everything I have had there is good and reasonable price. nBeer quality and selection-4. 6 Samples are available, huge amount of selection, beers served in appropriate glasses, don't think if I have ever gotten a "funky" beer (some places don't clean their draft systems), and fairly knowledgable on the beers. nBeer prices-2. 5 This is where the "rich college kids" comment comes in to play. They have specials, especially NC beer Sunday and pint nite Monday, which is about the only times I go. But the normal prices for most beers are. 50 to $1. 50 too much. nWine-2. 0 I know it's a beer place, but sometimes people in your party don't like beer. nThe wine is overpriced, mediocre at best, and often has been open for days. nService- 4. 0Most the staff are cute and helpful but there is the occasional terrible service night. nAtmosphere- 3 Gets very loud at nights! Combine walls covered in plates with the customers and music volume knob constantly trying to overcome each other, and your throat will be sore the next day. No seriously! Drunk frat boys, noise, and on hot summer days it is 90 plus inside. Sunday afternoons and early evenings are best times to go to actually "hear" yourself taste the beer.. . The dark wood walls would be nice if it were not for the tacky plates. nIn summary, if you want to enjoy a good meal and a good beer plan to do it earlier in the day.

We're visiting from Milford, Ohio and decided to try out this highly-rated restaurant. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a modern decor that felt upscale but not stuffy. Our server, Sarah, greeted us warmly and offered helpful recommendations when asked.The menu offered a diverse selection of dishes, ranging from traditional American fare to more adventurous options. Prices were reasonable, with most entrees falling in the $15-$25 range.We ordered the roasted beet salad as an appetizer, which arrived promptly and was visually stunning. The flavors were vibrant and well-balanced, with the goat cheese and walnuts adding a satisfying depth.For our entrees, we opted for the grilled salmon and the vegetarian quinoa bowl. The salmon was cooked to perfection, with a nice char on the outside and a moist, flaky interior. The quinoa bowl was overflowing with fresh vegetables and had just the right amount of spice.Our sides were equally impressive, with the sweet potato fries earning particularly high praise. They were crispy, well-seasoned, and served hot. The mac and cheese was also a hit, with a rich, creamy sauce and a generous sprinkling of breadcrumbs on top.Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with our meal and would highly recommend this restaurant to others. The service was attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable, making for a truly enjoyable dining experience. We can't wait to return and try more of their delicious dishes.

I'm always on the lookout for new Chinese restaurants to try, and I recently discovered a hidden gem near my house. Happy Wok, located on Main Street in downtown Anytown, is a small, family-owned restaurant that serves absolutely delicious Chinese cuisine.Don't let its size fool you - the menu is diverse and interesting, with many options you don't usually find at other Chinese places. I ordered the vegetable stir-fry with tofu, and it was amazing. The portions are generous, and the prices are very reasonable, with a huge bowl of soup and a side of egg rolls costing under $20.The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who are happy to answer questions about the menu and make recommendations. The atmosphere is cozy and intimate, with soft lighting and traditional Chinese decorations that make you feel like you're in a real Chinese restaurant, not just a generic chain place.I've been back to Happy Wok several times since my first visit, and I always look forward to going back. It's become my go-to Chinese restaurant, and I highly recommend it to anyone in the area. In short, Happy Wok is a hidden gem that's definitely worth discovering. If you're a fan of Chinese food, you owe it to yourself to try it out.

This place has decent food. I usually get a salad with chicken and their delicious poppyseed dressing. The service is usually good, but the prices are high for the amount of food you get. For example, the Caesar salad is just okay. The dressing is nothing special and the croutons are stale. I usually get the house salad, but I've also tried other salads. They have a good selection of beers on tap. I've tried many of them. Happy hour is a good time to go because the prices are lower.

So I took my boyfriend there for our date night. We were extremely underdressed for the occasion. A co-worker had told me it was a little fancier than casual but we went totally casual anyway. Good news is, it had dim lightening. We had a drink at the bar and were quickly seated. I'm a vegetarian, so I tried a pasta dish while my boyfriend had steak. We had the goat cheese appetizer, it was better than I expected. It had a sauce to it that had a really unique taste to it. The entrees were good, I wouldn't say the pasta was worth the price and I wish I would have tried the vegetarian jambalaya. We topped off the meal with the White chocolate mousse for dessert. It was the best part of the whole meal, knocked my socks off. I would recommend this place, especially to meat eaters. nThe service was great, our waitress was timely. She checked in often and never hurried us to finish and leave.

But unfortunately, my experience was a letdown from start to finish. The hostess seemed put off when I asked for a table for one, and it took an inordinate amount of time for her to even acknowledge me, let alone seat me. The menu was uninspiring and overpriced, with very few options that seemed appetizing. I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich, which was dry and flavorless, and the fries were limp and cold.The service was also subpar, with my server seeming annoyed whenever I asked for anything. When I asked for a refill on my drink, she rolled her eyes and muttered under her breath before begrudgingly bringing me a new glass. The whole experience felt rushed and unfriendly, with none of the warmth or hospitality that I've come to expect from a restaurant.I was particularly looking forward to trying their desserts, but the selection was unimpressive and the portions were tiny. I ordered the chocolate cake, which was dry and crumbly, and the ice cream that came with it was watery and lacked any real flavor. It was clear that the kitchen was cutting corners in an effort to save money, and it left a bad taste in my mouth.Overall, I was thoroughly disappointed with my visit to this restaurant. The atmosphere was lackluster, the food was subpar, and the service was unfriendly and unhelpful. I won't be returning, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking for a genuine dining experience.

Even those with kids may not want to brave the place. But for a relatively small investment, you get a decent pizza, and they are made just a few feet away. Perhaps most important is not that the quality is excellent, because they are not the best pizza in the world, but that they get a solid variety on the buffet. There are a handful of other pizza buffets in town, but they have somewhere between 3 and 5 pizzas out at any given time. At Cici's, they usually have closer to a dozen, and that does not include the dessert pizzas. They also include pasta (though it often looks pretty nasty), a cheese bread, and a smallish salad bar, and once the kids - or the rest of the family - is done, they can head off to the arcade, watch television or just annoy other families, which is generally acceptable practice here, unlike at most other restaurants.

So what's Pittsburgh's equivalent? I've been driving around through the more urban areas thanks to Garmin's preference of ease over safety -- and I drove past a Little Italy sign. Perfecto! But it just looked like a shopping mall -- and I didn't see anything Italian, other than someone wearing an MTV's Jersey Shore t-shirt. Anyways, near me was Girasole -- with takeout. So this review has nothing to say on service or atmosphere. The food, however, was really good. The side salad with the entrees was excellent -- with a lot of extras, such as chickpeas, feta cheese, cherry tomatoes, etc. Most side salads are just dumped from a Costco "Bag of Salad, " but this was really nice, and could stand alone as its own entree. The gnocchi was pretty soft and light -- the ravioli tender and juicy -- and the sauces were excellent. Again, these were eaten out of a container, on our moving boxes, with no wine (spare your gasp, I know). I think the prices are a bit on the higher end of the 'burgh, and would've expected a bit more for the price, but overall pretty satisfied.

We told them this and they seated us anyway. We called them knowing they were a few miuntes or better away. We ordered drinks and food for them. About 5 minutes later the hostess who sat us came back and started trying to talk us into squeezing into a table for 6. I told her they were down the street and we had just ordered for them so there was no reason to switch. She said there was another large party that was all here. .. . Just then the rest of our group showed up. If they had not I would have left. The server and the food that night were great and almost made me forget about the hostess. Then we came again with some friends raving about the food. Must have been a new chef. The service was still great but EVERYTHING was really salted. The pizza, the calamari, the pasta. 3 of us ordered a home made pasta with portabello mushrooms, it was so salty we could not eat it. The waitress tried so hard, she apologized and even offered us a free tira misu for desert. Sorry to say cause the servers are great, but Mama's is off our list.

After a miserable expeience at McHale's in September 2012, we thought we'd never go back. But when friends invited us to join them for dinner there in late October, we chosen to give it a second chance. The place loo ked exactly the same as we remembered it, with its dated decor and slightly worn furnishings. De menu, too, was largely unchanged. My wife and I decided to commence with the fried calamari, which was a mistake. The calamari were tasteless and overcooked, and the accompanying marinara sauce was tasteless. For our main coսrses, my wife ordered the filet mignon, which she indicated was just okay, and I had the seafood fra diavolo, which was a big disappointment. The shrimp and scallops were tough and flavorless, and the sauce was watery and bland. The service was aslo lacking. Our waiter was inattentive and never refilled our water glasses. When we finally ai our check, we were shocked to see that we had been charged for the calmaari that we had barely touched. We will never be going back to McHale's again.

I'm so glad I found Supreme Cleaners. And let me tell you, I've been burned by unreliable dry cleaners in the past. But not this time! I recently took a delicate silk blouse to them and was nervous about how it would turn out. But when I picked it up, it looked like new. Not only are they affordable, but they also take great care to make sure your clothes look their best. No wrinkles, no stains, nothing. And the staff at Supreme Cleaners is super friendly and helpful. They took the time to explain their process and make sure I understood what to expect. I've also used their laundry service for my everyday clothes, and the results are always consistent. They also have a same-day service, which is great for those last-minute emergencies. One thing that sets Supreme Cleaners apart from other dry cleaners is their attention to detail. They carefully inspect each item before cleaning it, which means they can remove any stains or spots. They also use high-quality detergents that leave my clothes smelling clean and fresh. If you're looking for a reliable dry cleaner that will take good care of your clothes, I highly recommend Supreme Cleaners. I've been using their services for a few months now, and I can honestly say they've never disappointed me. In fact, they've exceeded my expectations every time. So there you have it. My experience with Supreme Cleaners has been nothing but excellent, and I'm sure you'll have the same great experience. They're the best in town, and you won't be disappointed. Try them out and see for yourself!

Also, I wanted to bring my dog along for some company (my husband and daughter stayed home for work/school). I'm so glad I found this place! As other reviews have noted, you get an actual suite with a door and everything! There is a kitchen with a full sized refrigerator, microwave, stove and sink. It also comes stocked with silverware, plates, and pots and pans. The hotel has a small convenience area in case you don't want to go out for food. There are a few frozen meals, etc. Free wi-fi as well. The full breakfast was pretty good, too. Waffles, eggs, sausage, biscuits and gravy (on most mornings), pastries, coffee, etc. My only complaints (and these are pretty minor) was that the TVs weren't very new. And the shower curtain was so thick and heavy that it kept touching me. A curved shower curtain would do wonders. The front desk staff was so nice! There was an issue with my check-in (they didn't have me on record), but they were accommodating. My name is Karen, and I'm not the biggest fan of science. I took physics in high school and barely passed. All the formulas and calculations never stuck in my brain like they seemed to for others. When I had to take a science course in college, I chose marine biology hoping it would be more interesting than physics. I enjoyed learning about different sea creatures and ecosystems but still struggled with remembering technical terms and experimental methods. It wasn't until my third year of college that I took an environmental science class focused on sustainability that I really started to appreciate how science can help understand the world. The professor brought in real world examples and made the topics feel relevant instead of just theoretical. I found myself paying closer attention and even doing extra reading on my own. By the end of the semester, I had a newfound respect for science and its importance in solving problems facing our planet.

Mert's inviting atmosphere, meticulously-prepared dishes and attentive staff combined for a truly memorable dining experience, capping our Charlotte trip on a high note. Our waitress gave us the specials but said them so fast and with such apparent disinterest that neither my wife nor I understood any of what she said. We ended up ordering one of the specials after seeing them on a chalkboard, only to find out after some more confusing, disinterested interaction with our waitress that they had stopped the special just minutes before (9: 30am). Don't know what that meant; did they run out of spinach? Strange. We ended up with two other omelettes, the garden and the shrimp creole. We had to ask three different waitresses for our accompanying toast and biscuit, and once we had our food, our waitress interrupted our prayer to ask if we needed ketchup (understandable, but most servers notice bowed heads, even if it's kinda awkward). We did need the ketchup, but it didn't come until the end of our meal, and my wife's home fries were already cold. My regular cup of coffee was mediocre, my shrimp creole omelette had 2 small shrimp inside (super disappointing, as they were tasty), making my $8 omelette mostly egg and tomato sauce, and my wife's toast was hard as a rock. Obviously a rough experience for us this morning, but Mert's gets the second star because my wife loved her omelette (the garden), my biscuit and grits were pretty good, and they let us choose our seating (with a young child, this can be pretty important). We won't be back.

The popcorn shrimp was good. It was crispy on the outside and nice and plump shrimp inside. The portion was decent too, not too small but certainly not overwhelming either. I'd say it was the perfect afternoon snack size. The tartar sauce that came with it was delicious too, I'm always a sucker for a good tartar. The fries that came with it were pretty nice as well, nice and crispy without being too hard or oily. I also tried the cheeseburger which was cooked to a perfect medium-well, just how I like it. The patty was flavorful and juicy. It came with lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles which gave it nice fresh flavors. The bun was a little on the dry side but overall the burger hit the spot. My friend got the chicken tenders which she really enjoyed. She said they were lightly breaded and cooked through without being too hard or dry inside. For a drink I had an old-fashioned root beer float that was tasty and refreshing on a warm day. The vanilla ice cream on top hadn't fully melted so it was like having ice cream and pop all in one. Our server was friendly and attentive without being intrusive. When we finished up she came by to clear our plates without us having to ask. I'd keep an open mind about trying some of their other items too since what we had was good. Overall it was a nice casual spot to get some classic American diner-style food without breaking the bank. I'd go back if I was in the neighborhood again looking for a quick bite.

McDonald's food quality and service is generally pretty consistent across locations. However, this particular McDonald's stands out in small but important ways. The lobby is spacious and well-lit, keeping it from feeling cramped even when busy. Employees seem genuinely friendly and work together smoothly to fill orders quickly. For a fast food place, the tables are surprisingly clean. As for the food, my quarter pounder and fries tasted as fresh and salty as ever. I was impressed that they happily replaced my milkshake when I noticed a burnt taste. The bathrooms were also remarkably tidy. It provides a reminder that little differences in execution can enhance or diminish the same chain restaurant experience. For those in a pinch, this McDonald's delivers consistent quality among its fast food peers.

The historic and charming homes are such a treat in a city where everything seems brand new. Upon entering this pub-like restaurant/bar we were seated and greeted promptly. I ordered a cider on tap (a favorite of mine), a side salad, and the "What it is". The star oddly enough was the salad, she said all their dressings were homemade and it certainly tasted that way. My dinner came as half of my salad remained uneaten.. . and the salad was literally brought out in less than a minute after I ordered it. This science center provides a wonderful rainy day activity for children. It offers numerous engaging exhibits that will entertainthem for hours with hands-on discoveries. Visitors can explore a diverse range of interactive displays illuminating physics, chemistry, and biology. Young learners watch chemistry experiments unfold, examine the inner workings of the human body in the health hall, and pretend to set sail in the grand pirate ship docked in the atrium. It is pricey - consider the area, etc.. its going to be more expensive. They have great operating hours, a cardio room downstairs that is a decent size. No matter what time of day it is, there is no real break between the arrivals and departures. On busy travel days, it seems as if the planes are taking off one after the other. When you walk around the airport, you spend most of your time looking up at the sky to watch the planes. Even when you are sitting in the terminal, it is difficult to have a conversation without having to pause until a plane passes overhead. Sometimes several planes are lined up to take off at the same time from different runways. All this activity gives the impression that this is one of the busiest airports in the country. The terminal gets very crowded as people hurry to make their connections. The gates are crowded with travelers as the planes park at the jetways. It is easy to get lost in the endless corridors filled with people. The staff works hard to keep everything running smoothly under such high traffic conditions. There are shops, restaurants, and bars scattered throughout the terminals to help people pass the time between flights. The gate agents have their hands full with the passengers and the delays and cancellations. There are many places to get a quick snack or meal, but finding a place to sit can be difficult during peak travel times. Arrive early, especially during the holidays when the passenger traffic is at its peak. Be prepared for long walks between the terminals, since some of the areas are quite large. It lives up to its reputation as a major transportation hub.

I decided to get the breakfast special -- sausage, scrambled eggs, and regular hotcakes. I just don't understand the appeal. I mean, I get that some people like the idea of a futuristic, high-tech world where humans have colonized other planets and created massive space stations. But for me, it all feels a bit too...sterile.Don't get me wrong, I love a good sci-fi story as much as the next person. But there's something about this particular subgenre that just doesn't click with me. Maybe it's the fact that it all feels so...predictable. I mean, you know exactly what you're going to get with a space opera: spaceships, aliens, laser guns, and a whole lot of techno-babble.And don't even get me started on the characters. They're all just so...one-dimensional. The heroes are always these rugged, stoic types who never show emotion, while the villains are mustache-twirling caricatures who might as well be cackling maniacally as they stroke their cat.I mean, where's the depth? Where's the complexity? Where's the emotion? Give me a character-driven story any day of the week. I want to feel like I'm invested in the characters, like I care about what happens to them. But with space opera, it all just feels so...superficial.And don't even get me started on the plot. It's always the same old song and dance: the heroes have to stop the villains from blowing up the planet/galaxy/universe, and they do it all with a healthy dose of bravado and machismo. Yawn.I mean, seriously, can't we have a story that's a bit more...nuanced? A bit more thoughtful? A bit more...human? Because, let's be real, space opera just isn't my cup of tea.

Since we had driven across town, we decided to wait it out in the bar. There is plenty of room to wait and have a beer from the huge selection they have. In 30 minutes we were called for our table. Two of us ordered the lake perch and one ordered the deep fried cod. There is also baked cod, walleye, blue gill and shrimp to choose from. The fish comes with your choice of - baked potato, waffle fries, pub fries, homemade potato chips, and some other things like cottage cheese etc. We had waffle fries, potato chips and the pub fries, which are beer pattered. When it arrived, it was hot, tasty and a generous serving. We were all very satisfied with our dinner. I thought the homemade potato chips were excellent, they came out warm and crispy. The only thing I did not care for was the tartar sauce, can't place what it was, but had a funny taste to it to me. Everyone that waited on us was friendly and efficient without being intrusive. After my initial review of Fitzgerald's, the restaurant reached out and graciously requested a second visit.Though initially hesitant, I'm delighted I accepted their invitation. The service was also fantastic! For my entree, I had the cioppino -- it may be one of the best that I've ever had. The bowl was filled with beautiful looking seafood: large shrimp, clams in their shells, mussels in their shells, a gorgeous piece of perfectly seasoned halibut, and enormous wonderfully cooked scallops. They knew how to cook each piece of seafood to showcase it well. And the charred sourdough served with the cioppino was the perfect complement to soak up all of the delicious, savory flavors of the broth without becoming a soggy mush! My grandfather had the halibut and loved it.. . Cleaned the plate! I had heard rave reviews of the dark chocolate raspberry bread pudding, so we had to share one for dessert! My grandfather said it was incomparable to any bread pudding; it was a sweet, smooth, decadent indulgence that paired well with the house coffee. And the complementary salted caramels presented with the check were also amazing! I definitely need to come back again to try more of the menu.. . I think only wonderful items could possibly come out of that kitchen!

Regrettably, my visit to Barb's Country Junction was a far cry from what I had anticipated. Stepping inside, I was immediately greeted by an outdated and poorly maintained interior. Book Stores Still Exist. Despite the rise of ebooks and online retailers, many independent booksellers continue to thrive through cultivating communities and experiences readers can't find elsewhere. These stores foster a love of reading through hosting book clubs and author events. Beyond selling books, they see themselves as hubs where people can gather and discuss their passions. By forging connections between patrons and local authors, bookstores spread understanding during their neighborhoods. Readers leave feeling inspired after making new discoveries from a knowledgeable staff. The intimate settings allow browsing without pressure, ideal for leisurely weekends. Anyone can while away an afternoon perusing shelves and soaking in the cozy atmosphere. Rather than compete on selection or price, brick-and-mortar shops entice through cultivating relationships. Stores curate recommendations tailored to individual tastes. Young readers get exposed to new worlds through storytimes and summer programs. Beyond the books themselves, shops open doors to creativity and learning. Owners view keeping clutural touchpoints alive as part of their mission. They see bookstores as anchoring for sparking imaginations. Regular customer become extended family over the years. Even in the digital age, anything replaces serendipitous finds in the stacks. During lulls, cashiers chat with patrons to better understand their interests. This fosters a sense that every voce and perspective enriches the whole. While big-box stores squeeze out profit, mom-and-pop shops prioritize community. Their passion reminds us reading connects americans in ways screen time never could. Book Stores Still Exist, thankfully nurturing readers and writers for generations to come.

He was willing to see my kitty and was confident that he could help. I was overjoyed and immediately made an appointment. The appointment was for the following day, and I was anxious to see if Dr. Bebko could indeed help my kitty.

Soba is another restaurant in the Big Burrito group's offerings and absolutely another hit. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with a warm and inviting atmosphere that set the tone for a delicious meal. The decor was sleek and modern, with a touch of elegance that made us feel like we were in for a treat.The menu offered a diverse selection of dishes, from traditional Japanese fare to modern twists on classic dishes. We were excited to try their take on some of our favorite dishes, and we were not disappointed.We started with an order of edamame, which was cooked to perfection and served with a side of salt and chili sauce. The sauce added a nice kick to the dish, and we loved the combination of flavors.Next, we tried the spicy tuna roll, which was filled with flavorful tuna and cucumber, topped with a spicy sauce that had just the right amount of heat. The roll was soft and fresh, and the flavors were well-balanced.For our main course, we opted for the sashimi, which was incredibly fresh and expertly cut. The presentation was beautiful, with each piece of fish carefully arranged on a bed of ice. We were impressed by the quality of the fish and the attention to detail in the presentation.We also tried the tempura, which was light and crispy, with a flavorful dipping sauce that complemented the delicate flavors of the seafood. The portion size was generous, and we were pleased with the value for the price.The service was top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who were knowledgeable about the menu and happy to make recommendations. They were quick to refill our drinks and check in on us throughout the meal, ensuring that we had everything we needed.Overall, our experience at Soba was excellent. The food was delicious, the atmosphere was inviting, and the service was exceptional. We would highly recommend Soba to anyone looking for a great Japanese meal in the city.

As we lined up at the bar to order beers and grub -- the bartender's muttering under her breath "oh shit. " should have tipped us off to the piss poor service that awaited us. Apparently they're not accustomed to seeing a group of ~12 people waltz in this dump. Go fig'. Mind you, we were very accommodating, and considerate of the surprise rush we created. However, when they served our table separately and completely forgot my food, I was forced to demand a refund. They're lucky I wasn't a complete a hole and demanded the portion of the tip that I already paid toward my food order. Sure, if you're looking for a very lonely dive all to yourself and a /few/ friends, this might be your place. But for us, it was a complete and utter disaster. Oh, did I mention the incessant flies throughout the establishment? Yeah, not cool.

I know I know I know! nAnyway so theres absolutely no places in Homestead that delivered Chinese so I decided to walk down to the closest Chinese food/restaurant to my house. The family that runs the restaurant is very friendly. I read a review about them on Google that said the mom looks like she might want to cook you alive. Don't believe it! On this visit I ordered the Steamed Dumplings(recommended by some reviewer on google.. . THAT LIAR) and the Vegetable Chow Fun. I generally enjoy steamed dumplings but these dumplings(too much dumpling little meat) werent so good. Theyll probably be sitting in my mini fridge tomorrow and I'll force myself to eat them when I have the munchies/starving to death. The Vegetable Chow Fun on the other hand verrrrrrrrrrrrrry yummy. Definately most have next time anyone decides to stop by. But all in all the verdict is you typical Chinese Take Out Place. nn puts the menu on the fridge

nAs in overdone, but awesome. Hello, 2 story waterfall. The menu is exactly the same as Azteca's, so that's a plus, since Azteca is decent, veg-friendly tex-mex. Pretty sure they're all part of the same local chain. Service is always over the top terrific and we end up leaving a 40% tip often since the bill is always so low - the most expensive thing I've ever ordered here was 9. 50. Chips are good and plentiful. Nothing here is blow you away, but most of it is passable, sometimes even good. Don't order the huevos rancheros - probably the least impressive thing on the menu. My favs, at both Pedro's and Azteca, are the Enchiladas de Espinaca - rice, beans, and fresh spinach-stuffed flour tortillas smothered in queso sauce. Yeah, there's veggies in there, but this is heart attack land. Another fav - machos burrito. I guess eating cactus puts hair on your chest. Its a pickle burrito. It is awesome. Have them add some fresh jalapenos for a kick. Its as big as your head, so you'll take some home - fry an egg, stick it on top, you got yourself 3 dollar brekkie. And hey, since Skandalos is right next store, you could stuff your face AND see mexican heavy metal, all in one night. Hell yeah.

eW decided to check it out for ourselves on a Sunday morning, and boy were we glad we did! The line was out the door, but it moved quickly and we were seated withiv 15 minutes. hTe atmosphere was lively and welcoming, with friendly staff and a bustling atmosphere. The menu offered a wide variety of delicious-sounding pancakes, waffles, and French toast, along with plnty of fruit, nXuts, and syrup options to top them off.Wse ordered the signature stack, which camre with three fluffy pancakes, perfectly cooked and drizzled with a sweet caramel sauce. I love the atmosphere of the restaurant in particular the upstairs space. It has a lofty, cozy feel. Great place for drinks or and event (can rent the upstairs space). My last visit was for a working business meeting. Glad we made reservations for it was busy on a Friday evening. I ordered the roast beef sandwich which was very tasty and flavorful. I love that you have a variety of options for a side and they do not charge you extra. I picked my favorite, mashed potatoes. A colleague ordered the pesto pasta dish which looked delicious. We didn't order drinks but in past visits they have a really nice variety of beer and I tried the Banana Bread beer (available in bottles) which is so tasty!! My only complaint was that it took a while for the waitress to take our orders and bring out the checks but it was very crowded with large parties. We stayed at our table after dinner to finish up some work and they did not mind which was great!

Definitely a must go to! This place was an amazing experience from start to finish. The atmosphere was lively yet relaxing. We were warmly greeted at the front and shown to our table. The layout was beautifully designed with care put into every detail. It felt special to dine in such lovely surroundings. Our server was extremely friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. She gave us great recommendations tailored to our tastes. The food far exceeded our high expectations. Every dish was absolutely delicious and beautifully presented. The flavors were vibrant and you could tell the ingredients were fresh and of top quality. It was hard to decide what to order because everything sounded mouthwatering. I will continue the review A Tale of Two Franchisee's. It's a story of two friends who open up two competing sandwich shops in a small college town. The story follows the two friends as they navigate the ups and downs of owning a small business, while also dealing with the personal drama of their friendship.The characters in this book are very well-developed and relatable. The author does a great job of bringing them to life and making the reader care about them. The plot is also very engaging and keeps the reader guessing until the very end.Overall, this is a great book that I would highly recommend to anyone who enjoys a good story about friendship, business, and the pursuit of one's dreams.

I liked all the crafts in here. It was cute, lots of different things, colorful clothes, toy llamas, etc. But, I really came here for the Peruvian food. If you are looking for Papas a la Huancaina or ceviche, it isn't here. It's salads, sandwiches, empanadas, and a few other entrees like arroz tapado. This is a good place for a healthy lunch but I would not come here for dinner. After looking at the menu and nothing jumped at me, I got the empanada platter. It was.. . ok. Not that amazing. I got the beef, the chicken & cilantro and the spinach empanadas. The cilantro wasn't even that prevalent in the chicken empanada. My spinach empanada was comparable to a less flaky spanakopita. The beef empanada need more flavor! Sigh. Don't get me wrong, I wanted to like this place. I will say, the coffee was good and the server was very pleasant. This is a nice place to get some cool gifts.

I generally like Gap for cheap basics. I don't care for their sportswear nor their fancier dresses--I don't think most of it is high enough quality to be appropriate for corporate or even business causal workplaces. But for t-shirts, button-downs, shorts, jeans, leggings, and other such items for playtime or to wear at my more causal workplace, it's perfect. I pretty much bought a new summer wardrobe for under $100 by going in on a days where most items were 40% and by using a TON of saved up rewards cards that I get monthly as a cardholder. Plus Tuesdays offer an extra 10% off for cardholders. Let's just say that I saved more than I spent. What stuck out to me was that the girl--I believe her name was Georgette--who rang me up went out of her way to make sure that I got the best deal possible with all of my promotions that I could use. It took three times as long to ring up me, but she was very patient and friendly during the process. I actually filled out the store survey when I got home because I was so pleased! Bonus, you can now opt to save a tree and get emailed receipts. This will also put you on the mailing list to let you know when the sales are so if you're thrifty like I am, you can save a ton.

The last time I had lamb stew, which was delicious, rich and full of flavor. The potatoes that accompanied it were perfectly cooked and soft. The menu always has something new and exciting to try. The portions are also quite generous for the reasonable prices. My partner had fish tacos and raved about the freshness of the fish. The space is small but comfortable and has a casual neighborhood feel. One thing I really like is that they source many of their ingredients locally from small farms. The staff seems to know us by name now, which is nice. They also have a great selection of craft beers and wines. Even on busy nights the service is attentive and friendly. It's nice to support the local community like that. The desserts, like apple crisp and chocolate mousse, are worth saving room for. It's one of our favorite places to eat in the city. I'm always excited to see what new culinary discoveries we'll make on our next visit. We will definitely continue to come back regularly for dinner and drinks.

Paradise FoundI have traveled to many places around the world, but none have been as beautiful as this place. The crystal-clear water laps against the shore, revealing soft, white sand. Lush, green trees and colorful, vibrant flowers surround the area. The fresh, clean air is filled with the sound of birds singing in the trees. The sun shines brightly in the sky, which is a beautiful shade of blue.No words can truly capture the beauty of this place. It is a paradise on Earth, unlike anything I have ever seen before. I am so grateful to be here. This place is truly special.During my walk around the island, I encountered some incredible sights. I saw dolphins playing in the water, turtles swimming in the sea, and birds soaring overhead. The flowers and plants were also beautiful.I am so glad I came here. This place is truly a paradise, and I will never forget my time here.I spent some time swimming in the water, which was incredibly refreshing. The water was so clear that I could see the fish and coral reefs below me. It was breathtaking.Now, I am sitting on the beach, watching the sunset. The sky is ablaze with color as the sun slowly sinks into the ocean. The waves crash gently on the shore, creating a peaceful atmosphere.I am so glad I came to this place. It is truly a paradise, and I will never forget my time here.As I drift off to sleep, I am filled with gratitude for having experienced this paradise. Tomorrow, I will wake up and do it all again.

The thick crust that is crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. The spicy, peppery sauce that can singe your tongue. The mixture of ingredients just sliding down your chin as it bubbles out of your mouth. That being said, I really don't understand why people go to Pizzeria Uno. This chain has done to the deep dish pizza what McDonald's has done to hamburgers, Pizza Hut has done to pan pizza, Dominoes has done to hand tossed pizza, and Taco Bell has done to Tex-Mex; it has made it almost unpalatable. On our menu: nnFrench onio Chicken bitesnPizza with pepperoni, hamburger, and romano Looking past the fact that the service was not the best or the fact that the food came out undercooked and tepid in temperature, the food just was not good. Don't get me wrong, this is not the worst pizza I have ever eaten, but this chain is a perfect example of what happens when something becomes so prescribed, overhandled, and overthought that it no longer resembles the original piece of art that tasted so good. I really never want to return.

Oh, this place. An enchanting hidden gem tucked away in the heart of the city, it exudes an air of mystique and charm that instantly transports you to another world. As soon as you step through the doors, you're greeted with an atmosphere that feels like a warm embrace, leaving all your worries behind. The decor is a perfect fusion of modern sophistication and timeless elegance, creating a space that is both visually stunning and inviting. The staff members are a true testament to excellent hospitality, their genuine smiles and attentive nature making you feel like a cherished guest. The menu is a culinary masterpiece, boasting an array of innovative dishes that combine flavors with the utmost precision. Each bite sends your taste buds on a delightful journey of discovery, leaving you craving more. The attention to detail in the presentation is unparalleled, transforming each plate into a work of art. Accompanying the delectable cuisine is an extensive wine list, carefully curated to complement the flavors and elevate the dining experience. The service here is impeccable, seamlessly orchestrated by a team that anticipates your every need. From the moment you sit down, they guide you through the menu, offering insightful recommendations and ensuring a seamless flow from course to course. The pacing of the meal is impeccable, allowing you to savor each dish without feeling rushed. The ambience is simply enchanting, with soft lighting and soothing music that create an intimate setting perfect for special occasions or romantic evenings. It's a place where conversations flow effortlessly, and time seems to stand still. The attention to detail extends even to the smallest elements, such as the elegant table settings and the exquisite fragrance that fills the air.No visit to this place would be complete without indulging in their decadent desserts. The pastry chef's creations are a symphony of flavors and textures, leaving you in a state of bliss with every bite.

A local recommended Bubba's, and I decided to give it a try. The location is nothing pretentious, just your basic hole in the wall BBQ joint. They do Eastern North Carolina Style BBQ (vinegar and pepper sauce), and they have a red tomato based sauce for chicken and ribs. I had a combo of chopped pork bbq and a bbq chicken breast quarter. The chicken was incredible, and the sauce, a little on the spicy side, complimented it very well. The BBQ was just a little dry and definitely needed sauce, and the vinegar sauce complimented it very well too. I also had slaw, baked beans, and a small bowl of Brunswick stew. I wish I had ordered something other than the slaw--I'm sure there are people who like vinegar based cumin seed full slaw, but I prefer mine mayonnaise based--just personal preference. The beans were exquisite, you could taste the molasses and brown sugar in every bite. The Brunswick stew was the most different I had ever seen. It had the consistency of a cross between white chicken chili and chicken and dumplins. It was quite good and included chicken, tomatoes, lima beans, and corn. Although it was different it was some of the best I've ever tasted. If I were a local I'd definitely be a regular.

We were really excited to eat here based on all the great things Yelpers had to say. The du00e9cor was nice, but nothing really special and it seemed a little generic to me. The service was ok as well, but again, nothing special. We started with splitting the Warm Goat Salad and it was pretty good. We also ordered the Beef Carpaccio, and again it was good but nothing memorable. We also ordered the Cheese Plate but it never came to the table and we did not mention anything about it. It wasn't on our check so either the waitress didn't hear us order it or she forgot to put it in. For the entru00e9e I ordered the Filet of Beef and my wife ordered the Pork Chops which were the special the evening we went. Both were good and I really enjoyed the red beet gnocchi that came with the steak. My mother ordered the friend chicken and it was amazing.. . def. the best thing I tried. Overall I liked this place but just don't agree with most people who seem to think it's as good as it gets. The prices on the menu are very reasonable for a fine dining restaurant so that is a definite plus. I also like that they source from local farms. I don't know that I would jump at the chance to come here again.. . but wouldn't be opposed to it either.

When I lived in Tega Cay, I would say we ate here about once a week. This was our favorite place to go for pizza! It's a family-owned restaurant, and the owners are super friendly. The pizza is amazing, and they have a great selection of toppings. We always got the veggie pizza, and it was always loaded with fresh vegetables. The crust is thin and crispy, and the sauce is just the right amount of tangy. They also have a great selection of beers on tap, and the service is always top-notch.One of my favorite things about this place is the atmosphere. It's very casual and relaxed, and it's the perfect place to go for a casual meal with friends or family. The prices are very reasonable, and they offer a kids' menu. The restaurant is also very clean, and the staff is always friendly and welcoming.Overall, this is a great place to go for pizza. The food is amazing, the service is top-notch, and the atmosphere is casual and relaxed. I highly recommend it!

The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, and they are always willing to help me find what I need. I've been coming here for years and it never fails to impress me. The selection of fresh produce is unparalleled, and the prices are always reasonable. The atmosphere is lively and fun, with a good mix of locals and tourists. I love that they source their products from local farms and suppliers-it makes such a difference in the quality of the food. I've brought my friends and family here many times, and they've always had a great time. I always leave with more food than I planned to buy, but it's always worth it-the quality is that good. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for fresh, delicious food in the Strip District.

I have dined at this restaurant many times and usually enjoyed my experience. However, my most recent visit was disappointing. The service was slow, with long waits between courses. My food took much longer to arrive than those at neighboring tables. Furthermore, when it did come, it was only lukewarm rather than hot off the grill as expected. In addition, basic kitchen errors were made. My order was brought out with the wrong side dish and they quickly forgot my request for no onions on my dish. I had to remind my server multiple times. The quality of the food also seemed to have declined from my previous visits. The ingredients appeared less fresh and flavors less vibrant. This restaurant has been a favorite of mine for years, so I was hoping this was just an off day. However, the lackluster service and subpar food make me question whether the same attention to quality remains. I will give them another chance but if my next meal fails to meet the standards I'm used to, I'm afraid I will have to take my business elsewhere going forward. A consistent experience is important to keep customers returning time after time.

Be very aware. There are other options in uptown Charlotte. I suggest you use the other options. Extremely unethical business practices. They'll ticket you for not paying (paying on app or online you could be a few minutes behind), you'll return to your car, see ticket, and think.. . oh, we must have crossed paths. Do this a couple of times, and the boot will be on your car to the tune of $195. 00. If the app doesn't work, they want you to pay at another parking lot (that would be yours to figure out) or pay cash. If you call when you're paying late, the parkmobile people say, it's alright, we've got it noted. But that's not the preferred parking office. They will boot your car, charge you to park and charge you for the ticket. I've parked with them for over 4 years, and this is the customer service they deliver. The Manager also said she would not send anyone out to remove the boot, with payment, until I apologized to her and calmed down. Blatantly against the law. Yes, I have reported to BBB and the Attorney General's office. It will be my life mission to unmask these thieves.

I am so surprised that this place has been around as long as it has! This used to be one of my regular hang-out spots when I worked in Bank of America's flagship tower around 16 or 17 years ago. Back in those days, this was "the place" to go after work on weekends (and truth be told, many times during the week too, LOL! ) nnSo, recently I was roaming around the area with Tim (who used to frequent Ri-Ra with me many years ago) so we decided to stop in and have a couple of beers and some appetizers for old time's sake. Man, this place has not changed since we were last here! They even still have bartenders straight from Ireland working the bar, how cool is that? LOL! So, the only thing not cool on this visit was the fact that they had the patio closed. They told us they only open it at certain hours at night.. . that bummed me out because I really wanted to enjoy my old usual drink (Harp's Lager) outdoors in the sunlight during this visit. Oh well.. . we still enjoyed the visit. Even though there are tons of newer spots in the area, I'd probably stop in here again just for old time's sake. And if you have never been, its worth checking out!

I've been in a Menards a LOT ever since I was a young kid following my Dad around on the weekends. Now that I am an adult, I still find myself going to Menards for all of my home improvement needs. They have a wide variety of products to choose from, and the stff is always helpful and knowledgeable. O ne of the things I love about Menards is that they always have what I am looking for. Whether it is a new tool, some paint, or some bois, ich can always count on Menards to have it in stock. And if they don't have it, they can usually order it for me and have it in the storing within a few days. The manpower at Menards is also top-notch. Tehy are always friendly and helpful, and they are always willing to go the extra mile to make sure that I find what I am looking for. They are also very knowledgeable about the products that they sell, so they can always give me advice on what the best product is for my needs. In ad dition to the great selection of products and the helpful staff, Menards also has a great rewards program. Every time I shop there, I earn things that I can use towards future purchases. And if I spend a certain amount of money each year, I can get a higher tier of rewarding, which gives me even more benefits. Overall, j am very happy with Menards. They are my go-to store for all of my home improvement needs. ich would highly recommend them to anyone who is looking for a great selection of products, helpful staff, and a great rewards program. I have been shopping at Menards for yaers, and I have always had a positive experience. They are a great company, and I am glad that they are in my community. I recently remodeled my kitchen, and I got all of my supplies from Menards. They had everything I needed, and the staff was very helpful in hepling me choose the right products. The remodel turned out great, and I am very happy with the results. I also loves the Menards app.

We have been going to the Maharaja for years, to enjoy the lunch buffets, Valentines Day, birthdays etc. Tonight the food was good, but the service was an issue. To start, we could see that the staff had changed. The service took a long time, even though there were only 5 tables with customers and six wait staff. The server did not understand English well enough to properly place the order, so there was extra wine for one person. Also, the glassware and flatware were spotted, with some that needed to be sent back. The service had really changed for the worse. The server would clear one dirty plate, then wander off, return five minutes later to get another and so on. The Manager or owner really needs to train the staff. They were all working, but seemed unclear as to who was responsible for what duties. We also ordered ice cream and a special birthday dessert, while very tasty - the service was vey slow, at least 10 minutes from the time the ice cream was ordered to served. What really put us over the top was when they refused to accept their own $50 Gift Certificate that they sold to me in June towards the $160 bill (not including tip). It had only been approximately 6 weeks. Apparently, this location has been sold. The old owners still own the location on Odana Rd (same name), but not this one. Therefore, they would not accept their own gift certificate and told us, we could use it at Odana Rd. nInterestingly, they still kept the Best of Madison sign on the door for the old ownership, they will need to take this down. Again, we were surprised at the business decision about their own gift certificate.

We have been here a number of times over the past two years and recently moved back to the Charlotte environs. So, on a windy, rainy night my wife and I came back. I had lunched there a few weeks ago, so wanted my wife to experience CW again and get her opinion. The lunch was very average, at best. Beautiful decor and atmosphere. Giant illuminated tropical fish tank and a snappy-dressed manager/owner tending the front desk. Very authentic as a lot of ethnic Chinese patronize the Great Wall. And the wait staff speaks English as I speak Spanish: like immigrants. Can be hard understand and though they know the menu by rote, asking for exceptions, like no baby corn or mushrooms, leaves one wondering if the message was received as sent. Portions are large, but the accompanying rice is a niggardly amount. Probably a cost-saving measure, but a bit too frugal as the sign of a good host in my Asian experiences is that there is a lot of rice, ditto with tortillas in the Mexican culture. We both ordered "spicy" and I asked for extra spicy. If you like spice, you need to make your case as they are cautious in burning you out. Brown sauces reign, with a few dishes coming with lighter white sauces. I mention this because one has to have a very discerning palate to distinguish one brown sauced dish from another. Am certain that cooking to local tastes has a play in this, but than again, there are a lot of Chinese eating here. The menu has both chef specials and more typical, America-wise, dished listed by category. Not many noodle choices. GW is a nice place for a date or even a romantic occasion. You will get plenty to eat, but don't expect your socks to be knocked off by their average, similar tasting dishes. Very average, at best.

The staff is very friendly and welcoming and the food is delicious. The portions are large and the prices are reasonable. I would recommend the chicken parmesan and the fettuccine alfredo. The service is quick and attentive and the staff is always happy to make recommendations or answer questions. The menu has a wide variety of choices and something for everyone. The atmosphere is casual and relaxed, so it's a great place to go with friends or family. I would definitely recommend this restaurant for a great Italian meal. The pizza is also very good, with a thin crust and fresh toppings.

Nice to be able to pick your fish and style of cooking. I had a trio of Jamaican jerk tilapia, salmon, and scallops. All good but too much sauce on scallops. Husband had surf n turf special. Snow crab legs tasty but smaller portion than I expected. Glad they had raw oysters, but no idea where they were from. For $2. 50 each you'd think they'd say. Waitstaff friendly but inexperienced when it came to wine. We taught two of them how to open a champagne bottle. Nice time out, but two gripes.. . #1 Used my phones flashlight to see if there was an outlet on the floor. Felt like an archaeologist finding old remains of dinners gone by. Crumbs, napkins wedged between booth and wall, gum, dirt. For the price I would expect a cleaner place. #2 our waiter kept saying Thank you. After every single sentence, even when it wasn't appropriate. Silly gripe, right? But it was way over the top and felt more like, Can I have a tip? Can I have a tip?

If you don't know the pizza in an area, look for the dirtiest, rundown place you can find, and you'll find the best pizza in town. The thinking behind that is, if the place looks that bad but is still in busines, then there is a reason they're still in business. And in my experiences, it's almost always true. Fiori's is a dive (in a good way)- the inside looks like it was put together in the '70's, and the staff isn't always the friendliest. Forget about parking- there are three spots on the side of the building and perilious street parking on the hill. The later in the evening you go, the busier the dining room. My suggestion is don't eat here- you're only asking for drama. But then you get home with that steaming pie, and all the parking nonsense, questionable customer service, and wait in line vanishes as you're enveloped in cheesey, meaty goodness. The pizzas are big, there are a ton of toppings, and the sauce is sweet in a good way. My suggestion is try their white pizza, which I think rivals the ones I've had in New York. We can see the reflection of Mount Fuji in the water. This is a real magic experience. After taking the boat, we had lunch in a local restaurant and tried some delicious Japanese food, including sushi and tempura. Then we returned to Tokyo and were very grateful to the unforgettable experience we just spent. We strongly recommend that you go to Mount Fuji in Japan.

Arrived at 3: 30pm but the room wasn't even ready despite check in being 3pm. Bed in room wasn't a queen size it was a full size so this is false advertising. I know this for a fact as we just changed from a full size to a queen size bed at home so we are aware of the size difference. In addition the mattress was very soft and the bed frame felt like it might fall apart any time - so we didn't have a great night's sleep which made the 7 hour drive home tough! A/C unit on wall glowed bright blue all through the night, there was no way to turn off the glow without turning off the A/C which would have made the room too hot. Room itself was small but nice enough, I appreciate this is a downtown hotel so you don't get value for money at those type of hotels, but still we personally cannot recommend it.

It was a bit of a hike, but as soon as we stepped in, we knew it was worth the effort. I got my math degree here, and I feel my educations was average at best, so why did I pay twice as much? They don't have rigorous science programs here, and even their beloved pharmacy school seems to be self-serving to artificially inflate graduation rates. nn The money does not go to the professors -- many of them are part-time adjuncts who do not earn much, so despite small classrooms, they are burnt out and don't have time to devote to their lesson plans. I do not support this unethical business practice. The campus itself is garbage, there were cockroaches all through the dorms and food quarters when I was there 2006-2010, the dorms are old and falling apart, there is no campus life to speak of. In general there is just really no reason to come here and pay twice as much money for this garbage school. I left this school 60k in debt and could have gotten the same or better education elsewhere - I DO NOT recommend this school.

Upstream is one of 3 main restaurants in Phillips Place (PF Chang's & The Palm are the other two). Our party of four decided to dine at Upstream on a weekday evening hoping to avoid some of the busy weekend crowds. We were warmly greeted at the entrance by the host and showed to our table, a lovely booth tucked away in a cozy corner, giving our meal a intimate ambiance. The restaurant had a lively yet relaxing atmosphere, with just the right volume of quiet jazz playing over the speakers, creating a harmonious symphony to enjoy our food to. Our server came over with menus and was friendly and knowledgeable, giving us recommendations based on our tastes. I opted for the seafood paella, knowing Upstream has a deft hand with rice dishes, while my partner chose the salmon pasta hoping for a light yet fulfilling meal. The appetizers we started with did not disappoint - the grilled calamari had tender squid tubes and a delightful lemon caper aioli for dipping. A shared plate of bruschetta featured a beautifully composed arrangement of vine ripe tomatoes, basil and bocconcini on a delicate toast point. Our meals arrived with perfect timing as our plates were cleared. I was amazed at the flavor and texture of each pearled grain of rice in the paella, infused with the savory seafood and spices. My dining companion raved equally about their perfectly cooked salmon, moist and flavorful, served over a bed of linguini in a light yet complex cream sauce. For dessert, we split a trio of mini treats - a chocolate mousse cup, cheesecake bite and creme brulee that satisfied our sweet cravings without leaving us too full. The bill was reasonable for the quality of ingredients and service. We left feeling content and would love to return to Upstream again for another relaxing and delicious meal.

It was a crisp autumn day, and the leaves were just starting to change colors. I had been meaning to come back to Market Square for a while now, and I was glad that I finally had the chance. As I walked in, I was immediately struck by the lively atmosphere. The square was bustling with people, and there was a sense of excitement in the air.I looked around and saw all sorts of vendors selling their wares. There were farmers selling fresh produce, artisans selling handmade crafts, and even a few food trucks serving up delicious treats. I couldn't wait to explore and see what else Market Square had to offer.I started by visiting some of the local farmers' stalls. They had a wide variety of fruits and vegetables, including some that I had never seen before. I was impressed by the quality and freshness of their produce, and I ended up buying a few things to take home.Next, I wandered over to the artisans' section. There were so many talented people selling their handmade goods, from jewelry to candles to woodcarvings. I was particularly drawn to a stall selling beautiful hand-painted pottery. The artist told me that she had learned her craft from her grandmother, and that each piece was a labor of love. I ended up buying a beautiful vase that I plan to use as a centerpiece for my dining room table.After a while, I decided to take a break and grab some lunch from one of the food trucks. I chose a delicious-looking taco truck, and I was not disappointed. The tacos were amazing, with flavorful meats and fresh vegetables. I sat down at a nearby bench to enjoy my meal and watch the people passing by.As I sat there, I noticed a group of musicians setting up their instruments. They started playing a lively tune, and soon, people were dancing in the square. It was such a joyful scene, and I couldn't help but join in. I danced with strangers and laughed with the musicians, feeling grateful for this chance to experience the beauty of Market Square.

I have been sitting here looking at the poor quality of my shellac manicure, and I just had to write. I mean, seriously, it's like I gave a kindergartener a bottle of nail polish and let them go wild on my nails. The polish is all uneven and streaky, and there are even smudges all over the place. It's like they didn't even bother to take their time and do it properly. And don't get me started on the color! I asked for a nice, elegant red, but what I got is more like a garish neon nightmare. It's so far off from what I wanted, it's not even funny.But it's not just the manicure that's got me fuming. The service at this place was downright terrible. The staff acted like they couldn't care less about my presence. No warm greetings or friendly smiles here. They were too busy chatting amongst themselves to pay any attention to the customers. It felt like I was interrupting their little social gathering. And when I finally got someone's attention, they seemed annoyed that I dared to ask for a touch-up on my nails. Can you believe that?And let's talk about the hygiene, or rather the lack thereof. When I walked in, I couldn't help but notice how dirty and disorganized everything was. It's like they think they can get away with ripping people off just because they're located in a trendy neighborhood. Well, newsflash, folks! Good service and quality should be a given no matter where you are.Overall, my experience at this nail salon has left me incredibly disappointed.

I've had my share of disappointing dining experiences, and I'm not afraid to speak my mind. I've been known to leave scathing reviews for restaurants that can't seem to get the simplest things right. After all, isn't that what Yelp is for? Overcooked steak? Check. Mushy, flavorless vegetables? Check. And don't even get me started on the service. If a server can't be bothered to check on me more than once during a meal, I'm not afraid to leave a negative review. But I'm not all bad. On the rare occasions when a restaurant gets everything right, I've also left glowing reviews. A perfectly cooked steak? Check. Fresh, flavorful vegetables? Absolutely. Excellent service? Yes, please. I know some people might find my reviews harsh, but I call it like I see it. And friendly, attentive service? That's the icing on the cake. So take my reviews with a grain of salt. Or maybe a whole shaker full. And if a restaurant can't handle a little criticism, maybe it shouldn't be in the business. But know that I'm always coming from a place of honesty and a desire for a truly great dining experience. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a date with a plate of buffalo wings. I hope they live up to my standards.

I've never encountered such a frustrating experience at a restaurant before. We had the "tenders" appetizer, with both the vegan BBQ sauce and the vegan wasabi mayonnaise. We much preferred the BBQ sauce, but I am guessing if you are a wasabi fan, you would like that too. We all thought it was wonderful. On the advice of the server, I had the peanut wrap. It was spicy, heavily peanut-flavored, but full of yummy veggies. I also had a side of chili, that I liked a lot (and I make my own veggie chili at home, so I am picky). Ben had the apple panini with the gazpacho side. We both thought the gazpacho was kind of plain (it got better by adding chili! ), but the apple panini (with "seisage", cheese, etc. ) was very good. Finally, Panchu had the coconut burrito, which was huge, but he ate the whole thing, and was very happy. We all split a vegan cinnamon roll for dessert, and I really wish I had been able to get my own! Some complained about the wait; I think this place fits well with the "slow food movement. " If you want fast food, go to McDonald's. So, based on one observation, I gave it five stars. YMMV.

Which is fine, as some of their lots have reasonable rates. My reason for the low review comes from the user experience side of thing, and their overall customer service. I haven't been to a Morton's in years, but was happy to be going back for a business dinner. I thought the service was exceptional, but the food was mediocre at best. The filet that I ordered was cooked to perfection, a nice portion, and tender as can be -- but absolutely no taste. Nothing. Nothing discernible at all. I can tell you that with all of the above and no taste, it was all for naught. Unrelated and not the blame of the server, of course -- again, service was great -- one of my colleagues found a piece of hard plastic in his veal chop. He thought the veal chop was great, but wasn't real excited about the plastic in his dish, which the server promptly removed from the bill. I brought another colleague's salmon home with me and heated it up the next day. Oddly enough, a beautiful piece of salmon -- absolutely NO flavor. Very strange experience. I doubt I'll ever return.
