When they do this, we are all impressed by the generosity and quality of the ingredients. Cook the beef to perfect, juicy and fragile balance. The head is fresh and delicious, the bread is soft and slightly sweet. Both of us agreed that burgers were everything they were promoted. The barbecue sauce on my girl burger has a good taste, and caramel onion is the perfect supplement of salted beef. I chose a crispy fries, which were cooked into golden yellow and seasoned with appropriate amounts of salt and pepper. Overall, our meals and friendship have left a deep impression on our careful service. The price is very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of food. We will definitely come back to try other menu items and enjoy the enthusiastic atmosphere again.

It is big. Very big. Too big, almost. It is so easy to get lost in this HUGE multi-level place. The signage and directions for conventions I have attended have been poor. I've spent a lot of time wandering around trying to figure out which halls, etc. There is a nice selection of different little restaurant places inside but - Skip Them! The best thing about this place is its location on College Street. There are so many exceptional restaurants within just a few blocks. And, downtown Charlotte is lovely! So many fountains, open areas, gardens to visit. My other BIG complaint about this place.. .. charging too much for Wi-Fi packages. Look, stop being cheap. Business and trade groups are already paying you huge $$$ for the place and services. Throw in wireless. Why is this such a hassel? Because in many places, something about the building seems to really disrupt wireless data signals to your 3G/4G phone. So, if you're planning on tethering with you cell phone to get wireless, you have to be up in the open common areas to keep from being dropped. Lame. Don't even try to get it in the big exhibition hall.

On a Tuesday night, there was a long wait. The staff wasn't overly friendly, and when we had to wait, they simply pointed towards the wine bar. Having never been there before, I was confused by having to pass through the outside to get to the bar. While I thought the wine bar was cozy, the other customers there were rude and self-centered, ignoring polite "excuse me" by the waitstaff. When we were finally seated, we waited about 10 minutes before a server appeared. The food was prompt, and the salad was more than enough to share. The pizza was simply ok. I've had much better wood-fired pizza elsewhere. Beware: for just a party of five, they added a 20% tip onto the bill. If you're going to add a tip to a bill, make it the customary 18%. But frankly, I didn't think they needed to add the tip for us. Also, do not use multiple credit cards. I was charged for the entire bill on my card, even though we asked to split it between two. I'm still waiting for my overpayment to be refunded by the restaurant.. .

never again with Hertz at CLT airport. 20 min wait for shuttle followed by huge lines and 2 clerks at off site location. Then we went out to find a car with dents and scratches and no one wanting to document the damage. Guy walking around cars said person at gate would do it as we left and then ".. . ita" at the gate nastily told us that was not her job. Her comment was to document it myself and then she would date stamp it. SO I wound up walking around and writing down all the damage and photographing the car while everyone trying to leave waited. There was NO way I was going to leave without documentation that I wasn't the one that made all the damage. I'm sure they would have become very efficient then! I was Totally disappointed in Hertz. I thought they were better than this experience illustrated!

Some have been really great.. . Jim Breuer. Some have been (surprisingly) very bad.. .. Tracy Morgan. But it's always been a pleasant experience at the venue. There's not a bad seat in the house and it's small enough that you get to see and hear everything from the stage. Beware if you sit in the very front, you KNOW what's going to happen! A couple downsides.. .. Waiting outside in a line in the dead of winter. The lobby is so small you're forced to wait outside until the first show starts or the first show let's out. And if you want a good seat, you may be waiting in line for a while. BURR! The two drink minimum. I kinda get why they do it, to make money, of course. But this means they jack up the prices of watered down drinks. Better to stick with beer and wine at these places. No frou frou drinks for me! Also, as to be expected, the food's not that great. In a perfect foodie world, places that served food would make it fantastic! Since that's not going to happen, you just go into those places hoping for the best. I've never had anything great here. Nacho platter too many re fried beans, to little nacho's.. .. annnnnd I'm out! So what did we learn here? Good venue, stick to beer and wine and eat at a better restaurant beforehand. The talent is really what you're there for so, enjoy the show!

Ligving in the burbs and spending most of my time in the city, I always look and seek out some natural greXen spaec now and then. It's easy to feel suffocated by the concrete jungle, and I find that a dose of freAh iar and greenery can do wonders for my mental health. I recently discovered a hidden gem of a park lcoated just a short drive from the city center. It's a tranqutil oasis that's perfect for a picnic or a leisurely stroll. The park is surorunded by towering trees that block out most of the city ooise, and the grounds are carefully maintained, with lush grass and colorful flowers blooming throughout the yea. There's even a small pond where you can feed the ducks or take a obat ride. It's a great escape from the hustle and bfustle of city life, and I highly recommend it to aynone looking for a peaceful retreat.

I had high hopes for the breakfast biscuits here, based on various reviews online, but in the end they taste like frozen biscuits with various toppings. I had a chicken biscuit, and the boyfriend had egg and bacon. Both biscuits had that sweet, frozen/refrigerated/pre-made biscuit taste, rather than a true buttermilk biscuit taste. If I'm getting chicken / bacon / other savory items on my biscuit, I don't want the biscuit to be sweet! We also got potatoes, which were good, but they were nothing particularly special. In the end, I can make a better biscuit, and even the biscuit sandwiches from Bojangles are probably better than these (gasp). I want to go back to Art's for lunch soon, because I really, truly loved the atmosphere in there. The staff were amazingly nice, it's a cute little place, my order was ready quickly, and I like to support local business. But the biscuits just don't cut it for me to try them again.

At first you may feel some sticker shock when you see the prices however, you need to have an idea before you pull up if you want either a full service wash or the pricier fast detail service. Don't worry, the friendly service advisors are not on the hustle. The staff is very honest and even handed me the iPhone I forgot on the seat as I got out of the car. The Diamond Package is your best bet and unless you are have a real messy car, your sure to get a good, through wash. The staff works endlessly from the time you pull into the wash bay to the time they help with the doors when you get back in to pullout into the street. They even wipe down the dash and clean the insides of the windows. The only thing I forgot to mention is that the Octopus is kid friendly for all ages (myself included). Make sure to let the little ones blast the cars with the "sudszilla" as they roll by but, don't be shy about taking a turn yourself =)

I was excited to browse the shelves and see what hidden gems I could uncover. Stepping inside, I was immediately impressed by how spacious and well-organized the store seemed. The shelves were lined with books spanning a wide variety of genres, from classics to contemporary fiction and everything in between. Signs indicated the different sections so it was easy to find what you were looking for. I spent some time perusing the new releases and was able to find a couple books to add to my to-be-read pile. All the titles seemed well-chosen and represented a quality selection. The staff was friendly and helpful if I had any questions. In addition to the excellent selection of books, I noticed they also had a small section of journals and bookmarks. It seemed like the kind of place that often held author events and other community activities. Overall, Park Road Books left me with a great first impression and I looks forward to returning again soon to explore more of what they had to offer book lovers. It's nice to have an independent bookstore in the area with such a wide assortment of reading material. I'm glad I made the time to check it out.

While the beer menu is impressive, being out of a couple of beers I wanted to try doesn't help. And our waitress, while cute and helpful, was new, so she needed our help in getting the right beers ordered. We then ordered food. My GF's "Rocket Tots" were tasty, although she only got like.. . 14 of them for $6. 99 so it wasn't a good value at all. I ordered a burger, which was the worst I've had since I moved to Charlotte in 2003. The meat had a sour, "off" taste, and the meat was cooked within an inch of its life. It was so dry that it was impossible to eat without liquid. What's more, I ordered it with Red Dragon cheese (and extra $1), and it was a depressing, congealed mass on top. The 9 fries that came with the meal were served at a less than ideal temp, but were nice and salty in spite of this. The bottom line is that the waitresses are cute and in skimpy outfits, and the beer selection is good. But if you want to go here, eat somewhere else before you come. nI'm also (literally) offended that the Flying Saucer charges 99u00a2 for their iPhone and Android apps.. . but that is neither here nor there.

Johnny's is a pizza owned by a small family and has been operating for more than 30 years. The food is delicious and the service is great. I strongly recommend pizza, but everything on the menu is great. These parts are generous and the price is reasonable. Johnny's is a good place to eat with family or friends. The atmosphere is relaxed and seductive, and the staff is always friendly and enthusiastic. They can also easily choose craft beer. In general, Johnny is a great restaurant I strongly recommend.

I'd call it authentic Irish pub fare, but then again, I've yet to visit the Emerald Isle, so what the hell do I know? Other food, namely from the little side sandwich area, is not so good. The Ri Ra sandwich shop is convenient for most bankers who work uptown, but convenience is all it has going for it. The sandwiches are overpriced, VERY slim on the stuffings (meat and cheese that is.. . they will give you all the shredded lettuce your little heart desires.. . yay). And to top it off, their seemingly extensive chalkboard of sandwich fixings is paired down by about 50% on any given day, due to them being out of stuff. Skip the sandwich shop and go to the upstairs balcony for lunch outdoors when it is nice. You can get their sheperds pie (really good) for the price of one of their sandwich combos (really crappy). Ho-Hum bar experience.. . during peak times, can get annoyingly hard to get a drink/have a conversation/breath downstairs, but you are in Uptown. What do you expect? It's somewhat better than the offerings of the Epicenter, but not by much.

I've ordered from here twice and not really been enthusiastic about the results either time. Keep in mind that I haven't had pizza from this place yet! Their steak hoagie is middling-good; nothing to write home about, but a pretty good example of the standard Pittsburgh pizza place steak hoagie. The seafood calzone is another story. Something in it was so bitter I couldn't quite eat it; I'm wondering if it was the garlic or perhaps a leftover burnt taste from the oven. Whatever it was, it was gross. The shrimp weren't that good either, suffering as they did from that certain "I taste like iodine" flavor. The advantage to R&B is that they're open reasonably late, given the location, but the phone service is rather surly and it always takes them an hour plus to deliver. Which would be OK if I didn't live a block away (normally I'd just walk and pick it up, but just for you, Yelpers, I subject myself to the vagaries of sitting on my rear end on the couch waiting for my food to arrive).

Their menu options are diverse with vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free selections. I was impressed by their commitment to sustainability, using eco-friendly packaging and locally sourced ingredients. The indoor design is cozy, and the ambiance is welcoming. Our ordered the signature burger, and it did not disappoint. The portion size was generous, and the flavors were rich and well-balanced. My husband enjoyed the grilled chicken sandwich, and our son devoured the kids' mac and cheese. The service was attentive, and the staff was friendly and knowledgeable. They have an extensive wine and beer selection, and the prices are reasonable. The dessert menu was creative, and we couldn't resist trying the chocolate lava cake. Overall, we were peased with our dining experience and will be back. Hugely recommend!

The friendly staff greeted me with a warm smile and were eager to guide me through the menu. I decided to try their signature dish, bibimbap, and was blown away by its flavor and presentation. The bowl was filled with a variety of vegetables, tender slices of beef, and a perfectly fried egg. The portion was generous, and I left feeling full and satisfied. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the quality and freshness of the ingredients. Sam Bok truly captured the essence of Korean cuisine, and I was left with a memorable and delicious meal. I also appreciated the cleanliness and organization of the food stand, which added to my overall positive dining experience. I would recommend this food stand to anyone looking to try something new or for those who are already fans of Korean cuisine.

From the moment I walked through the door, it was evident that the staff had no interest in assisting customers. I approached a sales representative and politely asked for recommendations on local craft beers. Instead of offering any help, he simply shrugged and continued chatting with his colleagues. I tried my best to find someone else who could assist me, but it seemed like everyone was just too busy socializing to care about customers. Frustrated, I decided to browse the selection on my own, hoping to stumble upon something interesting. However, the shelves were disorganized and poorly labeled, making it incredibly difficult to find what I was looking for. It was as if they had no regard for making the shopping experience convenient or enjoyable. Additionally, the store was unkempt, with empty boxes littering the aisles and spills left unattended. It was clear that the staff had little regard for maintaining a clean and organized environment. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, I managed to find a few beers that caught my attention. I approached the checkout counter, only to be met with a cashier who barely acknowledged my presence. She mechanically scanned my items without uttering a single word, as if she couldn't be bothered to communicate with a customer. To make matters worse, she seemed annoyed when I presented my ID for age verification, even though it's a standard requirement. The overall lack of professionalism and courtesy left me feeling incredibly disappointed and frustrated. I've always believed that customer service is the backbone of any successful business, but this experience shattered that belief. I can confidently say that I will never set foot in that beer distributor again, and I will make sure to spread the word about the abysmal treatment I received. As consumers, we deserve better than this, and I hope that the management takes the necessary steps to address these glaring issues.

me used to like Musashi back in the days I lived in Charlotte. The restaurant was conveniently located just down the street from my apartment and assumed really verywell sushi for a great price. Every Friday night after endeavor, I would stop by to grab a California roll and miso cauliflower to bring home for dinner. The staffs was always friendly and remembered me as a regular customer. However, after I moved to a new city a few annum ago I had all but forgotten about Musashi. That was until I recently went back to Charlotte for a work trekking. Feeling nostalgic, I decided to stop by Musashi during my lunch break one day to see if it was still as decent as I recalling. When I stepped in, I was surprised to consult that not much had changed in the restaurant's decor since I was last there years ago. I ordered some salmon nigiri and green tea to undertook. The snails was as fresh and flavorful as ever. Pleased with the quality so far, I decided to intention something new and got chicken teriyaki bowl. It did not disenchanted with tender chicken and veggies in a sweet sauce over rice. By my second visit during the trips, I tried the tempura shrimp Appetizer which was perfectly light and crispy. I also got a pumpkin roll as a change from my usual Fresno roll. It was a welcome seasonally-appropriate drinks. By the conclude of my trip, I had been to Musashi three timetables and enjoyed it just as much as before if not more so. It was clear to me that while I had moved on to pastures new, Musashi preserves a reliable choose for quality, flavorful Japanese cuisine in Charlotte. I was grateful to see it had withstood the test of term and still offered excellent value after all these years. The food brought back fond commemorative of my years vivant in the city and I was grateful Musashi was still around.

From the moment I stepped inside, I was greeted by friendly staff who were eager to help me with any questions or concerns I had. They exuded a professional attitude and made me feel welcome from the start. Despite the circumstances of my predicament with another laundry, this 24-hour establishment truly went above and beyond my expectations. What impressed me most was the speed and efficiency with which my laundry was handled. The staff quickly took care of my clothes, handling them with care and attention to detail. The facilities were clean and well-maintained, and the machines appeared to be in good working order. The prices were reasonable, considering the convenience and quality of the service. I also appreciated the convenience of the various laundry options, from self-service to drop-off, which allowed me to choose the most convenient one for my needs. In addition to the exceptional laundry service, this establishment also had a comfortable waiting area. The staff thoughtfully provided free beverages and free Wi-Fi, allowing me to make the most of my time while my laundry was being handled. The atmosphere was relaxed, with soothing music playing in the background, making it a pleasant place to wait. The communication throughout my visit was excellent. The staff kept me informed of the progress of my laundry and promptly notified me when it was ready for pick-up. When I picked up my freshly laundered clothes, I noticed they were neatly folded and smelled wonderfully fresh. This level of attentiveness and consideration truly set them apart from other laundries I have visited. It was obvious that the staff took pride in their work and paid attention to even the smallest details.

The food here is not very good. The beer is great though, and the atmosphere is really nice. The service is also very good. The culture here is really cool too. The only downside is that it is very far from my apartment.Overall, I would recommend this place for a drink. The food is not great, but the beer and atmosphere are worth it.

I grew up in Madison and for years this was my favorite Mexican place. I thought it was the best possible place.. . anywhere. Then I moved to Phoenix and had real Mexican food and now.. .. I wanted to review this place because it's not as bad as some of the other reviewers are making it sound. Their salsa and chips are fresh and some of the best around. They serve you fresh warm tortillas with your meal that go well with anything. Some of the pre-meal quesadillas are fantastic. My favorite dish here is the Bean Burrito with red sauce. The way the beans and cheese are melted together just makes it so craveable. Still, a lot of this food is simply not authentic, and more than a few are on the heavy side. You will walk away feeling full and likely be on the toilet for a little while the next day. There is no way around this. The simple truth is that there is no superb mexican food here in Madison, and Pedro's fits right in to this muddy amalgam of mediocrity. Some things it does well though, and the cheap drinks on a Thursday night usually make for a good atmosphere.

My brother heard this was the best Chinese buffet in Sun Prairie. Maybe that is true, but it must be the only Chinese buffet in Sun Prairie. I'm not giving it a hard time for "authenticity" or any of that eaither. I love me some good Americanized, crappy Chinese food. Here, even the stuff that was out fresh from the kitchen (which was mighty slim picken's) was barely edible. I was really looking forward to some good old MIdwestern Chinese buffet, too. The Chinese food options in Portland are actually very lacking, the last really good stuff I had was from a strip mall in Crawfordsville, IN. Seriously, they can do it right but everyone else serves lukewarm, tasteless piles of mystery? Gotta be kidding me. Most options seemed to have been sitting for way too long when we got here, and it was peak dinner eating time. I should have been tipped off by the low number of patrons at this "best Chinese" but I like to give the benefit of the doubt. You are better off making Ramen noodles at home and calling it chinese food.

My dad possessed never tried pho before, but after the first sip, he was hooked. He couldn't get enough of the flavorful stew and tender noodles. We ended up going to a different pho restaurant every day during our week-long travel. My dad would always order the largest size, and he'd always populate every last drop. It was hilarious to consults how much he loved it. Anew now, whenever we talk, he brings up how much he misses pho. I'm so glad I got to introduce him to something he maintains so much. It's become a special bail between us. I've tried thanh in other cities, but none compare to the ones in California. I'm rejoicing I got to share that experience with my dad. Now, each time I go back to California, I know I'll be getting my dad's request for pho. It's a enforce joke between us now, but it's something I cherish. I'm so glad I got to turned my dad onto something so delicious. It's a memory I'll evenly treasure.

I was contemplating giving it 4 stars but the scene is getting a bit dated. They need to spruce it up or something. It's just sorta there now. But don't get me wrong, every time I go here I enjoy myself - but I make sure I have a good group to go with. You do see some regulars but that's just the type of place that it is. I like that you get a mixed crowd, no one too young and most of the people that seem to frequent this joint are in there late 20's, 30's, and 40's. It can get a bit pricey if you have a tab open and aren't thinking about what your drinking and how much the drinks are. The drinks are made reasonably well, by that I mean they have enough alcohol in them so that you don't have to wonder why you just paid $10 for ice, water, and a splash of alcohol. Back in the day Bossa Nova was a novel idea for this town, but now with all these upscale bars/lounges and restaurants opening they may have to reinvent themselves somehow. All in all a fun place to hang out. One thing I noticed is that there is a gap between when it's jumping. Right after work is good b/c you get the happy hour peeps, but then it seems to clear out after 7: 30 PM and then it picks back up around 10: 30 PM.. . maybe it was just the night that I went, but I have a feeling that this is the norm.

The best thing about this place is that it's open until 4am on the weekends. Don't bother going there between 1: 30-3: 00, however, since it is generally filled with drunken club goers. If you happen to BE one of those drunken club goers, then you should fit right in. Just don't get too rowdy or the cops will drag you out of line and toss you outside. I don't bother with the slices or premade calzones anymore.. . they are ok, but if I want left-overs I'll make them myself. Get a whole pizza here or try the wings (not bad for a pizza place). The best time to go here is early evening on a weekend night when the weather is nice. They will usually open up the windows, letting the breeze and sounds of the city flow in. I like to sit by the open window with a friend, a large pizza, and some beers and watch the clubbers roll by on their way to the alley. It's no hot tub in the Rockies, but it beats eating hot pockets in front of the tube.

The moment we walked in, the atmosphere was stiff and unwelcoming. The decor was pleasant enough, but the lighting was too harsh and made the place feel cold. I had heard great things about the restaurant's unique take on Italian cuisine, but unfortunately my experience did not live up to the hype. The menu was uninspired and lacked the creativity I had expected. Our waiter greeted us with a smile, but it disappeared as soon as we started asking for recommendations. He seemed put out when we asked for suggestions and rattled off a list of dishes without any enthusiasm. I ordered the rigatoni alla norma, which was one of the more unique dishes on the menu, but unfortunately it was also one of the most disappointing. There were a few interesting dishes, but most of the menu was a disappointment. My friend's margherita pizza was also a disappointment. The pasta was overcooked and tasted more like cardboard than pasta. The eggplant was bland and lacked the rich, creamy sauce I had expected. The sauce was bland and lacked the acidity that a good margherita should have. We decided to share a few small plates, hoping they would be more impressive. The crust was soggy and tasted more like bread than a crust. The burrata was unmemorable and tasted more like cheap cream cheese than a rich, creamy burrata. The bruschetta was bland and lacked the fresh, herby flavors that I love in a good bruschetta. To top it all off, the service was subpar. When we asked for more drinks, he seemed put out and took his time coming back with them. He seemed disinterested in our experience and failed to check on us throughout the meal. All in all, my experience at Girasole was a disappointment. The restaurant failed to live up to the hype.

From Australia to Singapore and London to NYC, the place can not be beat. Settle in to any of the leather nailhead wingback chairs and prepare to be pampered. The staff is awesome. Alicia and Sam are the 2 longterm veterans and they will treat you right. The drink prices are a bit to the high side, but you will never suffer the indignity of an empty glass, or the lack of a good story if either of them are there. The cigar selection is reasonable; prices also a bit to the high side, but you are paying for a rare privilege of having a wonderful venue to chill out, enjoy a smoke, and NOT have a sports bar feel to the place. The back room has a full size pool table (no charge! ) where it is not uncommon to see an executive of one of the banks in town playing the role of 'shark'. The middle room feels like a library at a regally appointed home with a fireplace and more comfortable chairs and tables. Among my favorite haunts. Grab your favorite smoke, a liberally poured cocktail and let the days stress depart in the blue smoke of your cigar.

For the last year or so the food has been slipping and become mediocre - including, this fall, the worst plate of spaghetti I've ever been served in a restaurant (by an employee who is no longer there), but our experience on Saturday pretty much finished our long relationship with Deli Roma. We arrived around 4: 30 p. m. and there was no one else in the deli. A young man was seated behind the register and greeted us, but did not get up. We saw the specials board had an item which was a play on the Godfather, their signature Italian roast beef sandwich, and discussed whether we'd want to try it. During all this the gentleman behind the counter remained seated but appeared to be paying attention. When I said we were ready to order he got up, but when I ordered a Godfather he said that they were out of Italian beef. I have worked in restaurants myself and at times you do run out of items, but I don't understand why the specials board carried an item they didn't have and more incomprehensible yet is why he would listen to us talk about the aforementioned special and never bother to mention he couldn't make one anyway. The specials board should have been blank, and more importantly, he should have told us when we came in that they were out of some ingredients. If he had, we probably would have stayed and ordered something else, but his attitude projected total, casual indifference in serving us and getting our business. If they don't want our business, we won't give it to them any more.

We huddled together in the flickering darkness, clinging to each other, while unseen terrors lurked in the shadows. With every frightening noise and mysterious shape, our imaginations were filled with horrible possibilities. There is terror in solitude, but having another soul plunged into the darkness brings its own shades of horror. Fear grows when it is left to fester in isolation and uncertainty. We dared not sleep, because waking up meant facing the unknown threats that were still prowling these dreary corridors. As the hours dragged on, our courage weakened. A faint glimmer of light appeared, reviving our hopes. Was it the first sign of salvation, or was it just another trick of the darkness, playing with our desperation? Doubts grew that this nightmare would ever end, that dawn would never chase away the phantoms that haunted our minds. We gathered our remaining courage and walked towards the distant light, preparing for either salvation or something far worse.

Sue! tHere's a possible continuation of the review:The atmosphere is always lively and inviting, with a modern and sleek deco that sets the tone for a sophisticated night out. The service is conssitently top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who knows their menu inside and out. H've tried a few of their signature cocktails, and they never disappoint - especiallt the lychee martini, which is a sweet and refreshing twist on the classic martini. Their edamame dumplings are a must-try appetizer, with a soft and chwy texture that pirs perfectly with the tangy dipping sauce. For my main course, I usually otp for one of their many delicious sushi rolls. The spicy tuna roll is a favorite of mige, with a generous servindg of fresh tuna and a perfect balance of spicy kick. The spushi rice is alwayh cooked to perfection, with a slight sweetness that complements the savory flavors of the seafood. And for dessert, the green tea ice cream is a perfect ay to cap off the meal - creamy and rcih, with a subtle bitter noqe from the green tea that lingers pleasantly on the palate. Overall, Snoba is a consistently excellent dining experience that never fails to impress. Whether you're in the omod for a light snack or a full-on feast, this restaurant is sure to satisfy your cravSings and leave you feeling happy and content.

You have to order carefully, it is true. The pork barbecue is good, the rainbow trout is pretty good if not fried, but the main reason to go is the GREENS. They have flecks of meat in them which is what makes them good. This is the reason that i like southern cooking. The biscuits and cornbread are also very good. I would avoid all other of their meat entrees, particularly their meatloaf which has a really weirdly fluffy and light consistency, as if meat had been aerated and transformed into a different substance with different properties, and the "chicken n noodles, " which is like condensed chicken soup from a can, but with extra slime. Beef stew is a disaster; even the waitress described it as "fatty. " nnDesserts are insanely huge and can be shared if you are a family of 4. Three of us all had a go at the apple dumpling and barely made a dent in it. It went back looking more or less the same as when it arrived. The thing I like the most about this place is its multicultural democratic bent. Despite the downhome theme of this place, which might seem off-putting if you are not a white person from the midwest, I have always had excellent service here. It is also the only restaurant in our town that I have seen that has both a white and a black clientele (I have never seen Asian people here, except for some people who were clearly part of a bus tour and therefore not there of their own free will).

Let's talk about the weird interaction I had with a Barista here. I walked into the coffee shop, eager to start my day with a hot cup of joe. As I waited in line, I noticed the Barista seemed a bit... off. She was fidgeting with the cups, glancing around nervously, and generally acting like she didn't want to be there. I brushed it off as nerves or a bad day, but boy was I wrong.When it was my turn to order, I stepped up to the counter and gave her a friendly smile. "Good morning! I'll have a medium latte, please."The Barista looked at me like I had just asked her to solve world hunger. She blinked slowly, then replied in a monotone voice, "Do you want it hot or iced?"I was taken aback by her strange behavior, but I tried to roll with it. "Uh, hot, please?"She nodded robotically and started making my drink. As she worked, she refused to meet my eye or engage in any small talk. It was like she was trying to avoid human contact at all costs.I paid for my drink and waited patiently for my order to be ready. When it was finally done, the Barista handed it to me with a sigh and muttered, "Enjoy your drink, I guess."I thanked her and took a sip, trying to shake off the weird encounter. I really wanted to love Upstream, but it totally fell flat. Don't get me wrong - the idea of a seafood restaurant right on the river had me so excited, like who doesn't want to sit outdoors throwing back oysters and watching the boats go by? But man, what a bummer this place turned out to be. We showed up on a Saturday night hoping for a nice lazy dinner since it was finally warm out, but nope, total CF - the wait was like 45 minutes just to get a table. And I'm sorry, but if it's balmy out why are you trying to stuff us into some lame ass tent? Let me breathe some fresh air with my dinner! When we finally sat down, the menu looked pretty good - lots of fresh seafood options straight from the pier. But then it took another 30 minutes just to get our drinks. By that point we were parched and hangry. The one high point was this crab cake appetizer - it was out of this world good. Dense and meaty, with just the right amount of seasoning. I could have marinated in that sweetie sauce all night. But then our meals came and it was such a letdown. My fish tacos were dry as heck and the slaw didn't have much flavor. My friend's pasta looked sad and tiny for the price. And what was up with that weird grainy something in the mash potatoes?I didn't even have room for dessert after that unimpressive meal. Shame because the homemade ice cream and pies looked bomb on the menu. Is it too much to ask for some decent service and fresh food when you're on the water? I wanted so bad for Upstream to be a great new spot but it's definitely a pass for me going forward. Maybe stick to pizza and 12 year aged balsamic elsewhere.

A few others were in the restaurant but not crowded at all. Like other reviewers, I liked the dress of the servers and the decor of the place was pretty cool. As I enjoyed my sake, I ordered the steamed shrimp dumplings. Totally not what I expected.. . two roll-like, dough things came out and it tasted like it looked.. . just like raw dough stuffed with lots of crunchy lettuce-like pieces and tiny chopped meat. " I didn't have the heart (or the energy after a long day of travel) to say anything except "I want to have room for my Pad Thai". So, I awaited my Chicken Pad Thai hoping it was what I am used to. Once in a while, I got the taste of mayonaisse but I was starving at this point and it did the trick. i actually took it back to my hotel for lunch the next day but decided in the morning that the taste wasn't worth the risk of Pad Thai all over my rental car. Wow, a martini bar not named the Blue Martini? OK, I'm in! So I strolled over and walked in. First impression was it was a cool, cozy, and trendy joint. Liked the exposed brick walls, lighting, etc. Only problem is, I don't go to a restaurant or a bar to eat and drink the atmosphere! So I grab a table in the bar. It was about 5pm and there might have been 15 people in the whole place. Two bartenders made eye contact with me so I figured they would be waiting on me. I figured wrong. I sat there for a good ten minutes and was getting ready to get up and leave when the younger tender came over and said with a "deer in the headlights look", do you want a drink or something?? ? ? Well hell, what was your first guess? I refrained from quoting Foxworthy and saying "here's your sign"! So OK we were off to a bumpy start. I didn't have a martini, however there was a few options on the drink menu. I was just here for a bite, so my review is based on that. A few minutes later the other bartender comes back with my water and gives me a menu. I ordered some turkey wrap with a fruit salad for a side. I say "some" turkey wrap because it was really that unimpressive! It seemed to take forever for it to arrive. Given the fact that it wasn't busy, it did take a long time to arrive. When it did, it looked OK. The fruit salad looked as if it was ready for the trash, so I bypassed that. The wrap just had zero flavor and was loaded with lettuce.. .. .. .. way to much. The only flavor that presented itself was blandness! It was very disappointing. All in all, I think this is probably a way better bar to have a drink in then a restaurant. I will return to try a martini, but I will pass on the food.

I typically enjoy the standard "tex-mex" type restaurants, but this was a pretty poor example of the style. Like most of these places the experience starts with chips and salsa; this salsa was bland and watery. The chips were cold and stale; not sure when they made them, but I'm sure that it was not the day they served them to us.. . At this point I should have left and drove up the road to Azteca, Don Pedro or any of the other taco shacks the Queen City has to offer; but sometimes I am not so sharp so we proceeded to order lunch. I ordered the chimichanga; now usually a chimichanga is a flour tortilla filled with a wide range of seasoned flavorful ingredients and deep fried until it is a golden brown color and slightly crispy on the outside. This thing was filled with bland, unflavorful, grayish colored "shredded beef" and was soggy, they then smothered it in some sort of unseasoned canned tomatoes that they tried to pass off as salsa, I assume to mask the lack of flavor in the dish itself. On the side was some wilted lettuce with sour cream and something that vaguely resembled guacamole, and some oily rice that was nearly as flavorless as the rest of the meal. Phenomenal. I managed to eat about a quarter of this flavorless, oily, soggy train wreck before I gave up and threw in the towel. When the server finally came back around several minutes later, she acted like she didn't even notice that none of us had eaten more than half of their meal, and quietly picked up the plates and brought us our checks. None of us were asked how our meal was, if everything was OK, if we wanted any desert or more chips and salsa, and none of us received a refill on our drinks. All in all, this was one of the worse restaurant prepared meals that I have had the pleasure of experiencing. Kudos to the good folks at El Cancun

Reading the other reviews, it makes me wonder if people were a the same restaurant I was. Sure, it isn't a world class dining establishment, but it is decent considering it is a chain. You should know that going into any chain, really. It was basically exactly what I expected in terms of food quality and price. We were greeted immediately upon entering, and while the hostess went to grab menus, another server asked us if we were taken care of. Service at our table was very attentive and water and other beverages were promptly refilled. I ordered soup and two appetizers instead of an entree or pizza and the server made sure to ask me about the order in which I would prefer receiving my food. My fiance ordered a deep dish pizza and we know they take longer to make than other food items. It was quicker than we thought it would be and he really enjoyed it. I had the potato skin appetizer. It reminds me of a "baked potato pizza" that I used to enjoy at a local place back in Buffalo. It was delicious, especially with the addition of a little bit of hot sauce. Overall, it doesn't even come close to visiting an Uno's in Chicago, but then again, when does a copy every live up to the original? It won't be a regular location in our dining rotation, but it is good to know that when we have a craving for deep dish, Uno will do the trick and cost a lot less than a trip to Chicago.

North Carolina's laws on serving alcohol make it nearly impossible to just open a "club", so you see a lot of these in Charlotte, especially downtown. The staff is super friendly and doesn't hassle you for walking in and realizing "Saturday night" hasn't started yet because the dining patrons still haven't cleared out. So don't be afraid to check it at 11pm and then come back again at midnight or 1 if it's still slow. I've never been here to eat but it's a great place to stop in for a late night weekend drink to see what's going on. People dress nice and behave well. So you can actually get an expensive drink and not worry about someone elbowing it across the room. There's plenty of seating on both the first and second floors and they have a respectable, if predictable, Scotch selection that helps me keep them in mind when I'm downtown, so I'm sure the rest of the liquor options are pretty good. Coming from Illinois where you can buy booze at grocery stores, it's depressing to walk into a bar in Charlotte and only have one or two choices. Cosmos expands the horizons and I appreciate that.

Our dog spent two nights here and I can't believe the damage that was done in that time. Upon pick up we asked how she had done, and were told, "She's on Facebook! " (which she wasn't.. . ) but weren't given any legitimate information. What actually had happened was that ALL of her gums were bruised and her teeth were covered with metal from chewing on a cage for 2 days straight. If you love or care about your dog spend the extra 5 dollars for a place that cares about animals.

Favorite thing about Bruegger's? The Jalepeno Cheese speciaty bagel. Yummy, chewy, cheesey, and spicy.. . all at once! Oh, and the decor/cleanliness could use a little UMPH.

I like this airport. Its layout is very clear and intuitive to navigate through. The terminals are spacious and bright, avoiding the cramped and claustrophobic feel of many other airports. Signage throughout the airport provides good guidance to find one's gate with time to spare prior to takeoff. Outside of security, food prices are reasonably priced which is always welcome when traveling. Overall, it is one of the most pleasant airports I have visited.

The staff is friendly and there is a fantastic restaurant located in the lobby. So, why only 2 stars you ask? Years ago, this was a regular spot. I remembered the room was dark, food was good, and the infamous pole in the lady's room. So on a recent cold winter night, while Melissa & I were trying to figure out where to eat, knowing this is her regular spot, I said Alexander Michael's! Parking is always a challenge. Luckily we got a spot down the road off the side street. However the darkness is a little creepy.. . I feel like I need a buddy system to park there (find a friend, hold hands, and walk together like we were in grade school). The embiance was perfect for a cold night with the lit candles and closely spaced seatings. We got a table very quickly, but that's as much service as we got that night. There wasn't any incident. The waitress wasn't rude, but she just wasn't there. For a small place like this, it should be pretty easy to take good care of every table. The food was ok as well. I ordered the london broil sandwich with the soup as side. I forgot the "crab" soup was made with fake crab, which I think should be illegal to be called crab. My sandwich had enough meat on it that I pretty much just ate all the meat, which was average. Tender enough, not too much taste to it. I guess for $9. 50 I couldn't complain. Years later, I felt that their menu was limited, a little overpriced, and seems to be lacking a spark in general with food and service. I will give it a 2nd chance and visit again, maybe not anytime soon.

It's a mouthwatering fajita/taco salad concoction that In a. can't get enough of andn b. can't finish. I have tried a few other dishes and nothing ranks near the crazy taco. Warm, thick chips and a mild salsa are served bountifully. The chips aren't greasy and are not heavily salted which makes me happy. I like to add my own anyway. They have three versions of guacamole. Yesterday we tried the most basic which was delicious and simple. We also tried an appetizer with cheese and chorizo. It was good, but quickly coagulated which resulted in an undip-able dip. MARGARITA ALERT- their house margarita.. . not a traditional margarita. In my opinion, it tasted like watered down orange soda. And the color is a light peach color. If you want a classic, lime margarita I have yet to find one I love here. I'm not your typical margarita drinker. The aftermath of too much sweet margarita mix and I do not get along. I admit, I'm kind of picky about margaritas, but these, these should have a warning when ordering.

nI was at Carolina Place around 1: 30 pm and decided to give this restaurant a try -I was told it's the best Eyetalian in Charlotte. First the good part: I ordered the baked rigatoni with meat sauce and hot Italian sausage. It was excellent -if like me you like strong flavors and spicy both- nothing I'd expect from a chain restaurant. The lunch portion was huge, too much in fact. nthat's it for the good. Service was absolutely dismal for no good reason. It was neither busy nor a late hour for lunch. I think the dinner prices are very high for Southern Italian style pasta dishes, especially considering we're in Charlotte and I think their idea of "family dining" makes life easier for the cook but does nothing for the customer. My idea of fun dining is exactly the opposite, I want to taste as many different things I can, not pig out on a mound of carbs.

I had a taste for fish, and so was pleased to find more than a few appealing options on the dinner menu. I opted for the trout, preceded by the classic french onion soup. David X. had the special, a smoked salmon pasta. The good: the trout was delightful, well complimented by potatoes and a light tomatoey sauce. The portions were perfect, aka not too big. Basically this dish saved the experience for me. The ok: the bread was warm (not hot) and the salmon special was pretty good too. Smoked salmon plus creamy sauce, yum. The underwhelming: the french onion soup was not hot. The cheese was not bubbling or gooey, it was a bit congealed. Meh. And, to echo the words of others, the service was more than just pokey. This was a bit absurd because we were the only people eating in the restaurant. Would I come back? Maybe, to try the breakfast everyone seems to enjoy so much. Maybe they're a bit more on top of their game for breakfast/brunch. But probably not for dinner.

We recently celebrated a birthday party at this restaurant, and it was a fantastic experience from start to finish! The venue was elegantly decorated, creating a sophisticated ambiance that set the tone for a special night out. The staff were friendly and attentive, offering us a variety of menu options that catered to everyone's tastes. The food was exceptional, with generous portions and reasonable prices.The live band played a lively selection of music that kept us entertained throughout the night, and the sound system and lighting were both well-done. The bathrooms were clean and well-maintained, adding to the overall sense of quality and attention to detail.Overall, we had a wonderful experience at this restaurant, and we would highly recommend it to our friends and family. The service was top-notch, the food was delicious, and we're eager to return and try some of their other dishes.

The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive from the moment we walked in. They greeted us with warm smiles and made sure we felt welcomed. The restaurant was also exceptionally clean and well-maintained, which was a pleasant surprise for a fast-food chain. We placed our order at the counter, and the cashier was efficient and accurate. Within minutes, our food was ready, and it looked exactly like the pictures on the menu. The burgers were juicy, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. The fries were crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, and the frosty milkshakes were the perfect treat to complement our meal. The dining area was spacious and comfortable, providing a relaxed atmosphere to enjoy our food. The manager came by our table to check if everything was to our satisfaction, and we appreciated the personal touch. The prices were also reasonable, offering great value for the quality of food and service. It was clear that the entire team took pride in their work, and it showed in every aspect of our dining experience. We left Wendy's feeling incredibly satisfied and eager to return. I highly recommend this location to anyone craving a delicious and hassle-free fast-food meal. This was hands down the best Wendy's experience I've ever had, and I can't wait to go back for more.

The location of the hotel was very convenient for our purposes, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable, and we had a great view of the city. We would definitely stay here again if we are ever in the area again. It was a great value for the price, and we would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a place to stay in the area. The location was perfect for our needs, and the staff was incredibly friendly and helpful. We would definitely stay here again if we are ever in the area again. The location was perfect for our needs, and the staff was incredibly friendly and helpful.

Located on the back of Mt Washington, you will only find locals here. First, the ambiance I so pleasing. It is an eclectic place, tastefully done and offers inside and outside seating. My favorite is sitting at the bar which is a split bar, like a mirror image. There is something magical about this place in addition to great food. The lighting in the main dining room is artful--adorned by CX design lighting like walking into a forest of glowing hanging flowers. nFor starters we had the humus sampler which was a meal in itself. I cut my teeth on the RW&B in the mid nineties and just revisited it for the first time since then!! I always looked for thrift stores like this in LA and SF but.. .. hell no. Wow, has she gotten a makeover: ATM in the corner, a bathroom for patrons (one that is actually somewhat clean! ) and the absence of that old person-Ben-Gay smell. Prices have gone up slightly.. .. but where else can you buy a brand new tennis racket, framed photo of Kermit the Frog (signed! ) and an oversized pair of Joan Collins a la Dynasty sunglasses.. .. true story! I recently visited Treadquarters Pineville for a tire repair issue and was impressed with the exceptional service I received. Upon arrival, I was warmly greeted by a friendly staff member who asked how they could assist me. I explained my concern about a slow leak in my tire and was reassured that they could fix it.The staff member efficiently inspected the tire and returned with a diagnosis: a small tear in the sidewall. They provided a clear explanation of the issue, recommending a replacement tire instead of a patch repair. The staff member showed me the tear and explained why a replacement was necessary, taking the time to ensure I understood the process.I appreciated their transparency and commitment to safety, and decided to replace the tire. The staff member assisted me in choosing a new tire within my budget and even drove me to a nearby restaurant while they worked on my car.The repair was completed promptly and with great care. Before returning my keys, the staff member ensured everything was in order, providing exceptional customer service. My experience at Treadquarters Pineville was outstanding, and I highly recommend them for any tire repair or replacement needs. The staff's knowledge, friendliness, and dedication to customer satisfaction set them apart from others in the industry.

Welcome to my yard. This is my little slice of heaven, where I come to relax and enjoying the beauty of nature. My backyard is a haven for all sorts of widllife, from birds and squirrels to rabbits and deer. I've spent countless hourly here, watching the seasons change and the animals go about their daily lives. In the spring, my backyard comes alive with color as the flowers bloom and the trees bud. The birds are sung in the trees, and the air is filled with the scent of fresh-cut grass. I love to sit on my patio and watch the hummingbirds flit from flower to flower, or take a walk through the woods and admire the wildflowers. As summer approaches, my backyard becomes a playground for the neighborhood kids. They run and games on the lawn, while I relax in the shade of the trees. Ours have picnics and barbecues, and I love to watch the kids play in the sprinkler. In the fall, the leaves on the trees turn a beautiful shade of orange and red. The air is crisp and cool, and I love to take walks in the woods and collect refill. I also like to sit on my patio and watch the chipmunks gather nuts for the winter. In the winter, my backyard is a wonderland of snow and ice. The trees are bare, and the ground is covered in a thick blanket of snow. I love to go sledding down the hill with the kids, or Build a snowman in the yard.

Still sitting here waiting for someone to give a care. So, we finally got the attention of a server who was not our server, Michael. She was kind enough to take my steak back to the kitchen. Michael, our server, finally shows up 10 minutes later with a half-hearted apology and to let me know that my steak was being prepared again. He does not offer to refill our drink glasses that have now been sitting empty for 20 minutes. The manager makes an appearance and brings me a strip steak that looks rare from the sight of it. He informs me that my steak is on him and apologizes. He goes away. I cut into my steak and it's, you guessed it, Pittsburgh Rare. I asked for medium rare. He returns and I tell him that the chef needs to go back to culinary school and learn how to prepare a steak. The manager apologizes again and asks me if I want to take this pathetic piece of beef home with me! Not only is it rare but it's a cheap cut of strip steak that is loaded with connective gristle. I said no thanks. He comped my husband's meal and we left. I never hope for people to lose their jobs but the cook and the server really need some serious retraining! I will never go back to this Applebee's again.

This game truly delivers an impressive spectacle of fighting gameplay. The tight controls allow for fluid combinations and counterattacks that feel immensely satisfying to execute. Players are treated to a diverse cast of unique characters, each with their own fighting styles and special abilities. This variety ensures the matchups stay fresh across numerous replays. The stages are beautifully crafted with interactive elements that dynamically impact battles. Vibrant colors and fine details bring the characters and environments to life. Meanwhile, the pumping soundtrack stirs adrenaline across diverse genres. Story mode weaves an engaging plot that motivated exploring each fighter's motivations. However, where this title truly excels is its multiplayer modes. Local and online battles offer endless replayability whether teaming up or going head-to-head. Building strategies with friends provides endless entertainment. Customization allows tailoring favorites with unlocked items. Moreover, free updates continuously introduce novel content, maintaining long-term engagement. Achievements and leaderboards provide goals that incentivize mastering every challenge.Most impressively, the polished presentation delivers buttery-smooth gameplay without technical hitches. At its best, fights feel like well-choreographed performances. This sets the new gold standard for quantity and quality within its genre. For devoted fans of fighting games seeking depth and lasting appeal, this masterpiece undoubtedly satisfies. While five stars fails to do it justice, everyone can agree this title deserves relentless praise. Its excellence keeps drawing players back for more incredible battles time and time again.

We were escorted to a table and were cool, the waitress was friendly and tentative since our conversation was rollin'. Long story short we were there for 5 hours, just drinking, and if our waitress could of re-worded her words, our experience wouldn't have been so sour. She came over and stated "I'm leaving here is the check, if you would like to stay you're more then welcome to order from the bar. " So we continued to talk not thinking anything of it, or someone was going to pick up her tip. WELL not two minutes later she comes back to us and says " IM LEAVING, I need you to pay your check. " At this point me being me, gets a little annoyed, as my friend is looking at me like no she didn't! So he paid as a gentlemen do, and we continued the night, as they dimmed the lights and shut off the music we got the hint we've been talking way to long. If she could have been a tid more polite, it would have been a good experience. The atmosphere was great, the food looked good, but your sour mouth ruined it all.

The atmosphere is pretty fancy.. . high ceilings, white table clothes, snooty looking hosts and waiters, however, looks are deceiving. This is a family-style restaurant, disguised as a fine dining. We went here with 6 adults and 2 young children.. . arriving a little too early for dinner, they let us wait inside. I was hoping they'd give us some free appetizers, but no such luck =(. They seated us right at 5p and seats started filling up fast, so it was probably a good idea we got there early. We ordered 5 of the pasta trios and I ordered the Zuppe di Pesce (seafood stew). The pasta was good.. . I wouldn't say it was amazing, but definitely worth the price.. . $20 for just the pasta, but yo u can add a ceasar salad and desert for I think $7. For people that don't know, everyday, there are 3 different pasta dishes the chef makes for this pasta trio. They have servers for each of the individual pastas (pretty neat IMO). They give you a sampling of the 3 at first, which, quite honestly was plenty. Then you can pick one, two or even all three for the subsequent rounds. I don't know if it's all you can eat, but even the big eaters were done after their 3rd plate. There is a child's menu, but our kids eat like birds, so we asked if they could have a little of the pasta. The servers were very accomodating.. . bringing everyone plates to share. My wife ordered the pasta trio with a salad and desert. The ceasar was perfect (she shared it with me) and she had tiramisu that was probably the best we've ever had. The Zuppe di pesce (my entree) was AMAZING.. . I'm a seafood lover though. Overall, I'd say this is an upgraded version of Olive Garden.. . which is NOT a bad thing.

Personally, I love this bar. This place is 5 miles from my office and 5 miles from my house, no wonder I made it to 200 beers so easily! The Flying Saucer literally has approximately 300 unique beers, with at least 100 on tap, and some of them are rotating beers. Additionally, they have daily specials, like pint night with $3 pints and biggie beers for the price of a pint and even beer poker. Their loyalty program is also rad, drink 200 unique beers and get a $100 tab on the house to have a party with your friends (I'm 421). Fear not non-beer drinkers, they also have liquor drinks. Their food menu is decent, I mean, it's bar food.. . The pretzels with queso dip are the best! And the scenery, aka the waitresses, aren't bad to look at either.. . in their school girl uniforms. They have pool tables in the back and good music streaming, unless a crappy band happens to be playing. If a band is playing and there is a cover, Beer Knurd members get in for free. Prost!

This establishment's cuisine is unremarkable. The beer selection, however, is excellent, and the atmosphere is very pleasant. The service is also very good. The culture here is cool as well. The only downside is that it is very far from my apartment.Overall, I would recommend this place for a drink. The food is not great, but the beer and atmosphere are worth it.

Pamela's Restaurant failed to impress us despite its high ratings. The line to get seated was lengthy, taking over an hour to be escorted to our table. Given the restaurant's acclaim, we were anticipating a more remarkable dining experience. You have to love the idea that there is luxury in every bite, I mean it's a darn good sandwich. I live in Seattle, we have no Chick-Fil-A.. . we don't get to taste this wonderful delight, that make people line up in cars, bleeding into parking lot of the neighboring Office Depot, blocking traffic, and generally proving that if you are hungry, there is no good reason to go anywhere else, because you have it right here. Whenever I find myself in the Strip District, I make it a point to visit this place for their delectable chicken on a stick and mung bean pancakes. There's just something about the combination of flavors and the vibrant atmosphere that keeps me coming back time and again. The grilled chicken on a stick is absolutely perfect, with a smoky char that adds a wonderful depth to each juicy bite. And let me tell you, the mung bean pancakes are a delightful surprise. They're light, crispy, and have a subtle nutty flavor that pairs beautifully with the dipping sauce they serve. The portion sizes are more than generous, ensuring that you leave feeling fully satisfied. What's more, the staff is always friendly and attentive, providing prompt service and helpful recommendations. The restaurant itself has a cozy and inviting ambiance, adorned with warm colors and charming decor. It's the kind of place where you can enjoy a leisurely meal with friends or have a quick solo lunch during a busy day. And to top it all off, the prices are reasonable, offering excellent value for the quality of food and experience you receive. All in all, if you're looking to indulge in mouthwatering chicken on a stick and mung bean pancakes in a welcoming atmosphere, this spot in the Strip District is an absolute must-visit.

I want this grocery store to succeed. It's got all the right ingredients: fresh, high-quality produce; a wide selection of organic and specialty items; and friendly, helpful staff.Plus, it's in a great location-right in the heart of downtown. So why isn't it more popular?I think there are a few reasons. First, the prices are a little high. I'm not saying that they're outrageous, but they're definitely not the lowest in town.Second, the store is a little small. It's not cramped, but it's not exactly spacious either. This can make it difficult to get around, especially when it's busy.Third, the store doesn't have a very good selection of prepared foods. This is a major drawback for me, because I'm often looking for something quick and easy to eat.Finally, the store doesn't have a very good marketing strategy. I've never seen any ads for it, and I don't know anyone who has. This is a shame, because I think the store has a lot to offer.So, what can be done to improve the store? Here are a few suggestions:Lower the prices. This is the number one thing that I think the store needs to do. If the prices were more competitive, I think more people would shop there.Expand the selection of prepared foods. This is another important thing that I think the store needs to do. Offering more prepared foods would make it more convenient for people to shop there.Improve the marketing strategy. The store needs to do a better job of marketing itself. This could be done through advertising, social media, and word-of-mouth.If the store can make these changes, I think it has the potential to be very successful. It's a great store with a lot to offer, but it just needs a little help.I hope that the store's owners will take my suggestions into consideration. I want this store to succeed, and I think that these changes would help it to do so.

This sites is A-OK! From the moment I stepped foot inside, I was greeted with warm and friendly chuckling. I'm from NY. I grew up in Queens surrounded by the hustle and bustle of the city. Everything was always moving fast paced whether it was the cars honking down the block or strangers rushing by on the sidewalk. But it was home - the sounds of sirens in the distance and smell of pizza wafting out of every other store always made me feel comforted. Winters were brutal battling snow storms just to get to the corner bodega. Summers brought a different energy with street markets popping up on every corner selling anything from knock off purses to fresh mangoes. I spent my free time exploring new neighborhoods with friends, our adventures always ending with greasy slices from one of the hundreds of pizza joints dotting the five boroughs. It instilled a love of exploring new places that still drives me today. Leaving for college was tough leaving that lifestyle behind. But NYC will always have a piece of my heart, and I know that no matter how long I've been gone, it will feel like coming home the second I smell that unique subway scent again waiting for the train.

Pretty darn good! This movie really delivered on the action and excitement. From the opening scene, it was fast paced and never lets up. The plot moves along at a breathless pace that keeps you engaged the whole time. Al the actors brought their A-agme with convincing performances that made it easy to get caught up in their characters. I've experience better. "nnI have a love-hate relationship with PAT. The buses are unreliable timing wise and a majority of the drivers are jerks. Yes, some nights it is smoky. And some nights it is crowded and filled with loud and somewhat annoying hipster types. But it's our little place. This is the bar where my friends and I gather to watch sporting events, sing karaoke (albeit badly), and generally hang out. The beer is decently-priced, not CHEAP CHEAP, but it won't cost you an arm and a leg. Wednesdays are pizza and a pitcher -- we LOVE the Chili Pie and pair it up with Yuengling or the similar. And the other food is pretty good too -- among our other favorites: the wings, Nico's Platter, and fried cheese. YUMMY! Jason and Nicole who both bartend and wait tables are both AWESOME, always friendly, always generous with the booze, and always quick with a smile. They're great! PS -- As a reply to reviews complaining about the guy who does karaoke: if they reviewed prior to early 2011, there is someone else there now and we think he's pretty great. : -) If he doesn't have a song that you want, let him know, as he's constantly adding new music and updating his collection.

I visited on a weeknight, and enjoyed the darker, upscale ambiance. However, based on previous reviews, the food is hit or miss. My dinner there was a substantial miss for a pretty substantial price. I ordered the mixed green salad and it was nothing special -- the dressing was blah and it was just regular goat cheese -- no crust, no heat, etc. I ordered the NY Strip because the waiter said it was amazing, as did another member of my group. Side note: the service was phenomenal, no problems in that department. When it arrived, we both found the steak to be EXTREMELY tough. I know it's not a filet, but you're supposed to be able to get your knife through it without breaking a sweat. I didn't try my friend's steak, but he actually sent his back for being virtually inedible. He swapped out for a filet with blue cheese and was quite pleased that he did. Maybe I should have done the same.. .. I don't know, but if you have to send your food back in order to get a decent meal, it's a pretty bad sign, especially at an expensive establishment. In Blue's defense, I believe they were pretty upset about my friend's meal -- we basically got an entire desert tray for free. Those were luckily delicious, as they made up a substantial part of my otherwise sub-par meal. Bottom line, I will not go here again except for cocktails, some appetizers, and some jazz. Or if someone else is picking up the tab.

The location was perfect -- close to the convention center, yet not right in the middle of all of the hubub. The park was pleasant to walk next to while heading over, but I was glad to have someone with me who had been there before. While ordering, the staff was polite and friendly, noting our convention badges and asking where we were from. They recognized the members of our group that had been there the previous day. I ordered the two corn-dog combo; others in my group ordered the hot dog combo and the burger combo. The fries were piping hot and perfectly seasoned. Our corn-dogs were the perfect combination of golden batter and awesome dog, and the burger and regular dogs were gone before I could ask the others how they were: ) The ketchup on the table was a little low, but I think we were there just after the lunch rush, so that was understandable. By the time I was ready for a refill on my diet coke before heading out, there was a small line at the register. The cashier waved me to the front of the line when he saw my cup, so I didn't have to wait while others ordered -- I was highly surprised, and very thankful for his consideration. I wish more restaurants did that. One of the earlier reviewers mentioned confusion with picking up baskets right next to the utensil area -- when I visited, there was a young woman running food out (she called the number and waited for the correct person to raise their hands). It seemed to work much better than having customers pick up their order. I would definitely recommend Matt's Chicago Dog for anyone in the area.

From the moment you enter, you are greeted by a warm and friendly atmosphere that makes you feel at home. The walls are adorned with old photographs that add to the nostalgic charm of the place. It's a long time to go to the same place, but Max's has managed to keep me coming back year after year. Let's talk about the food. Max's menu is a delightful combination of classic comfort food and creative cuisine. The staff, many of whom have been with the restaurant for decades, is friendly and attentive, always willing to go the extra mile to make your dining experience exceptional. One of my favorite dishes is Max's special burger, a mouth-watering masterpiece piled high with toppings and served with a side of crispy golden fries that are simply irresistible. Whether you're in the mood for a juicy steak cooked to perfection or a hearty bowl of homemade soup, Max's has it all. The chefs are true artists, and they present each dish with impeccable attention to detail. When it comes to quality, Max's never compromises. The ingredients are always fresh, and you can taste the difference in every bite. Another thing that makes Max's so special is their commitment to accommodating special dietary needs. Whether you're a vegetarian, a vegan, or have food allergies, they have a wide variety of dishes to suit every palate. Every dish that leaves the kitchen is a work of art, both visually and in taste. Max's has become a cultural institution in the city, hosting countless celebrations, milestone events, and intimate gatherings. The staff is knowledgeable about the menu and can guide you through your choices, so you never feel left out or restricted.

Review #200nnI got hooked on this bakery while living in Brighton Heights. The moment you step inside, you're embraced by the warm aroma of freshly baked treats. It's like a sweet siren's call, luring you deeper into this pastry paradise. The display case is a technicolor dream, filled to the brim with an assortment of pastries, bread, and cakes that would make anyone's mouth water. Trust me, you'll be drooling within seconds of laying eyes on their delectable creations.Let's talk about their croissants. Oh boy, they're a work of art. The flaky golden layers just melt in your mouth with each bite. It's sheer buttery goodness that transports you to Paris in an instant. And don't even get me started on their pain au chocolat. The decadent chocolate filling oozes out, blending harmoniously with the buttery pastry. This heavenly delight is my go-to treat whenever I need a little pick-me-up.Now, let's switch gears and talk about their cakes. Where do I even begin? Their red velvet cake is the stuff of legends. Moist, velvety layers of heaven, slathered with cream cheese frosting that strikes the perfect balance of sweetness. It's pure indulgence. And if you're a chocolate lover, their triple chocolate cake is a must-try. Each bite is a symphony of rich chocolate flavors that dance on your taste buds.Apart from the exceptional baked goods, the customer service here is outstanding. The staff greets you with warm smiles and is always ready to assist you in finding your next treat. They're knowledgeable and passionate about their craft, and it reflects in the quality of their products.I must mention their coffee too. The bakery takes pride in brewing a mean cup of joe. Whether you prefer a velvety latte or a robust espresso shot, they've got you covered. It's the perfect accompaniment to their pastries, completing the whole experience.One thing I appreciate about this bakery is their commitment to sourcing local and high-quality ingredients.
