My initial visit left me satisfied yet underwhelmed. The spacious dining area was clean with booths along the perimeter and tables in the center. On a weekday evening, it was not crowded when we dined. Service was attentive without being intrusive. For appetizers, we tried egg rolls and fried wontons which were average - edible but unexciting. The main dishes of kung pao chicken, sweet and sour pork, and broccoli with garlic sauce lacked depth of flavor. The sauces tasted heavily of cornstarch and the meats and vegetables were overcooked. While portions were large, the food lacked flavor intensity. Plain white rice offered no excitement. Fried banana for dessert was adequate yet boring. The meal was palatable but failed to inspire a return visit. Better Chinese restaurants near our home satisfy far more with authentic flavors. This place suffices in a pinch but offers no reason to seek it out over more flavorful options elsewhere. When high quality Chinese is available, I would not go out of my way for the familiar but underseasoned fare here.

The selection is still great with many brand-name choices. I find I usually need to order online because my size isn't in the store, but shipping is usually pretty fast. I really like shopping Kohl's online. I find things so much easier online and shipping is generally fast and easy. I have had an issue with curbside pickup and an online order not being ready for pickup when they said it would be, but that seems to be a fluke occurrence. Overall, I am happy to have found this location and will likely continue to shop here or online. I would definitely recommend this location if you are looking for clothes, shoes, and home goods at a good value. They also have a great rewards program, which is free to join. You get Kohl's cash for every purchase you make and they send out 30% off coupons all the time! This is really my favorite place to shop for clothes! The quality is great for the price.

We started by exploring some of the new restaurants that had opened up in our neighborhood over the past year. The first place we stopped at looked promising, but they were already booked up for the night. Not wanting to go too far, we walked a few blocks to a casual Italian spot called Bruschetta Bakery. We were seated right away at a cozy corner table. The aromas that hit our noses as we walked in were absolutely divine. We started with some fresh bread and olive oil, which hit the spot. We split a bottle of Chianti, which paired nicely with our meal. For dinner, I had the lasagna bolognese, which was rich and filling. My husband had the chicken parmigiana, which he raved about. After we finished eating, we sat and chatted for another half hour or so, still sipping our wine. It was so nice to be out on a warm evening instead of bundled up inside. The restaurant wasn't too crowded for a weeknight, which made for a relaxed atmosphere. We wished we lived somewhere warmer where evenings like this were more common during the winter months. Feeling stuffed, we paid our bill and walked back out into the cool air. On our way home, we passed by the local park and noticed that quite a few people were still out enjoying the weather. Even on busy work nights, it's nice to make time to get out and enjoy simple pleasures together. Once we got home, we curled up on the couch, feeling content with our little dinner date adventure. The unseasonably warm weather had certainly made our experience all the more enjoyable.

Generic, prefabricated and typical describes this restaurant perfectly. All of the dishes feel like they could come from any chain across the nationale. The food is nothing alfred and lacks any real distinguishing flavors. It's fine for a quick, inexpensive meal but don't expect to be stunned. The dining room is crowded and noisy, with hard plastic seating that isn't uncommonly comfortable. Tables are jammed close together so you feel like you're consume in someone else's lap. Service is average - servers rush through orders without much personas. Drinks are made from syrup conjugate and taste artificially sweet. Menus are limited and repetitive, with all the usual suspects like burgers, sandwiches and salads overpowers the options. Something ventures outside of well-worn territory. Ingredients seem low quality and portions tends to be on the smaller side. Lodging is utilitarian with food shoved together on plates. Atmosphere is lacking with blank white walls and generic decor that provides no local color or identity. Muzak plays overhead at a comfortable origin volume. Kids meals try to engage little ones but grownups will find little to hold their significance. Bidet are clean if basic. Parking lot is small so hopes a bit of a hunt for spaces during busy times. Location is convenient for a quick bite on the run but won't make for a memorable dining enjoys. It's suitable for families with picky eaters or those observes their budgets closely. But adventurous food lovers will believes frustrated by the lack of inspiration. In the end, it does what is says on the tin - contains a filling but boring meal at legitimate costs. Just don't envisaged any surprises, passion or creativity from the cooks in the back. This generic chain restaurant excels at consistency but receding short on excitement.

I'm not sure I can even give this place one star. My stay at this hotel was an absolute nightmare from the moment I walked through the doors. The check-in process was a disaster - long lines, disorganized staff, and a complete lack of efficiency. I couldn't help but wonder if they were intentionally trying to make my experience as unpleasant as possible.Once I finally got my room key, I made my way to the elevator, only to find that it was out of order. Great, just great. I had to lug my heavy suitcase up five flights of stairs, which was not the ideal start to my stay. As I entered my room, the disappointment continued to mount. The decor was outdated, and the whole place had an unpleasant, musty smell.The bed looked like it hadn't been changed in weeks, with visible stains on the sheets. I immediately called the front desk to request fresh linens, but it took them over an hour to bring them up. I couldn't believe the lack of attention to cleanliness and basic housekeeping.As if that wasn't enough, the noise level in the hotel was unbearable. I could hear everything that was happening in the adjacent rooms and even in the hallway. It felt like there were no soundproofing measures in place whatsoever. I tried to call the front desk to complain, but the phone in my room was dead. It was just one frustration after another.The bathroom was another disaster. The shower had poor water pressure, and the temperature kept fluctuating between scalding hot and freezing cold. The towels provided were worn out and scratchy. It's a shame that such basic amenities were not up to par.Throughout my stay, I encountered several rude and unhelpful staff members. When I approached the front desk to voice my concerns, I was met with indifference and a dismissive attitude. It was as if they couldn't care less about their guests' satisfaction. The lack of professionalism was astounding.The hotel's facilities were also severely lacking.

I'd actually give this place a 3. 5. The food is nothing special.. . just basic, greasy, diner food. The rating is not for the food, or for what the places looks like or feels like. This rating is for what Ritter's REPRESENTS. Ritters represents late nights after the bar with friends. Ritters represents the meal that will soak up the alcohol and save you from a wicked hangover. Ritters represents 3AM with your friends, not because anyone is particularly hungry for chicken tenders, but because the bars are closed and no one is ready to go home quite yet. The laughter and fun shared at late night at Ritters can be replaced by nothing else. If you are looking for awesome food, you will be disappointed. If you are looking for standard, 24 hour diner food and an awesome place to people watch once the bar doors close, this is your place. It is so awesome to see all of the club goers pile into Ritters after dancing on a dark dance floor.. .. hair a mess, mascara looking more like a raccoon than the model they were just a few hours ago and limping in those fierce heels they thought looked SO cute when they hit the dance floor. This place is an institution among those who spend their early/mid twenties in the Oakland/Shadyside/Bloomfield area. If you haven't spent a late night at Ritters, you are missing out.

The Harris is my favorite bar in Pittsburgh and they have fantastic bartenders.. . Byron, Caleb.. . mix excellent cocktails w friendly smiles. BUT. They keep changing the menu and I know many restaurants do this but its starting to get tiring. If you dine here, please ask what they are out of first and have a back up menu selection made just in case. If you do eat here, I recommend: nnThe Chicken RiggiesnThe hamburgernthe mac n cheesenThe wingsnthe pierogiesnThe Henny PennynThe Garden Weasel I suggest you avoid: nnThe greek salad. For some reason I ALWAYS get a hair in this salad. And no, they are not strings from onions, they are dark hairs! Eww. The tarragon dressing: It's basically liquid salt and will render anything you are eating inedible. More effective than Sensa. Trust me. The Delmonico A go go: sounds like the sandwich is going to be good, but its very gristly and not that great I really, really, really wish they'd bring the falafel sandwich back but it seems it's gone to Harris Menu Item heaven. Also, they have good brunches here on Sunday's but it is buffet style when the weather is nice. I like their brunch, but I prefer it when they have a menu in the colder months. With the buffet you can't, for example, just get fried eggs or anything like that. But it still pretty good. I like this place, but maybe I've just dined here too often? I don't know. I just havent had my mind blown here in awhile.

Don't ask me what that is really but he's got it. He is never rude but does manage to make me laugh. I have had my fair share of issues with this place but it really depends on who you get. I was trying to get the antennae off the car but could not for the life of me. One of the workers was there immediately to help. One of the guys at the end of the wash also put all of our belongings back into a careful pile and closed the door for me as I sat down. I was very impressed with the service this day! I came to this establishment with an open mind, excited to try a new local barbecue spot. The parking lot was quite full upon my arrival, but I found a space without too much trouble. Inside, the restaurant had a warm, inviting atmosphere despite how busy it was. I quickly placed my order at the front counter then found a small table to wait. It didn't take long at all for my number to be called. The portions were generous and the food looked delicious. I took my first bite of pulled pork and was impressed by the flavor. It was tender and smokey without being over powering. The accompanying baked beans and coleslaw also hit the spot. Throughout my meal, the staff seemed friendly and attentive without being overbearing. When it came time to pay, I handed my check to the cashier along with cash for the total owed plus what I thought was a standard 15-20% gratuity. However, I was surprised when she informed me that they do not accept tips at this establishment. I had simply missed this policy on the menu or signs. While tipping culture is entrenched for better or worse, I appreciate a business owner paying workers a living wage over customer subsidies.I inquired further and was told that prices were set accordingly to fairly compensate staff. Reassured, I thanked the cashier and left satisfied with both my delicious meal and the restaurant's approach. Overall, it was a very positive dining experience and I'll be sure to return again soon. In the future, I'll be sure to note any no tipping policies to avoid similar mix ups. But ultimately I feel this is a restaurant worth supporting.

Its a bit pricey (~$15/person), but the quality and quantity is superb. The service is pretty good. The atmosphere has a nice feel to it, perhaps its the antiquity.. Needless to say, after leaving this place, I felt like the dumbest person alive and am now frightened to ever enter another legit coffee shop. I walked into Fortunes with a couple of friends and looked at the menu dumbfounded because I had no idea what I was reading. All I knew was that I had drunk a "macchiato" before and had enjoyed it. So I thought, "What the heck, I'll order a caramel macchiato. " This is how the conversation went with the barista: nnMe: Hi, I'd like a medium caramel macchiato. nBarista: So, you want to order OUR macchiato? nMe: Uhh.. . sure.. . ? Two minutes later I get a tiny cup with a meager amount of liquid in it. I turn around and look to my friends confusedly, wondering where I had went wrong. The barista notices this and gets my attention: nnBarista: That's why I asked you whether you wanted OUR macchiato. nMe: Oh.. . ok.. . The barista, clearly frustrated, takes my cup, pours it out and makes me a caramel latte. Alright all you avid coffee drinkers, laugh all you want that I had no idea that there is a difference between a Caffu00e8 macchiato (espresso macchiato) and the American replicate (Latte Macchiato?? ? ). I'm not even sure if what I just said is correct. For the drink I got, I can't complain about the price (Did I over- or underpay the actual price of a caramel latte? ), especially given the prices at Starbucks these days. Also, given the fact that I made such a stupid mistake means that this place must be a good coffee shop. Beyond that, unfortunately, I can't make any judgment -- hence my modest rating. Perhaps when I start drinking more coffee, I'll re-examine this review and re-rate it.

By far the best Pho in the area and over many places I have visited. If you want good service & environment, you'd better stop here. It's a hole in the wall by a seemingly angry asian (he's actually quite nice). Expect to wait on water or wait on refills. If you make your order too complicated, it'll probably get messed up. With that, the Pho. It's amazing and I've had a lot of Pho. However, it has it hit and miss days too. The meatball is more tender and flavorful than the beef which can be dry or tough to some that haven't had Pho before. I wouldn't recommend any other versions. A small is available as most Americans I bring here are unable to finish a bowl. Spring rolls are great (cold/fresh) with a peanut dipping sauce. The egg rolls are just amazingly full of flavor (fried) with a fish style dipping sauce. Place is very inexpensive too. Oh, this place is BYOB in terms of alcohol. Forgot to mention it's cash only. There's an ATM at the entrance or any of the nearby gas stations.

We decided to try The Farmhouse, a local restaurant that focuses on using fresh, locally-sourced ingredients. The interior was rustic yet polished, with worn wood tables and a brick fireplace. Upon being seated, the friendly server brought us menus encased in butcher paper and offered a few nightly specials. I opted for the mushroom risotto, hoping the earthy flavors would warm me up on the chilly night. My husband went for the lamb chops, drawn by the reputation of the kitchen's herb-crusted renditions. The first sips of mulled wine soothed both body and soul. When the food arrived, it did not disappoint. Creamy rice mingled with sautéed mushrooms in my bowl, comfort in a bite. As for the chops, fall-off-the-bone tender with just a hint of rosemary and thyme. Both entrees were complemented by simple seasonal sides. Too content to linger long, we boxed leftovers for tomorrow. Over slices of apple crisp, we continued enjoying relaxed conversation in the low light. It was the perfect night for staying in but we were glad to have ventured out instead. The Farmhouse will remain at the top of our list for casual evenings together, whether winter or summer. As we stepped back into the now balmy air, full and satisfied, we looked forward to warmer days and repeat visits soon.

MCV is a modern, upscale salon owned by Estee Lauder. The atmosphere is clean and trendy. The staff is friendly and very professional. They offer a variety of services, including hair, nails, skin, massage, and makeup. I always have a wonderful experience when I go there. They greet you with a smile and make you feel relaxed as you sit in the comfortable chairs and drink the free drink. I have been going to MCV for years and have always had a great experience. I highly recommend this salon to anyone looking for a great experience and excellent service. It's definitely worth every penny. They have a wide range of services, so you can get everything you need in one place. The staff is very friendly and welcoming, and they always go out of their way to make you feel good. They use high-quality products that are gentle on your hair and skin. One of the things I love most about MCV is their attention to detail. They take the time to listen to your needs and create a plan that suits you. I highly recommend MCV to anyone looking for a great salon experience. The staff is amazing, the service is excellent, and the price is reasonable. I always leave MCV feeling refreshed and rejuvenated. You won't be disappointed!

The fourth time was not the charm for Soba Lounge, as our meal was a disaster from start to finish. After reading old reviews, I figured that some change had to have occurred over the last year and gave it a shot. And boy, was I pleasantly surprised! The transformation in this place is nothing short of remarkable. From the moment I stepped in, I was greeted by a completely different ambiance, one that exuded warmth and sophistication. The updated decor and revamped menu were clear indicators that the establishment had undergone a significant makeover. The attention to detail was evident in every aspect, from the tasteful artwork adorning the walls to the impeccable service provided by the attentive staff. As for the food, it surpassed all expectations. Each dish was skillfully crafted, bursting with flavor and presented with artistic flair. I couldn't help but savor each bite, utterly impressed by the chef's creativity and expertise. Without a doubt, this hidden gem has reclaimed its position as a top-notch dining destination.

They know this so I get a call every year inviting me back and who am I to say no? From the minute you walk into the restaurant to the time you leave it's like they put these rose colored glasses on you and all you see is the awesome atmosphere, service, and food. nWe received 2 complimentary glasses of champagne, and prosciutto wrapped arracini to start us off. Lobster & Crab Cakes for sweetie and a tomato mozzarella salad for me. The tomatoes were cut thick and were complimented by sweet cherry tomatoes and a 12 year aged balsamic. All very well done. I admit that I did make a mistake. I wanted to save room for dessert, so I usually order the porcini rubbed delmonico, but I figured a bone in steak was a bit much. I ordered the 10 Oz Fillet instead and it was served with 2 large shrimp stuffed with lump crabmeat. The fillet was cooked nicely and the shrimp were prepared to my satisfaction, I just prefer a ribeye, so looking back I should order what I like and have the mindset to take home what I can't finish. Now, onto the side dishes.. . the Lobster Mac N Cheese is like heaven on a plate, I don't know or do I particularly care how much butter they add to it, but it is nothing short of spectacular. Creamed Spinach is also awesome. Cheesecake for dessert was like it came out of a magazine. I think someone told me that their Head Chef was a pastry chef in his past life which leads me to believe that their cheesecake at this location is better than most. nThe service at the Capital Grille is top notch. They take such good care of you and make you feel like you're the only customer. I will continue to go back for this reason and encourage everyone to do the same. See you soon Guys!

We were seated immediately and greeted by our server, Johnny, who was very friendly and attentive. The menu had a good variety of options, including seafood, steak, and pasta dishes. I ordered the grilled salmon with a side of garlic mashed potatoes, while my companion opted for the filet mignon with a side of sautéed spinach. We both agreed that the food was delicious and well-prepared. The salmon was cooked perfectly, with a nice char on the outside and a moist, flavorful interior. The garlic mashed potatoes were creamy and had a nice balance of garlic flavor. The filet mignon was also cooked to perfection, with a tender, juicy texture and a rich, savory flavor. The sautéed spinach was a bit overcooked, but still enjoyable. The restaurant had a cozy, intimate atmosphere, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. The decor was elegant and understated, with a few tasteful art pieces on the walls. Overall, we had a very positive experience at Alexander's and would definitely return. The service was excellent, with Johnny checking in on us frequently to ensure that everything was to our liking. The food was delicious and well-presented, and the atmosphere was pleasant and inviting. We would definitely recommend Alexander's to anyone looking for a quality dining experience in the area.

It's not fancy but the food is really good. You could miss this place easily if you weren't looking for it. But do look for it, you'll be glad you did. When you walk in, you feel like you're walking in to someone's home kitchen. There is a choice of indoor or outdoor seating. The outdoor seating is in a little open air structure, so you are still out of the elements if it's raining or if the sun is beating down in the summertime. The menu has a lot to offer, I usually get tacos and rice and beans, while my fella usually gets jalapeno poppers and a veggie quesadilla. There are also American choices on the menu. Portion sizes are generous. The police in the area seem to really like eating here, there is almost always an officer dining when we go there. That tells me 3 things, Miguel's treats our officers right, the food is really good and a good value, and I will be safe eating at this establishment. Service is always friendly. I wish Miguel's would come to Raleigh.

This situation happened to me a few years ago and it was not enjoyable, hopefully it has changed. I recently moved to the area and am impressed that daily parking is $5 per day. They are doing construction to expand the lots, hope the price will stay the same. Recently flew United for a very early morning flight, the gate agent was awesome! She was welcoming, comical, pleasant and professional. She made my morning! Previously, I have flown US Airways into and out of CLT.. both positive, negative and neutral experiences. Didn't really have time to check everything out, but they have some nice areas in the airport for lounging and relaxing, and also some nice eateries. Bathrooms were clean. Airport information was helpful in locating the bus stop for long term parking. The buses ran frequently and were large enough to accommodate a few families with luggage storage.

Ah, Sunday brunch back in Madison. It's been a while since I've been back to my college town, and I was excited to see if the brunch scene had changed at all. I was pleasantly surprised to find that there were still plenty of great options to choose from.One of my favorite spots is still The Old Fashioned, a classic Wisconsin supper club that serves up some of the best Bloody Marys in town. Their brunch menu is just as impressive, with everything from classic eggs Benedict to more creative dishes like their blueberry pancakes with lemon curd.Another great option is The Farmhouse, a cozy restaurant that serves up farm-to-table cuisine. Their brunch menu features seasonal ingredients and locally-sourced meats, making it a great choice for those looking for a sustainable meal.For something a little different, I recommend checking out The Tornado Room, a speakeasy-style bar that serves up some of the best cocktails in town. Their brunch menu is small but mighty, with dishes like their pork belly hash and their avocado toast with smoked salmon.No matter what your taste, you're sure to find something to your liking at one of Madison's many great brunch spots. So next time you're in town, be sure to check out the local brunch scene and see for yourself why it's one of the best in the country.Here are a few more of my favorite brunch spots in Madison:* The Brasserie at the Edgewater: This elegant restaurant offers stunning views of Lake Mendota and serves up a delicious brunch buffet every Sunday.* Harvest: This farm-to-table restaurant is known for its seasonal menu and creative dishes. Their brunch menu is no exception, with offerings like their sweet potato pancakes and their roasted beet salad.* Lazy Jane's Cafe: This cozy cafe is a great spot for a casual brunch. Their menu features everything from classic breakfast dishes to more creative options like their huevos rancheros and their breakfast tacos.

I found it on yelp and looked like they had some delicious menu items and were also close to where I was staying. I always try new places that are not chains and this one had lots of items I was interested in. I looked at the menu and ended up ordering the goat cheese and mascropone appetizer that you also got with crostini and marinera sauce, The salmon salad, and also the apple crisp dessert. When I called to order the person who took my order was very helpful and knew a lot about the menu items which almost never happens. Since I also ordered take out she made sure to tell me that everything would be packaged seperately so it would not get soggy. When I picked up my food it was so nicely packed and delicious as well! I loved all of the food and would defnitely love to go back there again. Definitely a nice place to just go and have a quiet dinner with some friends. The wine and beer selection was pretty great as well!

I asked what they use for their Chai Latte and they said they have their own "mix. " I'm here to tell you.. . I have no clue what they gave me. I felt like it was peppermint spiced tea, with half water half steamed milk. It was pretty gross, and wasn't even remotely close to a Chai latte. I also tried to make convo with the Barista's. They were having none of that. They just wanted to work, I guess. Maybe jam to their awesome playlist, which I can definitely give them credit for. Their desserts and pastries looked amazing! So I had to take home some cookies. I chose a sugar cookie and mexican cookie. The sugar cookie was that weird crumbly kind. I like doughy goodness. I'm not wasting my calories on a bad cookie. The mexican cookie was just the same consistency. Ugh! Too bad, the place is super cute, but in my opinion it's an utter fail. Oh wait, free internets. Not a total loss.. . Sorry buds!

First time because AMEX for whatever reason didn't book National this time. They even told me it was the same company which is clearly not the case. Arriving, the guy propose me all the insurance that I have to take. It increases the price of the renting by 3.. . (400$ to +1200$) So from cheap prices AMEX told me, I got a 3 times higher bill now. We quickly searched our phones and found a highly recommended Italian restaurant a few blocks from our hotel. We walked there, enjoying the sights and sounds of the city. The name of the restaurant was Pizzeria 311 and it sounded good. We were greeted by a friendly host who showed us to our table. The restaurant was located in a charming neighborhood with many shops and bars nearby. The atmosphere inside was cozy and inviting, with a warm and welcoming decor. We looked at the menu and were impressed by the variety of dishes. We ordered a few starters, including a salad and a bruschetta. The smell of freshly baked dough filled the air and made our mouths water in anticipation. For the main course, we ordered three different kinds of pizza: a classic margherita, a meat-lover's and a vegetarian with roasted vegetables. The pizzas were cooked to perfection, with a crispy crust and generous toppings. Both were delicious and fresh, with flavors that burst in the mouth. We also ordered a side of pasta, which was cooked al dente and had a rich, creamy sauce. The flavors were rich and well balanced, and we ate every bite. Throughout the meal, the service was attentive and friendly. Our waiter was knowledgeable about the menu and made excellent recommendations. Our overall experience at Pizzeria 311 was excellent. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food. We would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal in Pittsburgh. The food was delicious, the atmosphere was cozy and the service was excellent. We are already looking forward to our next visit.

I chose this restaurant based off its Yelp reviews. I had heard good things about the food and the service, so I was excited to try it for myself.When we arrived, we were immediately seated at a cozy little table in the corner. Our server was very attentive and quickly took our drink orders. We started with the calamari appetizer, which was lightly fried and served with a delicious marinara sauce.For our main courses, I ordered the seafood pasta and my husband got the chicken parmesan. The seafood pasta was loaded with shrimp, scallops, and mussels, and the sauce was perfectly seasoned. My husband's chicken parmesan was also very good, with a crispy breading and a flavorful tomato sauce.We were both very happy with our meals and the service. The prices were also very reasonable. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great Italian meal.Overall, the food was delicious and the service was impeccable. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a cozy and casual dining experience. The prices were also very reasonable. I would definitely come back again.In terms of the actual writing style, I tried to use informal language and colloquialisms, contractions, and personal anecdotes and experiences. I also used short, simple sentences, sentence fragments, and exclamations.

Based on food alone it would be a single star, however the staff really tried to make it up to us. My husband and I ate here this evening. First off we were accosted by a quasi-speed metal song that was completely inappropriate to the setting. We were seated promptly without a reservation and the waiter quickly took our order. The server brought some cold, salty garlic rolls. Not an encouraging start to the meal but we plowed ahead -- my husband ordered chicken parmesan and I ordered butternut squash ravioli. The chicken was breaded in what looked to be almost a cracker or corn flake crust rather than breadcrumbs, making it heavy. The plate was just a big pile of spaghetti topped with this chicken wedge glued with red sauce. Not attractive, adequately tasty. My ravioli was barely cooked. Some parts weren't cooked at all, making an unappetizing paste-y glob. The server was quick to notice something amiss and quickly replaced the plate with another entree, the eggplant parmesan. Way too salty and an unholy mess of cheese and overcooked spaghetti. The side of spinach was also much too salty and I finally threw in the towel, completely defeated by this awful meal. Maybe it was an off night but the people around us didn't seem to be having the same issues with their meals. If this is the best Italian food that Charlotte has to offer, than I am forewarned. The manager came over and asked if there was anything he could do, offered to comp us a dessert and generally tried to make things right. It was unfortunate that the meal was unsalveageable.

I finally decided to check out Bank of America Stadium for myself and witness the Panthers play in person. Nothing compares to experiencing the electricity of an NFL game live rather than on television. As I entered the stadium on game day, the palpable excitement and buzz from fans packed in was incredible. It was fun seeing jerseys and gear worn proudly by supporters of all ages filling the seats. Finding my lower level spot, a vast sea of black and blue stretched as far as the eye could see. The pregame flyover and ceremonies were an awesome spectacle to behold up close. When Carolina's offense took the field, the roar of the crowd was deafening. Watching Christian McCaffrey dart around in real time is breathtaking. It's astounding how fast players move in the flesh. Fans' energy and passion was infectious, amplifying my fandom. Nothing compares to celebrating big plays and scores with 60,000+ rowdy fans as one. Seeing 6'5" defensive ends barrel toward the quarterback right in front me was surreal. Being so near gave new respect for players' immense size and athletic prowess. Though the Panthers fell behind early, fans cheered loudly all game in support. Wandering concourses at halftime allowed taking in more of the stadium's sights. Giant screens and boards make following the action easy from anywhere. Improved concessions and amenities enhanced the fan experience. Even in defeat, attending my first Panthers game is a treasured memory that will long endure.

Concourse C.. starting with the nasty B at Wolfgang Puck.. .I ordered a breakfast sandwich hoping for something fast and filling before my long flight. However, the sandwich was tiny and overpriced. The egg was dry and tasteless. At least the coffee was decent, though it too was overpriced for an airport. Feeling disappointed by Wolfgang Puck, I browsed the other options in Concourse C. Most were chains I seen plenty of times before. Then I noticed a small stall serving Southern specialties. On a whim I ordered brisket tacos, not expecting much. To my surprise, the tacos were delicious! Tender brisket, fresh veggies and a tasty sauce hit the spot. I was sad to finish my tacos, as my flight was soon to board. While most of Concourse C was lackluster, those brisket tacos redeemed the whole airport experience. I left feeling satisfied instead of ripped off.

I visited this establishment on Saturday, November 29, 2014, and I must say, it was an unforgettable experience! From the moment we stepped inside, we were warmly welcomed and received exceptional hospitality. The interior decor exuded both elegance and coziness, setting the perfect ambiance for the evening ahead.We kicked off our meal with their renowned appetizer, the crispy calamari, and it was truly a delight. The batter was light and crispy, while the calamari itself was tender and bursting with flavor. The dipping sauce provided a tangy accompaniment that perfectly complemented the dish.For the main course, I took a leap and opted for the seafood risotto, and I was absolutely blown away. The combination of perfectly cooked shrimp, scallops, and mussels with the creamy risotto was divine. Each bite was packed with tantalizing flavors, and the portion size was more than satisfactory.Meanwhile, my partner went for the grilled ribeye steak, and it was prepared to perfection. The steak was tender and juicy, with a delicious charred crust. The mashed potatoes and roasted vegetables served alongside elevated the dish, providing a delectable depth of flavors.To round off our extraordinary dining experience, we couldn't resist indulging in their decadent chocolate lava cake for dessert. As soon as we cut into it, a warm and gooey chocolate interior emerged, creating a heavenly combination with the moist cake. It truly was a dream come true for chocolate aficionados.What truly stood out throughout our meal was the impeccable service. The staff was attentive and well-informed, offering expert recommendations and ensuring that our dining experience exceeded all expectations. Their attentiveness to detail and genuine passion for their craft was remarkable.The restaurant boasted a delightful atmosphere, with soft lighting and soothing background music, making it an ideal venue for a romantic dinner or a celebratory occasion.

The first thought that ran thru my head: Do they have prosciutto and cappicola? The answer: Prosciutto- yes; cappicola- no. So I ran in to get my cold cuts, looking forward to a phenomenal lunch. The quality of the meat was very good. The service, not so much. I stood at the counter nearly 25 minutes as he cut me 1/2 pound of turkey, prosciutto, american cheese, mozzarella, and bologna. 25 MINUTES! On top of it, the guy wrapped the meat soooooo tight that it took me another 20 minutes to unwrap to make a sandwich. Also, what kind of a market doesn't have bread you can buy? Literally, the entire store, NO BREAD! The only way I could have gotten bread was to order a sandwich and take it off. Will LBD be going back to this place you ask? Undecided. If I do, he will definitely order his meats before he goes, to ensure he doesn't have to wait any longer. This place needs improvement in the meats department. LBD scale- 3. PICK UP YOUR GAME!

The hostess barely looked up from her phone to greet us, and the waitress seemed put out by our presence. The bartender was the only friendly face we encountered, but even he couldn't make up for the overall unfriendly atmosphere. The menu was uninspired and overpriced, with few items that stood out. The entrees were similarly unimpressive, with the steak overcooked and the pasta swimming in sauce. We ordered a few appetizers, but they were all disappointing, especially the supposedly famous buffalo wings, which were bland and tasteless. The ambiance was also underwhelming. The dining room was cramped and noisy, with poor lighting and uncomfortable chairs. The decor was uninspired and lacked any real character. We were thoroughly disappointed with our experience and would not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

We decides to try out this new restaurant that we had been hearing a lot about. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a modern decor that immediately caught our atention. Our server greeted us promptly and had our drink orders. The menu offer ed a diverse selection of dishes, ranging from traditional fare to more adventurous options. We were eager to try their firma dish, the Truffle Burger, which did not disappoint. The burgers was cooked to perfection, with a juicy patty and crispy bacon. I was hoping that this new Indian restaurant would fill the void and become our go-to place for delectable curry and flavorful dishes. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted by the vibrant and inviting atmosphere, adorned with beautiful traditional Indian artwork. The staff members were friendly and attentive, eager to assist me with any questions I had about the menu. Now, let me tell you about the food. The buffet spread was an absolute feast for the senses! The aroma of spices wafted through the air, enticing my taste buds from the moment I approached the food counter. I was delighted to find a wide variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, ensuring that there was something for everyone.The flavors were simply exceptional. Each dish was expertly spiced, providing a perfect balance of heat and richness. From the creamy butter chicken to the fragrant biryanis, every bite transported me to the streets of India. The naan bread was soft and fluffy, complementing the curries perfectly. Moreover, the buffet was constantly replenished, ensuring that the food remained fresh and hot throughout my dining experience. The staff also made sure to regularly check on the diners, making recommendations and catering to any special dietary requirements or preferences.To top it off, the dessert selection was a delightful surprise. The assortment of sweets, including gulab jamun and rasmalai, was the perfect end to the meal. Each sweet treat was indulgent and full of authentic flavors, leaving me completely satisfied.In conclusion, I am overjoyed to have discovered this gem of an Indian restaurant. It has not only filled the void left by the closure of Maharaja but has surpassed my expectations in terms of food quality and service. I will definitely be returning to savor more of their delicious offerings and highly recommend it to anyone seeking a memorable Indian dining experience in Pittsburgh.

The front desk personnel were helpful in pointing us in the right direction to get started seeing what the city has to offer, and our room was clean and comfortable. The free breakfast buffet is standard Hampton fare: waffle maker, omelet or scrambled eggs, sausage or bacon, bread, muffins, bagels, a selection of cereals and yogurts, juices, coffee, etc. Wi-Fi is free throughout the visit, you just need to log in again once every 24 hours for each device. The location is good, just a few blocks from Tyron Street and very close to a train station that can take you around downtown. It's also very close to the NASCAR museum and the convention center. Parking is I think $10 a day for self-parking, which is a lot for a Hampton. It's in a garage, which is nice, but the speed bumps (four per level) are really obnoxiously big, requiring that you basically come to a complete stop before going over them unless you're interested in risking suspension damage and incurring the cost of reseating your kidneys. Park on levels 4 or 5 for direct access to the hotel via a small corridor connecting the buildings. It's much easier than the other levels, where you have to take an elevator down to ground level, walk through the entrance, then to the elevator up to your room.

That's hard to find in Uptown unless you are at the epicenter. The food - well, mixed bag. The beef short ribs.. tasty, but nothing to write home about. My girlfriend and I both had the red beans and rice with roasted turkey.. .. now when you hear roasted turkey what do you think? I'll wait a minute while you ponder this.. .. .. well what we got was turkey sausage.. . it was bizarre. It was sliced and didn't taste bad, but we were confused. Actually waited several minutes for our waitress to come back to check on us - we asked if we'd gotten the wrong meals.. she said no. Well, it took her so long to come back that by the time we dug in our food was only warm.. . now that's on us I guess.. . but, the food was luke warm and bland. I never reach for hot sauce.. and I reached for it here. The desserts.. . now those were on point. The coconut cake - best i've had beyond Red Rocks. So to recap: nnFood - 2 starsnDesserts - 4 stars For an avg of 3 stars.

The moment I walked through the quaint door, I was greeted by the sweet aroma of freshly baked bread and pastries. The display case was filled with mouth-watering treats, from flaky croissants to rich chocolate cakes. The warm and welcoming atmosphere made me feel right at home. It was obvious that the bakers took great pride in their work. After careful consideration, I decided to indulge in their signature almond croissant. The flaky layers melted in my mouth. The buttery croissant was a delight to the taste buds. It was pure bliss. Since that first visit, I have become a regular customer. The menu offers a wide variety of choices, catering to different dietary preferences and restrictions. The staff is incredibly friendly and always ready to offer recommendations or engage in a friendly chat. There are plenty of gluten-free and vegan options to choose from. What sets this bakery apart is not only the quality of the baked goods, but also the exceptional customer service. Apart from the delectable pastries, the coffee is also excellent. They serve a variety of specialty coffees, each cup carefully crafted. Their passion for baking is contagious and it shows in every interaction. The cozy atmosphere is perfect for a solo visit or a get-together with friends. The comfortable seating offers a quiet place to enjoy your treats while catching up on work or relaxing with a good book.

Cons: Management was extremely rude and condescending when I had a problem that needed fixing. You have to take care of the A/C units, maintenance doesn't do that unless it is irreparably broken. My shower leaked, but they told me just to turn the knobs tighter. .. sure dude. Still leaks. My toilet would run unless I jiggled the handle. When I moved in, I had to mop the floor 7 times to get clean water, the stovetop was caked with food, and oil was everywhere. Of course I cleaned as much to my ability, and then I got a notice saying that I wasn't keeping up with my lease b/c of some girl before me's mess. Sorry, but when the stovetop is brown from her burning shit, and I clean it to something passable, I shouldn't be penalized for this. Also, the water was shut off multiple times unannounced, and when I mentioned it and asked if they could just send out a notice, maybe detailing future outages, or even just an email saying how long it would be, I got a snarky reply saying that "emergencies happen, and blame the City of Pittsburgh because we won't be sending out any emails. "nnNOT worth your money. Find a better management who doesn't take your money and piss on you. I never write reviews, but was so irate that I had to post this. Just treat me with respect, that's all I ask.

Food is okay, and service is good, but it's just not that great. The food alone would be 4 stars if they were charging a bit less (Yes - I think value matters. Almost anyone can serve you an above-average meal if price isn't an issue. ) The empanada was pretty good, but $3. 50 for a tiny little beef empanada is ridiculous. They're street food, for chrissake. (The pickled onion condiment with them is really good, though. ) I had the tortilla de papa, which was pretty good, and my partner had a chicken dish (name escapes me) that was pretty good as well, and the salads were good. Back to the pricing thing: they do have Inca Kola, which I love, but they charge $2. 50 for a can. I only got one because my partner had never had one, but $2. 50? Really? I know the profit's in the drinks for restaurants, but a 12-pack of it cost the same as a 12 of Coke the last time I saw it in a grocery store. Service was good. Very friendly. 4 stars. Decor leaves much to be desired. This is usually an area that doesn't bug me too much with restaurants, but this place looks ratty - worn carpet, cheap tile, faded pictures of someone's trip to Peru, furniture that looks like it belongs in a chain motel breakfast room. The knickknacks for sale are nice, but they're not in a separate area, so it feels like you're eating in the middle of a gift shop. Again, not awful if you're charging $5-7 or so per plate, but not when you've crossed the $10 threshold. 1 star. I'm split between 2 and 3 stars, but I'm skewing low on this place.

While visiting Charlotte, we wanted a place within walking distance from our hotel, The Hyatt House (fabulous place). We asked the folks at the front desk for a recommendation and they immediately suggested Village Tavern. Figured we'd give it a shot since it was just down the street. The restaurant had a cool downtown vibe going with brick walls and dim lighting. We got there around 7 so it was starting to fill up but they squeezed us into a table right away. The waitress, Sam, was super friendly and quick with recommendations since we couldn't decide. I ended up going with the charcuterie plate and my partner got the shrimp and grits. Let me tell ya, the food did not disappoint. That charcuterie platter had like five kinds of meat and cheese and I was in hog heaven. The shrimp and grits were creamy and bursting with flavor too. We were too full for dessert but I spotted a couple cutting into a huge slice of pie that looked amazing. My only complaint was that the music was pretty loud so we had trouble conversing at times. After dinner we walked around the surrounding downtown area, it was neat to see all the old buildings Lit up at night. Ended up back at the Hyatt with full bellies and feeling right at home thanks to the Village Tavern folks. Definitely recommend stopping in if you find yourself in Charlotte for a night!

It's dying for Chef Ramsey to come in and do a turnaround on it. It's textbook "We've lost the love of cooking" and now takes the easy way out and used canned everything. Even the "world famous pies" are frozen perfectly round manufactured pizzas with congealed cheese in one gross layer and no flavor. It's like a mini-frisbee with a little cheap pizza sauce and gross elementary school cheese. I ate one of the 8 slices of the pizza and called it quits. The lunch side salad came in a little bowl with iceberg lettuce and an INCH of Italian dressing. Yes, an inch. It was ridiculous. The lasagna and spaghetti is very generic. The only thing I can say anything positive about (besides the awesome kitschy interior is the seafood dish with bechamel sauce, but you can only get it once every 2 years for fear of heart attack because it's so rich. I'm sounding hateful, not because I want them to go away, which I don't but because I want them to reinvigorate their menu to be authentic Italian (or heck, even Greek since they're greek! ) I love the place, but it's not enough to get me to eat the food, so that says a lot. I wanted to be a regular, but I just can't stomach it. I might phone up Gordon to save them from themselves.. .

I have updates on the gluten-free beer situation and the nacho situation. GF Beer: MUCH improved from what I remember. They had at least three varieties of the "deglutenized" beers - Estrella Damm Daura and both the Amber and Blonde Brunehaut (from Belgium! ). They MAY have had Omission as well. nThey also have at least three varieties of New Planet, and at least two of Greens. Dogfish Head T'weasonale. Possibly New Grist and Tread Lightly? I was in a haze of deliciously non-gluteny beer at this point. Nachos: Maybe I'm recalling incorrectly, but I think when I've had these in the past they are made with real cheese - you know, shredded and melted. This time they were served with that nasty-ass liquid cheese goop, like you get at a ballpark. Blegh. Still four stars overall! Avoid the nachos though. nn---nnThe only food I've ever had here is nachos, so I can't speak to that. I WILL speak to the beer selection, though! I've managed to collect quite an assortment of beer snob friends, who love spending hours (literally) in the Cave o' Beer. I have to eat gluten free, so most ordinary beers are off-limits for me, BUT, they have an enormous selection of hard cider! Many many different kinds, including my favorite cider in the whole world, JK Scrumpy. Totally reasonable prices, too. Now the bad: n1. They close at midnight! After the downstairs closes you can take your drink upstairs to a little bar, but it's super loud, has no seating, and you don't have access to the magical treasure trove of beer. Boooo. n2. This is totally a niche thing, but I wish they had a better selection of gluten-free beers. There are lots of tasty ones out there, but they often only have Bards and Redbridge.

Ladies and Gentleman, welcome to pancake heaven. I kid you not, this place is a breakfast lover's paradise. As soon as we stepped through the doors of this charming little diner, the sweet aroma of freshly cooked pancakes wafted through the air, instantly putting a smile on my face. The friendly waitress led us to our table, and I couldn't help but admire the rustic decor and cozy ambiance of the place.Now, let's talk pancakes. Oh boy, where do I begin? They have a pancake selection that will blow your mind. From classic buttermilk to decadent chocolate chip and everything in between. My taste buds were tempted to order one of each, but my waistline urged me to be reasonable. So, I settled on their signature blueberry pancakes, and my girlfriend went for the banana pecan option.When the pancakes arrived at our table, my jaw dropped. These golden beauties were fluffy and piled high, topped with a generous dollop of whipped cream and a cascade of fresh berries. It was like a work of art on a plate. And the taste? Pure magic. The blueberries burst with juiciness, adding a delightful sweetness to every bite. The pancakes were perfectly cooked, with a slightly crispy edge and a melt-in-your-mouth center.As we devoured our pancakes, we couldn't help but notice the heavenly symphony of laughter and chatter around us. The restaurant was buzzing with families, friends, and pancake enthusiasts alike. It was as if everyone had discovered this hidden gem and couldn't resist its tempting delights.Now, let's not forget the syrup. They had a whole array of choices, from traditional maple to unique flavors like caramel and blueberry compote. I opted for the maple syrup, pouring it generously over my stack, letting it soak into every crevice. Each bite was an explosion of flavors, the sweetness of the syrup melding perfectly with the fruity goodness of the blueberries.In between bites, I glanced over at my girlfriend, and her eyes were filled with pure joy.

Perhaps there is an Italian village where this is identical to what they serve, but I have never been there. I've never been to Italy at all. So I'll say this instead: This is not what qualifies as "Good Italian American. "nnI've enjoyed Mama Ricotta's catering before, and even dinner several times over the last decade. But tonight, despite not having to pay, having two glasses of Chianti, and having the gal at the bar give me her phone number, I was disappointed. Jamal served us with precision and a smile. One busboy was nice enough to crumble bread on my jacket, then look down at my jacket as if its presence offended him. The rolls.. . these are dinner rolls, coated in oil. They stiffened within minutes, which generally says they spent time in a microwave. The oily rolls also came with a dish full of oil. A dish of oil is a decent gesture in most Italian restaurants, but this oil was spicy. And more spicy than I prefer. But if you are from that Italian village where they dip oily rolls in spicy oil, this is your place. The highly recommended Warm Goat Cheese and Mascarpone Dip was pleasant tasting. Rich marinara surrounding creamy mascarpone, with bread of proper consistency. In fact, I wish they served a version of this bread as their dinner bread. The presentation could be better. Looked like a dying sunflower made of bread. For the main course, I chose Pasta Primavera. While flavorful, and a big heaping plate, this was also heavy laden in oil. A deep pool of oil. My benefactor ordered angel hair pasta with tomato basil sauce plus shrimp. She appeared pleased, although this may have had more to do with the man across from her, or her drink, or both. Or neither.

I came here for brunch last weekend with a big group. They were very accomodating to us throughout the reservation process and the brunch, which was good. And our waiter, Daniel, was great. The previous reviewer who said the Bloody Mary is the best drink was spot-on. It had a great spice and was the only drink that seemed like it had any alcohol in it at all. The mimosa and sangria were very "eh. " nnI loved my smoked salmon appetizer (and that did seem to be the hit at the table), but entrees around the table left people disappointed. The goat cheese and mushroom omelette could have had a heckuva lot more goat cheese and mushrooms, and my scallop/sausage/grits/egg dish just had way too much going on. The grits were actually fabulous, but the scallops were overcooked and got lost next to the scrambled eggs (? ) and sage sausage crumbles. If I lived in Pittsburgh, I could see myself coming back here for wine and appetizers, but I'm not sure I would make it a regular brunch or dinner spot.

The Good: nThis placement is in a pretty prime location downtown as it is situated to some of the best eateries downtown (Merts, Pita Pit), a few blocks from Bobcat Realm, walking distances to Bank of America Stade, and a stones throw from the heart of Charlotte (Trade/Tryon). The rooms are decently sized and retained clean. While the building is older, it has been well held. Staff are affable and helpful at the front desk. There is a 24 hour capability room with new equipment. Meals included basic options like pastries, fruit, yogurt and oatmeal which held me over. Parking is in a secure garage which is incessantly convenient. The walls are thicker than most hotels so noise from nearby rooms was never an problem. WiFi worked well and was fast enough for tranny. Pets are welcome which is great for tourist with furry friends. While not luxury, for the location and price this hotel given a comfortable stay and was perfectly insufficient for my needs. I'd happily stay here again when visiting Carolina. Other nearby hotels are usually more expensive for likened amenities. Overall it's a sounds budget-friendly option well-located downtown.

But to my surprise, the experience at Primanti Bros. was far from the catastrophic disaster I had anticipated. As soon as I stepped foot in the vibrant restaurant, the inviting aroma of sizzling fries and savory sandwiches enveloped my senses. The friendly staff immediately greeted me with warm smiles and guided me to a cozy booth. Lifting the burdensome menu, I was overwhelmed by the extensive selection of mouthwatering sandwich options. From their legendary "Almost Famous" pastrami and cheese to the hearty turkey club piled high with crispy bacon, every sandwich seemed like a cornerstone in its own right. Ultimately, I settled on the classic signature sandwich, The Pitts-Burger. When the colossal creation arrived at my table, piled high with a generous portion of tender grilled meat, tangy coleslaw, sweet and sour onion, and crispy French fries, my taste buds rejoiced. The combination of flavors was nothing short of heavenly, and the soft Italian bread held the robust ingredients together perfectly. In addition to the stellar sandwiches, Primanti B ros. also impressed with their selection of craft beers. I couldn't resist trying a local brew, and the hoppy IPA I chose paired beauitfully with the rich flavors of my burrito. Furthermore, the atmosphere at Primanti Bros. was energetic and lively, with a mix of locals and enthusiastic sports fans. The walls adorned with Pittsburgh sports memorabilia and the constant buzz of conversation created a sense of camaraderie that made me f eel right at home. As I indulged in my meal, I couldn't help but notice the efficient and attentive service. Despite the bustling crowd, the waitstaff ensured that everyone's needs were m et promptly and with a genuine smile. It was evident that they took pride in delivering an exceptional dining experience to each guset. To top off my extraordinary meal, I decided to sample their famous cheesecake.

We waited over an hour for our food to arrive, and when it finally did, it was cold and tasteless. The staff did not acknowledge us until we ordered, and could not answer the most basic questions about their products. The atmosphere of the restaurant was also very unwelcoming, and we felt like we were a burden to the staff. Besides the poor service, the food was also very disappointing. The dishes were bland and tasteless, and the portions were very small. We will never return to this restaurant. The prices were also very high, and we felt like we were ripped off. Our overall experience at this restaurant was terrible. We would not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

However, my recent experience disappointed me and hesitated. The quality of food has decreased significantly, and the dishes lack the flavor and freshness I have liked. In addition, some of the sizes were greatly reduced, which made me feel dissatisfied and questioned that it was worth it. The service that once concentrated and friendly has become bland. Our order took a long time to arrive. Even so, they were still incorrect and must be sent back to the kitchen. The villager's vibrant atmosphere has also been reduced, and the lack of attention to cleanliness and overall shabby appearance. The staff seemed to be at a loss and chaotic, and worked hard to keep up with the influx of customers. Sadly, the decline in quality and service made me explore other dining options to find a better experience. The glory of Villa may have passed, and it is a pity to see a once great institution from falling off the grace.

My husband & I went here based on the reviews from here. The restaurant had a cozy atmosphere and we were quickly seated despite it being a busy Saturday night. Our server was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. We started with the fried calamari appetizer which was light and crispy. For our entrees, I had the chicken parmesan and my husband had the shrimp scampi. Both dishes were delicious and the perfect portion caliber. The chicken was tender and full of flavor beneath the creamy parmesan topping. The shrimp were cooked to perfection in the light garlic buttr sauce over linguine. We decided to split a slice of the chocolate cake for dessert which was rich and moit. The service was attentive without being arrogant throughout our entire meal. I would definitely come back and attempt other items on the menu that we didn't have a chance to sample this time. While not the cheapest restuarant in town, the quality of food and service made it worth the price. We both left fully satisfied and looking forward to returning again soon. I'm glad we took the chance founded on the positive reviews and it did not disappoint. The atmosphere, food and customer service all exceeded our forecast. I would highly recommend checking this place out if you're looking for a quality dining experience without needing reservation.

Before I continue, I will come out and say that all of the food was a little tough - the eggroll especially(As was warned) - and the rice had some dark spots(I assume it was from the bottom of the cooking vessel). I'd never been to Casbah before until this past Sunday when we decided to check it out for their prix-fixe menu. For $22, you get your choice of alcoholic brunch beverage, an appetizer and an entree. An incredible price for a serious amount of great food. They had many options on their fixed menu - something for everyone. From huge waffles and omelets to lamb dishes, fish and the usual brunch regulars such as eggs benedict too. The appetizers list was equally as large. I started with a bloody mary. Was a nice middle ground between heavy and light - and it had some kick to it. Very good. For an appetizer I got the cheese and fruit plate with french baguette slices. There was a soft brie-like goat cheese, a blue cheese and a mild dry sheeps milk cheese as well. All were wonderful. For my entree I went with the Salmon Eggs Benedict. It was perfect. The fruit on the side was fresh cut, and the home fries were crispy on the outside, soft on the inside. I tasted a couple of other things as well. Both the polenta and the mushroom soup on the appetizer list were great. Didn't try any of the other entrees, but everyone seemed pleased. The only complaint was from a friend that ordered the truffle omelet - and it was that he thought they went too heavy on truffle oil, drowning out the eggs. Also, service was absolutely perfect. We had a tall waiter, forget his name, but he was one of the most professional servers I've ever had. The table was cleared and cleaned immediately.. . he was never pushy, always friendly, and had great suggestions. One of the best experiences I've had for restaurant service anywhere. For brunch in Pittsburgh, this is my favorite so far. Not to be missed! Now I just need to make plans to go back for dinner.

My first visit to this restaurant left me pleasantly surprised. From the moment I stepped through the door, I was greeted with a warm and inviting atmosphere. I don't think I ask much out of a driving range. Decent mats, clean balls and accessible hours. Hell you need even less people now with the advent of the machine that doles out the balls. This place has none of them. It is april and there are no grass tees yet. BTW they opened for the season this week although it has been golfing weather for a month. The mats look like the carpet at my 107 year old aunt Irene's house. Worn and thread bare. Let's talk about the hours. This place is equipped with lights yet they only sell buckets of balls until 730. It is still light out. Finally lets you have the pit to hit into. When I arrived I wasn't sure if this was a driving range or an excavation site for a mastodon or a strip mining operation. There is no grass on the range. Just mud. Makes it a good tool to figure out how far you actually are hitting the ball. Oh, they are cash only also. Bottom line, this place sucks. The best hope is that the owner sells it to someone that actually wants to make money and service golfers in Pittsburgh.

This is my favorite place in the area. If I can, I eat here every day. Food is always fresh and delicious, and the service is first -class. I have been here for many years, and I have never experienced bad experiences. The menu has a lot of options, and the price is very reasonable. I am a loyal fan of their breakfast, especially Benytik eggs. It is made of high -quality ingredients, while Dutch sauce is for death. I also like their lunch and dinner choices. These options are made of fresh local ingredients. The atmosphere is comfortable and attractive, comfortable and friendly seats. I bring many friends and family members here, and they all like it. In fact, my mother once worked here, and she still stopped visiting the staff occasionally. The only disadvantage is that it may be busy on weekends, but waiting is always worth it. In general, I strongly recommend anyone who is looking for delicious rice in a leisure and enthusiastic atmosphere.

Awful. No stars. n I guess we should have taken our clues form the emptiness of the restaurant and the fact happy our lasted until closing.. .. nThe margarita was a sickly peach color and was solid in the pitcher. nThe plates were served with the thumb of a dirty oven mitt in the food (I'm guessing they came out of the microwave). nThe enchiladas were slimy and water-logged covered in a dilute, flavorless "mole" (i wouldn't call it that. nThe rice was instant and without any seasoning, not even salt, with a couple bits of also favor less corn. We walked in and it was pretty busy. We waited a few minutes for an empty table and found one. We cleaned if off ourselves and that was okay with me. I was pretty excited about this place because of the reviews and other personal recommendations. I ordered a ham and cheese sandwich and my partner ordered one with more than one type of lunch meat. The sandwiches were simply sandwiches with coleslaw and French fries on top. There was nothing special about it and it's something easily made at home. The price was good. For a beer, coke, and two sandwiches we got of there for under $20. The condition of the women's restroom was horrible. It ruined my appetite. You'd think with such a reputation that that condition of the restroom would be a bit nicer. The restaurant itself was in crappy shape as well. I expect dive bars to look like this. Next time I'm in Pittsburgh, I won't be coming back to a Primanti Bros. There's surely better food out there and a better dining environment.

This is the BEST place in Pittsburgh to find lighting. We were in the market for a nice crystal chandelier for our kitchen and had more than enough choices to pick from. We have had a hard time before yesterday finding a nice enough crystal chandelier in town (or getting good customer service from other stores). Also, had the problem of not being able to see merchandise at other places. NOT the case at Lighting by Erik! We worked with one of the owner's and she was a complete joy to work with, and full of passion for her job (a rare find these days)! She took her time, was thorough and made sure we loved what we were buying. Also, very impressed with their selection of fan options. They also have a fantastic selection of lamps, mirrors, tables and other home decor items. Will absolutely be purchasing from them again. Check it out, you will be impressed.

Gradually, over the past year, the prices have continued to increase to the point of being dinner menu prices for lunch size meals. Too bad, we used to really enjoy lunch there.

I recently came here for a safety recall having to do with the cruise control of my 2002 Ford Explorer. With the Midwest reputation of having some of the finest meats, it was a no brainer to order the 1/3 slab BBQ smoked ribs and pork shoulder sandwich combination dinner ($14. 75). The staff mentioned the pork shoulder and the beef brisket were the top sellers besides the ribs. The pork shoulder was pigilicious! The shredded meat was perfectly seasoned with the rub and then hickory smoked which gave its own taste without the addition of the BBQ sauce. It also impressed me because there were was no sign of grease on the pork. The bun was a standard bread bun compared to the sweet roll which accompanied the dinner combination. We took the recommendation of the staff and ordered the extra meat (additional 5 ounces for $3) since were feeling extra carnivorous! The BBQ pork ribs came with five succulent ribs with the meat just waiting to fall off the bone. Each bite had a generous coating of their famous award winning BBQ sauce. Our dinner combination came with two choices of side orders which we picked the baked beans and cole slaw. Both were served in a small styrofoam cups along with the BBQ sauce. It's easy to see why the BBQ sauce won numerous award because of it's rich, sweet and peppery flavor. I'm not a fan of cole slaw but this one exceed my expectations with its creaminess and was extra cold. The baked beans maintained a firm texture and should be ordered with any meal because the sauce was so addictive. The cabin style interior holds 11 tables and is very close to the Madison airport. The actual BBQ pit is located a few miles away from the restaurant. So grab your dental floss and wet naps and eat some authentic BBQ at Smoky Jon's!

I was in the area and decided to pop in for a quick lunch. I was seated right away by the hostess and my server, Maria, came over shortly after to take my drink and appetizer order. The decor was a little dated but was clean and well maintained. I ordered the bacon cheeseburger and onion rings. The burger was cooked perfectly and had great flavor. The onion rings were nice and crispy. The service was excellent and Maria was very attentive to my needs. Overall, I had a great experience and will definitely return.The restaurant is located in a small shopping center and there is plenty of parking. The restaurant is open for lunch and dinner and the prices are very reasonable. The menu has a wide variety of items to choose from and everything is made fresh to order. The service is always friendly and efficient. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal at a reasonable price.The restaurant is family-friendly and there is a kids' menu available. The restaurant also offers catering services for special events. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal at a reasonable price. I will definitely be back!

We were in town for a football game. It is a nice walk from the Omni to the BOA Stadium. All of the staff that we dealt with were VERY friendly and helpful. Now for all the rest. nn1. Parking nightmare. We arrived shortly after check-in time, so yes it was busy. There was some kind of problem with a car, or not enough valets or something, but we could not even get turned into the driveway of the hotel. It was very backed up. nn2. You enter on the ground floor and must ride the elevator 1 floor to the lobby. I'm sorry but that is a personal pet peeve. A. Did you really not have enough room for the lobby and front desk on the ground floor? B. you just told me there were no stairs to this exit. If that is a case, how am I going to get out in case of a fire? nn3. Our room overlooked the pool, and some of Charlotte. This was scenic- and NOISY. We were not in the room all day Saturday, but the hotel was choosing to play the same songs on the loudspeaker at the pool OVER and OVER and OVER. So while we were trying to watch other football games before heading to ours, it was quite annoying. nn4. The room was pretty small. I have stayed in larger rooms in much smaller cities. For $9. 00 more we could have had more space- but they were out of those rooms. nn5. Electrical cords. Maybe it was just my room, but there were lamp cords all over the floor. It is a miracle one of us did not trip. nn6. Bad lighting. Even with all those lamps- I still felt like there was not enough light- and the bathroom lighting? terrible. nn7. Water Pressure. I thought it was going to rip my skin off. Overall it seems like this hotel was poorly designed, that seems to be the root of most of the problems we had. If we were to stay in Uptown again we would stay elsewhere.

We ordered the wedge salad, an appetizer trio, and the wings (which I ordered extra crispy). The salad came first and was pretty good but seemed to not have any toppings except for the salad dressing. The appetizer trio came out next and was a bit of a disappointment. The potato skins weren't that good- mushy and no seasoning (salt/spice). Also, the bacon was soft and mushy. The nachos were edible but nothing to write home about- again a little mushy once you got below the ones on the top and the guacamole was pretty bland. The buffalo chicken planks were a little under-cooked for my taste but were otherwise good. The buffalo wings came out last and I was happy with them- they were done (crispy) the way I like them. The wings were what I was craving when I walked into the place- the void was filled. The service was a little slow. We sat at the bar and there were only 2 other people at the bar and only 1 table with 4 people elsewhere in the place. They seemed to be starting to close up at that time. It took about 10 minutes to get our drinks because the bartender dropped a wine bottle- so we had to wait for him to clean it up and hear his amazing account of the accident before being served. I would go back again the next time I crave wings (because decent wings are really hard to find in the South Hills). Maybe during the day the service will be faster. I will definitely order the wedge salad again and the wings but will be more careful when ordering the appetizer.

I had the misfortune of becoming a patient at Dr. Goldberg's office recently, and it was an experience that left me utterly disappointed and frustrated. From the moment I stepped into the waiting room, I sensed an air of disorganization and chaos. The receptionist seemed overwhelmed and didn't bother to greet me or even acknowledge my presence for several minutes. When I finally got called in, my initial impression of Dr. Goldberg was far from positive. He was dismissive and seemed disinterested in listening to my concerns. It felt as if he was just rushing through the appointment without giving me the attention or care I deserved. Moreover, his diagnostic skills were questionable at best. He made a hasty diagnosis without even considering other possibilities or conducting the necessary tests. I left the office feeling more confused and unsure about my condition than when I arrived. The lack of follow-up from the doctor or his staff only worsened my frustration. Despite repeated attempts to contact them regarding my ongoing symptoms, I was met with silence and indifference. It's evident that Dr. Goldberg and his office prioritize quantity over quality, with little regard for the well-being of their patients. In conclusion, I strongly advise anyone in need of medical care to avoid this doctor and his office at all costs. There are plenty of competent and compassionate healthcare providers out there who genuinely prioritize their patients' health and well-being.

We came over this past summer for food and cocktails, but this last visit was just for the booze to have a celebratory drink with Laura M on her Birthday after seeing a great Ballet at the Benedum. nI don't mind O&T layout. It's a bit chopped up but very Pittsburghese reminiscent of most establishments. There is the upstairs where you can sit by the roaring fire on the 72" flat screen or lounge on many of the couches or loveseats they have available. There is also the downstairs that seems to have similar offerings, however at least in our experiences was a lot busier than upstairs. I pick less busy almost every time. This time around we found three bar seats available upstairs and settled down for a couple drinks. nI started with a Southern Tier XXX IPA, solid start to the evening. I know they specialize in Martinis but I specialize in craft beer. After that I decided to try a martini, I went with an Espresso Manhattan Martini. This was defreakinlishious.. . I love coffee and I love manhattans so the two went together like peas and carrots. Our service was mixed. Some bartenders seemed more helpful and interested in waiting on us than others. This was also my experience from last time. This time we didn't order food though we were pretty hungry and went elsewhere to eat. Our last meal here was not worth duplicating. We both had an Olive or Twist Burger, and I chose sweet potato fries and requested a med rare cook. We used the Yelp deal so it wasn't as expensive as it could have been, but the burger sells for $13. 00. I rarely complain about cost especially if it is good, however it really was not. The meat was way overcooked and dry. Surprisingly the fries were the best thing on the plate. To spend that on a burger I do expect a better quality. So lesson learned, we had some tasty drinks here last weekend, but ate at a neighboring facility afterwards. I'm sure we will be back for drinks again.

nWhen my son was receiving treatments for spine/ brain cancer, at UW Hospital, we did not have many choices at that time of where to stay during and between treatments. My son would become so ill from all the radiation plus chemo, and the radiation treatments were at two 6 hour intervals every day, So we couldn't venture far most days. nAltho we had spent time at the Ronald McDoanld house, after a time I needed to make my son feel less a patient and more like a celebrity for a day. So I decided to take a paycheck, and chose a day between visits to get a suite at the Marriott West. nAltho my son had to use a mobile IV unit, and was scarred on his head from radiation burns, this Marriott was most accomodating and incredible. nWe had a gorgeous suite, exquistie room service and gracious attentions. nThese attentions were NOT triggered by my sons illness, but sincerely born from true proffesionalism and great training. nThis is a beautiful establishment, and I personally cannot stand the voices of spoiled whiners on these previous reviews. nThis Marriott will hold dear to me always and is worthy of your travel time relaxing time, and most of all your needs no matter to what extent. nStop being so ridiculously spoiled and realize. nThis Marriott is above average.

I guess you could appealing this a minimalist approach, but I'm not sure that's necessarily a good thing. This restaurant is in a prime location on the North Side and has plenty of opportunity to capitalize on the growth in the area. That said, allow me to jump into some of the minuses: nnBeans and Greens appetizer - I love beans and greens, but was shocked by the amount of garlic the chef added.
