There's good reason - they have 4 pinball games! First of all, Pooley's is home to Mad Rollin Pinball (AKA Madison Pinball) - I haven't made it out for a tournament but it's exciting that they host. Madison Pinball is a group of local collectors and enthusiasts and the games you see at Pooley's come from them. Currently they have: Addams Family, Space Shuttle, Star Trek, and Fun House. I love Addams Family, in fact it's my second favorite pinball in Madison! It's a very fun game with some cool magnet effects, including a seance mode (you just have to check it out). Space Shuttle is really fascinating for an older game but may be slow-moving for folks who are interested in more modern pinball. Star Trek - variations of this game are common around Madison but its still a favorite game of mine. I first began to understand pinball strategy playing Star Trek and think its a great game to start a pinball obsession for anyone. Fun House is frustrating but a classic as well, another solid game. Next to Rossi's, I think this is the best place to bring a group for pinball. Outside of the games, Pooley's gets a win because the bartenders are always kind and a few of them are pinball nuts too.

from a distance this looks like a nice hotel. As I got closer though, I started to notice some issues. The outside looked like it could use a fresh coat of paint. When I walked into the lobby, it wasn't much better on the inside either. Everything just seemed a little dingy and worn down. I checked in at the front desk, but the lady helping me didn't seem very friendly. She barely looked up from her computer to greet me. My room wasn't ready yet so I had to leave my bags and come back later. Finally I was able to get to my room about an hour after checking in. The room itself was pretty small and basic. The carpet looked old and could have been replaced. The bathroom was cramped and outdated. The shower pressure wasn't great either. It took forever to get hot water. The beds were comfortable enough but the pillows were too flat. There was a tv but it was really old and the remote didn't always work right. Breakfast in the morning had very limited options. Overall, while the price was affordable, I don't think I would stay here again based on everything else. It needs some renovations to improve the whole experience.

Nonetheless oh boy, was I in for a surprise! From the moment I stepped into the establishment, I was welcomed with an overwhelming stench that made my eyes water. The decor was dated and tacky, with peling wallpaper and mismatched furniture that seemed to have seen better days. I reluctantly took a seat and ordered their highly recommended dish, hoping it would redeem the initial impression. To my dismay, the food arrived lukewarm and tasted as if it had been sitting under a heat lamp for hours. The presentation was lackluster, with sloppy plating and unappetizing color. The flavors were tasteless and lacked any depth or complexity that I had anticipated based on the reviews. It felt like the chef had completely lost their pass ion for cooking. The service was equally disappointing. The waitstaff seemed uninterested and inattentive, ignoring my requests for condiments and refills. It was clear that customer satisfaction was not a prioritize for them. As I looked around, I noticed other patrons sharing similarly frustrated express ions, their disappointment palpable. The prices, however, were exrbitant for the subpar experience. I couldn't help but feel cheated and wondered how this place managed to maintain any positive reviews at all. Perhaps those reviewers had never truly experienced quality food or exceptional service before. In conclusion, I can confidently say that this place fell far below my prospects. It was a complete letdown, and I woսld advise anyone considering dining here to look elsewhere. Save your money and treat yourself to a restaurant that truly values its customers and takes pride in delivering appetizing, meticulously prepared meals. Trust me, you won't regret avoid this disastrous dining experience.

I've looked up other hotels in the area and have decided upon the Omni. The Omni is very overrated. When we checked-in, they had a five day wedding celebration in progress. No bell captains available upon check-in. When we got up to the room, I was very surprised to see how outdated it was for the money. Ripped curtains, blown out light bulbs in bathroom. And most of the extra electrical outlets did not work. I had my cell phone charging, come to find out the outlet never worked. I switched it to another outlet, and, again, no charge. Upon my morning cup of coffee in the room, the mini creamers were sour. I called room service, and they never brought them up. Nor did they refresh the coffee station when they cleaned the room. No fresh creamers and two sugars for two days! I take my coffee serious. Lol. The second day in the morning starting at 7: 00 AM, I was woken by a pounding sound of music coming from the courtyard. This was the ritual going on for the wedding. It continued for two hours. If the wedding was going to be honored on the lower floors, they should have put the other guests on the upper floor to avoid all the commotion. The garbage cans on site were overflowing with garbage for two days. No one took the responsibility of emptying them. We paid good money for a nice, clean, quite break. Only to have nothing but a out of date room, tons of noise, and a unclean looking surrounding. Guests should have been forewarned of the wedding festivities when booking. Although, the staff was very accommodating, they weren't on a mini vacation, we were. The only thing we were offered was free coffee or a breakfast beverage in the morning! Also, be aware, if you don't join their rewards club, check your bill for a $9. 95 a day charge for Internet. We were really disappointed in this hotel and will not be returning at all. See attached pictures.

Every time I go there, food has always been good. They have a variety of choices on the menu to satisfy many different tastes. Although some dishes can be on the salty side, the taste is always bold and satisfactory. Sesame Chicken is one of my preferred orders -crispy outside and tender inside. Their kung fu chicken will not make mistakes. I also like them to choose to make lettuce packages. This is an interesting change in conventional meals. Even if they are busy, the service is usually fast. Most servers seem to know the menu very well and make suggestions. You can choose to eat or let food to eat food. Although it may not be the most affordable Chinese food, the weight is quite generous. Usually, you can get a lot of food you pay for you. I rarely feel that I have no money. Over the years, I have dine in many positions in Chang. No matter where I go, the quality has been consistent. Obviously, they have good standards and habits. The layout of the restaurant provides a considerable amount of space between the tables, so it will not feel too narrow. They are still clean, and you don't always see what you see in busy restaurants. All in all, Chang's burden, diversity, quality and convenience capabilities made me continue to come back. Even if there are many other Chinese food around, this chain is still one of my preferred choices.

The menu was extensive, with a wide variety of dishes to suit all tastes. The restaurant was comfortable, with soft lighting and comfortable seats, and the menu was extensive, with a wide variety of dishes to suit all tastes. I decided to try their signature dish, which looked good, but tasted disappointing. The flavours were not particularly strong, and the portion size was not up to the price. The service was adequate, with polite and attentive staff, but there were moments when they seemed overwhelmed and took longer to attend to our needs. The dessert menu was limited, and the one we chose did not leave a lasting impression. The food came promptly, but the overall experience was rather lacklustre, with average food and uninspiring flavours. I might consider returning, but would be careful what I ordered.

Alright, Casbah. You got me, you got me good. Dinner as I mentioned before was decent, but the brunch, amazing. Compared to dinner, brunch at Casbah is definitely the better meal and deal. I don't advocate playing favorites when it comes to siblings in the same family, but sometimes you can't help it. Brother Brunch gets the nod here. Brunch is basically a fixed set. For $28, you choose an adult beverage (or non-alcoholic), an appetizer, and an entree. They start you off with some pistachio scones, buttermilk biscuits, and cornbread. Perfect, I like to stretch before I get my grub on. For my Prix-Fixe (fixed set), I went with the mimosa, smoked salmon, and sea scallop fry. SMOKED SALMON: If you like smoked salmon, then you would enjoy this appetizer. It's what you would expect but also a larger size than I thought it would be! "Oh no, there's too much of something I like, " said nobody ever. Upon seeing the smoked salmon display fanned out on its plate with bits of egg, red onion, and aioli garnished over top, my salivary glands couldn't control themselves! SEA SCALLOP FRY: You know I love me some scallops. The dish came with two scallops, a small croissant, small bits of fennel sausage, a side of white corn grits, and a little bit of butternut squash and caramelized onions. I was tempted to go with the classic eggs/toast/waffle as an entree, but I am so glad I put on my big boy foodie stretchy pants and took a chance. It's not your typical brunch dish and it's one I would definitely recommend. All in all, fantastic brunch experience. Definitely felt comfortably full, but not in a self-hatred, "I-regret-this-decision-immediately" kind of way. Service was professional; our waitress kept the waters filled and came in to check on us a little after each dish was served.

CLT is one of those airports that is clean and straight forward but it really helps to know a few tips and tricks so you don't pull out your hair when you're waiting in line behind 26 teenagers who refuse to take their game systems out of the bag for security screening. Parking here is pretty affordable, I'm fairly certain that Daily Parking is still only $6 per day, and long term is $4 per day (thanks Bill F.! ). Coming from a Chicago native, that is ridiculously affordable. Once you head in, evaluate your security options. If you're a seasoned traveler, I recommend checkpoint A. It moves the fastest and its typically flooded with well-traveled business peeps. Oh, and really you can go through any security checkpoint and easily access your gate. That is, unless you're flying out of Gate E.. . prepare for a trek. To Faith D.'s point - use the moving sidewalks, but do offer the courtesy of moving to the side and letting walkers pass. If you've got some spare time, there are some cute little shops and restaurants around the 'port and tons of conveniently located ATMs. They also have a delicious little gelato place. So, yes, I can honestly say that I kinda like this airport. Yay for the QC!

Jimmy Tsang's Chinese Restaurant is a Pittsburgh institution, an iconic establishment that has stood the test of time. Stepping into this eatery feels like a nostalgic journey, with its vintage decor and delightful ambiance. The friendly staff greets you with warm smiles, creating an immediate sense of belonging.When it comes to food, Jimmy Tsang's truly shines with its extensive selection of classic Chinese dishes. The menu offers an array of tantalizing options, ranging from the ever-popular General Tso's Chicken to the delicate steamed dumplings. Every dish is painstakingly crafted with meticulous attention to detail, ensuring an authentic and gratifying flavor experience.One aspect that sets Jimmy Tsang's apart is their unwavering commitment to using only the freshest, highest-quality ingredients. Whether it's the crispness of the vegetables in their stir-fries or the tenderness of the meat in their savory soups, you can taste the difference that superior ingredients make. The flavors are harmoniously balanced, and the portion sizes strike a perfect balance between satisfying and overwhelming.Notably, Jimmy Tsang's goes above and beyond to accommodate diverse dietary preferences. Their extensive vegetarian and vegan menu boasts options that rival their meat-based counterparts in terms of flavor and quality. This inclusivity reflects their commendable dedication to catering to a wide range of diners, making it a fantastic choice for groups with varied eating habits.The service at Jimmy Tsang's is prompt and attentive. The knowledgeable servers are more than willing to offer personalized recommendations based on your preferences. They are also quick to refill your water or tea, ensuring you are well taken care of throughout your dining experience.The restaurant's atmosphere is cozy and inviting, characterized by dim lighting and soothing background music. It provides the perfect backdrop for a casual get-together with friends or a romantic evening out.

Was recommended by my coworker. However, I was a little unsure as I've read some bad reviews about this place. The first visit was great. The receptionists were helpful and gave me guidance on how to get my dog licensed. Everyone seemed happy and talkative. Dr. Bezak was very nice. He had a smile on him the entire time I was there. He was very quick to give me information about anything and everything relating to the dog. Overall, I had a good first visit and definitely going back. The only thing that made it didn't earn a five-star is that my appointment is at 12: 15pm. The entire office have their lunch at 1pm. So I can tell there was alot of hustle to get me out of their asap. I don't mind that it was a quick visit, but I would have liked to had time to ask more questions. If you want adequate time with the doc, consider making your appointment after their lunch.

Yeh, not impressed. yo had high hopes for this restaurant, given all the positive reviews I had read online. However, from the moment I walked in, I knew something was off. The atmosphere was lackluster, with d im lighting and outdated decor that seemed to lack any cohesive theme. As I scanned the menu, j struggled to find any dishes that truly excited me. The option were limited and unimaginative, offering the same tired classics that can be found at any generic eatery. When the food finally arrived, I was further disappointing. My dish lacked the vibrant flavors and creativity that I had anticipated. The presentation was lackluster, with sloppy plating and random garnishes. The taste fell flat, with the flavors lasking depth and complexity. It was clear that the ingredients used were of subpar quality, resulting in a bland and forgettable experience. To make matters worse, the service was incredibly slow and inattentive. It took an eternity for our orders to be taken, and even longer for the food to arrive at our table. The waitstaff seemed disinterested and untrained, often forgetting simple requests and neglecting to check on our satisfaction. It was evident that they lacked the vocational and enthusiasm that one would expect from a reputable establishment. The overall value for the price was sorely lacking. The portions were small and overpriced, leaving me feeling unsatisfied and slightly cheated. I had hoped for a memorable dining experience, but instead, I left the restaurant feeling underwhelmed and completely unimpressed. Perhaps this establishment has seen better days, or maybe it just never lived up to its hype. Whatever the case may be, I would not recommend this restaurant to someone seeking an exceptional culinary experience. There are far better options available in the area that are more deserving of your time and hard-earned money. Save yourself the disappointment and look elsewhere for a truly remarkable dining experience.

5 stars for food. I won't reminisce over the first visit as it was quite some time ago, but hubs and I strolled in there to grab a quick bite before heading to a show in Concord. Our server Colleen was fantastic - she seriously should work at Disneyland because that woman is so happy. She was also incredibly friendly, professional and efficient, making sure that we were in and out of there for our show with plenty of time to spare. Beyond the tasty (I presume freshly baked bread), I ordered the cavatelli primavera - an large portion of finely cooked cavatelli pasta loaded with tons of veggies in a light marinara sauce. The pasta was just what I was looking for and the veggies were fresh - my complaint? The sauce was quite bland. Perhaps more crushed red pepper? More garlic? More BAM? Regardless, I had leftover to eat for lunch for another day and for the price, $14. 95, it was a ton of food. One an alternate note, make sure you note the price of the specials if you're interested in them.. . hubs and I were both surprised that his chicken & pasta dish was $22. It was roughly the same portion and similar ingredients to my dish and seemed as if the chicken breast cost added $7 to the price. Strange. Regardless, next time I'm in the University area I definitely want to try their tiramisu - I hear it's phenomenal!

You can go there for any big game for any sport, and they will have it on one of their many screens WITH SOUND!! They even have a roll-down projection screen towards the rear of the bar that shows the big games as well. I recently went to Picassos one week night, and ordered a beer and an order of a dozen Cajun Garlic wings w/ranch. This is a tasty sauce I've had many times so I knew what I was given. The wings were brought to me pipping hot and the ranch was thick and cold. There's nothing I despise more than a warm, runny ranch. The wings were cooked with the perfect amount of crispiness but were not overcooked by any means. My only complaint with the wings is that they are not charred. I'm sorry to say, but if you're not throwing your wings over an open-flame and charring them at this point then you're simply behind the times. Plenty of establishments such as Fanz, Hickory Tavern and Mac's throw their wings over a grill before serving them. If your looking for a chill and relaxing WEEKDAY evening to watch your favorite team, Picassos is the perfect place. On football Sundays, Picasso's University is nothing short of perfectly organized mayhem. Fans often arrived at 11am-11: 30am even though their game doesn't kick-off until 1pm! Furthermore, you are very likely to see a skirmish or a squabble as Sunday day turns into Sunday evening and patrons start to get that liquor courage. Before I close, I want to make an important distinction in my rating. I give Picasso's Sports Cafe as a whole 5-stars. The staff is always friendly, prompt and efficient. However, I am not giving their Cajun Garlic Wings 5-stars! Though their wings are good, there are not "5-star" worthy. On a scale of 1-10, I'd give them a 7. At its soul, this is a classic, American sports-bar. Good food, done right.

First off let me say this TGIF is gonna get the brunt of a couple of other TGIF visits I've had around the Charlotte area.The service and food at this location are consistently subpar compared to other TGIF locations I have visited. The first time I went, our server pretty much ignored us the entire time and we waited over an hour for our food. The second time, our food was cold and the service was just as bad.I've given this location multiple chances to improve, but unfortunately, it has not. I will not be returning to this TGIF location again. If you are looking for a good TGIF experience, I would recommend going to a different location.The food is not very good either. The burgers are dry and flavorless, and the fries are soggy and undercooked. I would not recommend eating here.The service is also terrible. The servers are inattentive and rude. They take forever to take your order, and then they get it wrong. They also don't seem to care if you have a good experience or not.Overall, I would not recommend this TGIF location to anyone. The food is bad, the service is terrible, and the prices are too high. There are much better options out there.

I was drawn in by the promise of a chef on site doing cooking demonstrations and handing out samples. As I entered the store, I was greeted by the friendly staff and the aroma of freshly prepared food. I made my way to the chef's station and was impressed by the variety of dishes being offered. I sampled a few things and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food.As I continued to explore the store, I noticed that it was much larger than a typical Giant Eagle. There was a wide selection of organic and specialty items, as well as a large prepared foods section. I was impressed by the variety of ready-to-eat options, including sushi, salads, and sandwiches.Despite the larger size of the store, the atmosphere felt cozy and welcoming. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the overall vibe felt more like a neighborhood market than a large chain store. I will definitely be back to try more of the chef's samples and to explore the rest of the store.

The drink menu is extensive and features an impressive array of craft cocktails, fine wines, and refreshing beers. The deck is perched right on the edge of a picturesque waterfront, and the views alone are worth the visit. As you sit down, the gentle sea breeze caresses your face, adding to the overall charm. But let's not forget about the food! Whether you're a fan of fruity concoctions or prefer something classic and sophisticated, the skilled bartenders at this restaurant have you covered. Their attention to detail and passion for mixology are evident in every sip. The food menu is surprisingly good and complements the drinks perfectly. The freshest catches are prepared in a variety of ways and are bursting with flavor. The service is also worth praising. The staff is warm, friendly, and attentive, and they're always ready to help with recommendations or offer their expertise on the drinks. Despite the lively atmosphere, they manage to create a relaxed and enjoyable dining experience that never feels rushed. It's the perfect place to unwind with friends, engage in captivating conversations, and simply savor the moment. As the evening wears on, the deck transforms into a cozy haven, thanks to the warm glow of the twinkling lights and the soft music playing in the background. But keep in mind that popularity comes at a price. It can get crowded, especially during peak hours and on the weekend.

Let's start with the bad. The food here is just all kinds of disappointing. First of all, their labyrinth of a menu. I understand that they are trying to be cute and witty by concealing the item descriptions within paragraph-long stories and forcing you to read them due to the completely nonsensical names they give to said items. I truly understand the concept behind this. But can I be the first to say.. . IT'S NOT CUTE! For the drink menu, fine. I'll admit to having a few laughs at their PG-13 drink encyclopedia. I'm not that cold-hearted. But when I'm hungry, the last thing I want to do is spend 20 minutes trying to decipher what my options are. Clearly I have a vendetta against their obnoxious menu, but the real problem here is that the food is the definition of mediocre. I go here fairly often, so I've done a lot of hopping around their menu trying to build my go-to order. I still haven't figured it out, and it's at the point where if my friends want to grab food here, I'll make a point out of eating beforehand. Plus, oh WOW is this place overpriced! This was especially highlighted to me on a Sunday morning when our bill came to $42 for brunch. Not expensive, but the wheels started turning in my head.. . we just paid $42 for an appetizer, two entrees, and two bloodys, all of which were eh, passable. For exactly $6 more, we could have went down the street to Casbah and had TWO appetizers, two entrees, and two much stronger bloodys, all of much higher quality. The reason I still come here though is the drinks. My favorite is the Happy Ending which involves pineapple juice, ginger, and cucumber. You really can't go wrong with anything though except for the Statutory Grape--if the name doesn't dissuade you enough, just heed my advice and don't order it. Unless of course, you want to have flashbacks to that time you attempted to robotrip on Dimetapp in middle school. Memories! It's official, I am done with the food at Harris Grill. Drinks only! !

First off, if you are claustrophobic, probably not the place for you. I felt they packed way too many things in their greenhouses, and the walking paths are narrow. They shouldn't even allow carts throughout because it's too cramped. When it's busy there, it's extremely hard to get around in there. I found myself getting very crabby and wanting to walk out. Also, watch where you are walking - very uneven ground, cords and boards laying around. nI decided to get a few pepper plants there as they have a variety that I really like. My sister also bought this variety. A few weeks later after planting, we both started seeing problems in our gardens. The plants had been diseased, and it was spreading to other crops. The disease spread to other pepper plants that I purchased from elsewhere. It's very frustrating to put a lot of work and effort in to a garden, and now I'm not going to have any yield in peppers. Thanks Klein's! : (

The food was delicious and the service was excellent. The menu had a wide variety of choices and the prices were very reasonable. The atmosphere was relaxed and inviting and we enjoyed our meal immensely. The portions were generous and the food was cooked to perfection. The staff was friendly and attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. We would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great breakfast spot. We especially enjoyed the fresh fruit and the homemade bread. The coffee was also very good. We would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great breakfast spot.

! I was really excited to try this place as the reviews were excellent. Major disappointment! We arrived just before noon and the place was really busy. They were still serving breakfast but we were interested in lunch. We asked our server to see what the lunch menu to see all our options and she seemed annoyed. We ordered a couple of beers and they were prompt but not really cold. While we waited about 30 minutes in order to be able to order lunch, we had a lot of time to observe things. I was appalled to see the filthy salt, pepper, ketchup, and mustard containers. They looked like they had never been washed. I also watched the bartenders clear dirty dishes off the bar, then dig their hands in the cherry jar. The last straw was watching the woman cooking touch a handful of raw hamburger patties and then immediately touch the buns on the grill. It was calm and quiet and had lots of pretty organic produce. Here? Well, first of all, the parking lot is a death-trap full of upscale SUVs who have no idea how to drive courteously. I will not be bringing it back any time soon. My shocks were broken in the back of my car. They told me they needed to be replaced and they had the parts in stock. Now that I'm retired, I needed something to fill my time and keep my mind and body active, and building furniture and other wooden items seemed like it would be the perfect retirement hobby, and so far it has been.I've now built more pieces of furniture and other projects than I can count, and have gifted quite a few pieces to family members and friends, as well as selling a few. And now that I'm retired, I need something to fill my time and keep my mind and body active. nBetter to stay clear and save your money. nJudging from the empty tables the luster and joy of the Namaste we remembered is no longer. Looked around, and realized that this restaurant looks awfully like one of the restaurants I saw on the food network where the guy goes around and eats these ridiculously large meals. After eating a Pittsburgher (the second most popular dish) and trying the colossal fish sandwich, and a capicola sandwich, I've decided that the best part of my meal was the IC light. My friend's colossal fish was the best of the three and it's best eaten as two meals. My Pittsburgher was the pitts and I wouldn't order it again. Unlike your pitts on a 90+ degree day, it was really dry. The sandwich was only salvaged by my grotesque use of hot sauce. The concept isn't that ridiculous either. The Winter Olympics inspired us to hit the ice rink. We laced up our skates and headed to the local rink, eager to emulate the grace and skill of the Olympic figure skaters. The cold air bit at our noses and cheeks as we stepped onto the ice, but we couldn't help but feel a thrill of excitement.As we glided across the ice, we couldn't help but feel a sense of awe at the sheer beauty of the sport. The way the skaters effortlessly soared through the air, their blades slicing through the ice with precision and grace. We felt like we were part of a magical world, where gravity didn't exist and anything was possible.We started with some basic strokes and turns, trying to find our footing on the slippery surface. At first, it was a bit shaky, but soon we found ourselves gliding across the ice with increasing confidence. We even tried a few jumps and spins, feeling the rush of adrenaline as we landed gracefully (or not so gracefully) on the ice.Despite our amateur status, we couldn't help but feel like Olympic contenders ourselves. I have no idea who gave this place high reviews but they must either own the place or be time travelers from back in the day when this place might not have sucked. Oh Whole Foods, you are so so very overpriced. I mean, seriously, every time I walk into that store, I can practically feel my wallet crying in despair. But I have to admit, they do have a great selection of organic produce and specialty items that are hard to find elsewhere. So, despite the hefty price tag, I decided to give their prepared foods section a try. I meandered through the aisles, my eyes scanning the colorful array of salads, sandwiches, and ready-to-eat meals. Everything looked fresh and enticing, but that price tag kept lingering in the back of my mind. However, my growling stomach couldn't resist the temptation any longer, so I grabbed a container of their herb-roasted chicken with quinoa and roasted veggies.As I made my way to the checkout counter, I mentally prepared myself for the moment of truth - the taste test. Back at home, I eagerly opened the container, and the aroma of the perfectly seasoned chicken wafted through the air. The first bite confirmed what I suspected: Whole Foods knows how to make some seriously delicious food. The chicken was moist and flavorful, with the herbs adding a lovely depth of flavor.The quinoa was cooked to perfection, each grain separate and fluffy. The roasted veggies, a mix of zucchini, bell peppers, and carrots, were slightly caramelized and bursting with natural sweetness. It was like a symphony of flavors on my plate.Sure, the portion size was a bit on the smaller side, but I guess that's the trade-off for quality ingredients. And let's not forget the convenience of having a healthy, ready-to-eat meal on hand when you're short on time. It's a lifesaver for busy folks like me.Now, I won't deny that my bank account was weeping a bit after the Whole Foods escapade, but I have to say, the taste and quality justified the splurge. It may not be an everyday indulgence, but once in a while, treating yourself to Whole Foods' prepared foods is definitely worth it.

And I usually avoid hotel restaurants for this very reason, but I was tired and I was staying at the Westin, so here I am at the Original Fish Market.. . I sat at the bar and ordered dinner. The bartender was very friendly and made sure she was taking care of me. So props to her! I got a menu and a sushi menu. OK, I'm pretty sure Pittsburg isn't the most awesome place for sushi, but let's give it a shot! I started with the gumbo, which came out warm and kind of bland. It wasn't good at all. And then I had a roll, which was decent. And a spicy scallop roll. Now, everyone has their own take on spicy scallop, but this was by far the furthest from what I could imagine a spicy scallop roll could be. It was a small roll cut into 6 pieces (maki). It had a very small amount of raw scallops, which didn't taste super fresh. Then the roll was topped with the "spicy". I can't identify exactly the spices that were on top, but I've had this type of spice combination on other Japanese dishes. So I know it's an off the shelf thing. Basically, this was the worst roll I could imagine. So all-in-all, the food was sub-par at best. And the entire menu was overpriced. I would definitely eat somewhere else if I had any energy at all. I'm sure the room service would have been better.

The lobby is dimly lit and the carpet is stained, giving it a rundown thinking. The front desk staff is neighborly, but the service is slow and inefficient. I visited in the spring of 2012. The day started with a Bark for Life walk off of Morrison in lovely South Park on a picturesque day with one beautiful blonde date, and culminated with another first date a petite, cute redhead at this location. To get right into it, I have to say, they gave us great service at the Palm. That's something you can't put a price on. I mean really good service. Imagine having butler service for three hours, and the butler is driving a Mercedes, so you know he takes his job seriously. I met my date among a bustling crowd on a beautiful Saturday night. The waiter went out of his way to make us feel comfortable, and he was very attentive to our needs. I ordered the steak burger, it was very juicy, delicious, and bursting with flavor. It was an excellent portion size. The type of meat, we'll lets just say it was the expensive part of the cow, not rump roast. Unfortunately, I had only six bites of it because I had already eaten a sashimi appetizer at the Village Tavern in the Rotunda building in between dates. My date ordered the filet mignon, and it was delicious, cooked to perfection. One goes to a place like the Palm for a special occasion, or like me for a blind first date on rare occurrences, but either way, you go for the service and the great food. They treated me like a king, and I will be back for sure. Come see how the other half lives at the Palm. It is sure to be a delight for you and your significant other. I wouldn't recommend the Palm for kids, unless they are very well behaved.

I could not believe it when I saw the price for a package of Boar's Head honey ham! $14.99 a pound are you kidding me? I get that Boar's Head is some fancy ham but no sliced meat is worth that much. I know costs are higher at D&D but come on, you guys are just getting greedy now. I shouldn't be surprised though, their prices are out of control all over the store. A dozen eggs for almost $4? Give me a break. And don't even get me started on the bottle water, yikes. I swear they just triple whatever the normal price is and call it a day. It's like a trip to Menards - you think you're just swiping a 6 pack of soda but look out, your bill is now $150!Not to mention all the extra checkout lines are always closed. Who cares that there's 20 people waiting, can't pull another cashier off the floor I guess. The self checkout is always a nightmare too, those machines are perpetually broken. Oh but don't worry, seven employees will swarm you to "help" while staring at you the whole time like you're about to pull a heist. Real friendly guys. At this point I'd rather schlep to Sentry and deal with their massive parking lot than give D&D another dime. I know quality costs more but come on, have some compassion for us regular folks just trying to get through the week. We get it, you're fancy but maybe dial the prices back 10% and you'd have a lot more happy customers, including this one. Until then I'll be avoiding you like the plague, or at least until I'm out of lunch meat again!

The man and I are on this thing now where we are trying to eat at a few places famous for their fish fry's thanks to an article in Madison Magazine. The first place on the list was the Weary Traveler Freehouse. I had no idea what to expect, and I didn't really look at the menu ahead of time. All I knew was that they were known for their fish fry.When we got there, the place was packed. We ended up sitting at the bar, which was fine with us. The bartender was really friendly and attentive, and he made some great recommendations.For my meal, I ordered the perch fry with a side of coleslaw and tartar sauce. The fish was lightly battered and fried to perfection. It was so flaky and moist. The coleslaw was also really good, with a nice tangy flavor. And the tartar sauce was the perfect complement to the fish.My husband ordered the Friday Fish Fry Basket, which came with two pieces of fried fish, a side of coleslaw, and fries. He loved the fish, and he said that the fries were some of the best he's ever had.We both really enjoyed our meals at the Weary Traveler Freehouse. The fish fry was delicious, and the service was great. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a good fish fry.In addition to the great food, the Weary Traveler Freehouse also has a really nice atmosphere. It's a cozy, relaxed place with a touch of nautical flair. There's also a nice outdoor patio, which is perfect for enjoying a meal on a warm summer evening.Overall, we had a great experience at the Weary Traveler Freehouse. The food was delicious, the service was great, and the atmosphere was cozy and inviting. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a good fish fry.One thing to note is that the Weary Traveler Freehouse is only open for dinner on Fridays, so be sure to plan your visit accordingly.If you're looking for a delicious fish fry in a cozy, relaxed atmosphere, I highly recommend the Weary Traveler Freehouse.

Coulwood Tire & Auto in NW Charlotte came recommended by a friend, and my first visit went as well as a trip to the mechanic could. Coming from a guy who never learned how not to get ripped off at the mechanic, that's saying something. John, the manager, was courteous and professional. He didn't try to upsell me on anything. The waiting area was clean and inviting. I even got a ride back to the office by Percy, one of the crew. Nice guy, too. The service took a little longer than expected, but not too bad. And hey, I was at work instead of a waiting area.. . so that's good. The work seems to have been done as expected; I checked the spark plugs, new S-belt.. . everything seemed in order. The price wasn't brutal. Tune-up, oil change and a new serpentine belt: $465. About what I expected. Still tough to swallow, but that's the life of a car owner, ain't it? All in all, I'm pleased and will likely head back to Coulwood Tire & Auto next time I need service.

I checked out Great Harvest this morning since I saw I had a BOGO coupon for a honey whole wheat loaf of bread in the Citipass book. Loving all things carbs, I checked online and they were open early. Such a nice change for a morning person like me since many things in Charlotte don't seem to be open early on the wknd! I walked in there and this place is HUGE! Of course the other thing I noticed was the smell of fresh breads being baked, so many flavors, so little time. IHowever, it was filled not only with bread but an inventory of dips, chutneys, sauces, etc. They also have a cart with dry soup mix that is gluten free and looked pretty tasty. I wasn't sure what to get there so I went with Rosemary Garlic loaf to get something with flavor. This girl cooks a lot of Italian food so I am sure I can incorporate it in a meal somewhere. They have toaster and round loaves-which just mean the size of the loaf (I had no clue what they meant when they asked this so I just said toasted in an inquisitive way). Their bread has no artificial ingredients or preservatives and according to their website, shouldn't be refrigerated but can be frozen (they gave me extra bags when I told them I want to freeze mine). They also have a bread card where you buy 12 loaves, you get one free. When I saw others put three $$$ for price on here, I don't agree. The loaves are about $5 a pop and most bread at the supermarket is an average of $3 so I don't think the price is too high, especially for freshly baked bread without preservatives or artificial ingredients. I dig how they have the nutritional info on their website so you can see what you're taking in. They also have sandwiches there besides bread so if you're looking for a quick treat, you should stop on in! Two Citipass coupons--one for a free loaf, the other is for BOGO sandwich.

First off, a heads up. The following is a review about a book written in the form of a memoir. The author describes in detail how he was in the Peace Corps in 1968-1970 in Ethiopia. It's not so much a story as a series of incidents and anecdotes, and it is rambling, repetitive, and unfocused. This will come as no surprise to anyone who read his previous book. But if you did not, then be prepared for a bumpy ride. I'm surprised this was even published, to be honest.The author goes on and on about the people he met in his village, the food he ate (injera, mostly), the things he did and didn't do. And on and on. Some of the stories are interesting, in a "Wow, that really happened?" kind of way. But mostly they are dull, and after a while, you just want to skip to the end.There is very little reflection in this book. The author simply describes what happened to him, without ever really trying to make sense of it all. As a result, the book feels like a jumbled mess.The writing is also pretty bad. The author uses a lot of slang and colloquialisms, which makes the book hard to read. He also has a habit of using long, rambling sentences that are difficult to follow.If you're looking for a well-written, thought-provoking memoir, then this is not the book for you. But if you're interested in reading about a guy's experiences in the Peace Corps, then you might find this book interesting. Just be prepared for a bumpy ride.

Yikes! This bizarre film defies comprehension from start to confusing finish. The plot lurches between disjointed scenes with no discernible story arc. One leaves as befuddled as when they began, scratching their head wondering what on earth the filmmakers were aiming for. The sloppy direction provides no guidance through this nonsensical maze. Characters act without reason or depth, mere stereotypes that evoke only eye-rolls. The acting ranks among some of the worst seen in recent memory. It appears the surrealism was the goal, but fell painfully short in execution. Scenes leave one perplexed as to their purpose or meaning. The cinematography and lighting add no beauty or clarity, but visual oddities that further cloud an already murky work. Choppy edits rupture any semblance of flow or timeline.Soundtrack choices frequently clash wildly with the on-screen action. Plus heaps of bizarre visuals inserted arbitrarily without advancing the incoherent plot. By the end, the sole relief came from the closing credits ending the frustrations. There seems little appeal here beyond bewilderment and annoyance. Skip this 90 minute endurance test unless confused frustration constitutes entertainment. Otherwise, time spent elsewhere would bring greater satisfaction and understanding. This film epitomizes an epic failure from beginning to its merciful conclusion.

However, with that admission out of the way, I had an absolute blast at Discovery Place. My boyfriend and I spent nearly 3 hours there on a Sunday afternoon - no children, just two 30-somethings - and enjoyed every moment. The IMAX theater is awesome, and there are typically a few different movies to choose from. Yes, this is an extra ticket/cost, but if there's something playing that interests you, it's definitely worth checking out. The exhibits span a broad range of ages, and whether you're 3 or 33 (or older), you'll be educated and entertained. The museum is multiple stories, and the cafeteria has options galore. Hot or cold, healthy or cupcakes, you can find something to please even the pickiest of eaters. There are two entrances (one on 6th Street, one on Tryon), and if the line is too crowded at one, I suggest checking out the other (when we were there, 40 people must have been waiting in line at 6th Street, but upstairs on Tryon was empty). A great place for taking out-of-town visitors, a much needed activity for those with wee ones, or a laid-back weekend date, it's a great place to discover!

The Original Pancake House (OPH) is my 2nd favorite place for breakfast on the weekends (Pewter Rose is the first). I always look forward to heading to OPH for a tasty and filling breakfast. The dining room is spacious and decorated in a classic diner style with comfy vinyl booths. Windows around the perimeter of the restaurant let in lots of natural light. Wash it all down with a fresh squeezed orange juice which is some of the best I've ever tasted. After eating at OPH I always feel fully satisfied and not at all stuffed. It's the perfect place to go to fuel up for a full day of activities on the weekends. Although it can get crowded, the friendly staff keeps service moving at a good pace. Setting aside the garish atmosphere, the first thing that established the tone of the visit was a server who came within a minute after taking our drink orders and asked brusquely if we were ready to order. Mind, the place was almost entirely empty and hours before closing time. My girlfriend ordered Quesadilla Roha with ground beef and a special sauce. The beef was utterly dry and flavorless. The primary taste of her meal was the burned tortilla. Accompanying it was a salad which consisted of shredded lettuce topped with a single, thick slice of under ripe tomato (totally inedible) and their 'special red sauce' which tasted like tomato paste with a bit of red pepper. I ordered the Burrito Loco which came with rice. It came with enough rice for three meals and a burrito the size of my head. The chicken inside was largely flavorless and there were some sizable bits of gristle inside. The enormous quantity of rice was entirely unadorned in a large sticky pile. I ordered a Lime Margarita. I wasn't asked how I'd like it prepared and it came with salt, but so little salt that there was barely a trace of it on one edge. It was also very sweet, and I'm not sure whether there was any actual Tequila in it. We shared a 'bean dip' which was sized for a party of eight, and was almost entirely cheese sauce with few discernible beans in it. Adding to the failure was that the food came out less than ten minutes after being ordered, which really highlights the fact that the food was almost certainly not cooked so much as reheated. I would urge them to go INTO fast food if that's what they want to serve, but their beef compared unfavorably to Taco Bell and their Burrito was vastly less appetizing than any I've ever had at Chipotle, so I'm not sure there's room for them there either.

There are lots of articles in the newspapers, regular protests, petitions, etc over route reduction and fare hikes and so on. Some people think its slow, unreliable and overcrowded. There's a general sense that its unfair that Pitt students ride for free while much of the Pitt staff do not. And, of course, the rest of the city has to pay too. But I think all this is just a testament to the health of the system. People - students at all the college and universities, long-term residents, downtown commuters, school kids - actually value and use the bus system. In other university towns (not to name names) the schools just give up entirely and shuttle their students around in private buses, which means, in the end, less ridership, fewer routes less frequently and less money for the public transportation. I also found the drivers to be considerate - especially of the elderly and disabled - and as helpful as they could be, given the demands on their time and attention. Depending on your living situation, the buses make it possible to live in Pittsburgh with one car, or none. And I found that it's safer to take a bus in the snow, too, (if not quicker, which it sometimes also is).

While its size may initially seem limited, don't be deceived by appearances, as this hidden gem offers an impressive selection of fundamental for Asian cuisine enthusiasts. To freeze section boasts a range of dumplings, spring rolls, and buns, perfect for a quick and convenient meal on busy days. Additionally, the produce section surprises with its freshness, offering a decent selection of exotic fruits and vegetable that can be hard to find elsewhere. When it comes to snacks, The Gist takes snacking severely, with shelves brimming with unique and flavorful treats, including crispy seaweed snacks, savory spised nuts, and traditional rice crackers. Their rice and noodle aisles are equally well-stocked, featuring various brands and types, from fragrant jasmine rice to chewy udon noodles. And let's not forget about their impressive sauce sollection! Whether you're in search of a classic soy sauce or a more audacious chili paste, you'll find it here, along with a multitude of other condiments that will elevate your homemade dish.

(I would typically spend a few hours, but I was trying to spare a friend not as keen on secondhand garments). With my carefully extracted finds I searched in vain for a fitting room, never to find one. After asking the staff where it was, I had to take a seat and leave my jaw dropped for a while because THERE IS NO FITTING ROOM! nI couldn't take this fact into my brain, and although there were some household items I wanted to go back and buy, I was too upset to continue. (Sidenote: yes, I can understand how this can work for the RWB, but imho it is unforgivable, and I wish there was at least some warning before spending my time searching for a bargain when I couldn't even see if it would fit). I would recommend this store if you are looking for something specific secondhand especially for dishes, or older electronics, or even beauty products. There was even a used Nikon SLR with a wide angle lens ($200 though)! nBut if you plan on buying a sundress, and don't plan on stripping down in front of your fellow thrifties, you'd better be confident in your purchase. RWB is just like any other thrift store, and you can't return or exchange your items, so you'd be out of luck and out of money.

Walking in at 3: 45 PM, there were maybe 3 tables occupied. The decor was inviting. I loved the huge fish tank they had on display. From there, sadly, it began to go downhill. A lady at the bar waved me to the dining room, and a waiter sauntered over to ask what I wanted to drink. Also he asked me if I wanted a menu.. .. .. strange. After getting settled with the menu, I ordered 2 egg rolls, hoping that since it was between mealtimes I would get freshly fried ones. Nope, not to be. Cold, hard and greasy. So back they went, with a request for fresh ones, told the waiter I didn't mind waiting for them. I ordered Sa Cha Scallops as an entree, with a small pork fried rice. The new egg rolls came out at the same time as the entree. I could deal with that, no probs. BUT.. .. egg rolls were NOT fresh, they were warmer, and just as hard. Scallops were good and plentiful, presentation was good, fried rice was good also. The egg rolls were the turnoff. I'm giving it 2 Yelp stars, but if you love good egg rolls, don't come here expecting to find them. Panda's Den in north Charlotte puts this place to shame.

While the menu isn't tremendously varied, they focus on homemade Italian favorites. The pastas are always perfectly al dente and the rich, flavorful sauces are highlights. I'm a big fan of their lasagna, which has extremely thin layers of pasta that you can see through. The large, tender meatballs nestled in a savory tomato sauce are also standouts. On nights when chicken parmesan is offered, it is incredibly moist and tender inside with a crisp breaded exterior.The cozy restaurant has a nice atmosphere with red checkered tablecloths and paintings of Italian landscapes adorning the walls. It can become loud when busy, but the conversations add to the lively buzz. Service is generally good - the staff seem to know regular customers and remember drink orders. On rare busy evenings, you may wait briefly for a table, but they offer a beverage voucher for the bar in the interim. Prices are very reasonable given the sizable portions. You'll always leave feeling fully satisfied. They offer lasagna and baked ziti as family meals to-go, perfect for busy weeknights. The light and airy tiramisu, with its perfect balance of ladyfingers, espresso, and mascarpone, is a delicious dessert.Though the dining room seats about twenty tables, it always feels full whenever I visit. They seem to have steady regular patrons as well as new customers sampling the offerings. The neighborhood staple has stood for over twenty years now. I've never had a poor experience in that time and think they do a great job with what they aim to provide. It's certainly not fine dining but you always know what to expect. A few dishes I wouldn't order, but overall quality is consistently good. Minor issues are sometimes the music is too loud and air conditioning insufficient on sweltering days when at full capacity.

The fourth time we visited, we were excited to try their new menu item, but unfortunately, the dishes we decreed were not up to par. The Edamame arrived cold, and the Sashimi was overcooked and tasted more like fried rubber than seafood. The main incidents, the Soba Noodles, was also a letdown. Per noodles were limp and lacked flavor, and the sauce that accompanied it was too salty. To top it all off, the service was unfriendly and unhelpful. Our waiter seemed uninterested in our concerns and failed to check in on us throughout the meal. Overall, it was a disappointing experience, and we likely won't be returning to Soba Lounge again.

I don't have too many chain restaurant reviews, so I figured I'd write one. We went for a surprise birthday party. My friend had made a reservation which they somehow didn't have (maybe she called the wrong one? Anyway, I'm not going to dock for this). The staff was very accommodating, they were able to put a table together for us on short notice. When we sat down, I was immediately hit by a gross smell. I asked my friend "Do you smell that? It smells like.. . " to which he replied "wet dog! " which is exactly what I was thinking. It smelled badly like wet dog. How disgusting. Maybe it was the table--can you say dirty rags? While we waited for the rest to arrive, we got breadsticks and were also told that dessert for the birthday would be a charge. Really? Come on now. The bread sticks were pretty underwhelming--there was no garlic or flavor really. Booo. Once everyone arrived, we placed orders. I got the Bruschetta Salmon. When I asked the waiter how it was, he said he hadn't tried it in forever but that people say it's decent--I appreciated that honesty! They served salad shortly My goodness this place was slow though. The food took forever. When it came out, it was pretty lousy. I found two bones in the salmon before I quit eating it. The risotto pasta thing under it was so heavy and the salmon was sort of hard and the toppings made no sense. It felt like two or three dishes in one. Others' food didn't come out, so the manager came out and apologized and comped several meals. He even went up to the birthday boy and told him he'd comp his dessert as well. Thumbs up. Dessert was actually pretty good--I got the chocolate tuxedo mousse cake which was quite good and it seems everyone else enjoyed theirs as well. The only reason this place is getting 2 stars instead of 1 is for service. Our waiter was personable and friendly, and the manager was excellent. I'd stay away from this garden like the plague, though.

The restaurant was able to accommodate our large group neither any issues. Our server was friendly and attentive, taking sure that everyone had everything they needed. The menu offered a good variety of options, including vegans and gluten-free dishes. To food was delicious and well-prepared, with generous portion sizes. We ordered a mix of apps, entrees, and desserts, and everything was consistently good. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and servicing. The atmosphere was comfortable and invites, with a cozy ambiance that made us feel right at home. The restaurant was also able to accommodate our request for a private rooms, which was perfect for our special occasion. Overall, we had a great experience at this restaurant and would definitely recommend it to others. The staff went above and beyond to make sure that we had a memorable jubilee celebration. The restaurant's location was convenient and easy accessible, with plenty of parking available. We were impressed by the attention to detail that the staff showed, from the decorations to the personalized touches. This restaurant e×ceeded our expectations and we can't wait to go back.

kindness. It is not even close to the movie, but a documentary. This is more like advertisements for the US Marine Corps or Navy, including many RAH-Rah, Gung-Ho, American, F-Yeah propaganda.
