The airport was spacious and easy to navigate between terminals. I had about an hour between flights which gave me time to grab a snack and explore some of the shops. There was a good variety of food options to choose from but the lines did seem long. I was able to find a comfortable seating area near my gate to relax during my layover. Thankfully the gates were well-signed making it easy to find my connecting flight on time. Overall my layover experience in CLT was pleasant and the airport seemed well equipped to handle connecting passengers.

The staff were not very attentive and seemed to be more interested in talking to each other than helping customers. There was also a very limited selection of used records, and the prices were quite high. I ended up leaving the store without buying anything.However, I did return a few weeks later and had a much better experience. The staff were much more helpful and friendly, and the selection of used records had improved significantly. I was able to find a few great records at reasonable prices, and I ended up spending quite a bit of money.Overall, I would say that this store is worth checking out if you are looking for used records. However, be prepared for a potentially disappointing experience if you visit during a busy time.Overall, my experience at this store was a mixed bag. While I was initially disappointed, I was ultimately satisfied with my purchase.

I have to admit that the Bobcats are a very far distant second team for me behind the Celtics. The history and tradition of the Celtics franchise is what first captured my heart as a basketball fan. While the Bobcats don't have the championships or great players of the Celtics, I still enjoy following their season. They have had some exciting players over the years like Kemba Walker and Gerald Wallace. However, it has been a struggle for them to consistently win games in the tough Eastern Conference. Their future looks a bit brighter now that they have drafted promising young talents like LaMelo Ball. If they can build a supporting cast around him, they may start competing for playoff spots in a few years. But it will be tough to seriously challenge the top teams with their small market limitations. Fans in Charlotte have been very loyal despite years of losing. I hope the front office makes smart moves to field a competitive team that can keep growing the fan base. Continued patience may be needed as the Bobcats try to develop into a contender.

Encore, upon entering the restaurant, I was immediately struck by the unimpressive decor. The tables and chairs were plain and lacked any real develop, and the lighting was harsh and overhead. The atmosphere was also lacking, with the exception of some minimalist Japanese decorations on the barriers. Despite my initial reservation, I was eager to try their sushi and had high hopes that it would redeem the sufficiently drab surroundings. Unfortunately, the sushi rolls were disappointingly small, and the gaskets were skimpy and lacked any real flavor or creativity. I ordered the spicy tuna roll, which was bland and had very limited spice to it. The tuna was also overcooked, resulting in a dry and viscous texture. The rice was also poorly prepared, being overcooked and overcooked. I also tried the salmon ravioli, which was surprisingly bland and lacking in flavor. The salmon was not fresh and had a strange, almost metallic tastes to it. The wasabi and cauliflower ginger provided little respite from the overall lack of flavor. The services was also subpar, with a waitress who seemed uninterested in our needs and missed to check in on us regularly. When we asked for refills on our drinks, she seemed put off and took her calendars returning with them. Overall, my experience at Umi was a woe. Despite its claims of being the best sushi in Baltimore, the food was subpar and the atmosphere was lacking. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone watching for a truly satisfying sushi experience.

First, I was the only customer, during my entire dining experience.. which somewhat scares me. I was seated and served a complimentary salad. The salad was good, but overdressed.. crazy overdressed. I ordered the onion soup and egg rolls. The onion soup was basically broth with a few onions, but no real onion flavor, which is what I was hoping for. As for the egg rolls, can I say frozen. nOnto the sushi. I chose a roll based on the waitresses recommendation, however it had a mango sauce that was so overwhelming I sent it back. I was not offered anything else and was charged for the roll, $13. 95, after eating only two pieces. I questioned the server about being charged and she expressed the fact she told me what I was getting and I ordered it. Whoa, was I surprised. I expressed my disappointment and said please do what you need to do. She disappeared and came out with an older women. Upon returning to my table she did remove the roll, but was very unpleasant about it. nAlthough I appreciate the fact they removed the roll, but was not impressed otherwise and will stick to my other favorites.

Your carnivore and herbivore friends will love the menu. They source local ingredients, cook "real" food and even bring in local products such as YumButter and create extra, super-duper healthy menu items by partnering with Jon Hinds at Monkey Bar Gym. However, I write this review because I recently ate the most amazing curry dish there. I've been craving it ever since and cannot wait to return. I'm serious, it was a hot, steaming bowl of freshly steamed vegetables with rice and a fantastic curry sauce. I want to eat this every day! Our server even told me that she actually DOES eat this every day and has since they put it on their menu. It was a huge bowl, so I took half of it home with me so I could enjoy a second meal of leftovers. Now drop everything and order this curry! And order a piece of pie or enjoy an iced sugar cookie, too.

This Charlotte staple has served the Queen City area for over 30 years and remains a neighborhood favorite. Their menu features well-executed Southern classics. The fried chicken is perfectly crispy outside yet incredibly moist and flavorful within. Patrons can choose between thighs and breasts; a mix is recommended. The collard greens are cooked low and slow, imparting plenty of smoky flavor from pork. The rich and creamy macaroni and cheese strikes the right balance of blended cheeses. Excellent options also include fried catfish, succulent barbecue ribs, and shrimp and grits flavored to perfection. Friendly staff are quick to refill iced tea in signature sweet tea. Sides like creamy potato salad, crispy fried okra, and fluffy buttermilk biscuits satisfy. Weekends see strong local support that maintains this Charlotte gem, as nightly dinners prove busy. Generations of families have dined here, fostering community and tradition over flavors that never fail. Whether dining in for lunch or dinner, patrons leave fully satiated. It's clear why after three decades they maintain status as one of Charlotte's most beloved eateries. Visiting the city always means looking forward to a return, appreciating their place among top Southern restaurants.

They started out easy to work with, but that was short-lived. Scheduling apartment viewing was simple, and the people who showed me the units were relatively friendly. The issue came when I actually went to sign a lease. I was told on the phone and in person by the person showing me apartments that I would not need a cosigner, but as soon as I showed up for my lease application appointment, they told me I would need a cosigner. I scrambled to contact my mom, who was willing to cosign, but they said they needed BOTH parents to co-sign, and they wanted me to sign an agreement saying I would forfeit the $1000 deposit I had to pay upfront if I did not return all of my cosigners' documents within 7 days. This was an issue because 1 of my parents was out of town for the week. I tried compromising with them and seeing if they could change the agreement to give me an extra few days to get the cosigner paperwork in, or to see if I could just have my mother (who was more than financially stable) be the sole cosigner. They were unwilling to compromise at all, and I left after about a half hour of unproductive back-and-forth discussion. I could have gone back a week later, when both parents were in town, as the unit was still available, but I figured any place that difficult to work with when I was trying to give them money would be even more frustrating once I was contacting them for things like maintenance requests. I wouldn't say "never ever rent from them", but I would definitely be aware of how rude / difficult they can be.

aisles full of hardware supplies, tools, bathroom accessories and even a small nursery for gardening. My favorite section is the tool section seeing that I'm a DIY-er. (Do it yourself) if you didn't already know that. I enjoy building, maintaining and fixing things in my own home as opposed to hiring a contractor and paying a boat load. I'm best known at the Home Depot in monroeville. I come in there so often a lot of the employees know me just by my dog. Yes my dog, who i have brought into this store several times. They allow pets i'm assuming because i've never been asked to leave and I've seen others with their pets as well. That's the best part about the store is the animal policy and the fact that they offer enough supplies for you to practically build a house. Some things are cost efficient while others are kinda breaking the bank. There not as modern as lowes but they have alot of the same products. I recently built my own in home bar. t's 8 by 2, a long bar that i (a girl) built by hand. I'm very proud of the work i did. I installed lights and polished it and it has a resin top with ceramic tiles beneath it. It's a real beauty and i got all the supplies at home depot. Cost me about $600 to make but i put it together in 2 months so that's a plus. But yea if your in need of some nice plants to go in the kitchen or patio OR you just want to spruce up a few things around the house, then this Mega home repair store is where you ought to be. Between this and lowes its not like you have a choice.

! Persian Hot Tea, five stars!! ! The Eggplant Dish was very good! The Belly Dancing gets Five stars!! ! Service also gets five stars! From there everything else was Good though none of it was better than three stars and not as flavorful as I hoped, still good! I'm the Only Dude here! Eleven Female patrons including my Bride.. . add two Belly Dancers and our Waitress, I'm out numbered 14 to 1! ! ! ! ! ! Great show! If you have never seen live Belly Dancing it is Usually Entertaining and though maybe initially awkward it is fun! Persian Ice Cream nice flavor combination of Pistachio, Rose Water and Saffron less dense than Kulfi - If I had never eaten (Indian Kulfi) I would have probably rated this Ice Cream Higher! Baklava a bit disappointing, papery filo, though drier than the overly syrupy version

I've had the dry rub ribs why were meaty and flavorful. I've also had the smoked turkey and brisket sandwiches which were both great- authentic, tasty, with a nice smokey flavor to them. The meat is the best here and one of my favorite bbq places in town. As for sides, they are a bit disappointing. The cornbread is ok, I don't like the corn pieces in it really. The fries kind of a look like cheap looking store bought crinkle cut fries and they are always soggy and limp as a take out order. I have also been to the Mooresville branch which is consistent too. So depending on which part of the city you live in, you can plan accordingly. TIP: If you go through the drive thru expect to wait longer than a fast food drive thru. The attendant who serves me at this location always smiles and is pleasant.

That doesn't make it bad - just different, so if you're wanting authentic, you may want to go elsewhere. Inside of this Salsa's, the decor is very nice. The only complaint is the lighting. Along the right side of the restaurant, the ceiling fans and the low lights combine to create a very annoying strobe affect. It was so bad we had to move. Once we did, it wasn't a problem at all. Service was excellent, speedy and efficient all around. Glasses were kept filled, and food came out quickly. One thing I'll typically do at a new restaurant (new for me, not necessarily brand new) is ask for advice, and the waiter offered it. A nice touch. I hate it when they can't do so. The food was tasty - ingredients were fresh, sauces were not overwhelming. I had a (steak) chimichanga, and it was one of the better ones that I can recall tasting. For this sort of Mexican, I'd highly suggest you try them out.

There's rows and rows of baskets and bedazzling jewels and paper and.. . oh my.. . scrap booking! When I want to find boring old felt.. .. it's like.. . where do I start? I'm in a hurry, as always, and I rush in and the first thing I look for is an employee. No one to be found. I could call out and my voice would come echoing back. I run between rows of paper, wood and gosh darn scrap booking.. .. no felt! Where do I find felt! Where do I find an employee!? FINALLY, I find one after 15 minutes of wondering around. She's incredibly nice and leads me to the felt. This is not the first time I've been hard up to find help. I tell her she was hard to find, and she tells me that they're "low on payroll" and can't have any one the floor BUT HER! In that WHOLE store, JUST HER! That's ridic! Not a month ago I was, again, in a slight hurry and stood in line for about 15 minutes to check out, with 2 employees at the register and 6 people per line, I gave up and walked out. Hey Michael, do you pick up what I'm putting down? You're not making any money because your costumer service SUCKS.. .. in fact, there's no service to be found!

! ! ! I thought this was a decent nail shop from the reviews; however, I was very disappointed. I went for my birthday and had a shellac manicure and regular pedicure. I was told that the shellac manicure would last 2 weeks; however, it started to chip in less than a week! I spent $30 for my nails to last 4 days!! So I called to see if they would redo the nails that were chipped and I was told to come in, which I did. When I got there I had to wait 40 min only for them to tell me that they do not guarantee their work. What kind of business doesn't stand behind their work. In the very least, she could have told me no over the phone rather than have me drive out and wait 40 mins. In addition, the shop is not well ventilated and the chemical smell is overwhelming. Better to GO TO SPA ENVY and pay and extra $5 for work that will last. WILL NOT BE GOING BACK

This place is amazing! Great atmosphere, friendly staff, and the drinks are top-notch. I had the Guinness and it was poured to perfection. My friends got the Irish Mule and the Irish Coffee, and they both raved about them. We also tried the sliders and they were delicious. The bartender was super friendly and knowledgeable about the drinks. He even gave us a few recommendations for other bars to check out on our crawl. The only downside was that it was a bit cramped, but that's to be expected on a busy night like St. Paddy's Day. Overall, I highly recommend this place for a fun night out. We'll definitely be back!

I was in town for several days for work, and I was looking for a place to grab a bite to eat that wouldn't break the bank. I had heard good things about Grit & Grace, so I decided to give it a try. The restaurant is located in the heart of downtown Pittsburgh, which made it easy to get to after a long day at the office.When I walked in, I was immediately struck by the atmosphere. The decor was modern and stylish, but still had a warm and inviting feel. The staff was friendly and attentive, and they showed me to a cozy table by the window.I ordered the Chicken and Waffles, which arrived promptly and exceeded my expectations. The chicken was crispy and flavorful, and the waffles were light and fluffy. I was impressed by the quality of the food, especially considering the reasonable prices.I also want to give a shoutout to the service. My server was friendly and knowledgeable, and she made sure that my glass was always full and that I had everything I needed. The entire staff seemed well-trained and enthusiastic, which made for a great dining experience.Overall, I was very pleased with my visit to Grit & Grace. The food was delicious, the atmosphere was comfortable and inviting, and the service was top-notch. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a tasty and satisfying meal in Pittsburgh.

My friend and I were in the mood for a culinary adventure, and this restaurant certainly delivered. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, with soft lighting and comfortable seating that made us feel right at home. Our server was friendly and attentive, taking the time to explain the menu and offer thoughtful recommendations.We started with a few appetizers, which were all exceptional. The flavors were bold and innovative, and the presentations were visually stunning. The portions were generous, so we were glad we shared them.For our main courses, we opted for the beef Wellington and the seafood paella. The beef was cooked to perfection, with a tender and juicy texture complemented by a golden, flaky puff pastry crust. The paella was a seafood lover's dream, with a medley of shrimp, mussels, clams, and chorizo all cooked to perfection.The sides were equally impressive. The roasted vegetables had a nice balance of tenderness and crispness, while the garlic mashed potatoes were creamy and rich with a subtle hint of garlic.We finished off the meal with a decadent chocolate lava cake and a glass of rich, creamy Baileys. The cake was warm and gooey, with a perfect balance of sweetness and bitterness. The Baileys was smooth and velvety, with a nice hint of Irish cream.Overall, our meal at this restaurant was outstanding. The food was creative, expertly prepared, and delicious. The service was top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, making for a perfect night out. We're eager to return and try more of their dishes!

The atmosphere at Schoolboy Diem was warm and inviting with dim lighting and soft music playing. We were seated quickly by our friendly server Alex who came over to greet us and deliver menus. There was an extensive wine list to choose from as well as craft beers and cocktails. For an appetizer we decided to share the Bruschetta which was fresh and flavorful. F or our entrees I ordered the Chicken Piccata while my friend chose the Seared Salmon. Both dishes were perfectly cooked and presented beautifully. Nova lemon caper sauce for the chicken was light and zesty. My friend enjoyed the seasoning uesd on the salmon and sad it was one of the best preparations she had ever tried. Alex checked in often to see how we were enjoying our meals and refilled our water glasses promptly. I couldn't resist ordering the Tiramisu for dessert, it was heavenly. Throughout our meal the service was attentive without being overbearing. After we finished eating we lingered over coffee and digested our meal while catching up. Based on the quality of the food and service yo would definitely return to Carpe Diem for another meal. I would resommend it to anyone looking for a special night out for dinner. The prices were reasonable for the upscale but fortuitous dining experience. Whenever we left we felt satisfied and content from the excellent food and wine. I'm sure Carpe Diem will continue to be a local favorite for date noche and gatherings with friends and family. The charming ambiance and thoughtful menu made it the faultless sot for our relaxed evening catching up over a great meal.

With a $20 minimum dinner order they'll deliver for free. When it comes to sushi it's easy to spend that much. I ordered a serving of won ton soup, the tempura roll, the lobster roll, and a bottle of water for a total of $25 before tip. The won ton soup hit the spot. The broth with scallions was delicous with a hint of ginger without being spicy. It was only two or three won tons, but it was enough of a serving. The tempura roll was average and fine. The lobster roll was a huge disappointment. The menu description was boiled lobter with cucumber. And it was just that, but the lobster was hard, like cardboard, and hard to chew. It came with duck sauce and soy sauce, but that didn't help. I couldn't eat it all, and I love lobster. I would try them again, especially since they deliver, but I would order different rolls.

They didn't even deserve a one star. n This company and leasing managers are racist and treat people like they are nothing. All they want is you to sign on the dotted line and they got you! The 1 bedroom apartment we rented was a fucking DUMP when we moved in. The ceiling fan was ready to fall on our heads, there was black all over the a/c vents and the shelves in the closet were literally falling off the wall and the carpet had huge nasty stains everywhere. We were told our place was clean and ready to move in. nI have a medical condition called Cystic Fibrosis, I am on a lot of medication and my meds get delivered by UPS or FedEx to the front office. After the third box of my meds arrived, in about a weeks time, the leasing staff labeled me as being contagious and treated me like dirt. nAfter being there for two months, my doctor at MUSC in Charleston told me I have to live close to the hospital in order to get proper treatment and be able to go into the hospital when I am sick. We gave a written notice to the leasing manager and a doctors letter. The manager said, oh that's fine don't worry about it feel better (in her fake voice). Now, two years later I see they have put me on collection for $2000. nNo way will they get away with this. Do not rent from these Losers! How do they sleep at night

I think Pittsburgh is a little weird. For one thing, the downtown seems to be obsessed with pierogies. I mean, I get it, they're delicious, but come on, can't we branch out a modest? Every time I go to a restaurant, there's continually a pierogi dish staring me in the face. And don't even get me started on the seagulls. They're everywhere! I've never seen where many pigeons in my life. It's like they're elected over the city or something. But despite all that, I have to accepts that Pittsburgh has a certain charm to it. The people are friendly, and there's a lot of great art and culture to analyzing. The Andy Warhol Museum is a must-see, and the Phipps Conservatory is flatly stunning. And of course, you can't go to Pittsburgh without trying a Primanti Bros. pizza. They're a local institution, and for buon reason - they're freaking delicious. Overall, I'd spoke Pittsburgh is a bit of an buys taste, but it's definitely worth a visit if you're in the area. Just be prepared for some... let's tell, unique experiences. like the pierogi obsession and the pigeon buys. But heh, that's all part of the fun, right?

However, my experience at this 24-hour laundry place quickly turned sour. As soon as I walked in, I was hit by an overwhelming smell of mildew and mustiness. It was as if the air hadn't been freshened in ages. Despite the off-putting odor, I proceeded to load my clothes into one of the available washers. To my dismay, the machine was dirty and covered in grime, which made me question how well my clothes would actually get cleaned. Reluctantly, I decided to give it a chance and started the wash cycle. As I waited for my laundry to finish, I noticed that the overall cleanliness of the place was severely lacking. The floors were littered with lint, dirt, and even some discarded detergent pods. The washers themselves were old and worn, with buttons missing and dials that seemed barely functional. It was evident that this laundry facility had seen better days. To make matters worse, the dryers were not much better. I had to use multiple dry cycles just to achieve slightly damp clothes, let alone fully dry ones. The lack of proper maintenance was quite apparent, and it left me frustrated and disappointed. Another major issue was the overall lack of hygiene. There were no hand sanitizers or even soap available in the restroom area. It felt unsafe and unhygienic to be in such an environment, especially with the ongoing concerns related to public health. On top of all the cleanliness and maintenance issues, the customer service was abysmal. The staff seemed disinterested and unhelpful, barely acknowledging my presence when I needed assistance. It was clear that they couldn't care less about the customers or the state of the facility. All in all, my experience at this 24-hour laundry place was nothing short of a disappointment. Despite being open all the time, it failed to meet basic standards of cleanliness, functionality, and customer service. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone in search of a reliable laundry service.

Sushi Kim is a clean and bright place with seats on all two floors. The Korean BBQ buffet is on the second floor and only available on Friday and Saturday evenings starting at 5pm. The service was wonderful and the servers really helpful. The Korean BBQ is buffet style, so you help yourself to the raw proteins and vegetables at the buffet bars and then cook them on your hot plate at your table. It's a really fun and interactive eating experience. There weren't that many choices for proteins, but the choices that were available were all delicious. Protein choices ranged from mussels and shrimps to pork, chicken and beef. My favorite was the bulgogi beef. There were a few things I disliked about the Korean BBQ at Sushi Kim though. First off, they offered no butter or oil for the BBQ. I understand that they are trying to keep things healthy and all, but without any grease, the food was easily burnt. Butter or oil should always be an available option. Secondly, I did not like the design of their hot plates--the interior cooking area was way too tiny so it took forever to cook the food. And finally, they need to add a DESSERT BAR. After eating all that grilled food, I craved something sweet and refreshing. But, Sushi Kim left me hanging. Sushi Kim is already charging a whopping $24 per person--it would be nice if they throw in a dessert bar to sweeten up the deal (pun intended). Overall, I'm very thankful there is a Korean BBQ place in Pittsburgh. For being the only Korean BBQ buffet place in the area, it deserves a standing ovation. I had a great time at Sushi Kim and would gladly recommend the Korean BBQ buffet special. Buffet price was a bit high though, so crack open that piggy bank!

This place has such potential, but the cooking oil ruined it for me. I came here with high hopes after hearing good things from friends. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, and the menu looked promising. We ordered a variety of dishes to try, including the chicken stir-fry, the shrimp tempura, and the vegetable spring rolls. Unfortunately, the taste of the food was completely overshadowed by the rancid oil it was cooked in. The first bite of the chicken stir-fry left a greasy film in my mouth, and the shrimp tempura had a distinct unpleasant aftertaste. Even the vegetable spring rolls, which should have been a safe bet, tasted off and left a lingering oily residue on my fingers. I couldn't help but wonder if they ever changed their cooking oil. The service, on the other hand, was quite good. Our server was attentive and friendly, and our water glasses were promptly refilled. However, no amount of good service could salvage the disappointing flavor of the dishes. I considered sending the food back, but we were in a hurry and didn't want to cause a scene. As we left the restaurant, the lingering smell of old oil followed us out the door. It was truly a shame because I could see the potential for this place to be great. If only they would invest in fresh cooking oil and improve the quality of their ingredients, this could become a go-to spot in the area. But until then, I will have to warn others about the overpowering taste of rancid oil that lingers in every bite.

A couple old magazines here and there but that was about it. - Would have been nice if they had like a TV playing in the corner or something just to break up the silence a bit. - Staff was super friendly though, they came around periodically to see if anyone needed anything. Felt like they genuinely wanted to help out.- Only interacted with one other traveler while I was there, an older guy who struck up a convo with me about our flights. Seemed nice enough.- Anyway after about an hour I was starting to get restless so I decided to walk around the airport a bit to stretch my legs before getting on my next flight.- All in all it was a pleasant experience and I'm glad the USO was there as an option. Beats sitting around on an uncomfortable airport chair, that's for sure.- Would absolutely use it again next time I'm passing through Charlotte, which hopefully won't be too often but you never know with flights.- Overall it seems like they put a lot of thought into making the space welcoming and comfortable for travelers like myself just passing time. Personal pet peeve of mine is having nowhere relaxing to wait so I was happy with what I found.

Bottom line: the place is relatively clean, easy to navigate (in comparison) and is almost done up-fitting the retail to come up to the current trend of "mall-like" experiences. All terminals are span out from a center like the hub and spoke system of the airlines. The center court in the middle is best known for its cluster of shoppes, restaurants and (best loved) row of white rocking chairs that ironically back up to the people-mover walkways. People watching, alone, is worth the price of admission and the vast open space feels busy and energetic during prime time, but never stuffy. E Terminal is they newest and definitely feels so. If you fly international from Charlotte, you will be there. Seems there is a bigger selection of stores here but all terminals have some options. For those parking at Charlotte, you've got the usual choices of hourly, daily, long-tern and remote- each with successive price decreases but increasing distances from the terminal. A flurry of busses constantly circuits from the lots to the terminal and, unless you arrive late at night, are plentiful and well-marked. After hours we have much better success contacting an airport employee to let them know which bus we fare looking for. Just remember where you park- long term one is very different from long term 2! For those wanting a higher level of service, there is also terminal level valet and business valet. While I get the convenience of pulling up to the terminal and dropping off they keys, I do not understand the business valet- it is further away than remote parking and you still have to ride a bus. Yes, they will change your oil and clean the car (for an additional price) but the premium you pay here does not justify the product. My advice: skip business valet entirely. Otherwise, CLT is a typical airport but modern, clean, and open enough to make your time there easier to enjoy.

The following is some of the specific examples of UIUC: -The size of the campus: UIUC is a large campus, but never feels overwhelming. There are always many people around, but never too crowded. -The diversity of student groups: UIUC has a very diverse student group, which is one of my favorite things. I met people from all over the world, and I learned a lot of different cultures. -Education quality: UIUC's professor is first -class. They are knowledgeable, enthusiastic and dedicated to their students. I learned a lot from them, and I really like class. -Curm activities: UIUC provides a variety of extracurricular activities. This is a good way to participate in campus and meet new friends. I joined the club volleyball team, the Student Union and the Honorary Association. I also volunteered in the local soup kitchen.

I realize that coming as a party of 5 on Saturday night without a reservation is usually tough to accommodate, yet I was pleasantly surprised when the hostess told me they would move a table around and it would be about 10 minutes. We waited for 15-20 minutes and watched about 4 parties get sat before we asked what was taking so long since she had told us they were just moving a table. The hostess was very defensive and said that we shouldn't expect to get sat so soon without a reservation on a Saturday night, so we asked why she told us it would be 10 minutes. She then said that she needed to seat people with reservations before she could seat us and completely refused to acknowledge that she had given us a misleading wait time. I understand that it's hard to guage wait times, but when you're wrong you should simply apologize and not blame the guests for how they planned their evening. When we finally got sat, our server Angel was very good and the Buffalo style salmon steak is delicious. I really like the food here, but the fact of the matter is their customer service tonight was inexcusable. Even when the customer is wrong, you don't blame them and say "I'm sorry, but.. . " You simply apologize and try to defuse the situation instead of getting defensive and escalating the situation. If the hostess had simply said "I apologize for the wait taking longer than expected, we should be able to seat you in 5 minutes" and thanked us for our patience there would never have been an issue. I love the food, but I won't be coming back.

90 minutes for two cold pizzas? Are you kidding me? I've waited longer for a pizza that's actually hot and fresh out of the oven, not lukewarm and lackluster. I swear, some restaurants just don't get it. They think we're paying for the privilege of eating cardboard? Gimme a break!This place takes the cake, though. Or should I say, it takes the pizza? Ha! I kill me. But seriously, folks, if you're gonna charge me good money for a couple of slices, the least you could do is toss 'em in the oven for a minute or two. I mean, come on, 90 minutes? That's like, a whole episode of my favorite TV show, and I'm stuck here, waiting for a pie that's colder than my ex's heart.And don't even get me started on the toppings. You know what they say: you can't have too much of a good thing. But apparently, the guys at Pizza Place didn't get that memo. I mean, seriously, who puts four measly slices of pepperoni on a large pizza? That's like putting a cherry on top of a sundae and calling it a day. Where's the beef? Where's the bacon? Heck, where's the flavor? I might as well be eating a plain ol' tomato sauce. Blech!And don't even get me started on the crust. It's like they took abatch of raw dough, rolled it out, and then promptly forgot about it for half an hour. You know that feeling when you bite into a slice and it's all crispy and crunchy? Yeah, well, forget about that here. It's more like chewing on a piece of rubber. I swear, this pizza's been sitting out since the Clinton administration.But you know what the real kicker is? They had the nerve to charge me extra for the privilege of tasting this mediocrity. I mean, seriously, who do they think they are? The Pizza Illuminati? Like, I haven't been inducted into the secret society of pizza connoisseurs, so I don't know the secret handshake or anything, but I know a thing or two about good pizza. And this, my friends, is not it.And the service? Forget about it.

The food is expensive (~$12 for two eggs, toast, bacon, coffee) and the coffee isn't great, but the atmosphere is nice and I didn't come all that often so it seemed like sort of a luxury. The staff also isn't particularly outgoing, though not downright rude.. . until today. Today is Sunday, and I arrived around 8am. I usually try to get there kind of early and leave before it gets busy so I'm not taking up a table. I bought a big breakfast (as described above) and sat down to work. Just over an hour later, I was approached by a middle-aged man whom I assume is the owner or manager but whom I've never seen before. He asked if I was aware of their "new policy" about Wi-Fi on Sunday mornings, and how they don't want people just hanging out using the internet when it gets crowded. (No sugar coating, that's almost verbatim what he said. ) For the record, I wasn't actually using their wi-fi, I was writing. Whatever. His point was obvious. I stared at him for a few seconds because I couldn't believe that a proprietor was actually asking me, a paying customer, to leave when I had been there only an hour and in fact still had toast on my plate. He suggested it was fine for now but that when it started to get crowded I should get out. I said that if that's how they felt I would leave now, and he responded, "That's exactly how we feel. " I was shocked, and still am. I have never, NEVER been treated so disrespectfully in a place of business. And I'm a regular, paying customer!! I always leave a tip! I still can't believe I was treated this way. I will no longer recommend this place, now that they've shown their true colors. If the food was exceptional I might try to swallow my pride, but it's really nothing special. There are several other breakfast/coffee shops in the area (including a Starbucks across the road) and I will be patronizing them instead from now on.

Upstream is a new seafood restaurant that had been getting a lot of hype around town for its fresh local ingredients and innovative dishes. Unfortunately, my experience there did not live up to the high expectations. The service when we arrived was slow, and it took awhile to even be greeted by our server. Once we finally ordered, the food took a surprisingly long time to arrive to our table. The portions were smaller than I expected given the price of the entrees. I ordered the halibut which was overcooked and dry. My partner's shrimp tacos were flavorless. The sides we got seemed like an afterthought. Even the drinks were underwhelming - the cocktail I got was weak and the wine list lacked variety. Towards the end of the meal, another table began loudly complaining to the manager about their experience. As we went to pay the bill, it seemed like the kitchen was in disarray. I'm sure Upstream has potential with their concept but they clearly have some kinks to work out in terms of execution. Unless they can significantly improve, I don't think I'll be willing to give them another chance based on how disappointing this visit was. It's a shame because I was really hoping this restaurant would elevate the seafood scene around here.

We each ordered a beer and were promptly served. After taking a moment to glance over the menu, we decided on the pita pizza app, the special (beer battered fish/Mac and cheese) and the fish tacos. nThe pita pizza: a soft pita shell with pesto, tomatoes, chicken and cheese. BORING. nThis appetizer reminded me of my mother's Irish cooking: tasteless. A simple addition of caramelized onions would have solved this problem. nEntree 1: Beer battered fish and Mac and cheese. Ruling: BLAND. My husband ordered this one and described the fish as "wet" and the Mac and cheese as "play-doh". They also served the dish with lettuce, tomato and onion, as if it were a sandwich. nEntree 2: Fish tacos. Ruling: OVERCOOKED/COVER-UP ATTEMPTED. Ok, so they weren't bad, but the fish was dry. Covered with tomatoes and a bit of lettuce, the tacos were, again, on the tasteless side. The attempt at adding flavor came with the chipotle mayo and sour cream. nThese only helped to moisten the fish. The corn relish was masked by jalapeu00f1o peppers and the rice came shaped as if out of a small flowerpot. nThe service was quite friendly, so, no fault there. The chef, however, needs a bit of training.

The deli section is a bit short on variety and one wonders how long the sliced meats have been hanging around. The salads are okay and the olive bar fairly good. The meat and seafood sections are very good and the bakery adequate but not exceptional. I question where items are stocked, as there is often no rhyme or reason to it. Things that should logically be together are in different rows. The flavored creamer selection is wanting (I have an addicition to the stuff). Staff is usually friendly and helpful. My biggest complaint about the place is that items disappear from the shelves. Things I bought for weeks or months on end suddenly are no longer stocked. Frustrating. This goes for items in the deli, olive bar, and any other goods. I realize that things not in demand need to be culled to make room for things people want, but it seems that I must have a taste for things no one else wants. Curious. In the end, it's a decent place to do reguler grocery shopping.

Its been there ages, and looks it. If you're all about ambiance, don't bother. If you pretend you're in a movie set in Pittsburgh 30 years ago it works pretty well. The service is sometimes hit or miss. Most of girls are good, one is very slow, one is amazing. They are all friendly and usually a few different people will check in to make sure that you're happy. Everything is made fresh so be prepared that nothing comes flying out of that kitchen - busy times it can take a good while to get food. The food is AWESOME! Worth any little complaints I might think up before it gets there. Once its on the table, I forget them all. nn-Fish Sandwiichn-Salmon (huge and delicious)n-Floundern-Shrimp a few ways ("Norfolk" style is oily for my taste, and I never had it growing up in Norfolk. )n-Hawkins St Specialn-Prime Rib (sized for two, watch it)nnThe prices are low, the portions are large, and just about everything on the menu is delicious. I'm not one to pick a place because they give you a lot of food, but if you like a good value and don't want to compromise on taste, this place is a gem.

Today I came to pick up my dog after going here for over a month twice a week. I was told that my dog attacked a small dog who "did nothing", which doesn't sound like him at all (we go to dog parks and he's never done anything like that). I was told that they had repeatedly had problems with him (but no phone calls to me or notes when I picked him up) and that I should take him to a place with a limit on the number of dogs. They clearly had over 30 dogs in a single group outside and only one staff member attending them. Sometimes when I arrived, I have had to wait 5 or more minutes and the dogs were entirely alone. Quite frankly it sounds like they are not supervising the dogs well enough. Nothing quite adds up with this business, and while I would have sang their praises just a month ago for giving me a calm dog twice a week, they are clearly poorly managing their daycare. EDIT: My dog just has a confirmed case of Kennel Cough and the vet says that there have been 3 other dogs they have seen (in one practice!! ) that have it and who go to Hickory Hills!! STAY FAR FAR AWAY! !

Preferred Parking's rates are way too high. Their daily rate of $35 is absurd for parking in a crowded metropolitan lot. Street parking is often cheaper and effortless to find. I question how Preferred Parking justifies these inflated pricing. They must be making extraordinary profits by t aking advantage of captive customers who need parking near their destinations. It's unreasonable to charge such a high premium just because your lot is in a convenient location. I hope more affordable options emerge that provide a worthwhile alternative to Preferred Parking's excessively prised facilities. Unless they reduced their daily fees to a more reasonable tiers that doesn't gouge customers, I cannot recommend parking with this company in good conscience. People should consider other parking services or structures if possible to avoidRewarding Preferred Parking's greedy business model. Hopefully increased competition will force them to bring their rates more in line with what average users are reasonably willing to pay.

75 stars) Charlotte-Douglas may be my favorite large airport in the Eastern US. The arrangement of terminals is easy to maneuver, while the terminals themselves are well-lit and airy. There are many dining and drinking options, and cool rocking chairs. The gate waiting areas are too small, but there are better areas to wait. The car rental experience is on-site and efficient. TSA Security at Charlotte-Douglas seems to be able to expand during busy periods, and hasn't caused me any issues in dozens of flights. While not close to downtown, getting to the airport (or from airport to city) has always been smooth. The information booth folks are actually helpful; quite a change if you're arriving from Miami or NY/JFK. A very late arriving flight once caused me to miss a connection and on that particular night finding a nearby motel was pretty easy.

It's been a while since I've been back to my college town, and I was curious to see if the Sunday-brunch scene had changed. One of my favorite spots is still The Old Fashioned, a classic Wisconsin supper club that serves the best Bloody Marys in town. I was pleasantly surprised to find that there were still plenty of great options to choose from. Another great option is The Farmhouse, a cozy restaurant that serves farm-to-table cuisine. Their Sunday-brunch menu features seasonal ingredients and locally sourced meats, making it a great choice for those looking for a sustainable meal. Their menu is just as impressive, with everything from classic eggs Benedict to more creative dishes like blueberry pancakes with lemon curd. For something a little different, I recommend The Tornado Room, a speakeasy-style bar that serves some of the best cocktails in town. Their Sunday-brunch menu is small but mighty, with dishes like pork belly hash and avocado toast with smoked salmon. Here are a few more of my favorite spots for Sunday-brunch in Madison: The Brasserie at the Edgewater: This elegant restaurant offers stunning views of Lake Mendota and serves a delicious buffet every Sunday. Harvest: This farm-to-table restaurant is known for its seasonal menu and creative dishes. So next time you're in town, be sure to check out the local Sunday-brunch scene and see for yourself why it's one of the best in the country. Lazy Jane's Cafe: This cozy cafe is a great spot for a casual meal. Their menu features everything from classic breakfast dishes to more creative options like their huevos rancheros and breakfast tacos. Their Sunday-brunch menu is no exception, with dishes like sweet potato pancakes and roasted beet salad.

Because lets face it most of us have the same experience every time we go to a fast food place. I feel obligated here though because it was one of the worst experiences I have had at any establishment. I pull into the parking lot and the line was quite long, so I decide to park and order inside and get it to go. I give the homeless guy outside a dollar and make my way inside, this is normal on this side of town. When I enter I see there is a long line inside as well. Note to anyone, do not let hungry control you it was my mistake on this day. There was ONE person working the front of Wendys, not only was she taking peoples orders. She was also bagging the food, frying the fries and she was most likely making the burgers as well. I stood inline for probably 15 minutes, to get Wendys. When I should have left and just went to Cook Out down the street or even Pinky's. At least at Pinky's you have food in front of you in under 15 minutes. I took my burger home, I was polite to the girl working because I truly felt bad for her. I get home and open my food. I wish I was surprised but it was ice cold. The bun was firm like it was quite old. The cheese was hardly melted. So not only did I wait 15 minutes but I also got horrible fast food. Oxymoron I know but COME ON!

The interior is very nice. As soon as I stepped inside, I was greeted by an atmosphere of elegance and sophistication. The attention to detail was impeccable, with beautifully crafted furniture and tasteful decor adorning every corner. The color scheme was carefully chosen, creating a tranquil and inviting ambiance. The plush seating was incredibly comfortable, inviting me to sink in and relax. The lighting was perfect, striking a balance between warmth and brightness, enhancing the overall aesthetic. I was particularly impressed by the quality of the materials used, from the softest fabrics to the finest woodwork. The layout was thoughtfully designed, allowing for a seamless flow from one area to another. Each room had its own unique character and charm, offering a different experience within the same luxurious environment. The clever use of space made the interior feel spacious and open, even in areas that were inherently more confined. The blend of modern and classic elements created a timeless appeal that would never go out of style. The attention to acoustics was evident, as the interior remained serene, even amidst a bustling crowd. The incorporation of technology was seamless, with discreetly placed screens and speakers enhancing the overall experience. The attention to comfort extended beyond the seating, with climate control perfectly calibrated to ensure a pleasant temperature throughout. The interior felt like a sanctuary, a haven from the outside world where one could truly unwind and indulge in the surroundings. It was evident that every aspect of the interior had been meticulously thought out and executed, resulting in a space that was both visually stunning and practically functional. The attention to detail and commitment to excellence were evident in every corner of the interior, making it a truly exceptional experience.

This was not a four star dining experience. It was a very pleasant service experience, friendly and not too stuffy and you could tell they really have a lot of pride for the place. I actually feel bad about giving them a negative review because they seem like really nice people. And the house is very old and interesting but that's not the definition of four star. Grandma's china and chilled forks and old fashioned service was adequate but certain things just put it off; like the dingy rugs in the bathroom and the shabby landscaping and I don't know what all actually. Just felt a little amateurish. I did really enjoy the pear salad but the mushroom soup starter was cold and what really loses the stars for me is the mediocre entree of undercooked pork and tough steak. Really disappointing. I loved the sweet potato puree that came with it but it was the only flavor on the plate. And that undercooked pork was inedible and I don't even mind a little pink. This was raw in the center and mine wasn't the only one. No one wanted to complain as it was a customer event. But I would have sent it back if I were on my own. The desert was your typical banquet style flourless chocolate cake but no coffee was offered. Which may have been the planners fault but I really could have used some. Overall, a pleasant experience but doesn't live up to the reviews or the price tag. My guess is they do much better for a standard service rather than a banquet service of 40 people.

Otherwise, negative stars would be in effect. WHO on earth could possibly find this place worth returning to? What a completely miserable experience. The bitchy emo service obviously leaves something to be desired, then again so does the ENTIRE restaurant! Sure, melted cheese in a crepe is good. Know what else is good? ANY melted cheese from any breakfast place and Not having to endure this hell hole. I am just upset that I went there in the early part of my day and am now in a foul mood as a result. I have been in Pittsburgh a few weeks and this place is without rival the worst brunch I've ever had (PA or CA) So, the one positive thing about it IS.. .. it has made me appreciate every other sub par brunch I've had up until this point. Absolutely will never return. EVEN THE Orange juice was bad. Are you kidding?

After we received out app, we got our biscuits (in my opinion the order should have been reversed). That butter is heaven-sent though. Ordered pork belly and scallops for 30 bucks. Came out as two scallops and a piece of pork belly about the size of the scallop. Pork belly was overcooked and scallops were cool in the middle. I've had better quality and quantity for ten bucks less. My boyfriend ordered short ribs and that was awesome. For dessert we got the creme bru00fblu00e9e (nothing special) and a pecan pie (crust dough was essentially raw). That said drinks were well priced and service was okay. For total price, I would not come back. There is better quality food and service at a better price elsewhere. We got 1 app, 2 entrees, two desserts, four drinks, and two coffees for 150 bucks before tip.

Great first impression. The menu offered a vriety of interesting options that caught my eye. When the server came to take our order, she was extremely friendly and knowledgeable about all the dishes. Our fod arrived promptly and was beautifully presented. I enjoyed light and flavorsome fish, cooked to perfection. The sides were also exellent and provided a nice balance to the entree. The ambiance in the restaurant was relaxed yt elegant. As we finished our meal, we felt satisfied but not overly full. For dessert, the chocolate froth was rich and creamy. Overall we had a marvellous dining experience and will certainly return soon.

hubs and I have put off framing a sizable Thomas Kinkade print for a long time. Like three years long. We finally took this gorgeous print out of hiding and took it to Fastframe, purchased Yelp deal in hand. Well, errr, in phone. The woman who works here is super informed on the framing goods - matte colors, double mattes, types of framing, etc. She's busy yet friendly and definitely guides your choices. And this little shop is filled with options. So many options! Because of this, it took us a little while to come to our decision on colors and frame type. But we got it done! And then it came time to redeem the Yelp deal and pay. The redemption went fine, even though it seemed like they're running a plethora of deals and it was hard to keep track. The final price was much more than I expected, but I'm no framing connoisseur. I personally like to use those dollars by way of clothing! At the end of the day, the print looks great. It was well done and nicely put together. Would I have liked to pay less? Sure. Would I have another print or painting framed here? Sure!

The cornbread is good, but they are stingy with the butter. (one little container for four small loaves). The servings for the kids meals were ridiculously small, and they burnt the outside of the chicken fingers! My kids would not even eat them. Another big problem.. .. . parking! Charlotte is not getting locals into downtown on the weekends because you have to pay to park everywhere! I called the restaurant before going and asked where to park. The person told me we could park for free in the Holiday Inn parking garage. Not so! We had to pay $8 just to park for lunch! All said, we spent $60 for soul food! Rice and bean, shrimp creole, one kids plate of 2 chicken fingers, and one kids vegetable plate. Also, kids meals did not include a drink, and they charge $2. 00 for a child's drink. It was hot in the restaurant, loud from the voices of other diners, and you couldn't hear the music. This place is not worth the price. I could have prepared that food several times over for what I paid in that restaurant!

I enjoyed eating here well enough. I'm honestly not a die-hard fan of German food, although I guess that wouldn't have mattered: a peak at the menu beforehand revealed that this place's menu is mostly Americanized - proof of this is the fact that my salad was topped with French fries (only in Pittsburgh.. . ). Trust me, even if you don't really like German food, there'll at least be a sandwich you'll like here. Thinking about my usual "overall" summary, I have to say this place wasn't bad and served as a reasonable place to meet - the beer menu looked nice from what I saw and the atmosphere was pretty cozy and even nostalgic and homely - but man, the dining options really weren't that extraordinary. I'm still torn as to how to feel about its menu, because on the one hand obviously it being Americanized meant even I could find something to enjoy, but on the other I feel bad for the people who do like German food and may not be getting what they hope for. It wasn't bad enough that I'd say don't try it and see - just understand it may not be exactly what you expect.

For what it's worth, dor-stop isn't good as people say it was. I had heard rave reviews about this restaurant and decided to give it a shot despite my reservations. Upon entering, I was greeted by a charming atmosphere with dim lighting and eclectic decor, which added a touch of sophistication to the place. However, my high hopes soon deflated as I delved into the menu.The first disappointment came with the appetizers. I ordered the much-hyped bruschetta, but the bread was overly toasted and lacked the fresh flavors I had expected. The toppings were mediocre at best, failing to deliver the burst of vibrant ingredients promised in the description. Moving on to the main course, I opted for their signature dish, the dor-stop steak. Sadly, the steak was chewy and lacked the tenderness and succulence one would expect from a premium cut. The accompanying sauces and sides did little to compensate for the underwhelming taste of the meat.Moreover, the service was subpar. The waitstaff seemed disinterested and inattentive, making it difficult to get their attention when needed. The overall lack of warmth and enthusiasm dampened the dining experience.The dessert selection offered some respite from the disappointment of the previous courses. I decided to try their famous chocolate lava cake, and it was the highlight of the meal. The warm chocolate oozing from the center provided a delectable and indulgent experience, momentarily redeeming the otherwise lackluster meal.In conclusion, while dor-stop may have garnered positive reviews from some, my personal experience left much to be desired. The underwhelming appetizers and main course, coupled with lackluster service, fell short of my expectations. The saving grace was the exceptional chocolate lava cake, but it wasn't enough to salvage the overall dining experience. Unfortunately, I wouldn't rush back to dor-stop anytime soon, as there are other establishments that offer a more satisfying culinary experience.

There are a lot of trees, which makes it difficult to hit the ball where you want it to go. The greens are slow and bumpy, and the fairways are not well maintained. In general, I was not impressed with this course and would not recommend it to anyone. Even if you are looking for a cheap round of golf. In addition to the poor course conditions, the staff was also very unfriendly. They were not friendly or helpful, and they seemed to be more interested in talking to each other than helping golfers. I would recommend that you check out some of the other courses in the area before you decide to play here. There are much better options for the same price or even less. The only good thing I can say about this course is that it is located in a beautiful area. The views of the mountains are beautiful and the air is clean and fresh. But that is not enough to make up for the poor course conditions and the unfriendly staff. There are much better options for the same price or even less. I would not recommend this course to anyone.

Because I had never heard of Sammy's, ergo could not verify its fame, particularly when using the following model of logic: nnMcDonalds? Famous. nTom's Diner in NYC? Famous - if only because of Jerry Seinfeld and Suzanne Vega. nSammys?. .. to.. .. .. Pittsburghers.. . ? But none of my pals had ever eaten at Sammy's. Sure, they'd driven by and read the signs, but they'd never gotten off their duffs and had a go at this 'famous' corned beef. So I decided to do it myself. Here's how it went: nnMy corned beef sandwich featured (drum roll, please): corned beef (!! ! ), Swiss cheese, rye bread, sauerkraut, and Russian dressing. I double-checked my notes on corned beef sandwiches I had previously consumed in my lifetime. ALL THE INGREDIENTS WERE THE SAME. So, I asked myself: what makes Sammy's corned beef famous? nn1. It's not the corned beef. I mean, it was good corned beef, but it wasn't life-changing. I certainly wouldn't challenge another deli to a Corned Beef Showdown with Sammy's in my corner. n2. It's not the Swiss cheese. I'm pretty sure that Swiss cheese served in Switzerland would be vastly superior. n3. Maybe it's the bread. Most rye bread is thin. Sammy's has thick rye bread. And it's soft. Very pleasant. n4. It's not the sauerkraut. My German grandmother whips up a mean sauerkraut, the kind her mom made in the Old Country 50+ years ago. Sammy's isn't anything to sneeze at. n5. It's not the Russian dressing. Can anyone stake a claim in truly superlative Russian dressing? Maybe the Russians. But not Sammy. It seems that I'm bashing Sammy, but I'm not. I just don't think it was anything special. I enjoyed my sandwich, but I might have enjoyed more the conversation I was having whilst eating the sandwich. Maybe, Sammy, you're famous for claiming you're famous. That's how Paris Hilton achieved fame, so you're in good company. I think.

I recently stayed at this hotel while in town for a business meeting. The hotel was clean and the staff was friendly. The room was a bit small, but it was comfortable. The location was convenient to everything I needed. The breakfast was good, but the coffee was weak. The pool was nice, but crowded. The fitness center was small, but it had everything I needed. The business center was great, and I was able to get everything I needed done. The meeting rooms were spacious and well-equipped. The staff was very helpful in setting up the meeting and ensuring everything went smoothly. The food at the banquet was delicious, and the service was excellent. Overall, I had a great stay at the hotel and would definitely recommend it to others.

The staff at the front desk and throughout the hotel were very friendly and helpful. My room had a view over the city, which was beautiful at night. The room was clean and spacious, with a comfortable bed. Here is my review in sixteen sentences: The bathroom was clean and well-equipped, with a large shower and a deep bathtub. The water pressure was excellent, and the towels were fluffy and soft. The bed linens were luxurious and soft, and I slept very well. The room was also very quiet, and I was not disturbed by any noise from outside. The hotel also has a fitness center, a pool, and a restaurant. The hotel is located in a great area, with easy access to shopping, dining, and entertainment. The hotel also has a great bar, with a wide selection of drinks and a great atmosphere. The restaurant had a great atmosphere, and the food was delicious. The staff was very attentive and friendly. The bartenders were also very friendly and helpful. I had a great time at the hotel, and I would definitely recommend it to others.

Rock Bottom exceeded our expectations with its inviting atmosphere and friendly staff. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted warmly by smiling faces and a lively ambiance. The interior decor showcased a trendy industrial vibe, with exposed brick walls and rustic wooden furniture, creating a cozy and inviting setting.Seated comfortably in a spacious booth, we quickly perused the menu, which boasted a wide range of options to please every palate. From delectable appetizers to hearty main courses, Rock Bottom had something for everyone. Our server was attentive and well-informed, happily providing recommendations and answering any questions we had about the dishes.To kick off our late-night feast, we indulged in their famous loaded nachos. The portion was generous, with a mountain of crispy tortilla chips topped with melted cheese, guacamole, sour cream, and zesty salsa. Every bite provided a perfect combination of flavors and textures, setting the bar high for the rest of our meal.For the main course, we opted for the restaurant's signature burger selection. I chose the Rockstar Burger, stacked with caramelized onions, smoky bacon, melted cheddar cheese, and a tangy barbecue sauce. The patty was juicy and cooked to perfection, with the toppings adding a delightful burst of flavors in each bite. The accompanying sweet potato fries were crispy and perfectly seasoned.My dining companion decided to go for the vegetarian option and ordered the Portobello Mushroom Burger. It was a delightful surprise. The grilled Portobello cap was marinated in balsamic glaze and served with roasted peppers, fresh arugula, and a zingy garlic aioli. The flavors melded together harmoniously, providing a satisfying and savory experience.To complement our meal, we each selected a craft beer from their extensive selection. The staff demonstrated deep knowledge about their beer offerings, suggesting pairings that perfectly matched our taste preferences.

The momnet I stepped into Rock Bottom, I was greeted by a warm and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant's rustic decor and cozy lighting instantly set the mood for a delightful dinner experience. The attentive staff promptly seated me and handed me a menu filled with enticing options. After careful considera tion, I ordered their signature burger accompanied by a side of crispy sweet potato fries. The burgers arrived promptly, cooked to perfection, with a juicy patty and a satisfying combination of toppings. Each bite exploded with flavor, leaving me impressed with the quality of ingredients used. We decided to order from Texter's fish camp. We ordered fish fried and shrimp. I will score the solid of the fish into 10, shrimp A 9, and the puppy and 8 years old. We arrived shortly after 12 and, like others have mentioned, the line was out the entryway. However, even though the line was long it moves smoothly and didn't take too long. The place we're talking about is called Murphy's and it's located in Urbana, Illinois. It's a sports bar that seems to be stuck in the past, with outdated TVs and a limited selection of channels. The service is also subpar, with servers who seem to be disinterested in taking orders and a lack of attention to detail when it comes to the basics, like making sure the TVs are showing the right games.As a sports fan, it's frustrating to go to a place that's supposed to be dedicated to showing live sports and find that they're not even doing the basics right. The TVs are old and not all of them are even showing sports, which is just unacceptable. And when you try to ask for a specific game, they seem to have a hard time accommodating you. It's like they're not even trying to make the experience enjoyable for their customers.I've been to other sports bars before, and I know that it's possible to have a great experience. The place should be jumping on game day, with plenty of screens showing different games and a lively atmosphere. But at Murphy's, it's like they're just going through the motions. They're not even trying to create an atmosphere that's conducive to enjoying a game. And the food, while decent, is not enough to make up for the other shortcomings.It's a real shame, because with a little bit of effort, Murphy's could be a great place to watch sports. They just need to get their act together and invest in some modern technology, like new TVs and a better selection of channels. And maybe they could train their staff to be a little more attentive and friendly. Until then, I wouldn't recommend wasting your time at this dump.

Went with BF's family for a family celebration. We had reserved the large room for our group. When we arrived, we were told by the hostesses to wait to speak with the manager. The bedraggled manager plodded over and informed us that the room had been mistakenly double-booked and another party had already been seated in the room. She tried for about 25 seconds to be pleasant and apologetic, but then her willingness to make her customers happy wore thin. She harumphed and threw her hands in the air while saying, "We made a mistake. What do you want us to do? " Well, I definitely want you to learn how to act like a professional. We declined being seated amongst the party in the large room and took one of the tables in the middle of the dining room. The place was shabby and the floor was filthy. I mean, I typically wouldn't notice, because I'm not looking at the floor, but it was noticeably dirty. The food was average. The one highlight: the chef was professional, light-hearted and entertaining. He couldn't save the day, though. I would not return, and I cannot recommend.

I recently visited this dealership for a safety recall related to the cruise control of my 2002 Ford Explorer. This was my second or third visit to this location for service on this vehicle. I have consistently been pleased with the service I have received at this location.I highly recommend this dealership to anyone in need of service on their Ford vehicle. Only you can be the judge on that one. There are pool tables, video games, and lots of TVs. There is also a small dance floor. The music is pretty good. The food is great; I would recommend the burgers and wings. The staff is very friendly. The place is usually pretty busy, but it is never too crowded. Whether you are looking to watch a game, play some pool, or just have a few drinks with friends, this is the place to go. I highly recommend it. This place is a hidden gem. The hotel is beautiful inside and out. We don't normally stay in nice hotels, so we were surprised by how nice it was, especially the extremely comfortable king-sized bed. It made for the perfect romantic getaway in a hectic weekend filled with bars, parties, and souvenir shopping on The Strip. There are some things you should know before you book at The Priory, however. The hotel is right across the street from a housing project. There isn't enough parking, especially if The Grand Hall is hosting a wedding when you arrive. If you get a room that is street-adjacent you may be woken up by sounds like people talking or shoveling the sidewalk. Overall, none of these things bothered me that much (aside from getting woken up by the snow shoveler, but I suppose that was better than cracking my head on an icy sidewalk later! ). However, if you're the type of person who gets easily annoyed at minor inconveniences or gets uncomfortable around lots of african-americans, you may want to stay at the Doubletree or Westin or something. If you're looking for a charming boutique hotel and you're not afraid of being on the North Side, you should definitely check out The Priory.

This film absolutely delivers on its promises of fun, adrenaline-fueled entertainment. From the explosive opening scene, it's crystal clear that this movie isn't taking itself too seriously and aims solely to provide an enjoyable ride. The straightforward plot serves as a solid framework to showcase breathtaking stunts and impressive visual effects. Several amusing cameo appearances enhance the movie's enjoyable nature. While the storyline lacks innovation, it moves at a brisk clip and maintains audience interest. Genre fans will appreciate nods to classic action films of yore. Moreover, all the central characters exude likability and charisma, pulling viewers fully into their on-screen exploits.The action sequences exhibit thoughtfully crafted choreography and thrill. Even the more exaggerated unbelievable moments carry enough wit and humor to avoid coming across as too self-important. Comedy and drama find an effective balance, widening the film's appeal. Visually, it's a treat bolstered by impressive cinematography that amplifies the excitement.While far from high art, as an action-packed romp, it fully delivers on promised escapism. It understands precisely what kind of film it is and commits accordingly. Those seeking a mindless yet enjoyable way to spend a couple hours will likely feel satisfied. The conclusion sets up future installments if the studio opts to continue the franchise. Overall, it's an entirely entertaining popcorn film that accomplishes its aim.

My fiance, a friend and I were trying pizza from three different places and Luigi's was one of them. I have driven by Luigi's many times before and for some reason had never stopped in but that did allow it to come to mind whenever I was looking for a pizza place I had not yet tried in the Bellevue area. Whenever I called to place my order I was told that my pizza would be ready in about 15 minutes. I arrived closer to 30 minutes later and was immediately confused whenever I walked into the restaurant. You see there was a large dining room on the left that was full of people and I didn't immediately see the are where I would get my pizza from. Finally after a few steps into the restaurant I noticed that the whole back area of the restaurant was where I needed to be and I made my way back there. My pizza was ready for me and I quickly paid and was leaving whenever the cashier told me "Stay out of trouble". I really hope that was a friendly sentiment and not one that was based upon my appearance or anything else. The pizza itself had a medium thick crust with a bland sauce which is weird since I could see a ton of green herbs in it. The cheese was just ok and nothing special while the pizza itself had a slightly sour taste to it which I did not enjoy. Out of the three different pizzas we ate that night this one was overwhelmingly our least favorite which was evidenced by the fact that 3/4 of it was left after the evening. The bottom line for me is that I will probably not head back to Luigi's in the future. I just don't see myself making a trip to Luigi's between the weird experience (although not bad) that I had in the restaurant and the fact that there are much better pizza places nearby.

Laundry Factory is located along Ellsworth Avenue next to Pitt's Dogg'n It and Tokyo Japanese Food Store. Your first impression of this place might range from "This place is clean" to "There are a lot of machines here" to "I can use my credit card to start the washer/dryer? " to "TVs?! Yes, please. " Your impressions are all on point. Indeed, this laundromat is one of the cleanest I've been to. Yes, there are many machines here! Even during the busiest laundry times (the weekends), you should be able to find a machine or two that are free. Some of the larger machines accept debit/credit cards. A word of caution: for the dryers, each time you add quarters or swipe to add extra time, you will need to press "Start" or else you will lose your money. The laundromat recently attached warning labels to each applicable machine. There are two television sets, so don't worry about missing that Penguins/Steelers/Pirates game, because there is a good chance those televisions are tuned in to those games. There is an ATM machine next to the front desk in case you are short on quarters, and the employees will gladly break your $20 bills into smaller ones. There are change machines next to the ATM machine and along the window facing Ellsworth Avenue. I counted 5-6 folding stations, which means you might have to wait or share them during the busiest laundry times. Oh, and feel free to bring your tablet or laptop because the facility has free WiFi, which is password-protected, but you can ask any employee for it. I didn't give the facility 5 stars because: 1, the place can get a little chaotic and very hard to navigate during its busy times, and 2, the overall cost can really add up, especially if you have lots of clothes (I don't know about what others think.. . perhaps I'm used to the super-cheap-economy pricing? Haha.. . ).
