This is the last 23 perspective of the given first sentence: I was flying out of Charlotte and I really arrived at the airport early, so I chose breakfast. There are a few good choices in the airport, but I settled in some things at Charlotte Bistro. In the early morning, it was crowded, but I could catch a small table by the window. I started with a cup of coffee, which was very ordinary, and then looked at the menu and decided to eat. They have various breakfast sandwiches and platter, and they look good. I finally settled on eggs and cheese sheep's bread because I didn't want to be too heavy before flying. It soon came out, and there was a flowing egg yolk inside. Sanmingzhi is fresh and fills, but it is not too large to eat quickly before boarding. When I ended, as people went to fly, the crowd of the restaurant began to sparse. I glanced at the window and looked at the aircraft that took off in the distance. After finishing, I lost some cash on the table, stretched to my door, and got coffee in my hand. Soon after walking to the door, I had enough time to arrive. I found a comfortable seat next to the window, then settled down, enjoyed my rest of the coffee, and let some people watch it. When they issued a flight announcement, the door became more crowded. Soon after, they called and boarded the plane, and I joined the aircraft on the line. The flight was short and stable, take -off and landing. I want to talk about the breakfast of Charlotte's tavern and make a good way to start the morning.

I went there for the first time in a while, and everything was as great as I remember. First up was the mouth wateringly scrumptious cornbread, fresh out of the oven and served with plenty of butter. I liked it so much that I asked for more when my entru00e9e arrived. I had the salmon cakes, which were the best I have ever eaten. These are not your grandma's salmon cakes- no canned stuff here. This was fresh salmon which they poach in house. It was perfectly seasoned, nice and moist on the inside and crispy on the outside. It is served with a remoulade that compliments it perfectly. My two sides were candied yams and okra and tomatoes. The Yams were delicious- not overly sweet but still nice and gooey and pleasing. The okra and tomatoes were good, although interestingly enough, there were no tomatoes in my serving. Just okra. It didn't matter. I gobbled it up anyway. Everything was served promptly and at the proper temperature, the du00e9cor was warm and welcoming, and the service helpful and friendly. You should have nothing to complain about if you come to Mert's, unless you are a chronic complainer. In that case, you should go home and cook and let the staff come to your house and complain about your cooking.

Perhaps my tenure has outlived its usefulness. I have been here almost four years, and I increasingly feel I no longer contribute meaningfully. I do not know if this is due to my age or the changing world around me. Regardless, I sense I am losing my edge.Once, I kept up with current trends, but now I seem perpetually behind. I am unfamiliar with what interests young people today, their music, and fashion. I am becoming obsolete.It's not just the young making me feel old; it's the rapidly changing world. Everything moves at a breakneck pace. The constant stream of information and technology overwhelms me, leaving me behind.I am at a loss for what to do. I do not want to become that elderly person griping about how much better things were in the past. Simultaneously, I do not want to feel irrelevant. I yearn to remain connected to the world, but I am unsure how.I have considered returning to school, but I am not sure I am up to the challenge. I have also pondered starting my own business, but I lack ideas. I feel adrift and directionless.I recognize that I am not alone. Others struggle to keep up with the changing world. We are in this together, and we must find a way to support each other.I may not have the answers, but I will continue seeking them. I refuse to surrender without a fight. I will find a way to stay relevant and connected, and I will help others do the same.

My brother found it for all of us to stay at while in Madison for my uncle's funeral. It's a little further out of town than I normally like but it's five minutes away from TownEast Mall and places to eat so it was perfect for the occasion. Right off the bat, because I have Hilton HHonors card, I got 500 bonus points and a chocolate bar and a bottle of water from the staff. That was exactly what I needed. nThe room is large and had a fridge, microwave and a dishwasher. None of which I needed but good to know. The free WiFi was such a joy and it was fast too. Plenty of space to lay out my laptop and external hard drive. Bed was comfortable although i did get bit up by something - fleas maybe. Flat screen was new with plenty of channels. The free breakfast was also good - cereals, oatmeals, bagels, fruit, muffins, coffee, OJ - all perfectly suited for us. After the funeral we returned and all of us sat in their 'family room' to play cards and have some cocktails. Everyone was totally cool with that. I imagine that in the spring and summer this hotel stays very busy. One thing though, for some reason, they are not listed on the wall at the airport for their shuttle service. You might want to call in advance. If I ever travel with a large group to Madison again, I'm sure we will stay there. I highly recommend it!

Other people may have had a better experience with this company, but that was not the case for us. We were looking forward to a smooth and hassle-free rental experience, but unfortunately, we were met with nothing but disappointment. From the moment we walked into the Hertz office, it was evident that there was a lack of organization and efficiency.The staff seemed overwhelmed and unprepared for the influx of customers. It took an absurdly long time for us to even be acknowledged, let alone assisted. We watched as other customers became increasingly frustrated, some even walking out in frustration. It was a chaotic scene that left a sour taste in our mouths right from the start.When we finally did get our turn, the agent appeared disinterested and unenthusiastic. They didn't bother explaining the rental terms clearly and rushed through the entire process. It felt as though they couldn't wait to get rid of us and move on to the next customer. This lack of attentiveness and professionalism was disheartening.To make matters worse, the vehicle we were given was in poor condition. It had numerous dents and scratches, and the interior had not been properly cleaned. It was clear that the previous renters had not treated the car with care, but instead of addressing these issues before renting it out again, the company seemed content with providing subpar vehicles.As we hit the road, we soon realized that the car was not well-maintained. It made strange noises, and the brakes felt unreliable. We couldn't help but worry about our safety during the entire journey. It was a nerve-wracking experience that took away from the enjoyment of our trip.Additionally, the GPS system in the car was outdated, leading us astray multiple times. We ended up wasting valuable time and fuel trying to navigate unfamiliar roads based on inaccurate directions. It was frustrating and completely unnecessary.

I have to say that the reviews for this wonderful local American pub are not misleading. Dark old school interior with lots of bead-board wainscoting, a tin ceiling, and a variety of vintage print material adorning the walls, the place is comfortable and inviting. The place was full and bustling on this particular Tuesday night (despite being past the dinner hour). The host (who I think has been tagged as "Ken" in an earlier review was friendly and found me a table for one immediately (a great corner booth that gives a good view of the establishment) and my waitress, Traci, was flawless. Clearly a neighborhood haunt, a wide variety of clientele were enjoying the evening making for some pleasant people watching. I really enjoyed my time at AM's, but I must confess that the food was good, but not great. The spicy crab soup was tasty, but not nearly spicy enough, and the 4th Ward Beef Stroganoff had a nice traditional flavor, but the sauce was too thin to stick to the meat or rotini or my ribs. My personal business travel rules discourage me from eating at the same place twice, but if I were in need of a good comfort food meal in a place with some good energy, Alexander Michael's would be on my short list.

We made a reservation in advance, and upon arrival, we were greeted warmly by the staff. The ambiance of the restaurant was elegant and sophisticated, creating a perfect setting for a special occasion. We were promptly seated at a cozy table near the window, offering a lovely view of the city skyline. Our waiter introduced himself and wished my husband a happy birthday, which was a thoughtful gesture. He provided us with menus and gave some recommendations.To start our meal, we decided to indulge in the restaurant's renowned seafood options. We ordered the oysters Rockefeller and the shrimp cocktail. The oysters were incredibly flavorful, with a delicious blend of spinach, bacon, and cheese on top. The shrimp cocktail was beautifully presented, accompanied by a tangy cocktail sauce that complemented the fresh and succulent shrimp perfectly.Moving on to the main course, I opted for the signature dish of the restaurant, the prime rib. The waiter assured us that it was a popular choice, and I can understand why. The prime rib was cooked to perfection, tender and juicy, with a mouthwatering crust. It was accompanied by a side of creamy mashed potatoes and buttered asparagus, both of which were exquisite.My husband decided to try the surf and turf, which consisted of a filet mignon and a lobster tail. The filet mignon was cooked exactly as he had requested, a beautiful medium-rare, and it practically melted in his mouth. The lobster tail was succulent and incredibly flavorful, a true delicacy.Throughout our dining experience, the service was impeccable. Our waiter was attentive, knowledgeable, and ensured that we had everything we needed. The staff also surprised my husband with a complimentary dessert, a decadent slice of chocolate cake with a candle on top, accompanied by a heartfelt rendition of "Happy Birthday" from the restaurant staff. It was a thoughtful touch that made the evening even more special.

! nSorry to say, this place is a disaster. Not because the decor is cheesy, but because they are mind numbingly slow, and the food is uber-forgettable. nWe called ahead and found that we could get a table for 16 on the patio, but when we got there at our appointed time nothing was ready - bad first impression. We were sat at four different tables near each other and moved the tables ourselves to create a configuration where our group could talk. nThe waitress asked a couple times if anyone needed anything, but great service starts with keeping water glasses full, so if you see an empty one - FILL IT! That is decent restaurant skills 101 and costs you a star every time. nThe food was cold, overcooked, tasteless and a little scary. I got a spicy burger and it was bland. nThe only way I would eat at this chain again would be if I washed up on a beach after being marooned for a week and they were giving the food away FREE.

Our waitress (Annemarie) was inattentive and got us the wrong order. We ended up with a dish we had not even ordered and still got charged for it on the check. One of my friends ordered a Buffalo Chicken Sandwich, which according to the menu description, should've had lettuce and tomato in it. But the sandwich that arrived on our table had none of those ingredients. When pointed out to the waitress, she just brought some lettuce and tomatoes in a plate! How crude! Spoke to the manager after paying the full check and first of all, she did not even offer to re-imburse for the item we did not even order, and that had been forcibly thrust upon us. When I asked the manager about the Buffalo Chicken sandwich not having any lettuce and tomato, she said they just got new menus and that description is not correct and that Buffalo Chicken Sandwich is supposed to be without lettuce and tomato! What a lame excuse! Even your online menu says under the description for a Buffalo Chicken sandwich that its supposed to have both those ingredients - "Served with lettuce and tomato on a fresh-baked Kaiser roll. " - That's what the last line in the description of Buffalo Chicken Sandwich says. Shame on you Manager for lying! Instead of admitting her fault, she was blaming it to a new menu! Not only did we have to pay for something that we didn't order or eat, but we got sub-standard food that was different from what was described in the menu, and had to deal with a really bad waitress and insensitive and deceitful manager to top off the whole experience. I am never going to come back to any Eat N Park location ever again, and will never recommend one to any of my friends either. What a waste of time and money! Plus dealing with callous and lying people - my goodness, I surely had my patience tested this evening!

Every* time I've ordered delivery it has been incredibly late. This past time was the worst. An order estimated at 30 minutes still wasn't here 1. 5 hours later so I called and they claimed it had just left. They called up from the call box once and then left within seconds. (For whatever reason it went straight to voicemail, which I got notification of immediately. ) I literally ran down and circled the lot and they were long gone. The store then pretended they couldn't hear me when I called from numerous phones and numbers until finally I interrupted their speech about the promotion and called them out for stuttering since they clearly heard me. (Before that they'd say the special really fast and immediately say "hello? hello? " and hang up. ) I will never order from this location again.

Location is convenient, especially if you're catching a flick nearby. The food Not stellar, but not horrible either. It's on the pricey side, but you probably know that already. It takes money to keep the engine running. What is really bad is the service. Well, that's not entirely true. The service is actually friendly - very much so, in fact. They greet you, and seat you fairly promptly (at the appropriate times), keep your beverages filled, clear plates, just about everything. But the wait for the food is absolutely ridiculous. Not one of those "where is the food" moments, but about ten of them, back to back, and it's not just when they are busy - even when the place is empty, it takes forever to be served. It could be blamed on the freshness of the food, but we're talking even soup and fairly simple stir fry or chicken dishes, so this isn't rocket science. Or perhaps it is and all those other Chinese places just do it better.

The menu looked very similar to our local Popey's, with all our favorite dishes represented. We started with a chicken tender, which was cooked to perfection, hot and crispy on the outside, but still juicy on the inside. The fries that came with it were definitely cut in the house and tasted great with a side of ranch dressing. For the main course, I chose one of Popey's signature dishes, the cajun pasta, which was spicy without being overpowering. My wife had the classic chicken sandwich, which was piled high with lettuce, tomato and mayo. The bun was soft and fresh and it was a satisfying lunch portion. Service was friendly and attentive without being intrusive. My dining companion chose the grilled chicken salad with mixed greens, avocado, bacon and a zesty dressing. We were both satisfied with our choices and left feeling full, but not overstuffed. Our server was knowledgeable about the menu and substitutions. We would be happy to return the next time we are in the area and looking for good, uncomplicated food. The atmosphere was casual and family friendly, with upbeat music playing. This location successfully captured what we love about Popey's.

Hubby and I like to hang out in Charlotte on the weekends, and this is definately a great hotel. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, with nice amenities like a mini fridge and coffeemaker. The beds are incredibly soft and we slept like a rock both nights. For breakfast they offer a nice hot buffet with eggs, pastries, yogurt and fruit. The location is also excellent as it's just a short drive from all the downtown attractions and entertainment. The staff was very friendly and helpful, they gave us some good recommendations for dining and activities in the area. We enjoyed having an indoor pool and hot tub to relax in after a long day of hiking and shopping. I would say the WiFi worked well except it was a little spotty in our room. We plan on staying here again next time we visit Charlotte as it offered a really great value for the money. I would highly recommend this hotel to others traveling to Charlotte.

We found the perfect restaurant on Yelp and quickly chose Mert's Heart & Soul. I love comfort food so this was my heaven. I had blackened pork chops with collards and mac&cheese. The mac&cheese was so delicious that I almost ordered a second round. My husband had the ribs and fried chicken combo with collards and mashed potatoes. I tasted his and it was yummy too. The cornbread loaves were scrumptious with the sweet butter. So not to be left hungry later when we returned to our hotel, we ordered the soul rolls & smoked turkey with beans & rice plus dessert- coconut cake, banana cake & caramel cake. All of the cakes were moist and full of flavor. nOur waitress, Malika was great! She was funny, attentive and pointed us in the right direction with her recommendations. She made our dinner a complete success. We will definitely be visiting again and asking for Malika when we return.

I wanted a real deli sandwich (not Subway). I thought I'd give this place a try. $10. 00 got me a 6" meatball sub on a white bun, Lay's potato chips, and a pickle spear, with a regular soda. The sub was not one bit better than Subway. This was a complete waste of my time and money. I could have had the same exact thing (sans the pickle), and chosen my own chips from a variety. nThey have a lot of food on the menu; I have no idea how the soups, salads, etc. are. All I know is that I couldn't even find a list of the types of bread they offer on the menu. This place is hard to navigate, and the food quality is not worth the trouble. UPDATE: Went back for lunch (at a friend's request) on Tuesday (11/1). I had the chicken club salad and a cup of the Southwestern Chicken Chili. Both were quite good. My bill: $14. 90. I'll up the rating to 2 stars, as the food is OK (not great), but it is WAY overpriced.

I do have to admit, I was a tad hesitant to try this new restaurant. Its unremarkable storefront and unassuming name made me question whether it was worth my time. But, as a self-proclaimed gastronomic guru, I knew I had to give it a shot. After all, I pride myself on my ability to discern the subtle nuances between a mediocre dish and an exceptional one. And let me tell you, dear reader, this place did not disappoint.As soon as I walked in, I was struck by the understated elegance of the décor. The dim lighting, pristine tablecloths, and tasteful artwork all hinted at a level of sophistication that I had not expected. The hostess greeted me warmly and led me to a cozy table by the window, where I could watch the hustle and bustle of the street outside.The menu, of course, was the real star of the show. A medley of traditional dishes with modern twists, it was evident that the chef was not afraid to take risks. I ordered the brioche-crusted pork chop, which arrived perfectly cooked and nestled atop a bed of fluffy mashed sweet potatoes. The flavors were expertly balanced, with just the right amount of subtlety to avoid overpowering the delicate pork.But what truly stole the show was the service. My server was attentive, knowledgeable, and downright charming. She guided me through the menu with ease, offering insightful recommendations and thoughtful suggestions. It was clear that she took pride in her work, and her passion for the restaurant shone through in every interaction.Overall, this restaurant exceeded my expectations in every way. From the refined ambiance to the creative cuisine, I was thoroughly impressed. And as I left, feeling pleasantly sated and content, I knew that I would most certainly be back. In fact, I can't wait to introduce my foodie friends to this hidden gem.So, if you're a fellow food aficionado looking for a unique dining experience, look no further. This restaurant is sure to delight even the most discerning palates.

I was a bit surprised by the slow pace of the restaurant, as I had expected it to be busier on a Sunday. However, our server was friendly and attentive, and she made sure that we had everything we needed. The menu had a good selection of options, and I was pleased to see that they had a few vegetarian dishes to choose from. I ordered the veggie burger, which was cooked to perfection and had a great flavor. My companion had the chicken sandwich, which he said was also very good. We shared a side of fries, which were crispy and well-seasoned. Overall, we were both satisfied with our meals and felt that the prices were reasonable. The atmosphere of the restaurant was cozy and welcoming, with a few tables and a small bar area. It was a nice spot to relax and enjoy a meal on a lazy Sunday afternoon. I would definitely recommend this place to others, and I look forward to coming back again soon.

Goulash in the Contrucci household was made of elbow noodles, beef and spaghetti sauce. I guess you can't believe everything your parents tell you right? So going in here, I was thinking, great.. . mom's goulash! What was set in front me looked NOTHING like what I was used to. It was a mish mosh of veggies, noodles, gravy and some random unidentifiable food items. I usually eat whatever is put in front of me, so I wasn't scared to dive it. Sadly, I just didn't like it. I thought it was actually not very appetizing at all. I know, I know, this is like "world famous" goulash, but I was NOT into it! What I was into was the German Potato Salad. I love it, and honestly, I feel like I never get the same version of it anywhere in the Burgh. This was a no frills version, with scallop sliced potatoes and a thick vinegar sauce. Maybe a bit too much, but not enough for me to eat it all! Would I go back? If someone else really wanted to go there, but I wouldn't suggest it nor would I go on my own. Oh well, on to the next one right?

This place is a hidden gem! It's located in a small strip mall, and the entrance is easy to miss. But once you step inside, you're transported to a world of delicious Mediterranean cuisine.The menu features a wide variety of kabobs, as well as other traditional Mediterranean dishes. I ordered the lamb kabob, and it was cooked to perfection. The meat was tender and juicy, and the spices were just right.The service was also excellent. Our server was attentive and friendly, and he made sure that we had everything we needed.Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant. It's a great place to enjoy a delicious meal and experience some of the best Mediterranean cuisine that the city has to offer.

I'm a mattress buying novice, but after extensive research and countless store visits, ich finally stumbled upon the perfect mattress that exceeded all my expectations. From the moment I laid down on it, I could sense the exceptional comfort and support it provided. The top layer of plush memory foam gently cradled my body, relieving pressure points and ensuring a restful sleep throughout the night. The mattress also boasted an innovative cooling technology that regulated temperature and prevneted any night sweats, enables me to wake up feeling refreshed and revitalized. Its superior motion isolation capabilities were a game-changer, as I could sleep undisturbed also when my partner tossed and turned. Nova overall construction of the mattress was sturdy and durable, making it a worthwhile investment for years to come. Additionally, the company's customer service was outstandng, guiding me through the entire purchasing process and addressing any concerns promptly. The delivery was seamless, and the mattress arried in pristine condition. I was also pleased with the ease of set up, as it took no time to unbox and expand to its full size. Cleaning and maintenance were hassle-free, thanks to the mattress's removable and washable covered. The value for money was remarkable, considering the high quality and luxurious feel of the mattress. It truly exceeded my expectations, and I couldn't be happier with my purchase. If you're a novice like me, l highly recommend this mattress for an exceptional sleeping experience.

Everyone hates it.. . and unfortunately I drive it frequently. Word of the wise.. . drive this road in the daytime, when it's not raining. You will thank me later for this advice.. . As mentioned by others, this road is not in the best shape. It seems like every couple of miles there's construction. Not anyone working on site.. . but hey, you still have to slow down. Another issue.. . most of the roadway is 55 mph. This drives me insane.. . because in certain spots it's 55, and in others it's 65. Luckily I haven't had any speeding tickets here.. . but my warning, be aware of your speed. The toll booth operators are ok, for the most part. You will get those with the evil attitudes. Like, I'm sorry I disturbed you.. . but lady you're the only one open. I'll make sure to sign up for EZ Pass so I can bypass you. And lastly.. . the price. So back when I was in college I frequented this road, from Pittsburgh to Philly and back. I believe the amount one way was between $12-15. Now.. . one way? Goodness I don't know the price.. . but let's put this in perspective. I now only drive the Pittsburgh/Breezewood route.. . and it's $12. 60 one way. And this isn't even the halfway point to Philly. In theory you can bypass the turnpike by driving I-80 but this road is impassable if it's snowing. And there aren't as many rest stops. So PA knows you have no choice.. . and will charge you whatever on the turnpike. FYI - prices are scheduled to go up Jan 1 2015. The toll booth operators are clueless as to how much the increase will be. One toll booth operator was snippy with me when I asked her. Oh well.

It has been my experience that even when the food is ok, the service can ruin the meal and experience! That being said my coworker and I stopped into Applebee's for the Pick n' Pair lunch special. The hostess sat us at our table with no greeting and lucky for us she was our waitress as well.. . sarcasm intended and required. She took our drink order walked away several minutes later she returned with our drinks.. . asked if we knew what we wanted to eat and we placed our ordered. I chose the Fiesta Chicken Chopped salad and new chicken tortilla soup. Now, I don't know how long it takes to put soup in the bowl and throw some salad on a plate but with maybe two other tables occupied and it being late in the afternoon it certainly doesn't take half my lunch hour. And for those of us who try to leave the office for some peace of mind and freedom during the workday.. . when you are on your lunch hour every moment counts. When our food finally arrived with the few moments we had left on a lunch break. I scarfed it down I think it tasted ok. From what I remember, the salad was spicy and the jalapeno dressing was yummy! The chicken tortilla soup was just ok. It could have used a few more pieces of chicken and spice to take it up a notch. Overall, the experience was horrible. The service was horrible. The food was ok. I won't be running back to this location any time soon.

The first reason is to warn others about the terrible service I received at this establishment. The second reason is to praise the delicious food that was served to me.I arrived at the restaurant with my family and was immediately seated. Our server took our drink orders and then disappeared for over 15 minutes. When she finally returned, she took our food order and then again disappeared for another 20 minutes. When our food finally arrived, it was cold and not as ordered.Despite the terrible service, the food was actually very good. The steak was cooked perfectly and the salmon was fresh and flavorful. The vegetables were also cooked to perfection.If you are looking for a great meal, I would highly recommend this restaurant. However, be prepared for terrible service.

nn1. The staff works hard to make sure you are getting the best prices on parts and they charge reasonable rates for labor. n2. They stand by their warranty. I had my timing belt changed, and after a couple of months i thought it was idling loud. They took care of the problem with no additional charges. n3. They don't nickel and dime you. At the Subaru dealership and Woodies, they charge me $75 - $90 just to look at the car. At tread quarters I asked for a couple of lights to be replaced on top of getting my breaks replaced, and they took care of it for no additional charge. n4. They stand by their quote, and charge you for the exact time worked, even if it comes in under the quote. At woodies they charged me the full price of the quote, even though they only worked on the car for half the time of the original quote.

this is the possible continuation of the comment: Shadyside is one of the best casual restaurants, and I always respond to the previous commentators in my list when I want a place. The atmosphere is comfortable and seductive. There is a warm and friendly employee who always makes me feel at home. The menu provides rich delicious dishes. I haven't tried something that I have not enjoyed. Their hamburger is juicy and delicious, and their salads are fresh and creative. I am also a loyal supporter of their sandwiches. They are made of high -quality meat and cheese. These parts are generous, and the price is very reasonable for the quality you get. They also provide selected craft beer and cocktails, and the list of wine is impressive. Overall, I strongly recommend that you seek delicious and pleasant meals in a relaxed and comfortable atmosphere.

My friend and I had been dying to get into the place but we really were excited and anxious about nothing.. . The meal started with the lobster mac&chz and stuffed hush puppies as appetizers. The good news were that the apps were presented well and very tasty. The bad news is that they were the best part of the meal. The m&c had good texture and balance but was highly seasoned and both my dining partner and I felt that it was too salty. The hush puppies were spot on. Loaded with shrimp & crawfish in a delicate white sauce with toasted onion slivers. Yummy! The crispy texture of the hush puppies, paired with the creamy sauce was just perfect. As for the entru00e9es, well that's a whole different story. I had the short ribs with the risotto. The ribs were cooked perfectly but the risotto was crunchy ( and I don't mean al dente) which made it difficult to enjoy the meal.. .. I'm not interested in just eating a hunk of meat. My companion had the Red Snapper which was served over jambalaya which was also lackluster. All in all, it was just oh-Kay. For dessert I had the apple pie cheesecake. It clearly had not been made the same day because it had developed that "skin" on it that comes from keeping things refrigerated but uncovered. It was not edible. This was $100 meal that was more like a 2 for $20 deal at Chili's or TGI Friday's. If I ever go back to this place again it will be for the apps only. Save your money.

After re-inflating it continues to lose air and we have to bring it to a garage due to being stranded. They showed us a defect in the tire where the side wall was bulging out the size of a golf ball. The garage mentioned that if we were on the highway we could have been killed as it would have been a total blowout. We then bring it to the Charlotte Volvo for repair and they send us a picture of another damage where someone had previously patched the tire. We then have the same sales manager for the next 2 months do the biggest finger pointing game we have ever seen. Calling and emailing that they are not responsible. Wow, 3 days after getting the car we had to have it towed and he is finger pointing. It shows what type of operation this is with no concern for our safety and the risk they put us in.

Wanted to check out another neighborhood in Pittsburgh. To an ignorant outsider, North Side didn't seem much more sketch than South Side or Oakland. After picking up two bottles of red at Wine and Spirits on Ohio Street, my team and I got a table at the warm, homey Legends of the North Shore, where it's BYOB. For appetizers we ordered the margherita bruschetta (best choice), fried polenta, and greens 'n beans (mainly because we went on a Tuesday when they had a special deal for 99 cents with any entree). The focaccia bread is great with the homemade mixture of olive oil and herbs. I ordered the mussels bianca over linguine--terrific. Also comes with shrimp. The portions are generous but delicious, in part because it's clear that the tomato sauces are all made fresh and in-house. I tried my coworkers gnocchi--good, but I was quite satisfied with my own dish. My coworker who ordered the eggplant parmigiano really enjoyed her dish as well.

The inside of the house is more like a gift shop with a pretty wide variety of gardening gifts and knick-knacks- from watering cans to small planters to all kinds of kitsch one can stick into their garden. If you are searching for a unique gift for the gardening friend, this would be an excellent stop. Outback they have an impressive selection of fountains and larger pots to hold your green-wares. It's fun just to stroll thru and look (and listen) to all the options bubbling thru all makes of vessels and sculptures. During the planting months, they do carry the obligatory selection of vegetables and herbs. They also sometimes carry some more interesting things to plant. The real reason you should visit here, though, is for the advice and expertise of the owners who know their neighborhood and the surroundings. They love to chat and will answer your gardening queries with lots of options.

With that being said I was hoping that all my stumbling around in the elements would not be in vain. The food at Thai Cuisine is more pitiful than my sense of direction. I ordered Threes Company: shrimp, scallops and calamari in a Thai chili sauce. The sauce is my favorite part of a Thai meal but Thai Cuisine came up short here. What I enjoy must about a Thai chili sauce is the complexity of flavors but this sauce in my dish was your standard thin runny brown sauce. The kind that comes with lets say beef and broccoli. I think the menu description was misleading and had I known it would be brown sauce I would have ordered something else. Some of the onions in my dish were cold which leads me to believe that the food was not cooked to order or at least not all of it. There was plenty of shrimp in the dish and the calamari tasted great, but the dish lacked flavor. The carrots and broccoli was cooked beyond recognition. For my hubby I ordered the Thai steak, it tasted like a frozen salisbury steak dinner and salisbury steak just so happens to be one my least favorite foods. Had I not sampled his dinner this would have been a solid three star review. I see no reason to go back here.

They have a good selection of olives, a decent cheese selection, a variety of ready-made dips and spreads which are pretty tasty, and some harder-to-find specialty items like rose water, pomegranate molasses, different grinds of bulgur wheat, bulk fava beans, etc. You can also get packaged bulk nuts, dried fruits, etc. When I go in here, it's usually because I'm looking for feta cheese or Greek-style yogurt. This place is pretty good. A couple times I've had some problems getting yogurt here, since they have a tendency to keep the yogurt on the shelf until it's almost at its sell-by date, but on the other hand, they have the cheapest price on Fage yogurt that I've seen in town thus far. My mom loves a lot of their dips and spreads, so I get snacks from here a lot when she's in town. The one caution I have (besides the yogurt) is that they sell an inferior brand of canned tomatoes here, which gives off a very strong flavor of metal and ruins your meal.

I visit Ellsworth ave plenty and I have been to Harris grill on numerous occasions. After working all day, and driving 2 hours to get home I was a little grumpy and wanting a good drink. My two friends and I decided on the sangria. I've had it on numerous occasions and it can really hit the spot. The waiter suggested the caraf but HB warned us saying that they stuff it full of ice. The waiter insured us we would get around a glass and a half. We bypassed HB and ordered the caraf. Upon arrival we knew it was no bueno! The caraf was heaping full of fruit on the top followed by way too much ice. Our serving glasses also were heaped with the stuff even though we had asked for lite ice. I asked the waiter to pour for us bc I knew sangria was going everywhere. We ended up with our glasses 3/4 full and a watered down juice cocktail. We all told the waiter that it was pretty awful but he did nothing to correct the insult. Never ever order the caraf!! To eat I had the pulled pork sandwhich and a side of mac n cheese. The flavor of the pulled pork was good and the pasta was delish. I will say the pork had some fatty bites that I didn't care for. All in all when the start of a dining experience starts the way ours did it can be salvaged with the right customer care. Ours wasn't plain and simple.

I have the best experience of Wendy! From the moment I came in, the atmosphere was very enthusiastic, and the staff tried to me with a real smile. This restaurant is clean and tidy, creating a comfortable dining environment. The ordering process was quickly and effective, and the cashier patiently answered any questions about the menu. Food exceeded my expectations. Cook the burger to perfect, juicy and delicious, and with fresh heads, adding an extra flavor of the taste. French fries are crispy outside and fluffy inside, just like I like them. The weight is very large, so I was completely satisfied at the end of the meals. The most impressive is the attention of the details of the ingredients. Lettuce and tomatoes are very fresh and vibrant, which enhances the overall taste of the burger. The bread is soft, with a slightly grilled bread, and perfectly replenishes the filling. Obviously, Wendy's is proud of the use of high -quality ingredients. The service during the entire visit is very good. The staff is very careful and regularly check to ensure that everything is satisfied. They quickly added my drink and provided other condiments without asking me. Their friendly and professional spirit created a pleasant dining experience. In addition, the cleanliness of the restaurant is commendable. The table was immediately cleaned and cleaned immediately after each customer, and the floor was not stained, which made me feel comfortable and hygienic in the entire meals. Following the details of maintaining a clean environment is worthy of attention and appreciation. The overall value of the price is very good. Wendy's provides various menu options at a affordable price without damage to the quality. Considering first -class services, delicious food and pleasant atmosphere, I think I got a wonderful dining experience for spending money. In short, my visit to Wendy is indeed very good.

We ordered a few bottles of red and white wine, and they were all delicious. The atmosphere was lively and fun, with a DJ playing great music. Our waitress was friendly and attentive, and she helped us navigate the menu. We also ordered some appetizers, including the spinach and artichoke dip and the Bruschetta, which were both delicious. The main courses were also impressive, especially the pasta dishes. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the wine. The portions were generous, and the flavors were rich and bold. The half-priced wine is definitely a draw, but the food and service are also excellent. All in all, we had a great time and would definitely come back. Highly recommended!

The staff They're also very knowledgeable and experienced, and they've always been able to fix my car quickly and efficiently. Here are some more details about the business: * They're located at 123 Main Street in Anytown, USA. * Their phone number is 0123456789. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a good auto repair shop. * Their hours are Monday through Friday from 8am to 6pm, and Saturday from 8am to 2pm.

The bathroom setup is stupid (like many hotels) with no counter for the sink and those old-fashioned separate hot and cold water knobs that make calibrating the temperature needlessly difficult. The shower pressure was adequate, but there is no place in the shower to put your shampoo, soap, washcloth, etc. That's just dumb. Toilet paper sconce is behind you and a pain to reach. An overall bad layout, design, and decor in the bathroom. The room is very dark with just some dim lamps scattered around the room. There is a desk, but its shape makes it painful to sit at (there was a wooden part jabbing into my legs) and you have to unplug something if you want to plug in a computer, a short sighted setup on their part. Because I was here for work I was too busy to eat their breakfast or spend any time at the bar, but I did need to get some stuff done in the room and the above features made that difficult and unpleasant. Also, you have to park in a public lot behind the hotel and get your ticket validated by the staff to not pay there, but you still pay Dunhill $12 per day for the parking. Not convenient, and one time I forgot to get the thing validated and therefore ended up paying more than just paying the garage itself. Bad system there too. But overall the bed was comfortable and the room was quiet and getting around is easy. As a business traveler I'd still prefer a Fairfield Inn or Holiday Inn Express, but this place is almost as good.

Look no further than Pizza People Pub! Not only do they have the best pizza in town, but they also have a cozy and intimate atmosphere that's perfect for a date. The dim lighting and classic rock music create a relaxed and romantic vibe that's sure to impress your significant other. And the best part? They offer a build-your-own pizza option, so you can customize your pizza to your liking. The crust is cooked to perfection, and the toppings are fresh and flavorful. Plus, they have a great selection of craft beers to choose from. The service is also top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who will make sure your date goes smoothly. Overall, Pizza People Pub is a great spot for a unique and delicious date night.

Despite my 3-star rating, I think I will be coming back here again to give it a second try. The initial experience was not entirely satisfying, but I believe there might be potential for improvement. The service was prompt and friendly, with the waitstaff attentive to our needs throughout the meal. However, the food was a hit-or-miss affair. Some dishes had impressive flavor profiles, while others fell short of expectations.We started with the calamari appetizer, which had a crispy texture and was accompanied by a tangy dipping sauce. It was a decent way to kick off the meal, but it didn't blow me away. For the main course, I opted for the grilled salmon with roasted vegetables. The presentation was visually appealing, but the salmon was slightly overcooked and lacked the moistness I prefer. The roasted vegetables, however, were seasoned well and had a delightful char.My dining companion chose the ribeye steak, cooked to a perfect medium-rare as requested. The steak was tender and flavorful, showcasing the chef's skill in preparing meat dishes. It was accompanied by a generous portion of mashed potatoes that were creamy and well-seasoned. The only letdown was the side of sautéed spinach, which was overly wilted and lacked freshness.For dessert, we shared a slice of chocolate cake, which was decadent and rich, satisfying our sweet cravings. The cake was moist, and the ganache frosting added a delightful touch. The dessert was the highlight of our meal, redeeming some of the earlier disappointments. In terms of ambience, the restaurant had a cozy and rustic charm. The dim lighting and warm color scheme created an inviting atmosphere. However, the noise level was quite high, making it difficult to have a conversation without raising our voices. Some soundproofing measures could greatly enhance the overall dining experience.

Oooeh I loves me some Mert's! This ocal diner has been a neighborhood staple for as long as I can remember. Every time I take a seat at the counter, I'm greeted by friendly faces both od and new. The food here is simple but so tasty - Iu'm a sucker for their fluffy pancakes and crispy bacon. And you really canMt beat the price of their early bird special. Whethr you're starting your day or needing a lunch break, Mert's always hits the spot. It's also one of the few plces left where you can find a true old-fashioned malt or shake. Lately they've started offering vegna and veggie options too, which is great for expanding their customer base. C'm glad to see new generations discovering this little gem. Even after all these yegars, Mert's still feels like part of the family. This place will alwasy have a special spot in my heart.

I'll preface my story with its probably the best Pho/vietnamese in Pittsburgh.. . yada yada.. . delicious.. . yada yada.. . cheap.. . yada yada.. . great pho BUT a lot of ppl have said its no-frills, angry servers who throw food at you. And this has been the case a few times before my story tonight. I've never minded. TONIGHT though.. . i went to get some take out pho on a snowy evening. I had to wait for a few minutes.. . and the owner was nice enough to engage me in conversation while I waited. I get my Pho.. . paid.. and I get in my car.. . and drove away.. . A block later, due to the snowy weather and my inability to slow brake.. . I squealed to a stop when some guy ran out into the street. I did stop in time, spared his life.. . BUT MY PHO WAS EVERYWHERE! Most of it was in the bag, but a good portion was on the floor.. . on the seat.. . MORE IMPORTANTLY, NOT IN MY BELLY. So I drove into a parking lot.. . had to dispose of the mess.. . and cried. Now not only did I NOT have pho.. . my car now smelled enticingly of beefy broth. So in a moment of frenzy, I thought.. . What the heck.. . im only a block away, IM GETTING MY PHO. So I went back.. . and got my pho! AND.. . the guy didn't even charge me. He was SO nice and he was like "You said you dropped it, I believe you! here! "nnomfg, I EFFING LOVE THIS PLACE.

But now I feel their pain. It really doesn't hit you, until it.. . hits you. You pay a premium at WF, you expect a premium, right? Well parking is part of the shopping experience. It's why they have parking lots in the first place. But never mind the atrocious parking lot and not being able to easily maneuver in it. I'm talking about being TOWED. Towed, not for leaving the parking lot, but for legitimately shopping at WF. Yes, this could happen to you too. Upon contacting the towing company, they demanded $135 (cash only) to return my vehicle. Upon contacting WF (since I was a legitimate shopper there and didn't leave the lot) they just shrugged their shoulders and just told me the name of the company that managed the lot. And that's it?! $135 is no chump change, but it seems like WF wants me to carry an extra $135 every time I frequent them (thankfully, never, since I don't live in Pittsburgh). This whole parking/towing situation is extremely shady, but the only company I'm going to point my finger at is Whole Foods for doing business with such a shady complex and passing the burden on to its customers. Tip: Bring an extra $135 to pay for parking, or just go to Trader Joe's/Giant Eagle for a better parking/shopping experience.

Pepperidge Farm remembers.. . I have dined with the King many a time across this fine land. I have watched their slow decline with sadness over the last thirty years. At one point, they actually challenged the Clown for burger superiority, but now, they're a weak shadow on the market, barely a player.. . nn.. . and the BK at this location is a perfect example of why. EVERYTHING at this BK takes ten minutes. Doesn't matter what you order, be prepared to wait. It's always dirty. When I was a kid and worked at the Clown, we were always cleaning. There was usually one or two people on any shift whose sole job was to keep the lobby clean. This place is a hole. Why does the food taste weird? If I want BK, I actually make the drive to Deforest, rather than eat at this location, which is actually a stone's throw from my house. The food here tastes bad, bleachy, and wrong. What are they doing to the food? Fix thyself, King, and maybe I'll return. Until then, I will take my cheap, poorly constructed eats elsewhere.

It's got a busy, friendly vibe and overall satisfying food. The good: to contradict a previous reviewer, I found the beer selection to be quite respectable. You've got mainstream goat piss, mainstream Irish, beer snob local, national and international. I was very pleased by the Gaelic ale from Asheville. Very pleased. Also, the nachos were truly a work of art. I can't stand flour tortillas but flour tortilla chips are great for this mouthwatering mountain of peppers, beans, tomatoes, olives, cream and little chicken bits. The ok: well, I found my pasta - the Honey Chicken - to be just ok. The chicken itself was nice and juicy. I don't know what I expected from the pasta. I think it was overall a bit sweet, and perhaps a nice pungent feta topping would have broken that up a bit better. What it came with was a bland kind of Parmesan, I think. I might return and try something else on the menu - like their massive 1/2 pound burgers - and we'll see if it'll make me a fangirl.

love the live music every night, great drinks, outdoor patio. I like the old house. It feels like going over an old family members house but better. nThe food was good overall. Appetizers Bbq shrimp sauce is great with bread and the Crawfish ceviche was flavorful and spicy! So when my gumbo came it tasted blah to me. Not very flavorful. So my dad ate it and liked it. My shrimp and grits were ok but the shrimp was bland and the skin on my sausage was hard. My sister had the dish several times before and said it didn't taste the same. Liked the grits though. tasted the blackened catfish.. . moist and delicious. Tasty desserts, but nothing to write home about. I do think it's a bit overpriced. The restroom paper towel machine was broken. And no other dryer or towels available. I know is out of their control but maybe need a backup. It's quite annoying. Great place for appetizers, live jazz and drinks.

The chicken is consistently juicy and flavorful, the pita is soft and fluffy, and the sauces are amazing. The staff is always friendly and welcoming, and the prices are very logical. I love that they have a variety of options, including vegetarians and gluten-free dishes. They also have a great rewards program that makes it easy to save money on your favorite meals. Shwomars is definitely one of my favorite restaurants in town. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and affordable meal. The atmosphere is casual and relaxed, making it a awesome place to eat with friends or family. Te location is convenient, and there is plenty of parking. Overall, Showmars is a great option for a quick and tasty meal.

I've experienced better. " perfectly sums up my feelings. I got something marked "spicy" on the menu and barely felt any heat, nor tasted any seasoning. It wasn't a terrible experience, but judging from many of the other reviews here, I expected better. nn Update So I gave the place a 2nd try (orange chicken) a few months ago which didn't turn out to be that bad, not great, but not bad. I went there again today, ordered the szechuan chicken and was very dissapointed. Yet again, supposed to be spicy, yet just tasted like MSG gravy, no flavor, no spice, just umami and cornstarch. I'm guessing that there are probably dishes that aren't bad, but so far, all I've gotten was bland. That coupled with the abrupt, bordering on rude woman who works the front desk and I'm not sure if I want to find out what those decent dishes are.

The weather was pretty nice so it was a good day for a drive in. I always try to keep an open mind when eating at a place for the first time which can be tough after reading reviews about the place. I ordered BBQ plate which comes with 2 sides. I got fries and slaw. My visit was on a Saturday between noon and 1 pm. The place seemed pretty busy with about 50% of the stalls occupied. It took a little while to get my food, but not so long as to start thinking, "where is my food. " The server dropped my tray off and quickly moved on the the next car without getting my money. Odd, but probably the most efficient. The pork was minced with sauce on it. The slaw was also minced rather than being shredded. There was also a sandwich bun along with the fries. I was able to get some pork without sauce to try first. The pork was moist and tender, but very bland. I then tried some of the pork with the sauce and the sauce was bland too. There was no smoke flavor at all. The fries were good, fluffy on the inside, but not quite crisp enough. The slaw was crunchy and fresh, but it too was bland. I don't really care about the sauce. Tastes vary and some like it spicier than others. But the pork although being tender and moist was disappointing. Overall it wasn't a bad meal, but it wasn't good either. Again there are better places to go for much better BBQ.

The food at Nakato is good, but the menu is limited and the service is just okay. The atmosphere is nice, but the restaurant is small and crowded. The prices are high for the quality of food. The location is good, but the parking is limited. Overall, we had a good experience, but we probably wouldn't go back again.

I like to hang out at Charlotte with Hubby on weekends. This is definitely a great hotel. The room is spacious and comfortable, with exquisite facilities, such as mini refrigerators and coffee machines. The bed was very soft, and we fell asleep like a rock two nights. During breakfast, they provided a good hot spontaneous meal with eggs, pastries, yogurt and fruit. This position is also great because it is only a short drive from all urban attractions and entertainment activities. The staff is very friendly and helpful, and they provide some good suggestions for dining and activities in the area. After a long day of hiking and shopping, we like to have an indoor swimming pool and hot water bathtub to relax. What I want to say is that WiFi is running well, except for our room a little spoken. We plan to stay here next time we visit Charlotte because it provides a very important value for this money. I strongly recommend this hotel for other hotels traveling to Charlotte.

We didn't have a reservation but the server seated us anyways (we had to be done by 7). It is BYOB but they deal you a $4 corkage fee per person drinking. The bread sticks were fresh and warm and were the perfect accompaniment to the delicious soup du jour, potato soup. The side salad that comes with the meal would make the hall of fame for any side salad league. It came with olives, Gorgonzola, julienned carrots and other veggies. I had the pork tenderloin with veggies and mashed potatoes. The tenderloin was perfectly cooked and the mashed potatoes were like having two aces in the hole. It would be tough to find a better waitstaff. Plates disappeared, water was filled, and I never knew they were there. If your looking for a place to try before going to the casino or bucco game this is a sure bet, just call ahead for reservations. They do have outdoor seating but the views wont show up on any postcard. PS The 7: 00 reservation called to say they were going to be late so we were allowed to relax at the table till 7: 30.

Unfortunately, my experience at BarB's Country Junction fell far short of my expectations. As soon as I stepped inside, I was met with a dated and poorly maintained interior. The decor seemed sutck in the 1970s, with faded wallpaper peeling off the walls and worn-out furniture that looked like it had saw better days. The service was equally disappointing. The staff appeared disinterested and lacked the warmth and friendliness that I had hoped for. It took forever to get someone's attention just to place my order, and when my food finally arrived, it was lukewarm and uninspiring. I decided to lend the menu a chance, hoping that the food would redeem the experience. However, the dishes I ordered lacked any sort of creativity or attention to detail. The flavors were bland, the ingredients tasted stale, and the presentation was haphazard at best. It felt like the kitchen was merely going through the motions witho ut any passion for their craft. To ma ke matters worse, the portion sizes were incredibly small for the price charged. I left the restaurant feeling սnsatisfied and still hungry, which left a bitter taste in my mouth both figuratively and literally. Apart, the cleanliness of the establishment was questionable. I noticed crumbs and spills on the tables and floors, giving the imprssion that the staff did not prioritize cleanliness or proper hygiene practices. It was certainly not the kind of environment where oe could enjoy a pleasant dining experience. Evn though I had hoped to find a gem in Barb's Country Junstion, it was clear that the restaurant was past its prime and desperately in need of an overhaul. The lackluster ambiance, mediocre service, and subpar food made it nearly impossible for me to f ind anything to like about this place. I left feeling deeply disappointed and regretful of the time and money I had wasted. If Barbs Country Junction wishes to regain its former glory and attract customers, it needs a complete transformation.

The Crowne Plaza Madison is an older property and its far from the "fun" part of Madison, but the friendliness of the staff really made the stay decent for us. Tom at the front desk was especially welcoming and personable. He made check-in a breeze. We did see a few of the issues listed by other reviewers. The hallways had an "smell" which can be attributed to the age of the hotel. Also, the wallpaper in our room was peeling in spots. Our pillows were quite awful, but in the morning I noticed that they offered a selection of other pillows, had we just called the front desk. I'll give them a pass there. Overall the place is alright. The friendly staff made up for some of the other shortfalls. It wouldn't be my first choice in Mad-Town, but really the location is the only issue that will keep me from coming back.

I decided to check the center of Pittsburgh in a recent family visit. When I strolled on the street, I was immediately attracted by the city's vibrant energy. The prosperous atmosphere and the architectural charm of the building create a unique atmosphere. The long history of the city is obvious in every corner, and museums and landmarks show the past. I can't help but explore the famous strip dance area, where fresh bread and countless spices are full of air. This is a paradise for food lovers, and local suppliers provide various cooking foods. One of the highlights I visited was to experience the magnificent scenery from Washington Mountain. The panoramic view of the urban Skyrim and the three rivers is exciting. I also walked leisurely along the river and passed through the iconic Roberto Clemente Bridge, which can enjoy the magnificent scenery of the PNC Park Stadium. The city's dedication to art and culture is obvious in many art museums and theaters scattered in the city. Pittsburgh's friendly residents have added the charm of the city. I found that the locals are very popular and are ready to provide suggestions for the best diet or exploration place at any time. The city's commitment to sustainable development has left a deep impression on me, its extensive bicycle lanes and environmental protection measures. It is refreshing to see a city that values its inheritance and future. During the visit, I had the opportunity to visit the Carnegie Natural History Museum, which made me awe collective fossils and cultural relics in awe. Interactive exhibitions are educational and attractive, and are ideal destinations for adults and children. I also spent one afternoon at the Andy Warhol Museum, immersed in the Poping art world, and had a deeper understanding of the life and work of the artist. Exploring the community of Pittsburgh itself is a kind of joy.

The equipment would often break down and never get fixed. Considering how small the gym is, it's inexcusable that two treadmills would be out of service for at least a month. I also had problems with the individual TVs on machines; sometimes they wouldn't work properly or would be completely broken. The gym was generally quiet enough in the mornings, but it would be pretty packed after work. It was hard to find a machine. The staff also didn't really enforce the 30 min time-limit policy, which caused people to have to wait for equipment longer than necessary. I was told on the phone I needed to let them know before the 25th of a given month to cancel my membership moving forward (and not be charged for the next month). I wasn't told that I had to give 30 days notice (aka pay for an extra month). Though they're technically right (it IS in the contract), I feel that their staff mislead me. If you live in Shadyside (or nearby).. . GO TO URBAN ACTIVE INSTEAD. It's cheaper and the facilities are unbelievably better than XShadyside.. . although I apparently have a membership at XShadyside for another month now, I am 100% done with that place.

When I think of Cafe Zinho, adorable, charming, cozy, and tucked away come to mind. This hidden gem is nestled in a quiet neighborhood, exuding an irresistible ambiance that instantly captivates you. Stepping inside, you're embraced by a warm and inviting atmosphere, as if wrapped in a soft blanket that makes you feel right at home. The interior is tastefully decorated with vintage trinkets, rustic wooden furniture, and delicate fairy lights, creating a whimsical setting that transports you to another era.The menu at Cafe Zinho is as delightful as its surroundings. Their selection of handcrafted coffees, teas, and artisanal pastries is simply impeccable. Each sip of their expertly brewed coffee is a heavenly experience, showcasing the barista's skill and dedication. The pastries, baked fresh daily, are true works of art-flaky croissants, decadent cakes, and delicate macarons that melt in your mouth. The attention to detail and the use of high-quality ingredients are evident in every bite, leaving you craving for more.The staff at Cafe Zinho are exceptionally friendly and attentive. From the moment you enter, they welcome you with genuine smiles, making you feel like a valued guest. Their knowledge of the menu is impressive, and they are always ready to offer recommendations or answer any questions you may have. Their passion for their craft shines through their service, adding an extra layer of charm to the overall dining experience.One of the highlights of Cafe Zinho is its outdoor seating area. Tucked away in a cozy garden with blooming flowers and whimsical decorations, it provides the perfect setting to enjoy your coffee or indulge in a leisurely brunch. The gentle breeze and the soothing sound of chirping birds create a serene environment that truly enhances the overall charm of the cafe.Although Cafe Zinho may not be located in a bustling area, it is definitely worth the search.

The portions were also huge, which was great for the price. We ordered the pierogies, the haluski, the hot sausage platter, and the stuffed cabbage. The pierogies were my favorite - they were perfectly cooked and the filling was delicious. The haluski was also very good, with a nice balance of cabbage and noodles. The hot sausage platter was a bit too spicy for my taste, but my dad loved it. The stuffed cabbage was good, but not as flavorful as the other dishes. Overall, we had a great experience at the restaurant and would definitely recommend it to others.The service was also excellent. Our waitress was very friendly and attentive, and she made sure that we had everything we needed. She even brought us a complimentary dessert at the end of our meal.We will definitely be back to the restaurant in the future. It's a great place to get a delicious and affordable meal. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a new place to eat.The restaurant is located in a bit of a sketchy area, but it's worth the trip. The food is amazing and the service is excellent. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great meal.The restaurant is also very kid-friendly. There is a large play area in the back, and the staff is very accommodating to families.Overall, we had a great experience at the restaurant and would definitely recommend it to others. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the prices were very reasonable. We will definitely be back!

I like the ambiance and the decor, although this year our corner table had chairs that sunk WAY down - we wanted to ask for telephone books. I usually choose one of the special salads and have the gnocchi with duck ragu; it is superb! So much flavor and the gnocchi are perfect. This year, though, there was a special fall prix fixe menu with Winter Squash. The ravioli with balsamic drizzle were delicious. I choose quail with apples and squash for my main course and was very satisfied. Terrific glaze! The dessert, however, was over the top! Creme fraiche and pumpkin ice creams, caramel sauce, AND pumpkin fritters. We enjoyed a couple of the $28 bottles. No, they aren't stellar, but for the price they are all good food wines. Everyone in our party enjoyed the meals and we will definitely return.

I was expecting more, but left a bit disappointed. First of all, the directions from Google maps is a bit off.. . it takes you through an apartment complex to a dead end. It's located in a shopping center (with Food Lion). The atmosphere is small with humble interior design. There are approximately 4 booths with high backs and hard bottoms with worn out cushions. The greeting was all smiles. The service wasn't fast, but not too slow either. Our drinks were always full and the server was very friendly. The sushi list was limited, but priced well. The spicy tuna roll was very good. Do not order the teriyaki chicken unless you like two marinated chicken breasts with sauce on top served with a cup of rice and a side of lettuce with ginger dressing for $12. Very disappointing. The restaurant was fairly busy, so I'm sure they have better dishes. I'll have to go back and try some of the noodle items.

After a few minutes of waiting, a hostess seated us at a large table. We quickly looked over the menu, hoping to find appetizers and entrees to share family-style. However, our server was very slow to come take our drink orders. When they finally arrived, they seemed distracted and in a hurry. It took some time for our drinks to be brought out as well. By the time we placed our food order, the game was about to start. We were hopeful the food would come quickly so we had time to eat and make it to the stadium. But as the minutes ticked by with no sign of our appetizers or meals, our pre-game plans were in jeopardy. I began to worry we wouldn't have enough time left to properly enjoy our food before rushing off...

I love every Zimbrick in the city for that matter. I have never had a bad experience here. There have been a few things where I was expecting a HUGE bill for things like the stabilizer for my rear suspension that had been slightly bent. I have a different feeling for Salon CercoNE. On the one hand, the atmosphere of the salon is very enthusiastic, and the stylist is always friendly and concentrated. However, my experience in service quality has been hit or missed. In my first interview, I was impressed by the thorough consultation provided by the stylist and the way she heard my concerns. She gave me a great hairstyle, looking like a photo I showed her. I make myself happy and satisfied. However, my second visit is not so good. The stylist seemed to be anxious, and did not take time to really understand what I wanted. The haircut is okay, but it doesn't look better than the first time. I decided to give the salon again and visit for the third time. Unfortunately, this time is the worst. The stylist completely wrong my hair color, and eventually looked like a completely different shadow I asked. Although I have experienced mixed experience, I am grateful to the salon for providing various services, including hairstyles, coloring, waxing and makeup. They can also buy a variety of hair care products. Overall, I will carefully recommend the Cercone. Although the atmosphere is pleasant and the staff is very friendly, the service quality may be inconsistent. Before leaving the salon, it is important to communicate with your stylist clearly and carefully check the work.

I know a fair amount about hair, and could have done it myself, but I love the ritual of going to a salon and having 'a girl. ' Dean's was basically the only place I could get an appointment same-day that looked halfway decent. I had a Level III stylist who was nice enough, but certainly not a conversationalist. I don't think English was her first language. That's no big deal, but a little good cheer would have made it less boring. Also, I love (LOVE) my former stylist in Michigan so I have high expectations for fun at the salon. I had no fun at this salon. Dean's is kind of a mid-range pricing scheme. Not too bad. I paid $60 for a partial. The concept of the salon is very bland--nothing remotely original about the place. Judging from the name, I thought it'd be kind of funky (I was thinking Dean of Shadyside as in academic dean and thought it might have a bookish vibe). They had one interesting product line I'd never seen before, but I can't recall the name. I think I'll find a place that's a little more.. . me.

It is a low(200) capacity venue catering to the off-center art crowd, and if you identify with that then you have probably already been called here by one of the many shows that it hosts. Shows here can range from 'The-Biggest-Name-You've-Never-Heard-Of" to simply "The-Name-You've-Never-Heard-Of". The art is usually local, and can obviously be hit or miss. The sound and conditions could be better, depending on what show you're seeing. In the summer the place can get unbearably hot, with people running for the exits between sets. Parking on the street is plentiful and free, and while there usually isn't too much within walking distance on a sparsely crowded night, Liberty Avenue is only a few blocks away to grab a bite to eat beforehand. The trip downstairs to the bathroom is somewhat disturbing. The toilet, appropriately, also lies at the end of a long hallway, behind a door which may or may not be able to close completely. Cleanliness of this one was an afterthought. However, while you hesitantly make your way towards the bathroom, be sure to check out the posters lining the wall of the stairs. Some of the past line-ups may astound you(And the prices you could have seen them for). Make no mistake, there is a fairly solid quality to the music here(especially from touring bands) and over the years many of them go on to be influential in one way or another. So if it's your thing, but sure to stop out and catch a show - the music will probably be solid, and the tickets are cheap! They're the only place on the street that requests donations for entry during Unblurred, but honestly I can't imagine the place is a gold mine regularly and the music they host is important to Pittsburgh(in my opinion), so I never mind tossing in a few bucks. Also, IMO, promotion isn't the best here, so check the website to find out the latest shows, or stop in during Unblurred.

I must say, the experience left a lot to be desired. As soon as I entered, the atmosphere felt incredibly cramped and chaotic, with servers rushing around and tables uncomfortably close together. It was difficult to find a spot to sit, and even when I did, the noise level was nearly unbearable. Moving on to the menu, I was disappointed by the limited selection of appetizers available. The options seemed uninspired and lacked any unique or creative twists. When the food finally arrived, it was underwhelming at best. The presentation was sloppy, and the flavors were mediocre, failing to leave a lasting impression. To make matters worse, the service was extremely slow and inattentive, with our server seemingly overwhelmed by the number of customers. Overall, my intended enjoyable pre-movie snack turned out to be a lackluster experience that I won't be repeating in the future.

Hmmm... Well, where do I start with this game? It's been a wild ride, that's for sure. I mean, it's not every day you come across a game that's been in development for over a decade, only to be released and then promptly forgotten about. I'm not even sure how to begin to explain the sheer amount of disappointment that comes with playing this game.First of all, the graphics are just terrible. I mean, I've seen better-looking games on the PlayStation 2. The character models are awkward and stiff, the environments are bland and uninteresting, and the special effects are laughable. It's like they took every bad video game cliche from the past 20 years and crammed them all into one game.And don't even get me started on the gameplay. It's like they took every tired, overused mechanic from every shooter and action game and mashed them together into a mess of a game. The controls are clunky and unresponsive, the weapon selection is limited and uninspired, and the enemy AI is laughably bad. I mean, seriously, who thought it would be a good idea to have enemies that just stand there and wait for you to shoot them?And then there's the story. Oh boy, the story. It's like they took every bad action movie cliche and crammed them into a narrative that's just barely coherent. I mean, seriously, who thought it would be a good idea to have a main character who's just a generic, silent protagonist with no personality or backstory? And don't even get me started on the supporting characters. They're all just cardboard cutouts with no depth or development.But you know what really takes the cake? The terrible, awful, no-good voice acting. I mean, seriously, who thought it would be a good idea to have voice actors who sound like they're reading from a script they've never seen before? It's like they took every bad voice actor from every cheap anime dub and put them all in one game.Overall, this game is just a mess.
