The satff is also very friendly and make the dining experience delightful. I'm lgad I got introduced to Cajun Queen early on as it helped me experience a reional cuisine I never knew before moving to the south.

I was told they wouldn't be able to get to it until early September. What?, well, ok I'll wait because they have nice nursery stock. I called mid September when they still hadn't planted the trees and I was given a date of Sept. 25. Not to my surprise, no one showed. I called and they said everything was delayed due to the rain. It hadn't rained for weeks, but they would be there next Tuesday. Tuesday has come and gone and no trees. I called and cancelled my tree order and asked for my 50%, $500 deposit back. It is now too late for trees to be planted and established by winter. I am waiting to hear back from them. I will give an update later on as to whether I get my deposit back! I have had trouble in the past with them not showing up for a job.. no call. . nothing. I should have learned my lesson then!

The outside may not look like much, but don't let that fool you. The moment you step inside, you'll be greeted by a cozy and intimate atmosphere that immediately makes you feel at home. I'm so glad I stumbled upon it while looking for a new restaurant to try. The food is excellent, with each dish showcasing the chef's creativity and attention to detail. The service is excellent, with friendly and attentive staff who are knowledgeable about the menu and happy to make recommendations. The decor is simple and elegant, with clean lines and natural materials. The portions are generous, so you won't leave hungry. From the freshest fish to the tenderest meats, every bite is a delight. And the prices? Very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the ingredients and the care that goes into each dish. I've already been back several times and can't wait to go back and try more of their delicious creations. Highly recommended!

When he lived in Uptown, he used to frequent the restaurant often, but it was my first time. You could say I got my cherry popped. Alexander Michael's is tucked away from the Uptown skyscrapers in the residential section. You probably wouldn't see it unless you knew it was there. It looks like it could be just another house on the quiet street. There are no big signs for it and not a lot of discernable noise from the outside. Once we got inside, though, we saw that it was quite packed. We were lucky to get seated right away in the crowded room that resembled something of an English or Irish pub. The lighting was low and the casually dressed crowd was "older" than a lot of Uptown bars, so we felt like we fit in with the 30- and 40-somethings. We started with a Woodchuck Cider (not everyone carries ciders! ) and it was sweet, bubbly, and refreshing. We enjoyed that our server wasn't overly attentive, but she was there whenever we needed to order and checked up on us only when necessary. I tried the blackened catfish and my partner had the honey chicken. Both were delicious. Mine (accompanied by spicy black beans) had just the right amount of cajun flavor. And the portion sizes were just right -- not enough to overfill you, but not enough to leave you hungry when you left. It was definitely an enjoyable experience, and I look forward to returning to this new (to me). The only disappoint is that we weren't able to see the famous pole that they talked about on the back of the menu. It's located in the women's restroom and apparently it's caused quite a few bruises. Funny!

Just got back from Taipei and I have to say, it was an incredible experience! The food, the culture, the people - everything was just amazing. I stayed at the Hotel P, which was super modern and comfortable. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the location was perfect for exploring the city. I tried so many different dishes, from street food to high-end restaurants, and everything was delicious. I especially loved the beef noodle soup and the stinky tofu. The night markets were a lot of fun to explore, and the Taipei 101 building was breathtaking. I also visited the National Palace Museum, which had an amazing collection of Chinese art and artifacts. The only downside was the language barrier, as not many people spoke English. But overall, Taipei was an amazing destination, and I can't wait to go back.

I hate paying full price for movies. Luckily, there are often discounts to be found if you wait a few weeks for films to come out on discount ticket sites or premium streaming services. While it's nice to see something as soon as it's released, I've found that I can still really enjoy movies even a month or two after they first hit theaters. In fact, I sometimes feel less pressure and am able to focus more on simply enjoying the film. Plus it's much more affordable to catch up on multiple movies all at once through discounted options rather than paying a small fortune seeing everything individually at full price. Of course this delayed viewing does make it slightly harder to participate in discussions and avoid spoilers online. However most of my friends are also bargain hunters who wait for deals too, so we can still chat about what we've watched. In the end, I'd rather save my money to use on other entertainment or necessities, since chances are good I'll still be thoroughly entertained even if I'm a bit behind the initial hype. With just a little patience, discounted ticket sites and services allow me to indulge my movie passions without breaking the bank.

Went here with a gift card from the restaurant week photo competition, and let me tell you, it was such a fantastic experience from start to finish! The moment we stepped in, the atmosphere gave off those cozy vibes that instantly put us at ease. We started with their signature appetizer, the loaded nachos, and they were seriously drool-worthy. The accompanying mashed potatoes were creamy and buttery, and the roasted vegetables added a delightful freshness to the dish.My dining partner went for the seafood pasta, and I must say, I had a serious case of food envy. They went above and beyond to accommodate our requests and made us feel like valued guests.In terms of value for money, this place definitely delivered. Girls night had to happen. It had been far too long since we all got together, and we were craving good food and great company. After some discussion and a quick online search, we decided to check out Olive or Twist, a popular spot in downtown Pittsburgh known for its vibrant atmosphere and delicious cocktails.As soon as we walked in, we were greeted by the lively chatter and upbeat music that filled the air. The place was buzzing with energy, and we knew we were in for a fun night. We found a cozy booth in a corner and settled in, ready to indulge in some culinary delights.The menu offered a diverse range of options, from classic comfort foods to unique dishes with a modern twist. Since we were all in the mood for something hearty, we opted for a variety of appetizers to share. The loaded potato skins caught our eye, and we couldn't resist ordering a plate. We were served crispy potato skins generously topped with melted cheese, bacon bits, and a dollop of sour cream. They were absolutely indulgent and disappeared within minutes.For the main course, I couldn't resist trying their signature burger. It came highly recommended by friends, but unfortunately, it fell short of my expectations. The patty was a bit overcooked, resulting in a dry and lackluster experience. The accompanying fries, however, were a redeeming factor. They were perfectly seasoned and had just the right amount of crispiness.But it wasn't just about the food at Olive or Twist; the drinks were equally impressive. Their extensive cocktail menu showcased a variety of libations that catered to all tastes. I decided to go for their specialty craft beer, as I've always been a fan of supporting local breweries. The selection did not disappoint, and I found myself savoring the hoppy goodness with every sip.As the night went on, the atmosphere at Olive or Twist continued to thrive.

With the colder weather picking up in the Pittsburgh area - it's easy to get dry wind-chapped skin and to just want to stay indoors. But, let's be real, hermitting ourselves away isn't the solution to our winter blues. We need to get out and enjoy the holiday season, even if it means bundling up like the Michelin Man.Thankfully, there are ways to battle that dry skin and stay cozy while still enjoying the winter weather. As someone who's been there, done that, and got the chapped lips to prove it - I'm here to share my go-to winter skincare essentials.First up, let's talk about the holy grail of winter skincare: moisturizer. You can't go wrong with a thick, creamy moisturizer that'll lock in hydration and keep your skin supple. I swear by my jar of Aquaphor - it's like a drink of water for your parched skin.Next, we need to talk about exfoliation. I know, I know - it sounds scary, but trust me, it's essential. Exfoliating helps remove dead skin cells and unclog pores, leaving your skin looking brighter and smoother. Just be sure to exfoliate gently, you don't want to scrub away your precious skin.Now, onto the fun stuff - face masks! There are so many amazing face masks out there, but my personal favorite is a good ol' fashioned clay mask. It'll draw out impurities and leave your skin feeling silky smooth. Just don't forget to follow up with a toner, you don't want any lingering dirt or bacteria.But wait, there's more! Eye creams, lip balms, and hand creams - oh my! These are the unsung heroes of winter skincare. Don't neglect your poor, dry eyes or chapped lips - give them some love with a rich eye cream or lip balm. And let's not forget about our poor hands, they're the ones doing all the hard work, after all. A good hand cream will keep them soft and supple, even in the harshest of winters.

This film provides an insider's view of the revolutionary decision to allow free agency in the NBA. It interviews many of the key figures involved, including David Stern, Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, and Michael Jordan, to get their perspectives on this radical change. The film explores the volatile situation at the time and the tense negotiations between the players' union and the league. The players felt exploited by the old system and dared to challenge the status quo, risking their careers in pursuit of freedom. The owners resisted the change, fearing that it would hurt their competitive advantage, but a court ruling forced the league to change its ways. Free agency leveled the playing field and increased the intrigue and competition between the teams, as they had to compete to attract and retain the best players. The film also examines the symbiotic relationship between players and owners as the stars began to change teams more frequently. It also shows how free agency affected the fans, who now had more reasons to follow certain superstars from city to city. In the end, the film makes a compelling case for how a change in the players' rights transformed the NBA into the progressive and lucrative league it is today. The film is interspersed with revealing archival footage from the time, and the personal anecdotes and recollections of its notable interviews bring the turbulent change to life.

The meals are a little bit more expensive than you normally want to eat as a student (I probably spend $20-25 with appetizer and dessert), but the food makes this hole-in-the-wall truly worth a trip. Christo is the owner of the restaurant and was at one time employed upon the Onassis yacht. Years ago when I first came to his restaurant, he was the head waiter on a staff of one. More recently when I have gone, there have been other hired waiters. The service isn't great, but it's not terrible either. The food offerings include standard middle eastern fare: hummus, baba ghanouj, phyllo-dough wrapped pockets, and kabobs. The desserts also include standard middle eastern desserts like baklava and strong coffees, but the signature dessert is the Onassis dessert, a syrup-soaked cake topped with custard and whipped cream, dusted with cinnamon. The last time I was there, he had added a chocolate Onassis dessert, which was also excellent. My normal meal there consists of baba ghanouj (which is about the best I've ever had.. .. it's a real hit-or-miss dish, and Christo's knocks it out of the park), a combination (lamb & chicken) kabob, and the Onassis dessert. It's out of the way, but well worth a trip!

We always get the sleeper car. When Amtrak is on time, or if it's less than say an hour late, it can be wonderful. The problem is that Amtrak is at the mercy of the freight railroads that own the tracks. Last year, according to my husband the train enthusiast, the train was constantly arriving into Chicago 4 to 5 hours late because of extreme frieght train congestion. We avoided it then, but since then the company that owns the tracks has gotten its act together and its been much better. It's also nice that your food travels with you and you can get up and stretch your legs when you want to. Amtrak used to run two trains a day to Chicago and two across Pennsylvania. Unfortunately, budget cuts a few years ago caused one of these to be cancelled, so it is much less convenient. Also, the train to Washington, DC leaves Pittsburgh in the wee hours of the morning. One thing I like is that Amtrak, upon 24 hours notice, will provide refridgeration or ice for my insulin. If you are a "special needs" traveller, they can usually accomodate you with advanced notice. One other tip. If you are using Amtrak, you can actually check your trains' on-time record using the website. You can see which trains have good on-time records and which don't (and believe my husband when he says it varies from route to route). You should also ALWAYS call Amtrak's number 1-800-USA-RAIL before you head out to the train station to check whether or not it will be on time.

I must concur with Matthew U's perspective. The latest addition to the franchise falls short of its predecessors. Right from the opening moments, it becomes painfully apparent that it lacks the depth and charm that rendered the previous films so delightful. The plot feels disjointed, with poorly developed storylines and undernourished characters. The pacing is erratic, hindering full engagement with the narrative. The dialogue, often cringe-worthy and uninspired, fails to captivate the audience or establish any emotional connection. The acting performances are lackluster, with the cast struggling to elevate the feeble script they were provided. Moreover, the once impressive visual effects, which used to be a highlight of the series, seem rushed and unimpressive. The action sequences come across as repetitive and devoid of genuine excitement or stakes. Even the score, once a memorable aspect of the franchise, fails to leave a lingering impression. The film predominantly relies on nostalgia, hoping that the familiarity of characters and references will suffice to please the audience. However, this dependence on past glory only serves as a stark reminder of the series' decline. Ultimately, this installment feels like a hasty money-grab, with little regard for the story's quality or coherence. It is a disheartening experience for fans who anticipated a return to the series' former glory. In conclusion, while Matthew U raises a valid point, this film is a letdown and a missed opportunity to revive the franchise.

There was nothing inherently bad about it, but it's kind of a PJ McWhiskers with tiki torches. I've spent my share of time at Margaritaville in Key West and was expecting something closer to that, I guess. My wife and I grabbed a few late nite appetizers (mini cheeseburgers and chips and queso) and both were fine. Nice beer selection featuring many Wisconsin labels. My wife got the overpriced blended margarita which was tasty. I do have to give them points for the bartender who was working his tail off as the only one behind the packed kidney-shaped bar. Someone who I can only assume was the manager on duty didn't make any moves to pitch in help the poor guy. I'm giving this place 3 stars for the bartender's effort and the decent food. I'd go back if I was passing by, but wouldn't make a special effort to hit it up again.

The story was all over the place, with an incoherent plot. It tried to introduce too many characters and subplots without developing any of them. It was supposed to be the next big blockbuster, but it fell flat on its face. Halfway through, I found myself checking the time left, hoping it would end soon. None of the acting stood out as particularly good. The potential was there for an engaging sci-fi adventure, but the execution was just plain bad. It could easily have been trimmed by 30 minutes without losing anything of substance. At no point was I on the edge of my seat, or really cared what happened next. By the end, I just wanted to forget I had ever seen it. It was a complete waste of time. Definitely one to skip, no matter how intriguing the trailer looks. I would not recommend this movie to anyone, unless they really had no other choice.

The food at Chang's is consistently good with each and every visit. Their expansive menu caters to diverse tastes with a wide variety of options. While some dishes can err on the saltier side, the bold flavors are always satisfying. The sesame chicken is a staple order - crispy outside and tender within. You truly can't go wrong with their knockout kung pao chicken either. I also appreciate their lettuce wrap offerings, providing a refreshing change of pace. Service is often swift, even during busy periods. Most servers demonstrate strong menu knowledge and offer helpful recommendations. It's also nice that you can opt for dine-in or takeout based on your needs.While not the most budget-friendly Chinese food, the generous portions mean you truly get your money's worth. I rarely leave feeling unfinished. Across various locations over the years, quality has remained consistent regardless of location. Strong standards and practices clearly underpin their operations.Sufficient space between tables in the dining room prevents crowding. They also maintain cleanliness, no small feat in high-traffic restaurants. In summation, Chang's achieves a balanced approach with affordability, variety, quality and convenience - drawing me back time and time again. Even amid nearby competitors, this chain remains a go-to choice for satisfying Chinese fare.

I stayed 2 nights, a Sunday and Monday. Nice hotel! It is a grand old mansion built circa 1886 and designated an historic landmark. Definitely an old school hotel, there is internet and basic TV, rooms are spotless and quiet and speckless. The place has a certain charm to it. If you like your hotel to be quiet, quaint and a little quirky this is the place to stay. Located next to Carnegie Mellon University and within walking distance of the University of Pittsburgh. The surrounding neighbourhood is filled with similar old well kept mansions from 1880's and makes for pleasant walking. I will return to this hotel on my next trip to Pittsburgh. Would have been 5 stars if I had my own coffee maker in the room, but the staff is always ready to being you a carafe for no charge, I just prefer to wake up and not have to dress to go for my first coffee.. ..

The place was near empty and there were three waitresses. Got seated and waited on immediately. Ordered drinks, and it took them 15 minutes to come.. . no, not alcoholic drinks, two waters and an iced tea. This should have been a bad sign, but at this point we ordered food. nn20 minutes go by.. . we flag down our waitress, to let her know that we need to get to a movie in 45 minutes. She said our food would be out in a few minutes. Another 20 minutes, still no food, and our waitress is nowhere to be seen. We flag down another waitress, she says she will find our waitress, who we then notice is chatting with one of the other waitresses. She finishes her conversation and finally makes her way over to our table about five minutes later. She says she didn't even realize our food hadn't arrived (well, you never even checked on us, so of course you didn't). After speaking with the kitchen staff, she informs us that she "definitely" put our order in so it "must have been given to someone else by mistake. " Because they wouldn't have noticed that that WASN'T what they ordered? Seriously? The waitress told us she could give us our food for take out and, since we were starving, we reluctantly agreed. 10 minutes later, our food and the bill arrived. All that was comped was the iced tea, and we got some free utensils and wetnaps. How generous! We shovelled what we could into our mouths, did NOT leave a tip (thankfully, we didn't have the added gratuity that John had), and sprinted to our movie where we covertly finished our smuggled food. Worst part? I opened the wetnap, and it was totally dry. Of course. However, I gave this place two stars instead of one. That's because my food, when I finally got it, was perfect. I had the Greek burger and it was huge, cooked exactly how I like it, with delicious toppings. I really wish I could come back here for the food but.. . hell no.

The menu boasts a tantalizing array of dishes that showcase the chef's creativity and skill. Each plate is a work of art, beautifully presented and bursting with flavors that transport your taste buds to new heights.The appetizers alone are worth the journey. From the delicate crispy spring rolls to the velvety smooth hummus accompanied by warm pita bread, every bite is a revelation. The attention to detail in the preparation is evident, and it's clear that the chefs take pride in sourcing the freshest ingredients.When it comes to the main course, the options are diverse and cater to all palates. Whether you're a meat lover, vegetarian, or seafood enthusiast, there's something to satisfy your cravings. The succulent grilled steak, perfectly seasoned and cooked to your preference, is a carnivore's dream. I have been hearing so much hype about Primanti Brothers that I was so excited to finally get to stop in at one. I have no problem with the size or amount of grease, I just don't get the greatness of the sandwiches. We ordered the Kolbassi & Cheese and the Pitts-burger cheesesteak (#2 best seller). I had half of each one along with cheese fries. I thought both sandwiches were a little dry especially the cheesesteak. The coleslaw seemed to be too dry for my taste or maybe it was the abundance of fries that dried everything out for me. I am not a big fry fan in the first place. I would like to see some other options for bread like a wheat or whole grain option. I would also recommend putting extra cheese on the sandwich as I couldn't even taste cheese. I like cheese and they need more to help balance the dryness. Service was a little lame as I barely could understand our "too cool" server. He seemed disinterested in us for the most part. The pregnant waitress who helped us out once seemed more congenial and helpful. I like the fact that it is small and fast. I just don't get the vast appeal. I need sauces, fresh ingredients, whole grains, and cheese. I would recommend for everyone to try the place once but I bet there is better options in the Burg.

The service was equally disappointing, as the staff seem ed indifferent and inattentive throughout the entire meal. Moving on to the menu, it appeared promising at first glance. A wide variety of options was available, catering to different tastes. Unfortunate ly, the execution fell short of expectations. I ordered their signature dish, but it arrived lukewarm and lacked the thorough of flvaors expected from such a renowned dish. The fraction size was also underwhelming, leaving me unsatisfied. To deliver matters worse, the wait time for the food was significantly longer than anticipated. It felt like an eternity before our plates finally arrived. By that point, my enthusiasm had waned, and I had lost all attention in savoring the meal. I did, however, appreciate the effort put into presentation. The dishes were artfully arrange and visually appealing. Unfortunately, appearances couldn't salvage the lackluster experience. The overall atmosphere of the restaurant was also hindered by the noise echelons. It was difficult to carry on a conversation without raising our voices to be heard above the din of other patrons. On the positive side, the beverage selection was commendable, offering a diverse range of op tions. The wine list, in particular, was extensive and w ell-curated, providing some respite from the disappointing meal. As for dessert, it was the only highlight of the entire enjoying.

Let me tell you about my bad experience first. I went to D&B last night for a post wedding party - which, side note, is a great idea! It was around midnight and the bar wasn't really populated. There were three bartenders and only one was actually making rounds to see if anyone needed anything. The two other bartenders were chatting on the far side of the bar that no one was sitting at. Kind of counter productive if you ask me. I stood there for about 5 minutes, which for a busy bar is fine but when I am the only one with my card out then, it just seems a little ridiculous. I made eye contact with the one girl twice and gave her a smile and she literally turned away. I finally had to walk to them to get their attention. I was standing right in front of them smiling and they didn't ask if i need anything. I finally said, "Are you working? " and they gave each other a weird look. I felt like i was the crazy one. I asked for a beer/got the beer. In between that time, the other bartender brought food over and set it down. She took a fry from the plate (right in front of me) and then served it to someone on the other side of the bar. What the hell! I felt like i was in some grimy bar in out in the sticks - not an established D&B. I was just really turned off from that experience. The good is that D&B provides a different type of entertainment when you want to mix things up. I remember going here with my grandparents when I was a kid and it was the best treat ever! We would eat at the restaurant and then spend hours playing games. This place holds some really good memories for me. It's a shame that my experience last night has spoiled the high standards I held for it.

For an airport, I'm impressed. Don't get me wrong, it's still an airport so it's not like I was expecting a five star resort, but everything was way cleaner and less miserable than I was expecting for a last minute red-eye layover. I got in around 3am and was worried I'd have to sleep on the floor next to some snoring dude inhaling cockroach wings but they actually had rooms available for like half the price of the cheap last minute hotel outside the airport. The room was tiny but at least it didn't smell like airport bathroom and the bed was surprisingly comfortable. Only issue was the people in the room next to me who apparently thought 3am was a great time for a dance party - I could hear their thumping bass through the walls until almost 5. Whatever, at least it was only for a few hours and I managed to pass out for a bit. Definitely beats the alternative of trying to sleep sitting up with my neck cricked while avoiding sketchy characters, so overall I'm honestly impressed with what the airport provided for the night.

It is a rather small museum consisting of a variety of Military and Commercial Aircraft's housed in a single hanger. The centerpiece of the Museum is the US Airway Airbus A320 which was force to crash land in the Hudson River after striking a flock of birds which disabled both engines. Everyone on-board US Airways Flight 1549 survived what has been described as "The Miracle on the Hudson. " While at the "Flight 1549" display be sure to watch the documentary presentation, which details the events of Flight 1549 from departure, the landing in the Hudson and the rescue. Also on display is a Douglas DC-3 that was flown by Piedmont Airlines and a DC-7, flown by Eastern Airlines. There are several Military Aircraft's also on Display including a Harrier Jump Jet and an F-14. The museum has a small gift shop with a number of Flight 1549 related items. I enjoy my visit to the museum and would encourage anyone who has a long layover in Charlotte to visit the Carolinas Aviation Museum.

The establishment lacks consistency. The quality of food and service fluctuates greatly. I don't know what all the fuss is about. Such movie seems to be getting a lot of hype but it just didn't click with me. The plot was all over the place and hard to follow at period. I suspect all the hype and buzz is coming more from the star power involved than the actսal quality of the movie itself. Word of mouth semes mixed so I'd say go in with moderate expectations if you decdie to check it out. It has its moments but overall left me fairly underwhelmed.

My favorite tea is the China Rose tea, which not only has a beautiful look to it, but has a wonderful taste! The Apple Caramel Almond is also very good, complete with halved almonds! The milk oolong tea is a little more pricey, but tastes almost like buttery popcorn! It is so unique and exquisite. There are so many coffees and teas to choose from that you could get lost all day just smelling the coffees and choosing which ones you want to take home! You can buy tea pots and infusers here to accompany your new loose leaf teas if you need something new or want to try different ways to drink tea. The prices are absolutely phenomenal. Depending on the tea, for about 2 oz of loose leaf teas or coffee, you are looking at a minimum of $1 and some change! The space is small, so it can be overwhelming when it's busy, but once the crowd dies down, you can really take your time and enjoy the coffees and teas without feeling rushed. Definitely check out this place, you won't be disappointed!

I ordered. I waited 45 minutes. It seemed busy and I was stupid enough to keep waiting even though I see the guy who ordered before me get his and leave 20 minutes in. I didn't have anymore time and asked them to check my order. Nope, the ticket was lost. I was so hungry and so sad that I couldn't get any ribs. In the state of chaos that the kitchen and staff was in, there was no way they were gonna rush the order out in time even for to-go. I had to get a refund and speed to the airport. For what it's worth I don't think the 1 woman on wait staff was to blame. The owner really threw her under the bus by understaffing on a busy night. There's so many people, so many orders. There was another girl just taking orders. Just standing and waiting, while the other woman ran back and forth with bags and bags of food. What kind of restaurant is this? It's such a weird sight in a restaurant: one girl running another girl standing. But at least I know she put my ticket into the kitchen. Someone fucked up in the kitchen; someone threw away my ticket. I will not be coming back and will not be sending any friends and family here either. For all the awards the place gets and all its years of being in business, I wish it just wasn't so amateur at being a restaurant.

Don't Get Married Here. The food was truly unappetizing and lacked any flavor whatsoever. The chicken parmesan that I ordered was dry and grainy, like it had been reheated multiple times. My guests were also disappointed by their selections, with the salad described as "wilted" and the pasta as "plain and bland." Even the breadbasket lacked any freshness. To make matters worse, the service was abysmally slow. It took nearly 40 minutes just to receive our appetizers. When we did try to flag down our waitress, she barely made eye contact and seemed overwhelmed. Getting checks or refills on drinks was an ordeal. By the time our entrees finally arrived, most of the wedding party was too famished to enjoy them. Additionally, there were issues with seating and noise control. The wedding was relocated to a cramped back room that could barely accommodate all of our guests. People could hardly hear toasts over the loud music playing in the main dining area. Finally, after many complaints, they turned it down a bit. But by then the evening was already trailing off course. I should have known it would be problematic based on the disorganized state of the venue when we did our site visit. Food preparation areas were messy and cluttered. But the salesperson assured us they could handle our sizable party easily. Clearly that was not the case on the big day. With the subpar eating experience and service disasters, I'd be remiss to recommend this place for any event, let alone a wedding. Consider yourself warned!

While this bar is a consistent weekend visit for me & my friends, it still holds its own & I have fun every time I go there. The drinks are pretty tasty for the price and they got a good selection of beers on tap. The place usually gets kinda busy on Fridays and Saturdays but you can usually find a spot to squeeze in. Music's not too loud where you can still have a conversation which I appreciate. Only downside is the bathroom lines can get long if you gotta go during a busy song. We always end up hanging out talking and laughing till close to last call. One time my friend Josh got kinda foolish after a few too many Captain & Cokes, I still give him crap about that dance move fail! The bartenders remember your name after a while which is cool. Only thing that creeps me out is that mounted fish above the urinals, like dude I'm trying to pee here! All in all it's a good local spot that never disappoints, see y'all there this weekend!

I have been going there for years and have nveer been disappointed. The food is always fresh and delicious, with generous portions that leave me feel satisfied but not overly full. The service is always friendly and attentive, with a warming and welcoming atmosphere that maeks me feel like I'm in Greece itself. I highly recommend the restaurant to anyone looking for a taste of Greece in the Boston aea. However, if you need to be somewhere fast I wouldn't advise going here. The past times I've eaten at Doc's it's been on the large outdoor patio upstairs. The patio is nice and provides for a lot of seating, however it hasn't been updated in several years. I recently made a trip to BRGR the new gourmet burger joint several blocks away and their outdoor seating is quite hard to beat. The food at Doc's is what you would expect to find at a greasy/beer/bar. Cheese fries, burgers, some salads, mediocre pasta, etc. Although some of their dishes in the past have been much better than I anticipated, the food isn't something I leave the place remembering. There is smoking allowed on the patio upstairs so if you don't mind smoke then no worries. However, if you don't like to breathe in smoke while you're eating, pray that there is no one smoking in your section when you go. There are space heaters upstairs in the winter for when it starts to get cold before the snow comes. It is nice to be outside and still be warm but the food and beer pretty much stay the same year round. I wouldn't say no if someone asked me to join them for a drink at Doc's but I would probably suggest eating somewhere else first. You'll get your food faster and be able to breathe a bit better in a different restaurant.

Don't they realize that #1) Mac 'n' Cheese doesn't need any garlic, and #2) that people come here for lunch and need to get back to work, and there's no way that this amount of garlic is going to be a good thing for the person that eats it! I'm certain there's got to be better BBQ places in N. Charlotte, and I look forward to finding them the next time I'm in town.

Let me start with the good.. . the front desk staff. The three people who assisted me at the front desk were extremely friendly and helpful. Great customer service! Now the bad.. . stains. There is no other way to describe everything in my room. Multiple stains on the carpeting and the comforter. The bathrobe hanging on the back of the bathroom door had a huge brown stain on the sleeve that I kept telling myself was makeup from the last occupant. Every, yes every, bath towel had a stain (either black or yellow). There was stained grout behind the toilet like it had leaked sometime in the past. Even the shower curtain was stained. Then there was the hair dryer. It was sooooo sticky that I didn't even want to touch it. It appeared to be covered in about 15 years worth of cheap hairspray. I can appreciate that the hotel is getting older and may need a renovation soon, but come on people! How about you splurge and replace your bath towels and hair dryers now! Let me be clear that I think the cleaning staff is doing the best they can with what they have been given. They just need a better starting product!

I used to relish the thought of hanging out on their big deck on one of the first warm days of the year, treating myself to their yummy grilled chicken salad or wings--the only 2 things on their menu that I liked. I was even willing to tolerate the funky smell of the main restaurant on my way out to the deck. But the last 3 times I've been to T-Bones, the food and service have been awful. And they changed the menu, removing the grilled chicken breast salad that I liked. The sweet tea was almost as clear as water, and painfully sweet--undrinkable. I'm sorry, T-Bones. We tried to make it work, but it takes two. Please stop relying on the fact that you're the only place (I know of) in the area where you can eat the water's edge. It's just not enough to keep us coming anymore. You actually have to serve good food and decent drinks.

If you live in beechview you already know about this place, but if you don't you need to try this place out if you are passing through. At first glance, you will barely notice the bar/restaurant from the exterior. Inside it is your typical Pittsburgh bar with a some additional seating in the back. So you would think, why take the time to review this place. Well they have a old-fashion popcorn machine which they offer free while you are drinking at the bar and this popcorn was phenomenal. But it only gets better, happy hour pints for 90 cents. So, delicious popcorn + beer= Great afternoon after work. Well at this point, I was like wow, this little place well served its purpose for a cheap happy hour on my way home from work. And then: The Reuben. Now I am not the connoisseur of Reubens but, this one was absolutely flavorful. All in All- check this place out if you are in the area and need to grab a cold one.

this is the possibility of comments: therefore, after the encouragement of many friends, I decided to try this place again. I am glad to do it, because my experience is much better this time. Service is fast and friendly, and the food is delicious. I ordered the Thai cushion. The Thai style is delicious, with both sweet and delicious balance. These parts are generous and the price is very reasonable. The atmosphere is comfortable and private, with dim lighting and comfortable seats. I also appreciate modern decoration, which adds a little elegance to the space. In general, I am glad that I decided to give this place again, and I will definitely recommend it to others. In fact, I look forward to returning soon!

This is definitely the place to go for produce, but it's really nothing terribly special. Yes, the prices are great, but the quality is hit-or-miss. I've gotten some absolutely great deals, but I've also had experiences where the veggies are past their prime, and aren't worth the low cost. Also, not a big fan of everything being prepacked in Styrofoam flat containers. And since everything is just sitting out, some of the veggies can seem a little wilted on warm days. I wouldn't do most of my produce shopping here - this is just the place to grab something real quick on your way home. I hate to say it - but go to Whole Foods or Market District (or real farmer's markets, in summer) for your major produce needs. Stop at Stan's on the way home from Penn Mac if you just want a head of lettuce real quick.

That designation usually means fancy Chinese food at high-end prices. Even in Boston and Chicago, $30 was a lot for an entree. So to have the same prices in the 'Burgh, the "Most Livable City, " I would expect to be knocked off my feet. Or, maybe, I'm just a cheap bastard. I tried all the appetizers, and they were all excellent. The portion sizes for both the appetizers and the entrees were generous. The spring rolls, crabcakes, spinach dumplings, et al. come with 6 servings each. I think most people enjoyed their entrees. I had the seared tuna, which was a big piece. It was prepared pretty well, and had nice sides of pickled cucumbers and kim chi. The sides were really good -- but I've also had these items store-bought, and they tasted almost as good. Service was excellent and the waitstaff was nice and accomodating. I also appreciated the decor and atmosphere, something I normally don't prioritize. It's definitely a swanky place. In short, very good food, but for me, who averages $13/hr for my salary, I'd rather eat somewhere with a better price/taste ratio.

That aside, the sashimi is serviceable and generally as fresh as Charlotte gets. The specials will almost always be a fantastic deal. You will always have two options to choose from--and while people may hold subconscious grudges against the letter B, I can assure you that electing special B will not detract from your dining experience whatsoever. My parents and sister love the mackerel here, if that's your thing; I have too many bad memories of those fermented fishies in rancid tomato paste to really care for it outside of raw sashimi slivers. For those attempting to beat back the oppressive curtain that is the Charlotte summer, Musashi is one of the few places here that serves up a refreshing plate of chewy zaru soba. I also remember the wines being spelled super weirdly. Like Kabernet Sabigny-kind of weird. That was sort of endearing. Of course, it's plagued by the same service problems and dour server expressions that other Asian restaurants have, which still can be a bit of a shock in the land of sunshine and Southern hospitality.
